papers.title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
papers.abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $ρ(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\leρ(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $ρ(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $ρ(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3]. The notebook to verify the computer search portion, Verify_RM(1,9).ipynb, contains all data and recomputes each check, and may be found in the repository https://github.com/FreemanSlaughter/Covering-Radius.

papers.title: Primary components and large prime factors of cyclotomic values
papers.abstract: Let $Φ_r(a,b)$ denote the homogeneous cyclotomic value. For sufficiently large $A$, uniformly for $1/2\leq B\leq A$, $r\geq3$ and $Z\geq2$, the number of coprime pairs in $(A,2A]\times(B,2B]$ whose greatest prime factor $P(Φ_r(a,b))$ is at most $Z$ is $O(AB/\varphi(r)+\sqrt{r/\varphi(r)}\,π(Z;r,1))$, where $π(Z;r,1)$ counts primes at most $Z$ congruent to $1$ modulo $r$. If $n=n(A)\to\infty$ through positive integers and $1\leq H(A)=o(\log A)$, then $P(a^{2^n}+1)>2^nAH(A)$ for almost all $a\in(A,2A]$, and $P(a^{2^n}+b^{2^n})>2^nA^2H(A)$ for almost all coprime pairs in $(A,2A]^2$, with no further restriction on $n$. For every fixed $α>0$ and every $r\geq A^α$, pairwise distinct primitive prime divisors of $Φ_r(a)$ can be selected for all but $O_α(A^{1-c_α})$ bases in $(A,2A]$, where $c_α>0$. For coprime positive integers $a,b$ with $\max(a,b)\geq2$ and $r\geq3$, put $C=Φ_r(a,b)$ and $S=\varphi(r)^2\log\max(a,b)$. Uniformly as $S\to\infty$, $\max_{p\mid C}p^{v_p(C)}\geq(5/16-o(1))S$. For every positive function $h(S)\to\infty$, $\sum_{p\mid C,\;p^{v_p(C)}>S/h(S)}v_p(C)\log p =(1-o(1))\log C$ uniformly in the same limit.

papers.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

papers.title: HideOut - User Protection Against Localization with Throughput Guarantees in Mobile Networks
papers.abstract: Channel state information (CSI) in cellular networks is primarily used to maintain quality of service (QoS), yet it leaks privacy-sensitive information, in particular the user equipment's (UE) location. CSI is reported in plaintext on a publicly available schedule; thus, capturing it on the air and using a well trained AI model to localize the UE is straightforward. This simplicity in the attack execution makes it a serious privacy vulnerability. Using conventional privacy enhancing techniques, such as additive perturbation from differential privacy, to protect location data can potentially degrade the downlink communication quality. We present HideOut, a client-side defense mechanism that preserves the user's location from neural-based localization methods, while maintaining their downlink Spectral Efficiency (SE). Unlike generic adversarial attacks, HideOut treats downlink SE as a strict constraint in an optimization setting. Under maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, we show that a user-selected SE loss budget can be converted into an angular rate-feasible constraint on the reported channel vector. HideOut then performs gradient-based localization obfuscation while projecting each update onto this rate-feasible set. We evaluate HideOut against four CSI-based localization architectures under both white-box and black-box assumptions. Across models, HideOut increases localization ambiguity (error) from approximately $1--2$ m to $72--85$ m while keeping downlink SE loss within a $1\%$ budget. These results show that CSI-based localization can be substantially degraded at negligible communication quality loss when adversarial perturbations are made aware of the wireless link.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient UAV Covert Communications via Metaheuristic Optimization
papers.abstract: Wireless communication systems increasingly require not only confidentiality but also transmission undetectability, motivating covert communications. This paper studies an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled covert communication system where a UAV serves a legitimate receiver in the presence of multiple active and colluding wardens with imperfect location information. We maximize covert energy efficiency (CEE) by jointly optimizing the UAV's 3D trajectory and transmit power while accounting for energy. To address the resulting non-convex problem with robust covertness constraints, we develop Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based metaheuristic algorithms and compare them with a Block Coordinate Descent with Successive Convex Approximation (BCD-SCA) benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed methods improve CEE while satisfying covertness constraints.

papers.title: Diagram of Geodesic Intervals in $C'(1/8)$-Groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a group characterized by a small cancellation $C'(1/8)$-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments $[x,y]$ of length $n$ can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise $C'(1/8)$-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment $[x,y]$. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by $n$, and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.

papers.title: Complete Bernstein functions and real powers of P-matrices
papers.abstract: We classify the nonzero complete Bernstein functions whose matrix functions preserve every real P-matrix in every order. They are precisely $f(z)=a+bz$, with $a,b\ge0$ and $a+b>0$, and $f(z)=a+cz/(z+s)$, with $a\ge0$ and $c,s>0$. For each fixed order $n\ge4$, the preservers vanishing at zero are exactly $cz$ and $cz/(z+s)$; every other such function admits a strictly totally positive counterexample. For a finite positive measure $μ$ on $(0,\infty)$, put $g(z)=\int z/(z+s)\,μ(ds)$ and $M_t=\int s^t\,μ(ds)$. In every fixed order $n\ge4$, a finite constant shift restores preservation on all real P-matrices if and only if $M_{r_n}$ and $M_{-r_n}$ are finite, where $r_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$. Every $a>c_n\sqrt{M_{r_n}M_{-r_n}}$ is sufficient, with $c_n$ depending only on $n$. A complete Bernstein function vanishing at zero admits a possibly different repairing constant in every order exactly when it is linear, or is a pure kernel mixture with all positive and negative integer moments finite. For principal real powers, the preserving exponents are $\mathbb R$ in order one, $[-1,1]$ in orders two and three, and $\{-1,0,1\}$ in every higher order. An explicit rational determinant-one totally positive family gives negative principal minors uniformly on prescribed compact subsets of $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$.

papers.title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
papers.abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.

papers.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
papers.abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.

papers.title: Four-Dimensional Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones: A Complete Classification
papers.abstract: We classify all four-dimensional semi-homogeneous convex cones, i.e., closed, pointed, full-dimensional cones whose connected automorphism group has principal orbits of codimension at most one. On such cones, the Monge-Ampère equation defining the canonical barrier reduces to an ordinary differential equation. This makes this barrier computationally accessible. The semi-homogeneous cones can then be used in modeling by conic programs. An obvious subset of such cones are the homogeneous cones. The key point allowing the classification is that for all other cones, the automorphism group has a three-dimensional subgroup acting locally faithfully on the principal orbits. This subgroup must have a Lie algebra which is either abelian or a direct product of a 1-dimensional algebra and a two-dimensional algebra generated by $A,B$ satisfying $[A,B]=B$. In both cases we classify all 4-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, and for each representation all invariant convex cones. For every cone an orbit invariant is computed.

papers.title: Classification of three-dimensional Leibniz dialgebras with two-dimensional annihilator
papers.abstract: A Leibniz dialgebra is a vector space with two bilinear products $\dashv$ and $\vdash$ satisfying the dialgebra analogue of the right Leibniz identity. This notion is obtained by the same standard procedure that turns the associative identity into the axioms of Loday's associative dialgebras. In particular, $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is a right Leibniz algebra, so a Leibniz dialgebra is a Leibniz algebra together with a second, compatible product. This paper recalls the definition of Leibniz dialgebras and continue the algebraic classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz dialgebras. This paper describes up to isomorphism all Leibniz dialgebras $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv,\vdash)$ for which the Leibniz algebra $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is isomorphic to one of the algebras $\mathcal{L}_{8}(α)$, $\mathcal{L}_9$, $\mathcal{L}_{10}$, $\mathcal{L}_{11}$ of the classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz algebras. The result consists 18 families of pairwise non-isomorphic Leibniz dialgebras, nine of which depend on a complex parameter.

papers.title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
papers.abstract: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 π^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 π^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

papers.title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
papers.abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $π$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $π((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-κ}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $κ>0$ solves $p^κ+pκ=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

papers.title: Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics
papers.abstract: What does it mean to tell the story of a mathematician? Written as a letter to a young Black mathematician, this article reflects on how stories shape our understanding of mathematics and our sense of belonging within the mathematical community. Through the lens of Hidden Figures Revealed, a project documenting Black mathematicians at The Ohio State University, I discuss humanity, mathematics, and context as three guiding principles for mathematical storytelling. In particular, I reflect on how this framework emerged through archival research, shaped historical narratives, and informed mathematical learning experiences.

papers.title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
papers.abstract: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{ρ,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\midρ$. For $c=2$ the graphs are exactly the cocktail party graphs, and for $c=3$ they are exactly the Cartesian product $K_3\,\square\,K_3$ of two triangles, the Petersen graph and its complement. We also show that such a graph need not be transmission-regular: Seidel switching the lattice graph $K_6\,\square\,K_6$ with respect to a line and the triangular graph $T(11)$ with respect to a maximal clique of size $10$ gives graphs on $36$ and $55$ vertices with distance spectra $\{54,0^{(26)},(-6)^{(9)}\}$ and $\{81,0^{(45)},(-9)^{(9)}\}$. Among the graphs of diameter $2$ obtained by switching a strongly regular graph with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ with respect to one part of an equitable partition, these two are the only ones that have exactly three distance eigenvalues and are not transmission-regular. We also observe that the transmission-regular graphs with exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues, the smallest one being $-3$, are exactly the complements of the strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ other than the cocktail party graphs.

papers.title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
papers.abstract: For Hermitian matrices $α,β$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^α$ and $m$ letters $e^β$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)\ge\Tr e^{nα+mβ}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.
papers.comments: Proof by Claude (Anthropic) checked by Gemini Opus (Google). The author guided Claude in finding the proof

papers.title: Partial $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings: (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$. In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,α}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property. In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$. We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations. Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.

papers.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
papers.abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Ważewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

papers.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
papers.abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.
papers.comments: 6 pages, including code; the final result remains exactly the same as in the original paper, only the argument changes. Erratum to arXiv:1703.06609

papers.title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
papers.abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

papers.title: The sum of sizes of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
papers.abstract: Families $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_m\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ are cross-intersecting if every member of one family meets every member of each other family. A family is nontrivial if its members have no common element. For $n>2k$ and $m\ge3$, we determine the maximum sum of the sizes of $m$ nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families. We prove the sharp bound \[ \sum_{i=1}^{m}|\mathcal A_i| \le \max\bigl\{m\,h(n,k,1),\ g(n,k)+3(m-1)\bigr\}, \] where \[ h(n,k,1)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+1 \] and \[ g(n,k)=\binom nk-2\binom{n-k}k -\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}k. \] We also characterize all equality cases. Two types of extremal configurations arise: copies of a maximum nontrivial intersecting family, and copies of a specific three-member nontrivial intersecting family together with its full cross-intersecting companion. The proof applies a known restricted lexicographic comparison to obtain the weighted bound for shifted families, and uses local generator reductions for critically shifted families. These reductions exploit shiftedness after removing the common core of a section, while preserving nontriviality and the required shadow relations between sections.

papers.title: Large Maximal Intersecting Families with Covering Number Three
papers.abstract: Let $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$. The largest size of an intersecting family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ with covering number at least three is \[ g_1(n,k)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k}{k-1}+3, \] attained by a unique family up to isomorphism. We prove that every other maximal intersecting family $\mathcal F$ with covering number three satisfies \[ |\mathcal F|\le M(n,k)=\max\{q(n,k),g_2(n,k)\}, \] where \begin{align*} q(n,k)&=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-3}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}{k-1}+3,\\ g_2(n,k)&=g_1(n,k)-\binom{n-k-3}{k-3}+1. \end{align*} This bound is attained for every $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$, so $M(n,k)$ is the second largest distinct size. For $k=4$, $g_1(n,4)=13n-69$ and $M(n,4)=12n-61$. For $k\ge5$, we have $M(n,k)=q(n,k)$ when $2k<n\le3k-2$ and $M(n,k)=g_2(n,k)$ when $n\ge3k-2$; the two terms coincide only at $n=3k-2$. We also classify all families attaining $M(n,k)$ that admit a critically shifted labeling, including additional nonisomorphic families at $n=2k+1$. The proof combines local replacements with an inverse-shift estimate and gives a new proof of the known maximum and its uniqueness.

papers.title: Inference in an interactive multi-type branching network
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between $d$ individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available. This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
papers.abstract: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.

papers.title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
papers.abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. This approach provides a dataset-independent framework for comparing complexity measures across their full range and reveals substantial differences between measures for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are largely hidden by conventional uniform sampling. Using the NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.

papers.title: Loss of Monotonicity in the Vector Play Model and Consequences for Newton-Type Solvers
papers.abstract: The vector play model (VPM) replaces the implicit minimization of the energy-based hysteresis model (EBM) by an explicit update. Its tangent contains the product of the Hessians of two unrelated potentials and is unsymmetric. Hence, the VPM has no co-energy density at frozen memory, and the skew part makes $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ lose monotonicity in a band just outside the pinning circle, into which small time steps drive the sliding states. In composite models, the determinant of the tangent can change sign, which explains published failures of the local inversion $\boldsymbol{B}\mapsto\boldsymbol{H}$, and where it is negative, $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ is not injective. In the scalar potential formulation, the exact tangent keeps a descent guarantee, whereas symmetric surrogates of the tangent, such as the symmetrized tangent or Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) updates, lose it and become ascent directions where the skew part dominates, as computations of TEAM Problem 32 confirm. It is therefore recommended to use solvers with an unsymmetric tangent.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Magnetics

papers.title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
papers.abstract: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is verified by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Coinduction in Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: A grounded arithmetic counts a sentence as true only when a terminating process establishes it; a sentence no such process settles has no value. Such a logic can state that an event happens, but not that it never happens under unbounded choice. This paper extends such a logic so that it can. The base is Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) with Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA)'s least-fixed-point reading and ground induction. It adds a separate greatest-fixed-point former $ν$ with Park's coinduction rule, proves that one former cannot carry both ground induction and coinduction, and adds a dichotomy rule: the classical disjunction between a least-fixed-point atom and the greatest-fixed-point atom of its dual, under a derivable premise that the body's leaves are decided. The systems are sound for an explicit model reading every $ν$-body at its greatest fixed point, hence consistent; they agree with the least model wherever it has a value and prove sentences it leaves without one. The dichotomy replaces the underivable hypothesis that an order is well-founded by the derivable one that its steps are decided; the change of model pays for the move. With ground induction the dichotomy derives the omniscience rule of the sibling arithmetic OGA, so the system has no semantics whose certificates for universals are its own proofs. The systems prove, as single sentences, that every decided tree is well-founded or has an infinite branch given by a term, total in the new model; that random assignment terminates while its divergent twin runs forever; that a fair loop terminates and the alternating-bit protocol delivers every message; that open games are determined; that the termination gap in Nakata and Uustalu's trace semantics closes; and that Cinderella wins the bucket game at capacity three. Isabelle/HOL checks every result.

papers.title: The Dilate Rollercoaster
papers.abstract: Given a finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ and a multiset of non-zero integers $Λ=\{λ_1, \ldots, λ_k\}$, the dilate sum \[Λ\cdot A:=λ_1\cdot A+λ_2\cdot A+\cdots+λ_k\cdot A =\{λ_1a_1+\cdots+λ_ka_k: a_1, \ldots, a_k\in A\}.\] For a non-zero real number $r$, say that $Λ_2$ $r$-dominates $Λ_1$ if we can partition some of the elements of $Λ_2$ into blocks summing to the elements of $r\cdotΛ_1$. Then for all finite subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, $Λ_2\cdot A$ contains a translate of $r\cdot(Λ_1\cdot A)$, and hence $|Λ_1\cdot A|\le|Λ_2\cdot A|$ for all $A$. In a recent paper, Kravitz (arXiv:2606.27087) proves the converse: if $Λ_2$ does not $r$-dominate $Λ_1$ for any $r$, then there exists a finite set $A$ satisfying $|Λ_1\cdot A|>|Λ_2\cdot A|$. For example, $\{2, 3, 5, 7\}$ does not contain two disjoint subsets with a sum ratio of 7, and so there exists a finite $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ for which $|A+7\cdot A|>|2\cdot A+3\cdot A+5\cdot A+7\cdot A|$. We extend Kravitz's method to apply it to multiple inequalities and multiple sets, showing that for multisets $Λ_{i,j}$ with $1\le i\le k$ and $1\le j\le\ell$, there exist finite sets $A_1, \ldots, A_\ell\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ such that for all $1\le i<k$ \[|Λ_{i,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i,\ell}\cdot A_\ell| >|Λ_{i+1,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i+1,\ell}\cdot A_\ell|\] provided there do not exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2\le k$ and a non-zero scalar $r$ such that $Λ_{i_2,j}$ $r$-dominates $Λ_{i_1,j}$ for all $1\le j\le\ell$. Along the way, we resolve the analogue of Nathanson's Problem 1 for his Theorem 4 (arXiv:1604.08940), as well as the problems in Section 1.4.3 of Kravitz's paper.

papers.title: Ad-conditions for higher-order recurrences: Dunkl and matrix-valued settings
papers.abstract: The ad-conditions of Duistermaat and Grünbaum characterize bispectrality for a pair of differential operators. M.~Reach observed that a sequence of functions which is simultaneously an eigenfunction of a second-order differential operator and satisfies a recurrence relation of arbitrary order must satisfy a different kind of ad-conditions. We prove that the Reach ad-conditions are also sufficient, by an argument which is purely algebraic. This motivated us to explore ad-conditions in two new directions: to Dunkl differential-difference operators, where the coefficients of the ad-condition become elements of the Dunkl algebra and the reflection enters as a coefficient, and to matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials, where we exhibit ad-conditions for several families of exceptional matrix-valued polynomials satisfying five- and seven-term recurrence relations.

papers.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

papers.title: Parameter-Free First-Order Method for Constrained Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: Constrained variational inequalities (VIs) provide a general framework for modeling and solving complementarity and equilibrium problems with functional constraints. In this paper, we propose a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding (PFAOS) method for solving monotone VIs with convex smooth constraints. For a single constraint, PFAOS achieves an operator evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ and a constraint gradient evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$, without requiring prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant of the VI operator or the smoothness constant of the constraint function. We further extend PFAOS to multiple constraints by incorporating a primal-dual hybrid gradient update, yielding a multi-constrained PFAOS (MC-PFAOS) method that preserves the same evaluation complexities. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted on large-scale games with coupling constraints to validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
papers.abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.

papers.title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we define a new partial distance on hyperspaces consisting of closed balls, which is a partial metric in the sense of Matthews. We prove that these partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the metric spaces from which the corresponding ball spaces arise are complete. Finally, we compare the topology induced by the new partial distance with that induced by the classical Hausdorff distance.

papers.title: Costate Estimation and Covector Mapping for Bernstein Polynomial Direct Methods in Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Bernstein polynomial approximation of continuous functions has a slower rate of convergence as compared to other approximation methods. ``The fact seems to have precluded any numerical application of Bernstein polynomials from having been made. Perhaps they will find application when the properties of the approximant in the large are of more importance than the closeness of the approximation.'' -- has remarked P.J. Davis in his 1963 book Interpolation and Approximation. This paper presents a direct approximation method for nonlinear optimal control problems with mixed input and state constraints based on Bernstein polynomial approximation, in which the dynamic and path constraints are imposed at the Bernstein coefficients (control points). We provide a rigorous analysis showing that, under convergence assumptions on the control polygons, the proposed method yields consistent approximations of time continuous optimal control problems and can be used for costate estimation of the optimal control problems. In particular, multipliers satisfying a relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system of the resulting nonlinear program, scaled by the quadrature weight, approximate the costate and the multipliers of the optimal control problem. Owing to the structure of the Bernstein differentiation matrix, the discrete transversality conditions are contained in the relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system, and no additional closure conditions need to be added to it. This result leads to the formulation of the Covector Mapping Theorem for Bernstein polynomial approximation.

papers.title: Upper bounds for packings of cylinders around the unit sphere
papers.abstract: In this note we study the problem of packing infinite circular cylinders tangent to the unit sphere. For a given number of cylinders $N$, $N\geq 3$, the maximal common cylinder radius $R_N$ is the maximum $R$ for which there exist $N$ circular cylinders of radius $R$ with non-overlapping interiors, all tangent to the unit sphere. In 1990, Kuperberg conjectured that there does not exist a packing of more than 6 cylinders of radius one tangent to the unit sphere, that is, $R_7<1$. This conjecture was recently confirmed by an exhaustive computer-assisted case analysis. Here we prove new bounds for $R_N$ for small $N$ by considering an auxiliary configuration of spherical quadrilaterals. In particular, we provide a short geometric proof of Kuperberg's conjecture and show that $R_7<0.9978$.

papers.title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
papers.abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.

papers.title: Generic Linear Momentum Escape for Twist Maps
papers.abstract: We prove that linear momentum escape is generic in the $C^{1,α}$ topology for smooth potential perturbations of exact symplectic twist maps, for every $0<α<1$. We assume a $C^2$ generating function, a uniform twist condition, and uniform upper bounds on $D_{11}S$ and $D_{22}S$. For an open dense set of potentials, every sufficiently small momentum drift is realized by an orbit. This genericity result does not extend in general to the $C^2$ topology. We give examples with no nonzero linear drift under $C^2$-small perturbations in every dimension. In dimension one, a second example has bounded momentum along every orbit under $C^2$-small perturbations.

papers.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
papers.abstract: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

papers.title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.

papers.title: A Directed Cubical Framework for k-critical Bipersistence Modules
papers.abstract: In topological data analysis, multiparameter persistence modules (MPMs) are used to analyze data with multiple parameters. Summarizing topological information for MPMs is a non-trivial task; one useful summary of bipersistence modules is the fibered barcode \cite{lesnick2015interactive,lesnick2025fast}. In this paper, we use a directed topological construction of the parameter space of a bifiltration to extend the fibered barcode. Specifically, given a $k$-critical bifiltration $F$, we build an associated directed Euclidean cubical complex $C$ whose directed paths each correspond to a one-parameter subfiltration of $F$. The path space of $C$, $\di{C}$, is used to define the \emph{extended fibered barcode}, which contains all possible monotonically increasing paths in $C$. We show that there can be paths in $\di{C}$ which generate filtrations not obtainable along a line with positive slope, and that all lines with positive slope have a path in $\di{C}$ that generate an equivalent barcode. We introduce two types of equivalence for these restricted modules: combinatorial equivalence of diagrams, and simplicial equivalence of the filtrations generating the modules. We show that removing certain cubes from $C$ yields a subcomplex on which dihomotopic paths induce simplicially equivalent filtrations, and hence combinatorially equivalent diagrams.

papers.title: Two moments suffice for Bessel approximation: conditioned differences, contingency tables, and probabilistic divide-and-conquer
papers.abstract: We develop Stein's method, with explicit constants throughout, for the discrete Bessel distribution: the law of a Poisson variable given its difference from an independent Poisson variable. The Bessel family is characterized by a birth-death operator with quadratic death rate $n(n+k)$ and as the exact fixed-point set of a centered quadratic-bias transform, and we prove a dependency expansion of Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon type: two joint moments of a column array control the total-variation distance from the conditioned row sum to a matched Bessel law. Applied to the row-constrained Fisher-Yates ensemble on $2\times c$ contingency tables -- independent Bernoulli or capped-Poisson entries conditioned on the row-sum difference, column sums free -- this yields a limit theorem -- which upgrades to the entire conditioned table at the same two-moment error -- a completely explicit enumeration estimate, and an exact divide-and-conquer sampler with certified acceptance. The entire apparatus -- operator, expansion, enumeration, sampler -- generalizes to $r\times c$ tables, where conditioning on all successive row differences produces a hyper-Bessel law. Verification scripts are included as ancillary files.
papers.comments: 46 pages. Numerical verification code included as ancillary files

papers.title: A nonarithmetic lattice from a mirror in the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga construction
papers.abstract: We prove that the stabilizer of a reflection mirror of the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga lattice $\mathcal{C}(G_{29},3)$ induces a nonarithmetic lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$. This lattice is not commensurable with any Deligne-Mostow lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$ or any lattice in the twenty-two nonarithmetic classes listed by Deraux, Parker and Paupert.

papers.title: Modeling and Analysis of Cooling Induced Isotropic Nematic Transitions in Pharmaceutical Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: This paper studies the phase transition from an isotropic to a nematic liquid crystal driven by controlled cooling, motivated by the manufacturing of next-generation pharmaceutical drugs. Using the non-isothermal Ericksen model for liquid crystals with a variable degree of orientation, we formulate the problem as a stiff, quasilinear system of parabolic partial differential equations. We establish a consistent thermodynamic framework, prove the well-posedness of the system, and conduct a rigorous asymptotic and numerical scaling analysis of the moving phase boundary in a cylindrical cell subjected to bottom-wall convective cooling. Our analysis identifies a critical sample thickness that separates two distinct physical regimes. Below this threshold, the transition follows the cooling dynamics and the material remains quasi-isothermal. Above the thickness threshold, bulk thermal diffusion governs the dynamics, imposing a dominant thermal delay characterized by a concave quadratic propagation front. These results demonstrate that scaling from laboratory characterization to industrial production fundamentally alters the spatial thermal history of the material, providing a predictive mathematical framework to optimize cooling protocols for kinetic arrest.

papers.title: Stein's method for negative binomial and hyper-negative-binomial laws, with applications
papers.abstract: We develop Stein's method for the negative binomial law and for the hyper-negative-binomial law, the law of the smallest row total of an array of independent geometric variables given the differences of the row totals, with every constant explicit. The main instrument is a comparison of two biasings of the approximated variable, which cancels the rate term exactly at the matched parameter. We provide total variation bounds for sums of independent geometric variables at drifting parameters, for sums of dependent geometric variables (the Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon theorem with geometric summands and the Poisson law as an endpoint), and for Poisson mixtures; the exact conditional law of negative-binomial counts given their differences, with the Bessel law as its Poisson limit; and a dependency expansion for the column direction of a contingency table. A final section verifies every bound numerically, with one script per result.
papers.comments: 45 pages. Ancillary files: a Python verification suite (NumPy only), one script per result, run with python3 run_all.py

papers.title: Phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We study the phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures of the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator (Kerr medium). Starting from the time-evolved state, we derive analytical expressions for the Dunkl-Husimi $Q$-function and a normalized angular Husimi profile. The Dunkl parameter modifies the coherent-state excitation weights and the parity-dependent phase accumulation, producing angular anisotropy and asymmetric phase-space separation. For the half-integer deformation $μ=0.5$, the dynamics generate asymmetric multicomponent Husimi patterns with unequal peak heights and an early reconstruction at $t=π/λ$. For the deformation $μ=1.0$, the Husimi distribution exhibits broadening while retaining its multimodal structure and unitary evolution. At the fundamental nonlinear revival time, the wave packet is reconstructed for the selected parameter ratio. The standard Kerr dynamics are recovered in the limit $μ\rightarrow 0$.

papers.title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective. We show that, if the density of $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$, measured with respect to a fixed reference metric, decays more slowly than $T^{-1/2}$ then $E$ is spectrally rigid. We establish analogous rigidity results for Culler-Vogtmann Outer Space and show that the $T^{-1/2}$ threshold is sharp in this setting.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 2 figures, to appear in Journal of Topology

papers.title: Fourier analysis on a class of Schwartz spaces and applications
papers.abstract: The study of regularity and solvability of partial differential operators on non-compact manifolds requires the construction of adapted functional spaces. In this work we introduce $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$, the Schwartz space on the product of a homogeneous space $\mathfrak{M}$ and the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$. We characterize $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ and its topological dual by employing discrete Fourier analysis in terms of eigenfunction expansions associated with a class of anisotropic elliptic operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We provide a characterization via partial Fourier coefficients and via full coefficients, that is, with respect to both components of $\mathfrak{M} \times \mathbb{R}^n$ simultaneously, which is achieved by studying the Fourier analysis on $\mathfrak{M}$. Our results provide new tools for the analysis of operators in this broader setting. As an application, we investigate the global existence and regularity of solutions for a class of partial differential equations on $\mathfrak{M}\times \mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Distortion of Random Max Filters over Reflection Groups
papers.abstract: A max filter with Gaussian templates $a_1,\dots,a_D$ is a $G$-invariant map $\R^d\to\R^D$, where $G$ is a finite reflection group. As $D\to\infty$ its distortion converges a.s to the condition number of $M_G^{1/2}$, where $M_G$ is the second-moment matrix of a standard Gaussian vector moved into a fundamental chamber of $G$. We compute this limit exactly for the sign and dihedral groups, and show it grows as $Θ(\sqrt d)$, $Θ(d^{3/2})$ and $Θ(k)$ for the sign, symmetric and dihedral groups of order $2k$. The symmetric case bound uses a lower bound on the covariance of order statistics. For any finite $G$ we also show that the infimum defining the optimal lower Lipschitz constant of a piecewise-linear $G$-invariant map is a minimum.

papers.title: Spectral unions of intervals with few rational relation tile the real line
papers.abstract: We prove that every spectral finite union of pairwise disjoint bounded intervals whose lengths satisfy at most four linearly independent rational relations tiles the real line, and that each of its spectra has at most five cosets modulo its least period. This includes every spectral union of at most five bounded intervals. The proof combines specialization preserving subset-sum equalities with rigidity of exchanges between finite spectral fibers. We also obtain common tiling complements for all spectra of primitive sets of at most seven elements in finite cyclic groups, and establish the sharp eleven-point range in which consecutive pairs force periodicity of the dual set.

papers.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperkähler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperkähler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperkähler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

papers.title: Quasi-polynomial valuations of lattice polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove that for any valuation $\varphi$ of lattice polytopes in ${\mathbb R}^m$, which is quasi-polynomial with respect to ${\mathbb Z}^m$-translations, and any lattice polytope $P$, the function $\varphi(nP)$ is quasi-polynomial in $n$.

papers.title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
papers.abstract: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families. We also study the varieties of Jordan algebra structures up to dimension three over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Besides explicit degenerations and standard arguments, we introduce the alicyclic and characteristic conditions as geometric obstructions to degeneration. We determine the rigid algebras and irreducible components in both dimensions. In dimension three, one component is the nine-dimensional affine space of square-zero products; unlike the other three components, it contains no open orbit.

papers.title: Variance-reduced First-order Methods for Finite-sum Function Constrained Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper studies finite-sum convex optimization with convex function constraints, where both the objective $f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and the constraint mapping $g(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n g_j(x)$ may have a large number of components. We propose a variance-reduced anchored constraint extrapolation method (VaRAn-ConEx), which combines stochastic component sampling with primal--dual extrapolation for nonlinear function constraints. Relative to stochastic approximation schemes such as ConEx, VaRAn-ConEx~method reduces gradient complexity by using epoch-wise full-gradient correction and variance-reduced estimators for both the objective and constraint components. In the semi-finite case where $n=1$, the method attains gradient complexities $O(\sqrt m/ε)$ under constant steps and $O(m/ε^{1/2}+1/ε^{3/2})$ under nonconstant steps. In the fully finite-sum case, we establish boundedness of the Lagrange multiplier sequence and derive convergence and gradient-complexity bounds for constant and nonconstant step-size policies. Under these policies, we then prove similar gradient complexity with $m$ replaced by $\max\{m,n\}$. We also show acceleration when the finite-sum objective $f$ is strongly convex, irrespective of components $f_i$.

papers.title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
papers.abstract: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.

papers.title: Painlevé VI superintegrability and Heun-Racah algebras
papers.abstract: We study the two fourth-order quantum superintegrable systems in the Euclidean plane that separate in polar coordinates and whose angular potentials are determined by the general four-parameter sixth Painlevé transcendent. One system has an oscillator radial term and the other an extended-Coulomb radial term. For both systems we give the fourth-order quantum integral explicitly, derive the cubic symmetry algebra and its Casimir, and construct a deformed-oscillator realization. At fixed energy the two algebras are specializations of the Heun--Racah algebra. Their structure functions contain the same quartic angular factor, determined by the Painlevé~VI parameters, while different radial factors distinguish oscillator and Coulomb dynamics. The Coulomb integral is obtained by transforming the Cartesian Hermitian symmetry at the operator level. The lower-order terms generated by the polar coordinate change are essential for commutation with the Hamiltonian. The two quantum systems are also related by the Levi-Civita transformation and coupling-constant metamorphosis, which gives a direct correspondence between their Painlevé parameters, algebras, Casimirs and representations. Earlier exceptional-Jacobi models arise at special rational parameter values, whereas the results here apply to the full four-parameter Painlevé~VI family. We also compare the quantum results with the corresponding classical Poisson algebras.

papers.title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
papers.abstract: We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds. For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.

papers.title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$ convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$ and $o(1/k^2)$ rates for the expected squared residual, as well as $o(1/k^2)$ almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-2}\big)$ and $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-1}\big)$ oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.

papers.title: Stability of Solitons in the Parametrically Driven and Damped Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability of soliton solutions of the parametrically driven and damped nonlinear Schrödinger (PDDNLS) equation with power-law nonlinearity $|Ψ|^{2κ}Ψ$ in $N$ dimensions. We identify two families of stationary solutions, $Ψ_\pm$, whose existence is determined by two conditions: one involving the nonlinearity exponent~$κ$ and the spatial dimension~$N$, and another involving the forcing amplitude~$r$ and the damping coefficient~$ρ$. By linearising around these solutions and introducing a convenient parametrisation through~$\varepsilon$, we reduce the stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schrödinger-type operators, $L_0$ and $L_1$. We prove that $Ψ_-$ is always unstable, while for $Ψ_+$, we carry out a complete spectral analysis by decomposing the problem into angular momentum sectors $\mathcal{S}_l$. We show that modes with $l \geq 2$ generate no instabilities and that no complex quadruplets arise on~$\mathcal{S}_1$. We also derive an analytical instability criterion on $\mathcal{S}_l$ by combining a Vakhitov--Kolokolov-type argument with a local analysis that determines the direction of the eigenvalue splitting near the origin. In addition, we uncover new phenomena at both small and large values of $κ$ that were not investigated in earlier one-dimensional studies. Numerical stability diagrams for $N = 1, 2, 3$ are presented.

papers.title: Exact Asymptotics for the Harmonic Descent Chain and Extended Convergence Bounds for Recursive Statistics
papers.abstract: We give an exact asymptotic expansion of the occupation probabilities $a(n,k)$ of the harmonic descent chain, introduced by D. Aldous, as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $k\in\mathrm{o}(\sqrt{n})$. In addition, we extend the recent results of Brandenberger et al. by giving a bound on the rate of convergence of sequences defined recursively by $x_n = \frac{1}{H_{n-1}}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{x_i}{n-i}$ for more general initial conditions. This result enables the application of an existing central limit theorem, also by Brandenberger et al., to statistics of the critical beta-splitting tree which satisfy our more general initial conditions.

papers.title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
papers.abstract: We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).

papers.title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

papers.title: Second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle for solenoidal fields: sharp constants, optimizers and sharp stability
papers.abstract:
The second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam is the uncertainty principle for the gradient of a function. Motivated by the question of Maz'ya on the uncertainty principle for divergence-free vector fields, solved by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam for $N=2$ and by Hamamoto for $N\ge3$, we study the second order principle for divergence-free fields $\mathbf{U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2dx\int|x|^2|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx\ge C_N^2(\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx)^2$, where $C_N=1+ rac12\sqrt{N^2+8}$ for $N\ge3$ and $C_2=1+\sqrt2$. For the velocity of an incompressible flow, $\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2$ and $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2$ are, up to constant factors, the enstrophy and the palinstrophy, so the inequality bounds the palinstrophy from below in terms of the enstrophy and the spatial spread of the velocity gradient. The constant $C_N$ is sharp and larger than the constant $ rac{N+2}{2}$ for general fields, and all the optimizers are explicit fields with Kummer function profiles. We also obtain the sharp constants on the poloidal and the toroidal fields of each degree. Then we prove the sharp stability of the inequality. In sum form, the deficit controls a chain of squared distances to explicit families of poloidal and toroidal fields, with all the constants sharp. In product form, we find the sharp stability constant in all dimensions. For $N\ge4$ it is $ rac12(\sqrt{N^2+4N-4}-\sqrt{N^2+8})$, and it is attained by swirling flows, the toroidal fields of degree one. On the Fourier side, the sixth order poloidal problem becomes a first order Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality for radial functions, and its stability follows from weighted Poincaré inequalities with Gaussian type measures.

papers.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
papers.abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.

papers.title: Beyond the reduced Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation: Singular potential, global well-posedness, and micromagnetic limits
papers.abstract: We study the full nonlinear mean-field Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation in micromagnetics arising from Garanin's spin-polarisation model [D. Garanin. Fokker-Planck and Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equations for classical ferromagnets. Phys. Rev. B, 55 (1997)] prior to the usual near-equilibrium reduction. The equation combines a singular inverse-Langevin potential with a mobility whose longitudinal component degenerates at saturation, together with exchange, anisotropy, and the nonlocal whole-space stray field. The natural state space is the closed unit ball $|m|\leq 1$. For any $H^1$ initial data satisfying $|m_0|\leq1$, including saturated data of infinite free energy, we construct global weak solutions and derive instantaneous separation from saturation $|m|=1$. This restores uniform parabolicity and yields the thermodynamic formulation and exact energy identity for positive times. We further establish a quantitative low-temperature limit to the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation and prove convergence of global trajectories to a single equilibrium. A spectral Curie-type threshold characterises the stability of the paramagnetic state and yields exponential relaxation above the threshold. Finally, for uniformly separated data we prove strong well-posedness, including global strong solutions in one- and two-dimensional domains, and exponential stability of non-degenerate equilibria, with a small-data global theory in three dimensions.

papers.title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of András Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$. Then every finite family of planks covering $Q\setminus H$ has total width at least $1$. More generally, if an axis-parallel box with side lengths $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ is removed from the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\sum_jh_j = d-1$, then every finite plank covering of the remaining set has total width at least one. The bounds are sharp.

papers.title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract: For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively. We also consider the first time $τ_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $τ_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[τ_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $τ_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.

papers.title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
papers.abstract: The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy. In previous work, some of the present authors gave a necessary and sufficient condition for convergence along a fixed ray, formulated in terms of analyticity of a longitudinal average of the balayage density. In the present paper, we extend these results to arbitrary physical solid planets, assuming only that the planet is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ and that its density belongs to $L^\infty$. We establish sharp regularity properties of the gravitational potential at the Brillouin sphere. The potential and its first derivative extend continuously to the sphere, the first derivative is locally Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$, and the second derivative satisfies the optimal bound $V''(z)=O\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\mathbb D)^{-1/2}\bigr)$ under nontangential approach from the exterior. We also obtain sharp estimates for the spherical harmonic coefficients: $a_\ell=O(\ell^{-3/2}).$ If, for almost every latitude, the Brillouin sphere is a one-sided Lebesgue point from the interior of the longitudinally averaged density, then $a_\ell=o(\ell^{-3/2}).$ Both estimates are optimal. We explicitly recover the balayage density on the Brillouin sphere from the exterior gravitational potential, and its circular averages from the potential along a single radial line. Finally, we give a physical characterization of convergence of the SHE below the Brillouin sphere. If the SHE converges at such a point, then, after truncating the planet at any suitable intermediate radius, the gravitational potential of the removed outer part is completely determined by that of the remaining truncated planet. This provides a direct interpretation of the strong constraint imposed by convergence below the Brillouin sphere.

papers.title: Krzyż's conjecture for the seventh coefficient
papers.abstract: A holomorphic function bounded in modulus by one in the unit disk has Taylor coefficients of modulus at most one. If the function has no zeros, Krzyż's conjecture predicts the stronger bound $2/e$ for every coefficient of positive order. We establish this bound for the seventh coefficient: $|a_7|\leq2/e$, with equality precisely for the functions $η\exp[-(1-ξz^7)/(1+ξz^7)]$, where $|η|=|ξ|=1$. Thus the largest possible value of $|f^{(7)}(0)|$ in this class is $7!\,2/e$, and the extremal functions are uniquely determined up to rotations of the variable and multiplication by a constant of modulus one.

papers.title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
papers.abstract: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term.
