Existing models of data center flexibility tend to bundle economic incentives with physical constraints, obscuring the tradeoff between economic willingness to shift load and technical limitations to do so. This paper proposes a temporal-redispatch focused framework that decouples data center demand flexibility into two independently parameterized dimensions: (1) systematic flexibility, capturing the economic environment through penalties for temporal shifting of data centers' scheduled demand, and (2) operational flexibility, capturing the physical envelope through the demand shifting time window and the limit on shifted data center demand. The framework relies on a direct current optimal power flow (DC-OPF) linear program which enables annual parametric analysis at hourly resolution. The framework is studied using a synthetic grid mimicking the Texas transmission system populated with the 2026 Adjusted Forecast from ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas). Results show that operational flexibility imposes a physical lower bound on unsatisfied demand that no economic incentive can overcome; longer shifting windows and higher limits on shifted data center demand reduce operational cost with different impacts on grid utilization; and, temporal redispatch shaves system-wide net load peaks while partially compensating for localized transmission bottlenecks that emerge under modeled coal retirement scenarios.

papers.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
papers.abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.
papers.comments: 49 pages (41 + 8 pages of supplementary materials), 11 figures, 5 tables. Code, Mathematica notebooks, data, print files of the 1:20 model, and a video: https://github.com/nurmaton/gqs-nets

papers.title: Nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
papers.abstract: We prove a nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation with a time-dependent trapping potential $V(x,t)$. If either (i) $V(\cdot,t)$ is smooth, subquadratic in space and with uniformly bounded spatial derivatives of order $\geq 2$, or (ii) $V(\cdot,t)$ is a uniformly bounded perturbation of a fixed non-negative potential which is asymptotically $|x|^m, m\geq 2$, then the GP equation has a global solution, which remains uniformly close to the instantaneous minimizer of the time-independent GP functional, provided the initial condition is a ground state. In fact, we show that the existence of a solution of the GP equation is the real bottleneck: If existence is assumed, then adiabaticity holds under very minimal assumptions.

papers.title: Weak and Sharp Stretched-Exponential Flocking in the Kinetic Cucker-Smale Model with Noncompactly Supported Initial Data
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model under initial data with unbounded support in both position and velocity. Such data invalidate classical diameter-based flocking arguments and make sustained spatial cohesion difficult to establish. We prove an estimate for spatial characteristics under a finite spatial second moment and a sufficiently high velocity moment, without any requirement on coupling strength. We also prove weak flocking, i.e. control of spatial variance and integrability of velocity fluctuations in time. Under stronger assumptions on the initial tails, we establish uniform propagation of spatial exponential moments of explicitly determined order, a substantially stronger conclusion than bounded spatial variance. These estimates lead to explicit stretched-exponential rates of velocity alignment and convergence of the centered spatial distribution toward a limiting profile. Another contribution is the construction of countably atomic solutions that show optimality of the decay exponent in the spatial-tail-limited class. Together, the results clarify how initial phase-space tails govern spatial confinement and quantitative flocking for kinetic distributions without compact support.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.

papers.title: Projective relativistic dynamics from a quantum Lorentz algebra: time-dependent deformed Hamiltonians on (anti-)de Sitter spaces
papers.abstract: A (non-standard) quantum deformation of the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ is used to construct novel time-dependent Hamiltonian systems on the (anti-)de Sitter spacetimes in $(1+1)$-dimensions. The specific deformation considered here contains, among others, the non-standard quantum deformation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and that of the `book' algebra $\mathfrak{b}_{2}$ as quantum subalgebras. The guiding idea is to apply the theory of Poisson--Hopf deformations of Lie--Hamilton systems to the Lorentz deformation, giving rise to a broad family of time-dependent deformed systems that share the same deformed Poisson--Hopf Lorentz algebra symmetry. In particular, this approach provides Hamiltonian vector fields expressed in terms of certain projective canonical variables, which, in turn, are related to the usual Beltrami variables via a canonical transformation. Under this construction, it is shown that the underlying Lorentizan spaces possess constant curvature $κ$ and the quantum deformation parameter $z$ can be identified with $κ$, such that the cosmological constant is $Λ=-z\equiv -κ$. Therefore, we deal with the anti-de Sitter, de Sitter and Minkowskian spaces for $z>0$, $z<0$ and $z=0$ (the undeformed case), respectively. Finally, as applications, we study time-dependent deformed oscillators on the (anti-)de Sitter spaces in detail, as well as time-dependent deformed Bateman and generalised coupled Caldirola--Kanai Hamiltonians.

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: Direct and Indirect Competition in a Two-Prey-One-Predator System : Global Dynamics, Chaos, and the Paine Conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper studies the global dynamics of a three-dimensional Lotka-Volterra system of two prey, with direct competition between them, and one predator. Under a symmetry assumption, the rescaled parameter space is sorted into four generic categories, which yield a complete classification of the global dynamics into 56 meaningful subcases. We determine the existence and stability of the boundary and positive equilibria, including global asymptotic stability and bistability of boundary equilibria, and necessary and sufficient conditions for local asymptotic stability of the positive equilibrium. We identify regimes of periodic solutions and chaos, including a period-doubling route to chaos. We further show that the parameters of Gilpin's chaotic dynamics fall within some cases. Biologically, we introduce the notion of extensive negative competition, which, together with trade-off competition and apparent competition, interprets the interactions among the three species. Our classification shows that the full system largely tracks the dynamics of the prey-only subsystem, and these competition mechanisms explain the differences between them, clarifying how predator-mediated interactions alter competitive outcomes and facilitate prey persistence, thereby providing mathematical support for Paine conjecture.

papers.title: Omitting Types for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
papers.abstract: For countable vocabularies, we extend the omitting types theorem for countable fragments of infinitary logic to Keisler's general real-valued structures by proving that the space of Henkin types of each such fragment is Čech-complete. The structures interpret function symbols arbitrarily and predicate symbols by bounded real-valued functions, while each formula carries a bound of its own. This extends the setting of Eagle's theorem from metric structures with a prescribed master metric to general structures whose vocabulary prescribes the sorts and bounds of the symbols. Following Keisler and Miller's treatment of logic without equality, we build models from closed terms. Morley's Baire category method then gives every satisfiable theory on a countable fragment a model with countable sorts omitting any countable family of types whose closed-term instances have empty interior in the space of Henkin types satisfying the theory.

papers.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $λ_0=0,\dots,λ_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $Λ_n=S_n$, and that $Λ_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $Λ_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[λ_m,λ_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $Λ_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $τ$) that realizes the point $λ_m+τ(λ_{m+1}-λ_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $τ<τ^*_m=\sin(πm/n)/(2\cos(π/n)\sin(π(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $τ=τ^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $λ_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partialΛ_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $Λ_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $τ^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partialΛ_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $τ^*_m$, at a corner at $τ^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $τ^*_m$.

papers.title: $P$-stationary structural equation modeling: Causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations
papers.abstract: Causal modeling of discrete-time processes often involves the assumption that the modeled processes are stationary. A general class of linear causal models for discrete-time stationary processes are structural equation processes (SEP), which generalize the well known structural equation model for i.i.d. observations. In this paper, we extend the SEP model from stationary to $P$-stationary processes, which are non-stationary processes whose $P$-periodically sampled subprocesses are jointly stationary. We will use this model to approach the problem of causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations from a graphical modeling perspective. To have a notion of generic identifiability, we restrict our analysis to $P$-stationary structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) processes, which are SVAR processes whose underlying coefficients can vary $P$-periodically over time. Our findings allow to detect, in any given temporally incomplete observational setting, if a certain set of instrumental processes qualifies to identify a causal effect between $P$-periodic subprocesses, and if this is the case, that effect admits an explicit expression as a rational function evaluated at the observational spectral density.

papers.title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians via path expansions
papers.abstract: We study the transport properties of Bose-Hubbard-type Hamiltonians. Kuwahara, Vu, and Saito proved sharp bounds on (i) particle transport and (ii) the Lieb-Robinson velocity for initial states with controlled boson density. We provide simpler and shorter proofs for both results using a new set of methods. For (i), boson transport, we use a class of weighted extended particle number operators that directly enables closing the associated differential inequalities. For (ii), the Lieb-Robinson bounds, we develop a bosonic version of the Chen-Lucas path expansion technique and recover the sharp velocity bound $t^{d-1}$ up to logarithmic corrections, where $d$ denotes the lattice dimension. We also extend the transport bounds (i) to long-range hopping with a power-law exponent $α>d$. The range $α\in (d,d+1)$ corresponds to an algebraic light cone for boson transport and has not been previously covered.

papers.title: The Non-Abelian X-Ray Transform on Simple Asymptotically Hyperbolic Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a gauge equivalence result for the non-Abelian X-ray transform with connection and Higgs field on simple 2-dimensional asymptotically hyperbolic spaces. Our approach is based on the construction of holomorphic integrating factors. To construct these, we analyze the geodesic X-ray transform on functions on simple asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds of general dimension and prove polyhomogeneous mapping properties and a surjectivity result for the adjoint.

papers.title: Nonpathological submeasures and $F_σ$ ideals
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between nonpathological lower semicontinuous submeasures, $F_σ$ ideals on $ω$, and matrix summability ideals. First, we construct in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ a non-analytic ideal on $ω$ which is representable as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. Then, we show that an $F_σ$ ideal is nonpathological if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of summable ideals if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. We also prove that the random graph ideal is pathological. Finally, we compute the exact degree of pathology of a certain submeasure related to a construction of Topsøe.

papers.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
papers.abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $λ_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ λ_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(ν\midγ_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $ν$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincaré constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $λ_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.

papers.title: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(Φ_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\leθ<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>θ$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-θ)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $θ=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.
papers.comments: 12 pages. An earlier version appeared as Revision 2 of ECCC TR23-200: https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/200/#revision2

papers.title: Unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null filtered Runge--Kutta methods for general nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We develop unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null (EIN) filtered Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with space-, time-, state-, and gradient-dependent diffusion coefficients. The methods are linearly implicit in the sense that they evaluate nonlinear terms explicitly and require only linear solves. Unlike classical EIN methods that are direct applications of implicit--explicit (IMEX) RKs, our construction is built upon explicit RKs. The key ingredient is two-sided symmetric filtering applied at each RK stage: a high-order filter is applied both before and after evaluating the original nonlinear residual. It leads to a dissipation estimate independent of the time step and retains the underlying RK order formally. Assuming time-dependent splitting operators with stagewise pointwise coefficient bounds, we rigorously prove non-increasing $L^2$ norm for arbitrary time steps. A quadratic matrix criterion covers explicit RK-based methods with positive weights, while strong stability preserving (SSP) compositions yield exact energy identities and weighted dissipation estimates. We present SSP methods through fourth order and a method based on the classical RK4. The framework accommodates spatial discretizations with discrete gradient structures including continuous Galerkin, Bassi--Rebay 1, the method of Brezzi et al., and local discontinuous Galerkin. Compatible summation-by-parts discretizations with simultaneous approximation terms are also covered in their discrete mass norm.

papers.title: Monotonicity and bounded variation for harmonic mappings with applications to special functions
papers.abstract: We investigate sufficient conditions for the close-to-convexity and univalence of planar harmonic mappings. First, we establish a unified monotonicity criterion for harmonic mappings that incorporates the ordinary and odd harmonic cases. We then develop a criterion based on the total variation of successive coefficient differences. Unlike conventional monotonicity conditions, this approach allows the coefficient sequences to exhibit non-monotone behavior. Several previously established criteria for harmonic close-to-convexity are recovered as particular consequences. Applications are developed for harmonic mappings associated with Gaussian hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials, with explicit restrictions on their parameters.

papers.title: Small-time controllability of affine systems and quadratic Lie brackets
papers.abstract: We prove a new sufficient condition for small-time global exact controllability of finite-dimensional control-affine systems. It points out that, under a natural Lie algebra rank condition, quadratic Lie brackets are the only possible obstacles to controllability. This result extends to infinite-dimensional settings such as the global approximate controllability of diffeomorphisms. It also allows us to interpret recent results in PDE control theory.

papers.title: Two teams that cancel: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for signed numbers from Grade 5 to Grade 7
papers.abstract: Signed numbers make learners revise what addition, subtraction and the minus sign meant for whole numbers. This paper presents the design rationale and a critical analysis of a three-level source progression for signed numbers (Grades 5-7, nominal ages 10-13), from which French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. One representation is presented first and taken up throughout: an integer is drawn as a collection of positive and negative units, a positive and a negative unit forming a zero pair that leaves nothing. An integer therefore has many drawings, which makes visible the construction of the integers as classes of pairs of natural numbers. The design hypothesis is that the gesture pupils perform with the units, inserting a zero in the form a + (-a), is shared by the subtraction of a negative number, by the worked examples that accompany the 2026 French programme, and by the derivation of the sign of a product of two negatives through distributivity; the progression does not model that product, it derives it from the zero pair, a derivation that holds only if distributivity is kept. The number line supports position, order and distance; contexts provide applications. The choices are related to the epistemological obstacles described by Glaeser, to studies of counter and number-line models, including a classroom comparison in which a path model gave better results than chips, immediately and five weeks later, and to the French and IB curricula. A block-level audit of the dated source documents found the representation absent from the first level, no exercise asking pupils to draw, and the decisive subtraction never drawn; the revisions made after the audit are recorded. No empirical evaluation is reported; hypotheses for one are stated.

papers.title: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n}^{(k)}\right)^{x}+\left(P_{r}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=P_{m}^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: The Pell numbers satisfy $P_n^2+P_{n+1}^2=P_{2n+1}$, and Bravo, Luca and Pomeo recently found all the cases in which the sum of the $x$-th powers of two consecutive $k$-generalized Pell numbers is again a $k$-generalized Pell number. We ask what happens when the two indices are arbitrary, that is, we solve $\big(P_n^{(k)}\big)^x+\big(P_r^{(k)}\big)^x=P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n\ge r$, $m$ and $x$. The answer is that nothing new appears: apart from $1^x+1^x=2$, every solution has consecutive indices. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms with an auxiliary Fibonacci equation which does not depend on $k$, and, for large $k$, with the fact that the dominant root of the sequence is very close to $\varphi^2$. For the reduction step, the method of Dujella and Pethő fails for large indices and has to be replaced by a criterion of Legendre type.

papers.title: Improved criteria for geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sufficient conditions for several geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions. Using differential subordination techniques, we derive parameter conditions ensuring lower bounds for the real part of the confluent hypergeometric function and sectorial subordination of its derivative. We also obtain criteria for strong convexity and strong starlikeness of prescribed order. In addition, we investigate the close-to-convexity and starlikeness of the confluent hypergeometric functions. Particular cases yield corresponding results for generalized Laguerre polynomials. The obtained criteria are compared with existing sufficient conditions, and their implications for the geometric theory of special functions are discussed.

papers.title: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}-\left(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=2P_{m}^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: For the Pell numbers one has $P_{n+1}-P_{n-1}=2P_n$ and $P_{n+1}^2-P_{n-1}^2=2P_{2n}$. We look for all the solutions of $\big(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\big)^x-\big(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\big)^x=2P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n$, $m$, $x$, where $P^{(k)}$ is the $k$-generalized Pell sequence. We prove that for $k=2$ the two identities above give all the solutions, and that for $k\ge3$ the only solutions are $(n,m,x)=(1,1,1),(1,2,2),(2,2,1)$. In contrast with the analogous equation for $k$-generalized Fibonacci numbers, there are no parametric families of solutions. The proof uses an auxiliary equation with Fibonacci numbers which does not depend on $k$, Matveev's lower bound for linear forms in logarithms, the reduction of Dujella and Pethő, and, for large $k$, the fact that the dominant root of $P^{(k)}$ is very close to $\varphi^2$.

papers.title: The module structure of ideals in degree $p$ extensions of $p$-adic fields
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be a degree $p$ extension of $p$-adic fields. We shall provide a complete characterization for the freeness of any fractional ideal $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$, $h\in\mathbb{Z}$, of $L$ as a module over its associated order $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ in the only Hopf-Galois structure on $L/K$, and an explicit description of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$. We show that there is no loss of generality in assuming that $0\leq h\leq p-1$ and that the normal closure of $L/K$ is totally ramified over $K$. If $L/K$ is maximally ramified, then $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ is the maximal $\mathcal{O}_K$-order in $H$ and $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. The remaining cases correspond to typical extensions. For these, we provide an $\mathcal{O}_K$-basis of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ and a characterization for the condition that $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. In the non-exceptional cases, which had been partially studied in the Galois setting, the characterization depends on $h$ and the continued fraction expansion of $\frac{a}{p}$, where $a$ is the residue class mod $p$ of the (fractional) ramification jump $\ell$ of $L/K$. In the remaining exceptional case, where $L/K$ is almost maximally ramified and $a+1\leq h\leq p-1$, it consists in a numerical common minimizer condition.

papers.title: Uniqueness of self-shrinking ends asymptotic to a cylindrical cone
papers.abstract: Let $C^m \subset \mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ be a regular embedded cone, where $n\geq 1$, and let $k\geq 1$. We prove that two smooth, connected, properly embedded self-shrinking ends whose blow-downs converge locally smoothly to the same cylindrical cone $C\times\mathbb{R}^k$ away from the axis $\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}^k$ must coincide. As a consequence, we obtain a rigidity result for complete self-shrinkers asymptotic to cylindrical cones. The proof uses Gaussian decay estimates and a sectorial Carleman estimate to establish backward uniqueness.

papers.title: A High-Dimensional LM Test for Cross-Sectional Independence with Serially Correlated Data
papers.abstract: We develop a high-dimensional Lagrange multiplier (LM) test for cross-sectional independence in Gaussian panels with a common stationary, short-memory temporal covariance matrix. The statistic is based on the trace of the square of R, where R is the sample correlation matrix. When the cross-sectional and time dimensions grow proportionally, we derive explicit expansions for the null mean and variance in terms of temporal spectral moments. Random diagonal normalization produces a non-negligible centering correction, while squared sample correlations sharing a cross-sectional unit contribute an additional variance term. Both corrections vanish under temporal independence. We establish a central limit theorem under the null, consistency against fixed alternatives, and a Gaussian-shift limit with a detection boundary under local alternatives. Monte Carlo experiments examine the size and power of the oracle test and feasible versions that estimate the temporal spectral moments. The asymptotic theory applies to the oracle statistic; feasible procedures are evaluated numerically.

papers.title: Motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces at the characteristic
papers.abstract: We provide a novel, homotopy theoretic model for the motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces $K(Z_{(p)}(n), 2n) \in Spc(k)$ over fields of characteristic p. Using this, we determine their motives and, consequently, determine the motivic Steenrod algebra at the characteristic. Applications include the Hopkins--Morel isomorphism over arbitrary base schemes as well as the computation of the p-completed motivic stable stems and algebraic cobordism groups of fields of characteristic p. Along the way we expand the theory of normed algebraic structures in motivic homotopy theory, compare them to derived algebra at the characteristic, and produce a functor computing the motivic homology of the $P^1$-loop spaces of (certain) motivic spaces in terms of the motives.

papers.title: Robust Closed-form Framework for Drag-Propulsive Control of Formation Flight
papers.abstract: To conserve propellant, Distributed Space Systems (DSS) can leverage environmental forces to produce low cost relative forces, such as atmospheric drag in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). This work maximizes this strategy by developing robust, closed-form algorithms for optimal "hybrid" control, defined here as complementing the magnitude and directionality deficiencies of differential drag with the superior control authority of propulsive maneuvers within the same control window. The use of drag introduces a significant source of dynamic uncertainty to the control problem, primarily from inaccurate atmospheric density modelling. This paper develops a robust control architecture that periodically re-solves the remaining drag maneuver plan in a diminishing horizon policy, rejecting operational and navigation errors while retaining the cost savings offered by differential drag. The approach is built upon reachable set theory, a control analysis technique that provides conditions for optimality for Linear Time Variant (LTV) systems with norm-like cost functions and optimally decouples hybrid control into separate propulsive and differential drag sub-problems. The optimality conditions are leveraged to prove the asymptotic Lyapunov stability of ideal reachable set-based control solutions and derive error bounds on this stability. A covariance analysis on the primary sources of error in hybrid control determines that the dominating source of uncertainty is the atmospheric density model. This conclusion allows the bounds on Lyapunov stability to be completely met by simply conditioning the atmospheric density value used in the control solutions. The derived Lyapunov stability bounds and performance of the algorithm are demonstrated experimentally in high fidelity full-force orbital simulations of the upcoming Space Weather Reconfigurable Multiscale Experiment (SWARM-EX) mission.
papers.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 2024 IEEE Aerospace Conference, Big Sky, Montana, March 2-9, 2024

papers.title: Fast Fuel-Optimal Constrained Impulsive Control with Application to Distributed Spacecraft
papers.abstract: This work extends a reachable set theory approach for fuel-optimal control to incorporate convex and non-convex state, time, and magnitude constraints. The solver is designed from a new set of optimality conditions, derived by reformulating a single reachable set into multiple time-ordered, step-wise reachable set waypoint sub-problems, where a waypoint is the state reached after a given maneuver. Non-convex constraints are satisfied at each waypoint, preserving convexity at each sub-problem without needing to convexify the full control problem, enabling the computationally efficient identification of constrained optimal maneuvers, and guaranteeing a user-defined bound on constrained cost. To produce an optimal maneuver plan, the solver rolls out constrained trajectories until the remaining unconstrained solution adheres to the problem constraints. The fuel-optimal control problem considered by this work is broadly applicable to many fields and particularly significant to Distributed Space Systems (DSS). Multi-agent guidance and propulsive control techniques, often for small spacecraft at close separations, require guarantees of collision avoidance, efficient maneuvering to preserve a restricted fuel payload, and numerically-simple algorithms functional under on-board computational processing limitations. The proposed solver offers both user-defined bounds on constrained maneuver optimality and enhanced computational efficiency to directly address these challenges, and these capabilities are demonstrated comparatively against baseline solvers from the literature through Monte Carlo analysis on a variety of relevant DSS scenarios. Overall, this work enables the benefits of reachable set theory, namely computational efficiency and provable optimality, to be extended to control problems of higher fidelity.
papers.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE Aerospace Conference, Big Sky, Montana, March 2025

papers.title: The Large-$N$ Limit of Ricci curvature in the Zeitlin Model on the Torus
papers.abstract: The Euler equations of hydrodynamics describe the motion of an ideal incompressible fluid. Arnold observed that their solutions are geodesics on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of the fluid domain, equipped with the $L^2$ metric, so that the curvature of this group governs how nearby fluid motions separate. Sectional curvature takes both signs, and Ricci curvature, its average over all directions, is the natural measure of which sign prevails, but in infinite dimensions the sum defining it diverges. When the fluid domain is the flat torus, we define Ricci curvature through Zeitlin's finite-dimensional models, which approximate the Euler equations by geodesic equations on the matrix groups $SU(N)$. We compute the Ricci curvature of these models exactly and prove that, normalized by dimension, it converges as $N \rightarrow \infty$ to an explicit integral. The limit is strictly negative in every Fourier mode and decreases logarithmically with the wavenumber, the behavior conjectured in \cite{lichtenfelz2026ricci} for the sphere. We also show that the diameter of $SU(N)$ in the Zeitlin metric grows at most linearly in $N$.

papers.title: Near-Critical Asymptotics and Radial Sharpness for a Two-Weight Hardy Inequality
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal constant $C(p,γ)$ in a planar two-weight Hardy inequality relating the gradient and Hessian of a scalar potential, posed by Maz'ya in [14, Problem 3.11]. For every $1\le p<\infty$, we prove \[ \lim_{γ\toγ_c} 2^{p/2}|γ-γ_c|^p C(p,γ)=1, \qquad γ_c=1-\frac2p. \] The proof reduces the curl-free constraint to an angular minimization problem and yields qualitative rigidity of almost extremizers for $p>1$. Moreover, we determine the sharp constant in the radial class for every $1\le p<\infty$ and $γ\neγ_c$, thereby resolving the radial case of Maz'ya's problem. We also show that the radial inequality remains valid at $γ=γ_c$, with the same sharp constant \[ C_{\rm rad}(p,γ) =\left[1+\left(γ-1+\frac2p\right)^2\right]^{-p/2}. \] For general, not necessarily radial, potentials, we identify explicit parameter regions where this constant remains sharp and establish two sufficient criteria for symmetry breaking. The exact transition remains open for $p\ne2$. In the quadratic case, we recover the known sharp constant and derive a decomposition of its deficit. At the critical exponent, we obtain an exact remainder identity for the logarithmic Hardy inequality, whose classical constant remains sharp among radial potentials. The logarithmic inequality fails at $p=1$.

papers.title: Random Walk on age-preferential random growth processes
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of \textbf{exponentially age-preferential random growth graphs} $G(m,β)$: at each time $n$ a new vertex $v_n$ is added, and $m$ edges are drawn to existing vertices independently, with the probability that a target $v_k$ is chosen proportional to $e^{βk}$ ($β>0$), so that the graph's growth strongly favors ``young'' vertices. We systematically investigate two fundamental probabilistic problems of this model and supply the proof details: (1)~\textbf{Recurrence}: when $β>0$, the simple random walk on $G$ is recurrent with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:rec}); (2)~\textbf{Infinite collisions}: for every $β>0$, two independent simple random walks on $G$ meet infinitely often with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:icp}). The core of the proof is the following: by the Borel--Cantelli lemma combined with the \textbf{memoryless property} of exponential weights, $G$ is almost surely ``sausage-like'' --- there exist infinitely many bottlenecks consisting of exactly $m$ parallel edges; the cascade of bottlenecks makes the effective resistance diverge, yielding recurrence; the renewal process $\{T_k\}$ constructed at the bottleneck times has i.i.d.\ stationary increments with finite moments of every order for the first-passage times, and combined with a moderate-deviation estimate we verify Peres' Green-function criterion for infinite collisions.

papers.title: On the Space Defined by the Modular Transformation Law for Multiple Eisenstein Series
papers.abstract: Motivated by a modular transformation law for multiple Eisenstein series established by Yu, we introduce spaces of holomorphic functions satisfying this law together with an additional filtration condition. We show that these spaces contain the spaces spanned by admissible multiple Eisenstein series, are finitedimensional in each weight, and share several structural properties with them. We also obtain an explicit formula for the generating function of their dimensions. However, the inclusions are known to be strict for certain weights. Thus, the defining conditions do not suffice to characterize the spaces spanned by admissible multiple Eisenstein series.

papers.title: The relative dimension set of an extremal subfactor of finite index
papers.abstract: Popa's relative dimension set $Λ(M,N)$ of an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors $N\subset M$ consists of the scalars $α$ for which some projection $p\in M$ satisfies $E_N(p)=\alpha1$. Popa computed it for index at most $4$, and for index $d>4$ outside the middle interval $(t_d,1-t_d)$, where $t_d(1-t_d)=d^{-1}$; whether the middle interval meets $Λ(M,N)$ for every irreducible inclusion of index $d>4$ has remained open. We show that for every extremal inclusion of finite index $d>4$, the whole interval $[t_d,1-t_d]$ is contained in $Λ(M,N)$. Consequently, $Λ(M,N)$ depends only on the index for all extremal inclusions of finite index, in particular for all irreducible ones. Extremality cannot be dropped: for $d>4$, Popa's locally trivial inclusions are exactly those whose relative dimension set misses the middle interval. Other non-extremal inclusions can contain the whole middle interval in their relative dimension set, or miss part of it.

papers.title: Embedding a de Rham Complex Structure into Eig-PIELM for Maxwell Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: The perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary condition alone does not eliminate the gradient nullspace of the Maxwell curl-curl operator. Consequently, a boundary-only Maxwell implementation of Eig-PIELM, an eigenvalue extension of the physics-informed extreme learning machine (PIELM), may retain represented gradient modes in its reduced trial space, producing nonphysical, gradient-contaminated modes. We develop dR-Eig-PIELM, a finite-dimensional structure-preserving extension that retains the linear-coefficient, boundary-null-space, and one-shot multimode architecture of Eig-PIELM. It combines compatible tensor-product grad--curl trial spaces with a constrained null-space construction to restrict the sampled PEC space to the mass-orthogonal complement of the represented gradient image before the eigensolve. Symmetric weak-form Gram assembly yields a symmetric-definite reduced eigenproblem without an eigenvalue cutoff under the stated sampling and material-positivity assumptions. For rectangles and cuboids, we establish fixed-degree exactness at the PEC vector-field space and derive rank and dimension identities. Numerical experiments show that dR-Eig-PIELM excludes the spurious eigenmodes with significant gradient components observed in the boundary-only baseline. The method exhibits rapid convergence with increasing polynomial degree and competitive work--precision performance in the tested configurations. A covariantly mapped waveguide example illustrates the potential of dR-Eig-PIELM for integration into design optimization workflows through a constrained local geometry update driven by computed cutoff frequencies and their sensitivities. This work provides a mathematical and computational framework for separating represented gradient modes from physical Maxwell eigenmodes within Eig-PIELM and supports its use in waveguide spectral analysis and geometry design.

papers.title: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
papers.abstract: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.

papers.title: Sharp Thresholds of Instability for the Biharmonic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the time-dependent biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with and without a mixed dispersion. We find the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence for the biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations without a mixed dispersion by establishing the modified cross-constraint variational method. Building on this work, we prove that the standing waves are strongly unstable without further assumptions on the frequency. The main new ingredients of which require us to provide a comparison of two variational problems, improved the method in Zhang [Comm PDEs, 2005, 30: 1429-1443]. In the latter part of the paper, we study the biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with a mixed dispersion, which destroys the scaling invariance. The single variational approach is utilized to obtain the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence, and strong instability of standing waves.

papers.title: Riemannian convex bodies with a geodesic segment on the boundary
papers.abstract: We construct compact convex bodies whose boundaries contain a nontrivial geodesic segment and are strictly convex elsewhere. The construction applies if sectional curvature is constant near a point, or if a normal Jacobi operator has a simple maximal eigenvalue. In particular, such a body exists in every smooth three-dimensional or four-dimensional Riemannian manifold.

papers.title: Alias Geometry and Density Compensation in Perturbed Fourier Sampling
papers.abstract: On a uniform grid with equal weights, Fourier modes that remain distinct on the grid are exactly orthogonal. When the nodes are perturbed, density compensation readjusts the weights. We ask how much of the resulting error reweighting can remove, measuring it by the Frobenius norm of the Gram defect, whose square is proportional to the mean-square error of density-compensated adjoint reconstruction. The answer is governed by aliasing. The grid cannot distinguish certain frequency differences, so a weight correction must treat each such alias class as a single number, while a node displacement affects every frequency difference in the class separately. To first order, reweighting removes the class average but not the spread. The irreducible error is a sum of covariance matrices, one for each class of colliding frequency differences. If no differences collide, every small node perturbation can be repaired exactly with positive weights. With collisions, a repair that works to first order can fail at second order. At the two-dimensional DFT, row and column shears are each exactly repairable, but their combination is not, and we compute the obstruction. In one dimension, oversampling protects a band of low-frequency node motions, and under random jitter optimal reweighting asymptotically removes a fraction $1-κ^2(2-κ)^2$ of the expected squared first-order error at oversampling ratio $κ\in[1,2]$. At critical sampling, node and weight perturbations are orthogonal: no reweighting helps, Voronoi weights can never reduce the error, and for the one-dimensional DFT the remaining error is a log-Vandermonde energy with the circular $H^{1/2}$ energy as its continuum limit.
papers.comments: 30 pages, 4 figures. Code reproducing all results: https://github.com/circlespie/alias-geometry-fourier-sampling

papers.title: Construction of stability conditions on some Kuznetsov components
papers.abstract: We construct Bridgeland stability conditions on the Kuznetsov components of smooth Fano hypersurfaces of degrees three, four, and six and dimension at least three, smooth quartic double fivefolds, and smooth Fano complete intersections of three quadrics. For odd-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces and quartic double fivefolds, every connected component of the numerical stability manifold is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C\times\mathbb H$. For general cubic sevenfolds and quartic double fivefolds, spherical twists produce infinitely many distinct connected components.

papers.title: Infinitely many negative terms in two weighted partition sequences
papers.abstract: Recently, Andrews and El Bachraoui introduced partition-counting functions $a_2(n)$ and $b_2(n)$, together with their signed analogues $a'_2(n)$ and $b'_2(n)$, and proved that $a'_2(n), b'_2(n)>0$ for all $n\geq 3$. For $m\geq 2$, the latter functions extend naturally to $a'_m(n)$ and $b'_m(n)$, defined by \begin{align*} \sum_{n\geq 0} a'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q}{1-q} \frac{(q^m;q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{(1-q)^2},\\ \sum_{n\geq 0} b'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q(1-q^{m-1})}{1-q} \frac{(q^{2m};q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{1-q} \left( \frac{1}{1-q} -\frac{q^{m-1}}{1-q^{m+1}} \right). \end{align*} They asked whether there exists an integer $m>2$ for which $a'_m(n)$ is eventually positive, and posed the same question for $b'_m(n)$. In this paper, we resolve these two questions.

papers.title: A Sharp Mutual Information Bound for Binary Pairs
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp upper bound on the mutual information between two binary random variables in terms of their distribution-dependent KL contraction coefficient. This resolves the binary-pair conjecture of Anantharam, Gohari, Kamath, and Nair. Equality holds if and only if the variables are independent or form a doubly symmetric binary source. The proof uses supporting tangents of an entropy curve to vary the input distribution and the channel while preserving the contraction coefficient. Together with tensorization and data processing, the result also bounds the mutual information between binary outputs obtained separately from two correlated observation sequences. When the observation pairs are independent copies of a finite-alphabet pair, this bound depends only on the law of one pair and not on the number of observations.

papers.title: On Lattice Tilings by Symmetric Limited Magnitude Error Balls: Q-polynomials and Ideal Characterization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the lattice tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by the symmetric limited magnitude error balls $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$, which play a crucial role in flash memory applications. Using generating functions and complete Bell polynomials, we derive an explicit formula for the $r$-th Q-polynomial associated with $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$. Then, an ideal-theoretic characterization of the lattice tiling condition is developed: for an odd prime $p$ dividing $|\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)|$ exactly once, a lattice tiling would force a certain polynomial to lie outside a certain ideal of $\mathbb{F}_p[Y_1,\dots,Y_{\frac{p-1}{2}}]$. Applying this criterion yields congruence conditions on the dimension $n$ that rule out lattice tilings; for $2\le t\le10$ and $1\le k\le10$, a systematic Maple computation over all primes $3\le p\le29$ excludes, on average, $35.65\%$ of all dimensions, with a maximum of $76.69\%$. Finally, we obtain two infinite families of parameters $(n,t,k)$ for which no lattice tiling exists: no lattice tiling exists if $k\equiv4\pmod9$ and the base-$3$ addition of $t$ and $n-1-t$ produces exactly one carry; and no lattice tiling of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by $\mathcal{B}(n,n-1,k,k)$ exists if $k\equiv8\pmod9$ and $n\equiv2,4\pmod6$. Their sizes are also estimated.

papers.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere. Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves $ X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x), $ where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$ has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$. After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$, the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic if its Newton polygon is minimal as $f$ varies over all Laurent polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$. For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$, we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$ and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$. Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize: there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$ in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$ and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$, whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in $U(\overline{\Q})$, the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field. This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.

papers.title: Minimum net-saturated graphs of even order
papers.abstract: Let \(F\) be the net, consisting of a triangle with one distinct degree-one vertex attached to each of its vertices. A graph is \(F\)-saturated if it contains no copy of \(F\), but adding any missing edge creates one. Zhao, You and Zhang determined the minimum number of edges and conjectured that the minimum graph is unique at every sufficiently large even order. We prove that for every even \(n\ge12\), there are exactly four minimum \(n\)-vertex \(F\)-saturated graphs up to isomorphism, each with \(3n/2\) edges. Three additional families therefore disprove their even-order uniqueness conjecture. Two have no universal vertex, that is, no vertex adjacent to every other vertex. We also construct a ten-vertex minimum graph with fifteen edges outside the four families, proving that the threshold twelve is optimal. The key structural step forces a pendant triangle, meaning a triangle with two vertices of degree two, in every even-order minimum graph above order ten. We classify the graphs containing such a triangle and bound the order of all remaining extremal configurations by ten.

papers.title: Inverse Design of Finite-State Channels by Dynamic Measure Matching
papers.abstract: Inspired by the optimization approach to biology, we formulate an inverse problem for communication with memory: construct a finite-state channel for which a given signaling behavior supports capacity-achieving codes. Dynamic measure matching is introduced to turn a directed-information converse into conditions on the channel dynamics. These conditions lead to a new notion of dynamic surprise: the log ratio of physical to test output probabilities with a continuation correction for future signaling opportunities. The matching inequalities bound its conditional mean. For fixed architecture, test law, and potential, channel row synthesis under convex physical restrictions is convex. For every signaling constraint represented by a finite irreducible constrained graph of positive entropy, we construct a channel law under which undesired inputs remain available and behaviorally distinct while incurring a strict information penalty. A noisy refractory family has an exact capacity plateau, followed by an interval in which Shannon and zero-error feedback capacities differ. Explicit zero-error codes attain capacity in the graph construction and on the plateau. In this family, a Gibbs choice maximizes the penalty and makes dynamic surprise equal its conditional mean on every transition, yielding an exact trajectory-wise likelihood identity, a finite-block bound on successful decoding with premature requests, and an exponential strong converse. An exact gap decomposition into action residuals and output-law divergence constrains every reliable capacity-approaching code. Within the strict plateau, positive discrimination exponents for unused dynamics require a positive rate loss, while sparse probing permits consistent estimation at asymptotic capacity. A chemical channel illustrates how premature stimulation can alter future responsiveness while leaving the immediate output law unchanged.

papers.title: Mean Field Games in Dynamic Ticket Pricing with Overselling and Cancellations
papers.abstract: We extend a finite-state Mean Field Game model of dynamic ticket pricing to allow overselling, stochastic cancellations, and terminal penalties for unresolved negative inventory. Cancellations generate upward inventory transitions, producing a bidirectional inventory process coupled with firms' pricing decisions. We formulate the representative-firm control problem and the population consistency conditions, and prove existence of a selected Markovian mean field equilibrium under the stated assumptions, including a compact price set and an explicit tie-breaking rule. Numerical experiments show that the quadratic terminal penalty can generate an endogenous soft-boundary mechanism that discourages progressively deeper overselling. Under a low-cancellation stress case, linear penalties more strongly reduce the prevalence of terminal overselling, whereas quadratic penalties reduce its conditional depth and lower-tail severity. A time-varying cancellation experiment suggests that anticipated future inventory recovery can support lower early prices and greater temporary overbooking exposure. Under the adopted demand normalization, stronger mean-field coupling is associated with lower equilibrium prices and slower inventory depletion. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing pricing and overbooking incentives in competitive ticket markets with cancellations.

papers.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
papers.abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

papers.title: Nonradial entire solutions of the critical Hénon equation for every $α>2$
papers.abstract: We consider the critical Hénon equation $-Δu=|x|^αu^{(N+2+2α)/(N-2)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$. Gladiali, Grossi, and Neves (\emph{Advances in Mathematics}, 2013) constructed nonradial continua bifurcating at $α_k=2(k-1)$, $k\ge2$, and conjectured that these continua are confined to the even parameters. Jiang and Xiong (2026) disproved this conjecture by obtaining nonradial solutions in punctured neighborhoods of $α_k$ for even $k>(N-2)/2$. We prove that positive nonradial finite-energy entire solutions exist for every $α>2$ in every dimension $N\ge3$. The proof introduces a global variational construction by direct minimization on a monotonicity cone on the Emden--Fowler cylinder. Angular and axial order restore compactness in every finite $L^r$, $r>2$, despite Sobolev supercriticality, and invariance of the linear resolvent yields the full equation. This constructs a solution at each prescribed parameter without continuing local bifurcation branches. The solutions have Newtonian decay, are invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and the Kelvin transform, and have energy strictly below the radial level. We also obtain a second solution for every $α>6$ in even dimensions, nonvertical branches at every $α_k$ with $k\ge2$ even without dimension restrictions, a cubic energy law, and rigidity near $α=0$ under bounded cylindrical amplitude.
papers.comments: This work was first announced on October 15, 2026, on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23384720)

papers.title: On the dichotomy of $p$-walk dimensions on metric measure spaces II
papers.abstract: On a volume doubling metric measure space endowed with a family of $p$-energies such that the Poincaré inequality and the capacity upper bound with $p$-walk dimension $β_p$ hold, for $p$ in an open interval $I\subseteq(1,+\infty)$, we prove the following dichotomy: either $β_p=p$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{β_p}{p}$ takes values in $(1,+\infty)$ and is strictly decreasing on $I$. Moreover, if the metric measure space is $d_h$-Ahlfors regular, we prove the following dichotomy: either $β_p=d_h+p-1$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{β_p-d_h}{p-1}$ takes values in $(-\infty,1)$ and is strictly increasing on $I$.

papers.title: High-Order Unconditionally Stable IMEX BDF--FEM Schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley Model on a Branched Axon
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze high-order implicit--explicit backward differentiation formula finite element (IMEX BDF--FEM) schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley cable system on a branched metric graph. The linearly implicit schemes combine constant-step BDF methods of orders $q=1,\ldots,5$ with conforming finite elements of any fixed degree $p\ge1$. Extrapolated gate variables are smoothly masked before evaluating the conductances, preserving coercivity without projecting the numerical gates. A voltage cutoff makes the gate rates globally bounded and Lipschitz. Each timestep requires one linear voltage solve followed by independent nodal gate updates. Under exact spatial integration, we prove unconditional stability of the complete fully discrete regularized scheme in discrete history energies. Under regularity and starting-history assumptions, the voltage and reconstructed gates converge in $L^2(Γ)$ at the optimal rate $O(h^{p+1}+Δt^q)$, without a timestep restriction or an $h$--$Δt$ coupling. The same rate holds with numerical quadrature when its full residual defect is $O(h^{p+1})$. Manufactured solutions recover the predicted orders through BDF5--$P_4$. Action-potential simulations illustrate pulse propagation and splitting, while a controlled work--precision comparison within the proposed family shows that higher-order variants can reach a prescribed accuracy at much lower runtime along the tested joint-refinement paths.

papers.title: Around the Clock. New Twists on Fitch Cheney's Five-Card Trick
papers.abstract: Fitch Cheney's five-card trick is one of the purest two-person effects in card magic, and it has attracted mathematicians for more than seventy five years. This article retells the effect and its classic method, surveys how far it can be pushed, and presents several new results that matter to performers. We give a version of Cheney's method that needs no fixed first suit and no fixed ``lowest card'': shifting every card one step in rank and one step in suit shifts the display in the same way. A heckler who may swap two neighboring cards of the display defeats every method with a full deck. We show that a 29-card deck is the largest for which such a swap can be corrected, and that the corresponding maximum is 14 cards if any two cards may be swapped. We give simple methods that achieve both bounds. Finally, we make Berlekamp's arithmetic method for the 124-card deck independent of where the numbering starts. We also describe a pocket version with eight cards.

papers.title: The Hubbard-Wigner model: from Aubry-Mather theory to Fractional Quantum Hall Effects
papers.abstract: The Hubbard-Wigner model describes binary lattice configurations with convex repulsive pair interactions. We give a unified classification of its periodic minimizers, minimizing invariant measures, and Aubry sets through a positive block-count identity, recovering explicit plateau widths and a complete devil's staircase for the minimizing density. This variational structure parallels Aubry-Mather theory and the authors' work on Aubry's completeness conjecture, where the staircase is related to the sliding and pinning mechanisms underlying the conducting and insulating interpretations of particle chains. In the binary model, completeness follows from discrete convexity and an exact sum of plateau widths. We then study how this classical structure persists for interactions arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect on a thin torus. At rational density $p/q$, the diagonal reference has a $q$-dimensional lowest eigenspace, a spectral gap uniform in the number of repeated periods, and an associated bundle of Chern number $p$. For the full $V_1$ operator, we prove persistence of a density-$1/3$ plateau and a positive spectral gap, uniformly in system size at sufficiently small fixed transverse circumference; the lowest-eigenspace bundle has rank three and Chern number one. For the full periodic Coulomb operator, we establish multiplicity, spectral-gap, and Chern-number conclusions at bounded denominators, and quantitative bounds on plateau-endpoint displacement and loss of width under explicit joint conditions on size and geometry.

papers.title: Reducible fibers of polynomials over integers: the Hilbert-Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$ and its applications
papers.abstract: Given a polynomial $f\in \mathbb{Q}[X]$, the Hilbert--Siegel problem asks for a description of the set of all values $t_0\in \mathbb{Z}$, possibly up to a finite set, such that $f(X)-t_0$ is reducible. Reducibility occurs trivially for $t_0$ in the value set of some non-linear left-composition factor of $f$. The problem therefore reduces to determining the polynomials having infinitely many further reducible values. The biggest step towards a solution so far was taken in joint work of the author with Behajaina and Neftin. We strengthen some of the methods obtained in that work to present the complete solution of the Hilbert--Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. We give applications to the problem of newly reducible iterates of polynomials, and to an unlikely intersection problem on simultaneous reducible fibers of two polynomial maps over $\mathbb{Q}$, generalizing a result by Bilu and Tichy.

papers.title: The polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden conjecture
papers.abstract: We study positive classical solutions of the polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden system $(-Δ)^m u=|x|^αv^p$, $(-Δ)^m v=|x|^βu^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $m\ge2$, $p,q\ge1$, $pq>1$, and $α,β\ge0$. We prove that there is no such solution whenever $\frac{n+α}{p+1}+\frac{n+β}{q+1}>n-2m$, in every dimension and without any assumption on the behavior of the solutions at infinity. Combined with an existence result of Villavert, this proves the polyharmonic Hénon--Lane--Emden conjecture of Phan for $m\ge2$: for these exponents and weights, a positive classical solution exists if and only if $\frac{n+α}{p+1}+\frac{n+β}{q+1}\le n-2m$. The proof has two parts. We first show that positivity forces $(-Δ)^i u>0$ and $(-Δ)^i v>0$ for $1\le i\le m-1$. For $m$ even this needs $pq>1$, and explicit radial examples show that it fails when $pq<1$ and when $p=q=1$. The system is then equivalent to a weighted integral system with a Riesz kernel of order $2m$. For such integral systems we prove the corresponding Liouville theorem for every Riesz order $μ\in(1,n)$, adapting a recent argument for the second-order case that combines a localized virial identity with an interval comparison along source layers.
papers.comments: This research was initially deposited on Zenodo on October 9, 2026 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23268558)

papers.title: The geometric case of the Erdős Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
papers.abstract: For a fixed $q\in(0,1)$, can a set of positive Lebesgue measure avoid every translated and dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$? OpenAI's release of October 6, 2026 shows that it can, with a compact subset of $[0,1]$ whose measure is arbitrarily close to one. We give a detailed exposition of the proof, using only finite probability and basic measure theory. The proof removes a small open set intersecting every copy, obtained from a random construction: fair random choices, attached to the cells of nested grids, route each point down a finite tree, and at the leaf reached a further random choice removes the point with probability $p$. The removed set therefore has expected density $p$, however large the tree, while the branching gives each copy many independent chances to intersect it. Each chance depends on only part of the tree, so its outcome changes at only a controlled number of dilations, and a union bound over finitely many representative dilations then covers every dilation. We also relate the proof to the earlier random-cell arguments going back to Kolountzakis (Bull. London Math. Soc. 29 (1997), 415--424) and to recent work on two-fold sumsets (arXiv:2607.03584) and on Rajchman measures (arXiv:2609.04456), and we show how the method of conditional expectations makes the construction deterministic.

papers.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$
papers.abstract: Let $c>1$ be noninteger, and let $Λ$ denote the von Mangoldt function. The averages \[ A_N^{c} f(x):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N} Λ(n)f\bigl(T^{\lfloor n^c\rfloor}x\bigr) \] satisfy the variational estimate \[ \bigl\|\mathcal{V}^r(A_N^{c} f:N\in\mathbb{N})\bigr\|_{L^p(X)} \lesssim_{c,p,r}\|f\|_{L^p(X)} \] for every $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$, on every $σ$-finite measure-preserving system. In particular, the normalized averages along fractional powers of primes converge almost everywhere. The main arithmetic ingredient is a uniform bound on the correlations of $Λ-1$ with fractional-power exponential phases, yielding arbitrarily large powers of logarithmic gain. We obtain this estimate through short-interval polynomial approximation of the fractional phase and higher-order discorrelation estimates. The same approach yields almost-everywhere convergence to for the Möbius-weighted averages along $\left( \lfloor n^c \rfloor \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ throughout $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Finding optimal measurement sequences for broken or constrained measuring devices
papers.abstract: Measuring devices do not always function perfectly due to fatigue, damage, or malfunction. When device repair or replacement is not possible, it becomes necessary to seek optimal measurements from a broken device. We show this is possible via a sequential decision making process where we optimize measurement sequences over the remaining available measurements using information theory. With dynamic programming, we show greedy measurement sequences are always suboptimal for a simple class of measurement constraints. Greedy measurement sequences generally lead to equiprobable measurement outcomes, while the optimal policy is found to select each measurement in such a way as to assign a low probability to any measurement outcome that triggers a constraint condition; leading to measurement outcomes that are not equiprobable. A measurement sequence generated under this policy is shown to decompress its source: that is, the expected number of measurement outcomes is strictly greater than the number of bits it encodes, defining a key property of constrained measurements. Dynamic programming is inefficient for finding optimal measurement sequences, so we develop an alternative algorithm related to optimal binary decision trees. By deriving upper and lower complexity bounds for the task, we propose this algorithm as an efficient means to find optimal measurements for a broken or constrained measuring device.

papers.title: Ricci flows and bracket flows on twisted principal bundles
papers.abstract: We show that Ricci flows of invariant metrics on twisted principal bundles with nilpotent fibres over \(S^1\) are immortal and type III. After normalisation and lift to the universal cover, a sequence of metrics converges in the Cheeger--Gromov topology to a homogeneous expanding Ricci soliton. The proof extends the bracket flow technique from homogeneous Ricci flows to invariant Ricci flows on twisted principal bundles.

papers.title: Validity of three-dimensional axisymmetric steady Prandtl expansion
papers.abstract: We study steady axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flows with swirl in the circular cylinder $\mathcal C_L=(0,L)\times B_2(0,1)$ with the no-slip condition on the stationary lateral wall. For the leading Euler velocity $(u_e^0,w_e^0,θ_e^0)=(1,0,r K(r))$, where $K(r)=H(r^2)$ is a prescribed smooth radial function, we construct and justify a Prandtl expansion as $\varepsilon \to 0$ for sufficiently small fixed $L$. The expansion accounts for both axial and azimuthal boundary layers, including the case of a Blasius leading axial profile with nonzero swirl. Weighted estimates at the symmetry axis and coupled remainder estimates yield a uniform velocity error bound.

papers.title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
papers.abstract: For $0<κ<8$, we prove a uniform dimension transformation theorem for SLE in natural time: on a single probability-one event, Hausdorff and packing dimensions of every time set are multiplied by $d=1+κ/8$, and the same holds for lower and upper box dimensions of every bounded time set. The result applies to self-similar SLE with stationary increments, chordal SLE in the half-plane, and chordal SLE in bounded piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domains. In the last case, the box-dimension conclusion holds under a positive-angle endpoint hypothesis. We also establish boundary-inclusive local Hölder continuity of every order below $1/d$ for chordal SLE in natural time and identify the exact local dimension $d$ of the natural occupation measure on compact time intervals.

papers.title: Relative trisection maps on 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that for an arbitrary compact orientable smooth $4$--dimensional manifold $M$ with a given open book structure on the boundary $\partial M \neq \emptyset$, which may be disconnected, there exists a generic smooth map of $M$ onto the $2$--disk which gives a relative trisection on $M$ consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$. This gives a new proof to the existence of a relative trisection on $M$. In fact, it turns out that every relative trisection can be obtained in this way. As a byproduct, we also show that $M$ always admits a decomposition into a PALF (positive allowable Lefschetz fibration) over the $2$--disk $D^2$ and a fiber bundle over the circle with a sutured compression body fiber, consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$ and with the surface bundle structure of the PALF over $\partial D^2$.

papers.title: On the Hasse-Sugawara problem and its application to Hilbert's twelfth problem
papers.abstract: We give an analytic proof of the Hasse-Sugawara problem by treating the seven remaining families of moduli. We also construct an explicit integer translate of a Weber value whose relative norms generate every intermediate field, and express these generators using extended form class groups.

papers.title: The topology of the amoeba map and maximal volume
papers.abstract: For a smooth complete intersection $V\subset(\C^*)^n$ of dimension $k$, $n\ge2k$, we bound the volume of its amoeba by $π^{2k}$ times a sum of mixed volumes, divided by the order of any finite group $Γ$ of symmetries commuting with the logarithmic map. For $n=2k\ge4$ almost every fibre of the amoeba map has a number of points divisible by $2|Γ|$. For $n=2k$ we characterise the varieties of maximal volume, show that for $k\ge2$ they are not real, and prove that no plane in general position in $(\C^*)^4$ has maximal volume. For $n>2k$ the bound is never attained, varieties of maximal volume have amoeba maps injective off a null set, and injectivity is generic. The amoeba map of almost every real $k$-plane is two-to-one, and that of the $k$-th symmetric power of a real line exactly $2^k$-to-one; conversely, real $k$-planes in general position in $(\C^*)^{2k}$ with $2^k$-to-one amoeba maps are symmetric powers. We also classify the real planes of $(\C^*)^4$ and study lines in $(\C^*)^3$.

papers.title: Exact Simes inequalities for two-sided Gaussian tests
papers.abstract: The Simes test combines marginal p-values to test a global null hypothesis. Whether it controls the type I error for two-sided Gaussian tests with arbitrary covariance remains open. We prove that, for every fixed number $m$ of tests, the rejection probability does not exceed the nominal level when that level is sufficiently small. The same range of levels works for every covariance matrix. Equality holds if and only if the p-values form independent groups with identical values within each group. For $m=3$, a computer-assisted proof establishes validity at $0.05$, and an analytic argument extends it to an explicit interval around $0.05$. As the number $m$ of tests increases, we prove validity in two settings: each test statistic is correlated with at most a fixed number of others; or the statistics form independent blocks whose sizes grow sufficiently slowly, at a specified rate of order $\log\log m$. Both settings allow arbitrary correlations within these restrictions. For any fixed $0<a<1$, validity holds for every $m$ above a threshold $M$ and every level $0<α\le a$; the same $M$ works for all allowed covariances.
