Further results quantify the difference between the nominal level and the rejection probability, and permit more correlated neighbors when their correlations are bounded away from $\pm1$. We do not obtain numerical values for the general small-level cutoffs or the required number of tests.

papers.title: Jensen--Mercer-type Inequalities and Strongly $f$-Divergences
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop refined Jensen--Mercer-type inequalities for strongly convex functions, including reverse inequalities in the differentiable case. We identify the relationships between these inequalities and known bounds. Our method exploits a structural decomposition of strongly convex functions together with classical convexity arguments. As applications, we obtain explicit and computable bounds for strongly $f$-divergences, leading to new quantitative estimates for major divergence measures such as the Kullback--Leibler divergence, $χ^{2}$-divergence, Hellinger divergence, Bhattacharyya-type divergence, and Jeffreys divergence.

papers.title: Substrate hypergraph cycles: unique steady states and persistence for every enzyme assignment; oscillations enabled by enzyme sharing
papers.abstract: We associate a directed substrate hypergraph with an enzymatic reaction system. The hypergraph records which substrates each composite reaction consumes and produces, and each composite reaction is realized by a Henri--Michaelis--Menten (HMM) module whose enzyme may be distinct, shared with other reactions, or absent. We call the hypergraph a cycle when it is strongly connected and every substrate is produced by exactly one reaction and consumed by exactly one reaction, each time with coefficient one; equivalently, its dual is a strongly connected ordinary directed graph. For a cycle, every HMM realization, under every enzyme assignment and for all positive rate constants, has exactly one positive steady state in each stoichiometric compatibility class that contains a strictly positive point, and no steady state on the boundary of such a class, and every trajectory in such a class is persistent. The interior dynamics, in contrast, depend on how enzymes are shared. When each enzyme catalyzes at most one reaction, every trajectory in such a class converges to its unique steady state. With enzyme sharing, convergence can fail even for the three-substrate transformation cycle $X_1\to X_2\to X_3\to X_1$: if two transformations share an enzyme and the third has its own enzyme or none, the steady state can undergo a supercritical Hopf bifurcation that produces a stable limit cycle. Thus the substrate structure controls existence, uniqueness, and persistence, while the pattern of enzyme sharing controls the interior dynamics. The results extend to weighted cycles, which allow higher stoichiometric coefficients, and to longer chains of intermediates.

papers.title: Radial and nonradial solutions for nonlinear scalar field equations and a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on the plane
papers.abstract: A nonlinear scalar field equation is studied, which takes the form \begin{equation*} - \triangle{u}=g(u) \ \textrm{in} \ R^{N}, \quad \quad u \in E, \end{equation*} where $E$ is a suitable Banach space.. The nonlinear term $g(s)$ has subcritical growth at infinity. Near $s=0$, the nonlinear term $g(s)$ grows like $s^q$ for any $q>0$ if $N=2$ and for any $q \in (0,\ (N+2)/(N-2))$ if $N\ge 3$. Through the technique of adding one dimension of space, by mountain pass theorem and symmetric mountain theorem, we prove the multiplicity of radial solutions if $N\ge 2$ and the multiplicity of nonradial solutions if $N\ge 4$. Unlike [1] and [2], the proof presented here does not rely on any decomposition results. During the treatment for $N=2$, we provide a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on $R^2$, which is originally due to [3]. Based on this inequality we get a Trudinger-Moser type inequality involving gradient norm through Taylor expansion. Eventually we construct a special path to obtain the least energy level for solutions. [1] J. Mederski, Nonradial solutions of nonlinear scalar field equations. Nonlinearity 33 (2020), 6349--6380. [2] L. Jeanjean, S.S. Lu, Nonlinear scalar field equations with general nonlinearity. Nonlinear Anal. 190 (2020), 111604. [3] D.E. Edmunds, A.A.Ilyin, Asymptotically sharp multiplicative inequalities. Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995) 71--74.

papers.title: No Borel upper bound for the $F_σ$ equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We prove that the family of coset relations of $F_σ$ real linear subspaces of Banach space $\ell_1$ has no common upper bound among Borel equivalence relations in the sense of Borel reducibility. These relations are indexed by a well-founded tree. Consequently, on a Polish space, a universal $Σ^0_α$ equivalence relation exists exactly when $α=1$, and a universal $Π^0_α$ equivalence relation exists exactly when $α=1$ or $2$. This strengthens the earlier nonexistence theorem for a universal $F_σ$ equivalence relation. This also answers a question of Kanovei and Lyubetsky about universal equivalence relations in Borel classes.

papers.title: Finite Groups with Few Almost Maximal Subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group. L. Morgana, C. E. Praeger, A.E. Zalesski \cite {MOR} introduced the notion of almost maximal subgroup of $G$. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be almost maximal in $G$ if $N_G(H)$ is maximal in $G$. In this paper, let $AM(G)$ denote the number of conjugacy classes of all almost maximal subgroups of $G$. First, we prove that $G$ is Dedekindian if and only if $AM(G)=0$. Second, we show that the finite groups with $AM(G)\leq 1$ are supersolvable. Furthermore, we characterize the structure of finite groups with $AM(G)=1$. Final, we investigate a lower bound of $AM(G)$ for certain non-solvable groups.

papers.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

papers.title: Total variation bounds for Schrödinger--Föllmer sampling of boundary-vanishing densities
papers.abstract: We derive total variation bounds for the Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler when the target density vanishes at the boundary of its support. This boundary behavior produces a terminal-time singularity in the drift near the boundary. We first prove a base estimate under a single quantitative hypothesis, finiteness of the relative Fisher information, without assuming boundedness or Lipschitz continuity of the drift. We then combine this estimate with a mixture regularization, thereby reducing the problem to determining the growth rate of the regularized Fisher information. For densities with an exact polynomial vanishing order on the boundary of a smooth bounded domain, we determine this growth rate and its leading constant. Orders above one yield the square-root rate in the number of steps, with a logarithmic loss at order one. For orders between one half and one, the rate exponent decreases continuously from one half toward one third. Finite mixtures of triangular kernel densities fall into the linear case.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a Cubic Nondegeneracy Conjecture
papers.abstract: Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko conjectured that a cubic Boolean generating function satisfying an ordered separation condition on its second polar must be equivalent to one of two symmetric normal forms. Two infinite families of counterexamples are constructed and proved analytically; both are direct sums of small seeds, and neither is equivalent to the proposed forms even after linear functions are added. The first adjoins a nondegenerate quadratic block to a ternary cubic seed and is distinguished from the proposed forms by the radical of its third polar. This radical determines the associative nucleus of every twisted quasialgebra with the given generating function, so the corresponding algebras are not isomorphic even when the grading is forgotten. The second family consists of direct sums of a five-variable seed and has zero third-polar radical. A criterion for quadratic-block presentations establishes the separation property of the seed; commutation-graph degrees, radical dimensions, and contraction ranks establish non-equivalence in all dimensions of the family.

papers.title: Convex Reformulation of Minkowski-Sum Outer Approximation for Matrix Ellipsoids in Data-Driven Control
papers.abstract: Approximating Minkowski sums of matrix ellipsoids by a single matrix ellipsoid provides a tractable description of noise bounds for controller design from noisy data. Existing linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions can be used to compute such approximations, but directly solving the resulting optimization problems can be computationally expensive. This paper develops an efficient method for finding a minimum-volume outer matrix ellipsoid under these LMI conditions. Although the corresponding problem for ordinary vector-valued ellipsoids is convex, the objective function in the matrix-valued case is nonconvex. We find that the problem admits an equivalent convex reformulation, which resolves this difficulty. We first eliminate the matrix variables using equivalent LMI transformations and objective monotonicity, leaving one positive scalar variable per matrix ellipsoid in the sum. We then show that the objective becomes convex after a logarithmic change of variables. The resulting problem contains neither LMI constraints nor matrix variables and can therefore be solved efficiently. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed method is substantially faster than the LMI-based method. An application to data-driven control further illustrates the tradeoff between guaranteed control performance and computation time.

papers.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations by One Noise Component
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus with multiplicative Itô noise which is driven by a single Brownian motion and acts only through the vertical velocity component. Such a noise is strongly degenerate: An infinite-dimensional part of the velocity field is not forced at all. We show that it nevertheless has a regularizing effect. For a linear noise, strong solutions whose initial data have no unforced part are global with probability tending to one as the noise intensity grows. For a suitable nonlinear noise, the same holds for arbitrary $\mathrm{H}^1$ data, together with smallness of the space-time $\mathrm{L}^6$-norm of the vertical velocity. As a deterministic counterpart, we give a self-contained proof that a quintic damping of the vertical component yields global regularity, and the same argument shows that, under the linear noise, blow-up can only occur if the vertical velocity leaves $\mathrm{L}^6_{t,x}$.

papers.title: Optimal Annuitization, Consumption, and Investment with Costly Capital Injections
papers.abstract: We study a joint optimal decision of portfolio, consumption, and annuitization for a pension-plan manager who balances retirement consumption benefits against the cost of maintaining the solvency of pension account. The pension sponsor provides costly capital injection to prevent negative wealth. Annuity purchases are irreversible, and injected funds remain in the liquid account and earn interest. Using the Legendre transform, we derive a semi-explicit solution to the associated free-boundary problem and verify the optimality of the resulting strategies. We identify an endogenous annuity-income threshold separating injection-active and injection-inactive regions and characterize six policy regimes arising from the interplay between capital injections and consumption constraints. Compared with the no-injection benchmark, capital injections delay annuitization, alter the structure of the annuitization boundary, and permit positive holdings in risky assets even at zero liquid wealth. Numerical results further reveal that cheaper annuities may increase the expected capital contributions required from the pension sponsor.

papers.title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
papers.abstract: We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.

papers.title: Explicit permutations of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ with uniformly bounded differential uniformity
papers.abstract: Symmetric primitives over Galois rings need nonlinear components whose differentials with respect to ring addition are controlled. Let $R=\mathrm{GR}(4,m)$ and $q=2^m$, so that $(R,+)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ has order $N=q^2$. For every $m\ge1$ we construct an explicit permutation $G_c$ of $R$ all of whose differentials with a nonzero input difference have probability at most $36/N$, whereas every permutation polynomial of $R$ has such a differential of probability at least $2/\sqrt{N}$ (Ronjom--Sandrib). The bound holds for the fixed permutation itself, not on average over keys. Equivalently, $Δ(G_c)\le36$ against $Δ\ge2\sqrt{N}$ for permutation polynomials; since every permutation has $Δ\ge2$, the least differential uniformity of a permutation of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ lies between $2$ and $36$ for every $m$. In Teichmuller digits $(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2$ and for $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of absolute trace $1$, $G_c(a,b)=(L,(L^2+L+c)a)$ with $L=(a^2+a+c)b$. The map is $F_c\circ J\circ F_c$, where $F_c(a,b)=(a,(a^2+a+c)b)$ is induced by a polynomial over $R$ and $J$ exchanges the digits: a single digit exchange between two polynomial layers yields a bound independent of $m$. The proof reduces the difference equations, in each of three types of directions, to one-variable polynomials whose degrees do not depend on $m$. For general maps $F\circ J\circ F$ with $F(a,b)=(p(a),h(a)+d(a)b)$, where $p,d,h$ have degrees bounded independently of $m$, $p'\ne0$ and $d$ has no zeros, a Jacobian identity in characteristic $2$ bounds the differentials with nonzero low input and output differences independently of $m$; the remaining directions need a separate argument, which we give for an explicit family ($Δ\le440$, resp. $510$, for odd $m$).
papers.comments: 8 pages. Source, verification scripts and recorded outputs: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23876071

papers.title: Supermodularity and robust optimization in elliptic PDEs
papers.abstract: We study distributionally robust optimization problems constrained by semilinear elliptic PDEs. Uncertain nonnegative loads enter the PDE through $m$ intensity parameters, and damage is measured by integrating a nondecreasing convex function of the solution. We prove that, for coercive operators satisfying a positivity-preserving lattice condition, a nondecreasing concave reaction $g$ makes the damage nondecreasing, convex, and supermodular in the load intensities. Under nonnegative loading and $g(0)=0$, concavity is also necessary for these properties to hold for all admissible operators and damage functions. For Wasserstein uncertainty sets based on a weighted $\ell_1$ distance and $N$ observations, we show that at most $m+1$ nested stress corners are needed per observation. These corners form a set of at most $N(m+1)$ points that does not depend on the Wasserstein radius and supports a worst-case distribution for every radius. We compute the exact robust value by checking $λ=0$ and at most $Nm$ positive breakpoints, and we construct a worst-case distribution that moves each observation to a chain corner and splits at most one observation between two adjacent corners. We apply the results to a convex remediation-planning problem with Monod biodegradation. Numerical experiments show that the method requires far fewer PDE solves than enumerating all corners. Finally, a counterexample shows that supermodularity can fail for the fractional $p$-Laplacian when $p>2$.

papers.title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.

papers.title: $S_n$-equivariant $L$-classes of Cartesian powers of Witt spaces and the Hodge index conjecture for symmetric products
papers.abstract: For a compact oriented even-dimensional Witt pseudomanifold $X$, we compute the $S_n$-equivariant Banagl--Zagier $L$-classes of $X^n$ in terms of the Goresky--MacPherson $L$-classes of $X$ and the intersection cohomology Euler characteristic of $X$. This generalizes a theorem of Zagier for manifolds. Our approach is based on analyzing the equivariant structure of the signature operator of $X^n$ using equivariant $KK$-theory and power operations in analytic $K$-homology. We establish an analytic $K$-homology analogue of Moonen's algebraic localization theorem by proving that the localized Chern character of the $n$-th power operation, evaluated at an $n$-cycle, agrees with the $n$-th homological Adams operation applied to the Chern character. As an application, we prove that the characteristic class Hodge index conjecture for singular varieties, formulated by Brasselet--Schürmann--Yokura, is preserved under taking symmetric products of complex projective varieties.

papers.title: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
papers.abstract: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index. We prove that, when the associated subfactor has finite depth, the 3-tensors satisfying the zipper condition correspond precisely to the quantum $6j$-symbols, also known as $F$-symbols, of the unitary multi-fusion category arising from the subfactor. This realization of quantum $6j$-symbols differs from their realization through a flat bi-unitary connection arising from the higher relative commutants of a subfactor.

papers.title: Dynamics of Transversal Matroids
papers.abstract: We propose a way of generating matroids by randomly picking indicator vectors, and since we will see that it mostly gives uniform matroids, which are transversal, we then look at randomly generated transversal matroids. In both models we also investigate threshold phenomena of certain monotone increasing properties. Non-monotone properties of transversal matroids will also be investigated. Moreover, we are going to see how to spot circuits of a transversal matroid from its bipartite graph presentation. In the last Chapter, we have a survey of the characterization of transversal matroids that admit acyclic bipartite presentations. We will also investigate when we can simplify a presentation for a transversal matroid.

papers.title: On the Diophantine equation $Cx^2+p^{2m}=y^q$
papers.abstract: We classify the primitive positive solutions of $Cx^2+p^{2m}=y^q$ under the hypotheses that $C>3$ is odd and square-free, $p,q$ are odd primes, $p\nmid C$, $q\nmid h(-C)$, and $y$ is odd. The solutions form six explicit families: one for arbitrary $q$ and five exceptional families with $q=3$, three of which arise from half-integral elements when $C\equiv3\pmod8$. The proof combines ideal factorization with Lehmer sequences and shows that representations with second coordinate $v=p^r$, $r>0$, contribute only when $q=3$.

papers.title: On a finite group in which every maximal subgroup of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that if every maximal subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent then $G$ is a solvable group having a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.

papers.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.

papers.title: Federated Affine Variational Inequalities: Exact Averaging and Complexity Limits
papers.abstract: We study the classical Local Stochastic Extragradient method (Local SEG) for monotone variational inequalities under intermittent communication, where devices perform several local oracle calls between synchronization rounds. For affine monotone mean operators, including nonsymmetric bilinear saddle systems, we prove that equal device averaging commutes pathwise with both stages of the stochastic extragradient update. Local trajectories may therefore drift apart while their mean follows a centralized stochastic-extragradient recursion driven by averaged noise. The identity remains valid when individual oracle realizations are nonlinear and query dependent. Under conditionally centered oracle errors that are conditionally independent across devices within each stage, the reduction yields a restricted weak-gap rate that uses the local sequential depth for deterministic progress and the aggregate oracle budget across devices for variance reduction. When every device makes at least two local oracle calls per communication round, the bound contains no additional mixed client-drift term and is also attained by a terminal-only aggregation schedule. An affine Gaussian lower bound matches the depth and sample dependences before statistical saturation for distributed zero-respecting algorithms; its statistical component applies to arbitrary randomized algorithms. A complementary lower bound for feasible distributed zero-respecting methods shows that bounded geometry and query-dependent noise can create an additional communication-locality obstruction. These results delineate the exact-averaging regime of unconstrained affine Local SEG and a complexity boundary that arises under active feasibility constraints.

papers.title: Degree and arity of tracial separation for self-adjoint contractions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent explicit counterexample to Connes' embedding conjecture, we study the degree and number of variables needed to separate normalized matrix traces on self-adjoint contractions from traces on finite von Neumann algebras. We prove that the two trace infima coincide for every Hermitian polynomial of degree at most two in at most three variables, with a dimension-explicit approximation bound. We give three explicit separators: an integer-coefficient polynomial of degree six in ten variables with 392 nonzero words, a quadratic polynomial in 214 variables, and an integer-coefficient polynomial in two variables of ordinary and cyclic degree 24. Each has normalized trace at least \(3/4\) on every matrix contraction tuple and trace \(-1\) at a finite tracial witness. We provide the source systems, transfer estimates, and exact coefficient recipes for all three constructions.

papers.title: A note on an extension of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-solvable group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that the intersection of all non-nilpotent maximal subgroups of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is $p$-closed, which provides a further generalization of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem.

papers.title: Invariance principle for long-memory linear processes under sublinear expectations
papers.abstract: We establish an invariance principle for long-memory linear processes with power-law coefficients under sublinear expectations. Under truncated-moment and capacity-tail conditions, we construct these processes on a canonical space and prove weak convergence in continuous path space of their linearly interpolated, normalized partial sums. The limiting sublinear law is represented as an upper expectation over stochastic integrals with a fractional Brownian moving-average kernel and predictable volatility controls, driven by a two-sided classical Brownian motion. When variance uncertainty vanishes, the limit reduces to the classical fractional Brownian limit. The proof combines a multidimensional Rosenthal inequality, coefficient approximation, and the invariance principle for independent and identically distributed random variables to establish finite-dimensional convergence. Tightness follows from second-moment increment bounds. Uniform approximation on compact sets then extends the convergence from bounded Lipschitz to bounded continuous test functions.

papers.title: Indecomposable Uniform Families on the Adams 4-Line
papers.abstract: We show that the $f_j$, $p_j$, $D_3(j)$, and $p_j'$ families on the 4-line of the classical Adams spectral sequence all conform to the Uniform Doomsday Conjecture. We do so by first using Bruner's formula to establish uniform families of differentials on these classes. We then study the Burklund-Xu and Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences to ensure that the differential targets are nonzero. The $f_j$ family requires further analysis of possible Adams $d_2$ differentials since the $f_j$ support uniform $d_3$ differentials. As a result of our work, only two indecomposable $\text{Sq}^0$ families remain to be settled in Adams filtration 4.

papers.title: Spectral radius and size conditions for 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs to contain a $k$-factor with $k\ge 3$
papers.abstract: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$ is called the spectral radius $ρ(G)$ of $G$. If $S$ is a vertex cut of a connected graph $G$, then $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of connected components of $G-S$. The toughness $t(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as $t(G) = \min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}: S \subset V(G), \text{ and } c(G-S) > 1\right\}$. A graph \( G \) is \( t \)-tough if \( |S| \ge t c(G - S) \) for every proper subset \( S \subset V(G) \) satisfying \( c(G - S) > 1 \). Combining the toughness and spectral conditions, we provide spectral radius and size conditions for the existence of $k$-factors in 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs. This settles a problem posed by Chen, Fan and Lin in [Discrete Appl. Math. {\bf 355} (2024), 223--231].

papers.title: Local null controllability of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis system by a Neumann boundary control
papers.abstract: We prove local null controllability for a parabolic equation coupled to an elliptic equation on a bounded interval. The drift depends on the elliptic variable, and a single control acts through the Neumann condition at the left endpoint. For every positive control time and every locally Lipschitz drift function, sufficiently small initial data in $L^\infty$ can be driven to zero by an $L^\infty$ boundary control. To construct the control, we extend the linear equation to a larger interval using an even extension of the initial datum and an odd extension of the drift. A distributed $L^2$ control in the added interval then gives a boundary control on the original interval. A heat kernel estimate bounds the derivative trace needed for this construction. We obtain the nonlinear result by a set-valued fixed point argument.

papers.title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations. Closed cell 6-plate geometries were also additively manufactured using LAPIS and experimentally characterized. The results indicate that a minimum of 6 plates is required to constitute an ultrastiff isotropic lattice, 7 plates would return the established plate Cubic Octet structure while 8 to 10 plate geometries did not show significant differences in properties. Despite the introduction of some plate bending due to sub-optimal plate placement strategy, relative stiffness of the PINNs lattices adheres closely to the Hashin Shtrikman upper bound, 90 percent of Hashin Shtrikman upper bound at a relative density of 0.4, and the lattices maintain near isotropic behaviour, achieving a Zener ratio of 0.95 at a relative density of 0.1. Benchmarking results show that specific stiffness of PINNs lattices is higher than the majority of isotropic architectures reported in the literature.

papers.title: Hereditary lowerability of diagonal entropy scales
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a continuous self-map of a compact metric space. For each integer $p\geq2$, we consider the upper capacity entropy scale obtained by dividing the $p$-fold logarithm of an orbit covering number by the $(p-1)$-fold logarithm of time. We prove that every nonempty compact set contains a compact subset realizing any value between zero and its own scale entropy. Every strictly intermediate value is realized by a countable compact set with exactly one accumulation point. The proof combines localization at a fixed spatial resolution, a finite-tree selection lemma, and refinements of orbit covers at dyadic times. An example shows that the assertion about one accumulation point does not extend to the upper endpoint. On the product-diagonal construction used in classical entropy lowerability, the diagonal scales preserve the values of the base subsets, although classical upper capacity entropy takes only zero or infinity.

papers.title: Spectral Response Geometry for Liouville Brownian Motion
papers.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion associated with a subcritical Gaussian multiplicative chaos measure on a bounded planar domain, we study the response of finite spectral blocks under Cameron--Martin perturbations of the underlying Gaussian free field. For each fixed $0<γ<2$, we prove that, almost surely, all unordered eigenfunction-product measures in every finite simple spectral block are linearly independent. This strengthens the corresponding diagonal independence statement and implies surjectivity of the joint eigenvalue and eigenframe response map. We use this transversality to construct real-analytic local deformations that preserve a prescribed finite block of eigenvalues while varying its eigenframe. We then identify the least Cameron--Martin energy required to realize a given infinitesimal angular response, expressing it through a positive Schur complement of the response operator. Finally, on finite-dimensional Gaussian slices, we derive the conditional law associated with the local isospectral leaf and compare the induced slice metric with the full Cameron--Martin minimum. The results provide a local geometric description of spectral flexibility for Liouville Brownian motion.

papers.title: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.

papers.title: The dual Orlicz-Minkowski problem for capillary hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $φ(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+hν$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.

papers.title: Extreme values of derivatives of Dedekind zeta functions on the $1$-line
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish lower bounds for extreme values of derivatives of Dedekind zeta functions on the \(1\)-line over arbitrary fixed number fields. Our result extends Yang's corresponding estimate for the Riemann zeta function in 2024, with the leading constant involving residues of Dedekind zeta functions and a moment of the Dickman function. A key ingredient is a uniform asymptotic formula for weighted friable sums involving the coefficients of Dedekind zeta functions.

papers.title: Meromorphic functions together with their partial derivatives sharing zeros and poles in $\mathbb{C}^m$
papers.abstract: In the paper, using Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$, we study the problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be two finite order non-constant meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $f$ and $g$ share $0$ and $\infty$ CM. If $\partial_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM and if for one $n>1$, $\partial^n_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial^n_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM, where $i=1,2,\ldots,m$, then $f$ and $g$ have special presentations. Our finding extends the result of Köhler (Meromorphic functions sharing zeros and poles and also some of their derivatives sharing zeros, Complex Var., 11 (1989), 39-48) into higher dimensions. Moreover, we show by an example that the restriction on the growth of $f$ and $g$ is necessary.

papers.title: Extensions at Nonzero p-Characters for Cartan-Type Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: For restricted simple Cartan-type Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, the reduced enveloping algebra at every nonzero $p$-character is a matrix algebra over a terminal symmetric corner, and this corner determines the extensions. Central-socle traces recover its radical and its simple factors, and the first radical layer determines the degree-one extensions. For the Witt algebra $W(1;1)$, at even height $2\le h\le p-3$, the unique simple module has self-extension dimension $\min\{p-h-2,h+2\}$. At height two in characteristic seven, we present the Yoneda algebra as an eight-dimensional symmetric algebra tensored with a polynomial algebra on three central degree-two classes. An equivariant Tate resolution and cocycle identities prove the presentation in all degrees.

papers.title: Information Complexity of Inner Product and Matrix Multiplication via Shannon-to-Min-Entropy Conversion
papers.abstract: We determine the information complexity of matrix multiplication over finite fields under independent uniform inputs, up to a universal additive constant. The binary inner-product case resolves the open question of Braverman, Garg, Pankratov, and Weinstein on the optimal dependence of information complexity on the error probability. For inputs in $\mathbb F_2^m$ and error at most $\varepsilon\in[0,1/2]$, the information complexity with output at Bob lies between $(1-2\varepsilon)m-c_0$ and $(1-2\varepsilon)m$, where $c_0<4.772$ is a universal constant. For independent uniform matrices $X\in\mathbb F_q^{t\times m}$ and $Y\in\mathbb F_q^{s\times m}$, where $t\le s$, computing $XY^{\mathsf T}$ with output at Bob and error at most $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ has information complexity $(1-q^{ts}\varepsilon/(q^{ts}-1))^+mt\log_2q$, up to an additive gap of less than $9.544$ bits. This gap is independent of the matrix dimensions, field size, and error. At zero error, the information complexity is exactly $mt\log_2q$. The information lower bounds for both inner product and matrix multiplication follow from a new Shannon-to-min-entropy theorem for convolution on discrete groups. Let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_k$ be the finitely supported distributions of independent random variables taking values in a discrete group, and let $s$ be the largest support size. We show that if $k\ge\lceil\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor\ln2\rceil$, then the min-entropy of their ordered product is at least the average Shannon entropy of the $Q_i$ minus $c_0$ bits. This holds for arbitrary discrete groups, including infinite and noncommutative groups, even when the input distributions differ. The leading coefficient of the logarithmic threshold is optimal.

papers.title: Design and Analysis of Pinching-Antenna Systems With Radially Deployed Waveguides (X-PASS)
papers.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide. A single waveguide, however, confines its antennas to one line, so that good coverage of an area has relied on several waveguides or waveguide segments with separate feeds. This paper proposes X-PASS, in which a hub feeds radially deployed waveguide arms, one pinching antenna on each, and drives them by arm selection, aggregation or multiplexing. It models the hub with its insertion losses, derives a unified signal-to-noise ratio expression for these three operating modes, and derives in closed form a radius inside which aggregation outperforms selection. Numerical results validate the analysis and compare the coverage of X-PASS with that of the other layouts at equal transmit power.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

papers.title: Finite Recovery by Extrapolation for the Douglas--Rachford Method on Affine Subspaces
papers.abstract: We completely describe the dynamics of the Douglas--Rachford (DR) method for solving affine subspace feasibility. We characterise the affine hull of the resulting iterates, and we show how the corresponding search space's dimension is an explicit function of the number of distinct nontrivial principal angles. This dimension can be much smaller than the ambient dimension, helping to explain why extrapolation can be so effective. Using this characterisation, we extend the Lyapunov surrogate method (LSM) to higher extrapolation orders and prove that it recovers the DR limit exactly from finitely many iterates. We show that LSM and a least-squares extrapolation (LeSE) share the affine search spaces used by the generalized minimal residual method (GMRES) applied to the DR fixed-point equation (DR-GMRES). The dimension characterisation gives bounds on the number of steps required for exact recovery by all three methods. We develop adaptive implementations that estimate the search-space dimension from differences between successive DR iterates and use this estimate to select the extrapolation order. Numerical experiments show how ill-conditioning affects recovery accuracy, and we identify cases where adaptive extrapolation runs faster than DR-GMRES.

papers.title: Estimates for Ratios of Low-Order Eigenvalues of the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt Weights on Euclidean Domains
papers.abstract: We study low-order eigenvalue ratio estimates for the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights. For weights bounded above and below, we prove a universal upper bound for $λ_2/λ_1$ with constant $1 + \frac{4}{n}\,\frac{C}{c}$, linear in the ratio of the weight bounds, and recover the classical Payne-Pólya-Weinberger bound as a special case. For radial decreasing weights, we prove that the ball maximizes $λ_2/λ_1$ among domains of equal volume, assuming that an admissible radial test function exists (Definition 5.8) and that on the ball the second eigenvalue is attained by the $l=1$ mode. The argument adapts the method of Ashbaugh--Benguria to the weighted setting via a weighted Chiti comparison theorem and a monotonicity property of the admissible radial test function (Definition 5.8). Higher-order eigenvalue ratios are estimated in terms of the $(n-1)$-Hausdorff measure of the boundary, under an explicit balance condition on the weight at the covering scale. The generalized Payne-Pólya-Weinberger conjecture for eigenvalue sums remains open in general; conditional results are presented for restricted families of domains.

papers.title: Weighted Sobolev regularity and failure of profile convergence associated with the scattering operator for the three-dimensional cubic Klein-Gordon equation
papers.abstract: The scattering problem for the three-dimensional nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation \begin{align*} u_{tt}-Δu+u=\pm u^3 \end{align*} is studied. It was shown that the scattering operator $\mathbf{S}$ for the equation is well-defined on a neighborhood of 0 in the Sobolev space $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}:=H^{1/2}(\mathbb{R}^3) \oplus H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, and that if $Φ_-$ is sufficiently small in $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}$ and belongs to $\mathcal{S} \oplus \mathcal{S}$, then $\mathbf{S}Φ_-$ is also in $\mathcal{S} \oplus \mathcal{S}$, where $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is the Schwartz space. In the present paper, however, we prove that for any non-zero real-valued $Φ_-\in\mathcal{S}\oplus\mathcal{S}$ whose $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}$-norm is sufficiently small, the corresponding solution $u$ satisfies \[ U(-t) \,{}^t(u(t),\partial_t u(t)) \not\to \mathbf{S}Φ_- \quad(t\to+\infty) \] in the weighted Sobolev space $H^{1,3}(\mathbb{R}^3)\oplus H^{0,3}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ although $U(-t)\,{}^t(u(t),\partial_t u(t))$ converges to $\mathbf{S}Φ_-$ in $H^{1,σ}(\mathbb{R}^3)\oplus H^{0,σ}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for any $σ<3$. Here, $U(t)$ denotes the free Klein-Gordon evolution group.

papers.title: Mathematical and Numerical Analysis of Tsunami Generation and Propagation: The Initial Tsunami Condition
papers.abstract: This work investigates the appropriate initial condition for tsunami propagation that allows replacing a kinematic system with its corresponding static formulation, where the bottom is fixed at its final earthquake-induced deformation. Using the two-dimensional (2D) nonlinear shallow-water equations (NSW) and a 2D dispersive $abcd$-Boussinesq system, we prove that for the NSW system, the appropriate initial free-surface condition is exactly the final bottom deformation. For the Boussinesq model, this condition is obtained by first applying a \textit{ Boussinesq filtering operator} to the bottom profile. Furthermore, for both models, we establish an error estimate between the kinematic and static solutions that depends linearly on the earthquake rise time. This result provides a rigorous mathematical explanation for the errors observed in previous numerical tsunami simulations. As a direct consequence, the error vanishes as the bottom motion becomes instantaneous. We validate the theoretical results using an Okada solution for the seabed deformation. In particular, both the NSW model and the passive approach, which initializes the free surface with the unfiltered bottom deformation, overestimate the amplitudes of the tsunami waves relative to the linear potential theory for the configurations considered.

papers.title: Semiprime Rigidity and Growth along Powers in Integer-Sided Cyclic Polygons
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $n$, let $a(n)$ be the largest number of sides of a simple cyclic polygon of circumradius $n$ whose side lengths are positive integers. For primes $p,q$ we show that $a(pq)\in\{6,8,18\}$ and characterize each value by conditions on Gaussian and Eisenstein integers. For every integer $N\ge2$, on the other hand, $a(N^e)\to\infty$ and $\limsup_{e\to\infty}a(N^e)/e\ge2\sqrt2$; a quadratic chord tower combined with Farey neighbors gives explicit polygons, for instance $a(8192)\ge38$. We also show that an odd-sided polygon of radius $n$ exists if and only if $n$ has a prime divisor congruent to $1\pmod4$, and that $a(n)$ is even whenever at most one distinct prime divisor of $n$ is congruent to $1\pmod4$; it is also even when the Gaussian part of $n$ is the product of two distinct primes congruent to $1\pmod4$. Moreover, $a(N^e)=O_N(e^{ω(N)})$ for every fixed $N\ge2$, and $a(q^e)=Θ(e)$ for primes $q\equiv1\pmod4$; exceptional semiprime extremisers have unique side-length multisets. The proofs use a splitting lemma for angle relations by squarefree class, arithmetic in imaginary quadratic fields, bounded zero-sum problems, and a one-dimensional Farey argument. No computer-assisted step is used.

papers.title: Triangle Relation Planar Algebras: Cohomology, Classification, and New Families
papers.abstract: We establish a finite system of consistency equations for triangle relation planar algebras. Within the Yang--Baxter relation class, we characterize triangle relations by $H^2(K;\mathbb C)=0$, where $K$ is the fusion complex recording the support of the fusion coefficients. Together with a reconstruction theorem, this gives an algebraic classification procedure. We classify bi-commutative triangle relation planar algebras with $\dim P_{2,\pm}\leq5$. In ranks two, three, and four, the classification yields respectively $2$, $7$, and $19$ realizable fusion-support pair strata, up to relabelling and shading reversal. These results recover the low-rank examples of Bisch, Jones, Liu, and Lu, and extend the rank-four classification beyond exchange relations. In rank five, we obtain two one-parameter families with different duality types whose generic members do not arise from representations of groups or quantum groups.

papers.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
papers.abstract: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.

papers.title: A counterexample to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures
papers.abstract: In 1988, J.~M.~Lee conjectured that a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold admits a pseudo-Einstein contact form if and only if the real first Chern class of its holomorphic tangent bundle vanishes. The necessity of this condition was proved by Lee. We show that the condition is not sufficient: in every real dimension $2n+1\ge 5$ there is a compact connected strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$ with $c_1(\Tone)=0$ in $H^2(M;\Z)$ which admits no pseudo-Einstein contact form. The examples are boundaries of small strictly pseudoconvex neighborhoods of a section $D\cong B$ with negative normal bundle in a $\PP^1$-bundle $\PP(E_e)\to B$, where $B=C^n$ is a power of a curve of genus two and $E_e$ is a non-split extension of $\cO_B$ by an ample line bundle $L$ with $K_B\cong L^2$. More generally, if $K_B\cong L^m$, such a boundary admits a pseudo-Einstein contact form if and only if $(m-1)e=0$, where $e\in H^1(B,L)$ is the extension class; the obstruction is detected on the first infinitesimal neighborhood of $D$.

papers.title: A counterexample to a three-step convergence bound for BFGS with exact line search
papers.abstract: We disprove a three-step error estimate for the Broyden--Fletcher--Goldfarb--Shanno {(BFGS)} method with exact line searches. We construct a globally strongly convex function $F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and a single nonterminating trajectory $x_k\to0$ for which $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+3}\|/(\|x_{k+2}\|\|x_k\|)=+\infty$. The Hessian of $F$ lies between $\tfrac12 I$ and $\tfrac32 I$ everywhere, and $F(x)-\tfrac12\|x\|^2$ is compactly supported with all derivatives vanishing at $0$. The proof first constructs point-gradient pairs satisfying the exact BFGS step identities. A five-step cycle produces a large three-step quotient and restores an invariant plane for the actual updated matrix, allowing the cycle to be repeated with arbitrarily small gradient errors. Disjoint smooth corrections to a quadratic then realize all the pairs by one objective. Strong convexity identifies the prescribed points with the unique exact line-search minimizers. Thus smoothness and strong convexity do not imply the proposed product estimate, even for an objective that agrees with a quadratic to every order at its minimizer.

papers.title: Inverse optimization for divisor methods of apportionment
papers.abstract: The apportionment problem is to allocate a fixed number of seats among regions in proportion to their populations. In this paper, we propose an inverse optimization approach to evaluate how fairly an observed apportionment treats each region. It is well known that every divisor method can be formulated as a separable discrete convex minimization problem. We introduce a weighted divisor method, in which a nonnegative weight is assigned to each region, as the forward problem. Then we formulate an inverse optimization problem that finds the weight vector closest to the all-one vector in the $\ell_1$-norm such that the observed apportionment is optimal for the forward problem. We show that the optimal weight vector is always unique and has a closed-form expression as the median of three values that depend on a single parameter. Based on this result, the inverse optimization problem is reduced to a one-dimensional monotone equation, and it can be solved in $O(n \log n)$ time, where $n$ is the number of regions. We also apply the proposed approach to the apportionment of the single-member districts of the House of Representatives of Japan.

papers.title: All-Disorder Localization for the One-Dimensional Anderson Model with Power-Law Hopping
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional random operator \[ (H_{λ,ω}u)(n) = \sum_{m\ne n}\frac{u(m)}{|n-m|^r} +λω_nu(n), \] where the random variables $ω_n$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ (i.e., \mbox{$ω_n\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]$}). For every $λ>0$ and $r>3/2$, we prove that $H_{λ,ω}$ almost surely has pure point spectrum and admits an orthonormal eigenbasis $\{ψ_j\}$ satisfying \[ \sum_{n\in\bbZ}(1+|n|)^{2τ}|ψ_j(n)|^2<\infty \qquad \text{for every }j\text{ and }0\leτ<r-\frac32. \] These conclusions establish spectral localization, thereby rigorously confirming the prediction of earlier analytical and numerical studies in the physics literature, which identified $r=3/2$ as the marginal exponent.

papers.title: Generalized Wishart processes under nonlinear expectation
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of generalized Wishart processes within the framework of $G$-expectation, with $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and the $G$-Wishart process as two typical examples. In contrast to the classical setting, we show that $G$-Dyson Brownian motion may exhibit collisions and provide a sufficient condition ensuring the non-collision of the eigenvalues of generalized Wishart processes. We then derive the equations governing the high-dimensional limits of the empirical spectral measures under $G$-expectation, leading to the corresponding semicircle law for $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and Marchenko--Pastur law for the $G$-Wishart process.

papers.title: Extension of kappa-additive measures
papers.abstract: We establish an extension theorem for kappa-additive probability measures, where kappa is an arbitrary uncountable cardinal. Starting from a <kappa-algebra, we define an outer measure using coverings of cardinality at most kappa and characterise measurable sets by approximation in outer measure of symmetric differences. We prove that these sets form a kappa-algebra carrying a complete kappa-additive extension of the original measure. The extension is unique on the generated kappa-algebra, and its completion is the minimal domain admitting a complete kappa-additive extension. We also establish attainment of the covering infimum and show why the closure assumption on the initial algebra is essential. Examples include a strict extension of classical Lebesgue measure under the additional hypothesis add N = aleph_1 < cov N.

papers.title: Capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $θ\in(0,π/2)$, we study the long-time existence and asymptotic behavior of an even normalized capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$. When $pq\geq0$, the flow exists for all positive time and the evolving hypersurfaces converge smoothly along a sequence of times tending to infinity to a stationary solution of the normalized problem. If $p\neq q$, a dilation of the limit solves the unnormalized problem.

papers.title: Edge spectral invariants and second-order Steklov asymptotics for the regular tetrahedron
papers.abstract: We give a two-term Weyl asymptotic for the Steklov spectrum of a solid regular tetrahedron. Its linear coefficient is the total edge length times an explicit, absolutely convergent dihedral invariant. A trace-class difference of massive Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators computes the full invariant, including the continuous spectrum. The main analytic step is a fixed-time cumulative trace comparison between the compact tetrahedron and its exact half-space or dihedral models. Localized Hilbert-Schmidt defects have vanishing high-energy tails; retaining the time factor in Duhamel's formula makes this sufficient for an $o(L)$ cumulative error. A separate trace-class face comparison fixes the model's infinite exterior primitive and permits one observation time independent of the inner collar width. Compact-band Mourre estimates and a harmonic comparison establish immediate reflection/transmission support for incident face waves. Triangular unfolding gives null periodic and dead-end sets for the maximal branching relation. Actual edge-window bounds, adapted conical annuli and an ordered-limit Fourier-Tauberian argument then prove the sharp remainder. The proof treats guided and continuum channels together in the edge trace and requires neither a guided metric graph nor a lower-departure estimate uniform at zero tangential momentum.
papers.comments: 27 pages. The AI system GPT-6 Astra was used in preparing this manuscript; see the disclosure on the first page

papers.title: Rigidity of shrinking Ricci solitons with low-dimensional focal sets
authors: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horácio
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the focal set of the potential function of a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, and that every complete five-dimensional gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is rigid. The first result follows from a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the focal set. For the second, when the scalar curvature is twice the soliton constant, we prove that total geodesy implies rigidity through an integral identity on the level hypersurfaces; the case of scalar curvature three times the soliton constant is treated by a separate argument. As further applications, we combine our methods with the rigidity theorem in the recent preprint of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou to obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension when the scalar curvature is twice or three times the soliton constant, and under integral Weyl pinching for four-dimensional focal sets.

papers.title: k-uniform l-Eulerian hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We consider $l$-Euler trails and $l$-Euler circuits in finite $k$-uniform directed multihypergraphs, where $k\geq 2$ and $1\leq l<k$. Let $D$ be such a directed multihypergraph. The notions of $l$-connectivity and $l$-balance are defined in terms of the $l$-tails and $l$-heads of its hyperarcs. It is shown that $D$ is $l$-Eulerian if and only if $D$ is $l$-connected and $l$-balanced. Moreover, $D$ is $l$-semi-Eulerian if and only if $D$ is $l$-connected and has exactly two states with unequal $l$-indegrees and $l$-outdegrees, one with $l$-outdegree one greater than its $l$-indegree and the other with $l$-indegree one greater than its $l$-outdegree. The proofs are based on an $l$-transition digraph and the classical Euler theorem for directed multigraphs. The corresponding conditions for $k$-uniform multihypergraphs are also obtained in terms of their orientations. For a given orientation, an expected linear-time algorithm is provided to determine whether an $l$-Euler trail or an $l$-Euler circuit exists and to construct one when it does.

papers.title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
papers.abstract: Kaczmarz-type methods often converge slowly when the coefficient matrix is ill-conditioned. In particular, when the smallest singular value is small, every row of the coefficient matrix is nearly orthogonal to the corresponding right singular direction, so that the iteration stalls along that direction. To break this slow-convergence regime, we borrow the delayed-step-size idea of the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) method and, within the framework of the residual-based surrogate-hyperplane Kaczmarz method, propose two new step sizes for gradient-descent-type methods solving linear systems: a delayed residual step size \(α_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\) and a residual-difference step size \(α_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\), which correspond, respectively, to the BB1 and BB2 step sizes in convex quadratic optimization. We prove that \(α_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\leα_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\), and we analyze the convergence of the resulting method in a canonical model with two singular values: although the step sizes are non-monotone, the residual norm is shown to decrease after finitely many steps. Numerical experiments on some ill-conditioned linear systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Bilinear maximal functions associated with some degenerate surfaces on the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: Motivated by the works of Lee--Shuin and Borges--Foster on the Euclidean space, in this article we consider bilinear averages on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ corresponding to some degenerate surfaces associated with the Korányi norm as well as Nevo--Thangavelu type averaging structures, and study the boundedness of the their full and lacunary maximal functions on various $L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{q}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ spaces, for $n \geq 2$. For the full maximal functions, we obtain optimal range except possibly at the end points.

papers.title: When GL(2) cusp forms meet CM points in GSp(4)
papers.abstract: Duke's equidistribution theorem shows that the nonconstant contribution of the $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ automorphic spectrum to CM packets becomes asymptotically negligible. CM packets on the Levi base index the fibers of Bessel quotients in $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$, and the symmetric cube correspondence carries $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ cusp forms to $\mathrm{GL}(4)$. In the holomorphic setting considered here, these two constructions meet inside $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$. We prove averaged decay for the resulting class group periods over imaginary quadratic fields, expressed as averages of conditional fiber integrals. More precisely, let $f$ be a non-CM holomorphic Hecke newform with trivial central character. The mean absolute value of the associated class-group averages tends to zero along the transverse unipotent direction.

papers.title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
papers.abstract: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice, and the N!/2-conjecture holds for two-row diagrams.

papers.title: Every tournament $T$ of order at least 3 admits infinitely many $T$-irregular oriented graphs
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a fixed graph. A graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if any two distinct vertices of $G$ belong to a different number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $F$. In this paper, we settle the strong conjecture about $F$-irregular oriented graphs (Dovzhenok, Lukashenko, and Filiuta, 2026) for the case of tournaments. Specifically, we prove that for every tournament $T$ of order $n \ge 3$, there exists an infinite family of $T$-irregular oriented graphs. Our proof is constructive. For $n \ge 4$, it is based on the vertex cloning method, and the underlying graphs of the constructed $T$-irregular oriented graphs are inherently $K_n$-irregular.

papers.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
papers.abstract: Physical-layer key generation (PLKG) exploits reciprocal channel dynamics to generate symmetric keys, addressing the key distribution problem in wireless communications. However, strong temporal correlation in slow-fading environments limits fresh randomness and results in low key generation rates. Movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom through antenna repositioning, providing a new approach to addressing the limitation. This paper investigates MA-assisted PLKG over temporally correlated channels. A first-order Gauss-Markov process is utilized to characterize the temporal correlation of multipath gains. We characterize the full-sequence mutual information (MI) over temporally correlated channels. For fixed antenna positions and beamforming, we establish a finite-horizon approximation error bound that vanishes as both effective signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) increase. We derive a closed-form expression for the one-step conditional MI and adopt it as a tractable key-information metric. A nonconvex problem is formulated to jointly optimize antenna positions and per-slot beamforming under transmit-power and minimum-spacing constraints. We develop an alternating optimization algorithm, combining an exact principal-eigenvector beamforming solution with feasible SCA-based projected gradient position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the MA-assisted scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna baseline. At a high temporal correlation coefficient, position optimization achieves approximately $51\%$ higher rates than fixed antennas. Joint position and beamforming optimization provides a further $106\%$ gain over position optimization alone, demonstrating more pronounced gains under strong temporal correlation.

papers.title: Colorings breaking prescribed families of graph automorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that for every continuous action of a compact group on a discrete set, each finite-color template admits a coloring from arbitrary lists of the same size whose stabilizer is contained in a conjugate of the template stabilizer. Consequently, the ordinary and list parameters coincide whenever the ordinary parameter is finite. In particular, we answer the question of Ferrara, Flesch and Gethner negatively for finite graphs, and establish the finite case of the conjecture of Kwaśny and Stawiski whenever a distinguishing edge coloring exists. We also show that every closed locally compact permutation group with infinite motion on a countably infinite set admits continuum many inequivalent distinguishing colorings from arbitrary 2-element lists. Using compact kernels and finite bases, we extend ordinary and list equality to countable graphs with countable automorphism groups and prove that one additional list color suffices for connected locally finite graphs. Using this multiplicity and a construction fixing all vertices of infinite degree, we prove that \(D'_\ell(G)\le 2\) for every countable connected graph with infinite edge motion, settling the list infinite edge-motion conjecture of Kwaśny and Stawiski.

papers.title: Comparison Principle and Semi-Lagrangian Methods for a Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman System with Recursive Utility
papers.abstract: We consider a system of coupled first-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations arising in continuous-time heterogeneous agent models with recursive utility, a class of models that has attracted increasing attention in macroeconomics. The first part of the paper establishes a comparison principle for the system when preferences exhibit early resolution of uncertainty. A key ingredient in the proof is an ordinally equivalent transformation of the recursive utility representation. In the second part, we develop semi-Lagrangian schemes and iterative algorithms for solving the associated nonlinear discrete systems. For preferences exhibiting late resolution of uncertainty, we establish a first-order error estimate for the semi-Lagrangian approximation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods yield results consistent with those obtained using the previously developed finite difference schemes.

papers.title: Equivalent Graphical Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization
papers.abstract: Angle rigidity theory provides a theoretical basis for characterizing the geometric shape of graphs embedded in the plane under angle constraints, and establishing global convergence of angle-based network localization algorithms. The related references, however, are largely restricted to graphs generated by triangulation or bilateration ordering, which are sufficient but not necessary for angle rigidity. This paper addresses this challenge by focusing on establishing the equivalence between angle constraints and bearing constraints. The conditions for cycle compatible frameworks (with possibly non-generic configurations) to be angle fixable are provided. Moreover, it is shown for the first time that Laman graphs equivalently characterize minimally globally angle rigid graphs, implying that a Laman graph is the simplest graph that allows a generic embedding in the plane to be uniquely determined by subtended angles. As an application, a distributed algorithm for angle-based sensor network localization is proposed, which guarantees global convergence under a much milder network topology condition than those in the literature.

papers.title: The critical line for modulation invariant bilinear multipliers
papers.abstract: We prove that the bilinear multipliers with symbols singular along a nondegenerate line, in the class of Muscalu, Tao and Thiele, map $L^{p_1}(\mathbb R)\times L^{p_2}(\mathbb R)$ into $L^{2/3,\infty}(\mathbb R)$ on the whole critical line \[ \frac1{p_1}+\frac1{p_2}=\frac32,\qquad 1<p_1,p_2<2 . \] This is sharp, as no estimate into $L^{p,\infty}$ with $p<\frac23$ holds uniformly over the class. Moreover, the generalized restricted weak type estimates of the class extend, without logarithmic loss, to the open short sides of the hexagon of exponents. For the bilinear Hilbert transforms, this confirms a folklore conjecture recorded by Thiele and the author, and removes the doubly logarithmic term in their endpoint estimates. The main step is an improvement over the multi-frequency Calderón--Zygmund decompositions already present in the literature. The bad part of this version has vanishing moments of order one at the top frequencies of the trees close to each Whitney interval, and vanishing moments of logarithmic order at the frequency bins where the tops of distant trees accumulate.

papers.title: Hyperbolic scattering in the planar n-body problem
papers.abstract: For the planar $n$-body problem with homogeneous strong force potentials, given an arbitrary pair of normalized collision-free configurations $(a, b)$, we prove that for any positive energy $h$, there are infinitely many $h$-energy scattering orbits between $a$ and $b$.

papers.title: Localization MSE Analysis for Cooperative OFDM-ISAC
papers.abstract: This paper develops a receiver-specific mean-squared-error (MSE) framework for cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) localization using random orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) payloads. It captures local peak perturbations and incorrect ambiguity-peak acquisition for two classical receiver processing schemes: matched filtering (MF) and reciprocal filtering (RF). For scatterers well separated in delay, we quantify how frequency spread and interference induced by symbol-energy fluctuations affect local delay errors under MF. RF removes symbol-dependent weighting but amplifies noise for low-energy symbols. Payload-conditioned joint Gaussian delay profiles yield peak-selection probabilities, which combine with nonlinear multistatic fusion errors to approximate position MSE while accounting for network geometry. Numerical results illustrate receiver-dependent estimation errors and the benefits of frequency-dependent constellation allocation.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 3 figures, submit to IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: POD-CNF: reduced order modeling of parametrized stochastic PDEs via normalizing flows and proper orthogonal decomposition
papers.abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) learned from trusted numerical simulations enable the real-time simulation of complex physical systems, making computationally prohibitive tasks-such as uncertainty quantification and optimal control-tractable. In particular, data-driven ROMs are opening the opportunity to learn from both numerical simulations and experimental data. However, integrating these sources of information is far from straightforward. Real-world measurements often involve multiple sources of uncertainty, including non-Gaussian noise, latent heterogeneities, unknown or hidden system parameters, and multiscale phenomena occurring below the resolution of the data. Consequently, real-world data are better described by parametrized stochastic partial differential equations, for which the development of effective ROMs remains relatively unexplored. In this work, we introduce POD-CNF, a data-driven generative ROM for efficient uncertainty quantification of parametrized high-dimensional systems. The approach combines projection-based model reduction and deep generative modeling. First, Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is employed to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the solution manifold. A Conditional Normalizing Flow (CNF) is then trained to approximate the density of the reduced coefficients conditionally on the input parameters. This formulation allows the surrogate to capture complex, multimodal output distributions, going beyond standard regression-based ROMs and least-squares predictions. We assess the effectiveness of POD-CNF through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to accurately reproduce output distributions while substantially reducing computational costs. Finally, a proof-of-concept application illustrates how the generative paradigm facilitates integration into Bayesian inverse problems, highlighting promising directions for future research.

papers.title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
papers.abstract: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates. Tensor-compatible similarity identifies the $G_2^{(1)}$ energy at level $l$ with one third of the pullback of the $D_4^{(3)}$ energy at level $3l$, yielding the same coordinate formula. The formula has no explicit level dependence, respects natural coordinate-set inclusions between levels, and allows direct evaluation without the combinatorial $R$-matrix or crystal-graph traversal.

papers.title: Quasiconvexity and Lower Semicontinuity in the Riemannian Setting
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of quasiconvexity for integrands defined on the bundle of linear maps between the tangent spaces of two smooth, connected and complete Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ and $(N,h)$, naturally extending the classical Euclidean notion. For continuous integrands, we prove that this Riemannian quasiconvexity is equivalent to the sequential lower semicontinuity of the associated functional $$ F(u,Ω)=\int_Ωf(du)\,dμ_g $$ with respect to the weak$^*$ convergence in $W^{1,\infty}(Ω,N)$, in the intrinsic sense adopted in the paper, for every bounded open subset $Ω\subseteq M$. We then establish the Riemannian analogues of the Acerbi--Fusco theorems for Carathéodory integrands satisfying the corresponding growth conditions, for every $1\leqslant p\leqslant+\infty$, with respect to the weak and weak$^*$ notions of convergence considered here.

papers.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
papers.abstract: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,α,β,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{λ_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $α/N$ and $β/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}χ_λ(x)\,Δ^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^β(x_a-p)^α\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.

papers.title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
papers.abstract: Convection-diffusion equations are fundamental models for transport phenomena, but their numerical solution becomes challenging in convection-dominated regimes due to steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. This motivates the development of accurate approaches capable of effectively resolving such features while avoiding costly iterative optimization. In this study, a modified ELM framework based on shifted Legendre polynomials is developed for convection-diffusion equations in steady-state, continuous-time, and discrete-time formulations.
