In this paper, we propose a Deep Neural Network with Nonsmooth Regularization (DNN-NSR) framework to address this issue by incorporating two complementary structural priors: sparsity of intermediate representations and low-rankness of layer-wise weight matrices. Specifically, the $\ell_1$-norm of hidden representations promotes sparse latent features, while the nuclear norm of weight matrices encourages low-rank layer-wise transformations. To optimize the resulting nonsmooth and nonconvex objective, we develop an extrapolated proximal gradient algorithm that employs soft-thresholding and singular-value thresholding to handle the two regularization terms, respectively. We further introduce a gradual regularization strategy that progressively increases the influence of these structural penalties during training. Under suitable assumptions, we establish convergence properties of the proposed algorithm toward a critical point of the training objective. The effectiveness of DNN-NSR is evaluated through extensive experiments on synthetic matrix recovery, single-image inpainting, and recommender systems using the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets. Comparisons with representative linear and nonlinear matrix completion methods demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to improve recovery performance by jointly exploiting sparse latent representations and low-rank network transformations.

papers.title: Koopman Regularization and Independent Koopman Eigenfunction Approximation
papers.abstract: The geometry induced from a dynamical system dictates its latent structures, conservation laws, and intrinsic coordinates. This paper provides two procedures to extract the governing equations of a dynamical system from its samples, \acf{KR} and \acf{IKEA}. These procedures leverage the prior knowledge from the Koopman Eigenfunction Space. Both techniques extract a functionally independent set of Koopman Eigenfunctions, which are the intrinsic coordinates. Consequently, despite its finite cardinality, the governing equations are immaculately restored. Thus, the principle of parsimony is implemented. Samples can be taken either from a vector field or from orbits of the system. \acs{KR} extracts the governing law from samples of the vector field, and \acs{IKEA} extracts it from samples of trajectories of the system. Both algorithms are based on constrained optimization methods for learning the governing equations from sparse and corrupted samples of the vector field or trajectories. These procedures yield promising results in denoising, generalization, and dimensionality reduction and achieve better results than \acs{DMD}, \acs{EDMD}, \acs{PINN}, and \acs{SINDy} in dynamical system restoration.

papers.title: Theoretical Guarantees for the Subspace-Constrained Tyler's Estimator
papers.abstract: We study the subspace-constrained Tyler's estimator (STE) for recovering a low-dimensional linear subspace from data contaminated by outliers. Under deterministic conditions on inlier spread and outlier alignment, we prove linear convergence to the true subspace from a sufficiently accurate initialization. The guarantee also applies when the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio is below one, where general robust subspace recovery is SSE-hard. When initializing STE from a candidate subspace, we provide a sufficient recovery condition based on the initial angular error and the size of the identity shift applied to the subspace projector. For noisy inliers, we prove a subspace error proportional to the noise level within an explicit iteration bound. Finally, under an asymptotic, anisotropic Gaussian inlier--outlier model, we show that Tyler's M-estimator (TME) provides a successful STE initialization even when TME's own leading eigenspace differs from the target subspace.

papers.title: Oscillatory free boundary problems in heterogeneous media
papers.abstract: We investigate a class of free boundary problems with oscillatory singularities within heterogeneous media. Our main result yields sharp regularity estimates along the free boundary, provided the power of the singularity varies in a Dini-continuous fashion below a certain threshold. We also reveal an interesting repelling estimate preventing the free boundary from touching the region where the singularity power oscillates above the threshold.
papers.comments: To appear in the J. London Math. Soc

papers.title: Quasi-$F^e$-splittings and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of quasi-$F^e$-splittings, quasi-$F$-regularity, and quasi-$+$-regularity.
papers.comments: 90 pages. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2208.08016 ver2:Several proofs and statements have been revised and the exposition improved. The main results remain unchanged

papers.title: The rigidity of Doyle circle packings on the infinite hexagonal triangulation
papers.abstract: Peter Doyle conjectured that locally univalent circle packings on the hexagonal lattice only consist of regular hexagonal packings and Doyle spirals, which is called the Doyle conjecture. In this paper, we prove a rigidity theorem for Doyle spirals in the class of infinite circle packings on the hexagonal lattice whose radii ratios of adjacent circles have a uniform lower bound in one fixed lattice direction. This gives a partial answer to the Doyle conjecture. Based on a new observation that the logarithm of the radii ratio of adjacent circles is a weighted discrete harmonic function, we prove the result via the Liouville theorem for discrete harmonic functions. Moreover, we establish a Ring Lemma for locally univalent circle packings with bounded degree, assuming that their carrier surfaces are the universal covers of $\mathbb{C}-\{0\}$, and the visual angles of all circles viewed from the origin are uniformly bounded away from $π$. This provides a new geometric sufficient condition for the rigidity of Doyle spirals.
papers.comments: 24 pages,9 figures. In the second version, we add a new rigidity theorem for locally univalent circle packings when the distributional property of their carrier surfaces are assumed

papers.title: Veronese sections and interlacing matrices of polynomials and formal power series
papers.abstract: The concept of a fully interlacing matrix of formal power series with real coefficients is introduced. This concept extends and strengthens that of an interlacing sequence of real-rooted polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, in the special case of row and column matrices. The fully interlacing property is shown to be preserved under matrix products, flips across the reverse diagonal and Veronese sections of the power series involved. These results and their corollaries generalize, unify and simplify several results which have previously appeared in the literature. An application to the theory of uniform triangulations of simplicial complexes is included.
papers.comments: Final version (19 pages), to appear in the Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society

papers.title: On the Stieltjes Approximation Error to the Logarithmic Integral
papers.abstract: We study the approximation errors \[ \varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{li}_{*}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \varepsilon_{0}(x)=\operatorname{li}_{0}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x), \] arising from the classical Stieltjes--van Boven and pure Stieltjes asymptotic expansions of the logarithmic integral, respectively. Our analysis is based on the discrete values \(\varepsilon_k=\varepsilon(e^k)\) and their increments \(Δ_{k+1}=\varepsilon_{k}-\varepsilon_{k+1}\), for which we derive new unconditional analytic bounds. Using precise integral representations of the increments and sharp upper and lower estimates for the associated kernel integrals, we obtain explicit bounds for \(\varepsilon_k\), valid for every integer \(k\geq 1\). These bounds yield corresponding estimates for \(\varepsilon(x)\) for all real \(x\geq e\). In particular, we prove that for every real $x \ge e$, \[\varepsilon(x) =\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{\frac{2π}{\log x}} + O\left(\frac{1}{\log x}\right), \qquad\qquad x \to \infty.\] We then use these results to demonstrate that for all real number $x \ge e$ \[|\varepsilon_{0}(x)| = \frac{\sqrt{2π}\left|\frac13-α\right|}{\sqrt{\log x}} + O\left(\frac{1}{\log x}\right), \qquad\qquad x\to\infty\] where $n=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ and $α=\log x-n$. This provides an explicit asymptotic description of the absolute approximation error associated with the pure Stieltjes expansion, including its dependence on the fractional part of \(\log x\).
papers.comments: Substantially revised and expanded version of arXiv:2406.12152v2. The presentation and proofs have been reorganized, and the main results strengthened. We establish positivity and monotonicity of the Stieltjes-van Boven approximation error, prove the asymptotic behavior conjectured in the previous version, and analyze the pure Stieltjes approximation. 33 pages

papers.title: Embedding a Quantum Rank Two Quadric in a Quantum $\mathbb{P}^3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify connected graded quadratic Artin-Schelter regular (AS-regular, henceforth) algebras of global dimension four that have a Hilbert series the same as that of the polynomial ring on four generators and that map onto a twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-two quadric. A twisted homogeneous coordinate ring is a construction that was defined by Artin, Tate, and Van den Bergh in \cite{ATV1, ATV2, AVdB1990} in the context of the classification of AS-regular algebras of global dimension three. In \cite{SV99,VVr}, the authors classified AS-regular algebras of global dimension four that map onto the twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-three and a rank-four quadric, respectively. We expand on their work to include the case of coordinate rings of a rank-two quadric.
papers.comments: This revision addresses concerns about whether the the map tau defined on the rank-two quadric lifts to P^3

papers.title: Algebraically trivial automorphisms of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract: Given an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS) manifold $X$, we call an automorphism $f$ of $X$ algebraically trivial if $f$ acts trivially on the Néron--Severi group of $X$. In this paper, we extend the approach of Brandhorst--Cattaneo to classify, by means of lattice data, all the pairs $(X, G)$, where $X$ is an IHS manifold of a known deformation type (to this date), and $G$ is a finite group consisting of algebraically trivial automorphisms of $X$ that are nonsymplectic. In particular, we classify even-order algebraically trivial nonsymplectic automorphisms, with or without trivial discriminant action. In the case of nontrivial discriminant actions, we show that such automorphisms only exist for finitely many deformation types and orders
papers.comments: 57 pages, 5 tables. Final version incorporating referees' comments - published in EpiGA
papers.journal_ref: Épijournal de Géométrie Algébrique, volume 10 (2026), article no. 20

papers.title: Sliced Wasserstein Geodesics and Equivalence Wasserstein and Sliced Wasserstein metrics
papers.abstract: This paper will introduce a family of sliced Wasserstein geodesics which are not standard Wasserstein geodesics, objects yet to be discovered in the literature. These objects exhibit how the geometric structure of the Sliced Wasserstein space differs from the Wasserstein space, and provides a simple example of how solving the barycenter and gradient flow problems change when moving between these metrics. Some of these geodesics will only be Hölder continuous with respect to the Wasserstein metric and thus will provide a direct proof that Sliced-Wasserstein and regular Wasserstein metrics are not equivalent. Previous proofs of this were done for various cases in [2] and [5]. This paper, not only provides a direct proof, but also fills in gaps showing these metrics not equivalent in dimensions greater than 2.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 2 figures, 4 page abstract, preprint. This is a more detailed version of the first version including an appendix on the infinity sliced Wasserstein distance and some reference to recent works

papers.title: Igusa Stacks and the Cohomology of Shimura Varieties
papers.abstract: We construct functorial Igusa stacks for all Hodge-type Shimura varieties, proving a conjecture of Scholze and extending earlier results of the fourth-named author for PEL-type Shimura varieties. Using the Igusa stack, we construct a sheaf on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ that controls the cohomology of the corresponding Shimura variety. We use this sheaf and the spectral action of Fargues-Scholze to prove a compatibility between the cohomology of Shimura varieties of Hodge type and the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Fargues-Scholze, generalizing the Eichler-Shimura relation of Blasius-Rogawski to arbitrary level at $p$. When the given Shimura variety is proper, we show moreover that the sheaf is perverse, which allows us to prove new torsion vanishing results for the cohomology of Shimura varieties.
papers.comments: Final version, to appear in Inventiones mathematicae

papers.title: Building blocks for $W$-algebras of classical types
papers.abstract: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,3,4,\dots)$ serves as a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$ in the sense that under mild hypothesis, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $W_{\infty}$. There is an $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ family of such $1$-parameter vertex algebras which, after tensoring with a Heisenberg algebra, are known as $Y$-algebras. They were introduced by Gaiotto and Rapčák and are expected to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras in type $A$, i.e., every $W$-(super) algebra in type $A$ is an extension of a tensor product of finitely many $Y$-algebras. Similarly, the orthosymplectic $Y$-algebras are $1$-parameter quotients of a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,4,6,\dots)$, which is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,4,\dots, 2N)$ for some $N$. Unlike type $A$, these algebras are not all the building blocks for $W$-algebras of types $B$, $C$, and $D$. In this paper, we construct a new universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra of type $W(1^3, 2, 3^3, 4, 5^3,6,\dots)$ which we denote by $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ since it contains a copy of the affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak{sp}_2)$. We identify $8$ infinite families of $1$-parameter quotients of $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ which are analogues of the $Y$-algebras. We regard $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ as a fundamental object on equal footing with $W_{\infty}$ and $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$, and we give some heuristic reasons for why we expect the $1$-parameter quotients of these three objects to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras of classical types. Finally, we prove that $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ has many quotients which are strongly rational. This yields new examples of strongly rational $W$-superalgebras.
papers.comments: Minor corrections and improvements, references updated, final version to appear in Forum of Math Sigma

papers.title: Automorphic form twisted Shintani zeta functions over number fields
papers.abstract: Automorphic twists of Shintani zeta functions encode spectral information about binary cubic forms and the shapes of cubic rings. We study their adelic integrals over an arbitrary number field, allowing ramified data, nonspherical vectors, and arbitrary unitary central character. For cuspidal twists the zeta function is meromorphic on the whole plane and holomorphic for $\Re s>1/4$.

papers.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
papers.abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.
papers.comments: 15 pages; now proves completeness of the diameter-six classification; also adds nonlinearity results, and updates discussion and references

papers.title: Second order regularity of solutions of elliptic equations in divergence form with Sobolev coefficients
papers.abstract:
We give $L^p$ estimates for the second derivatives of weak solutions to the Dirichlet problem for equation $\operatorname{div}(\mathbf{A}
abla u) = f$ in $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with Sobolev coefficients. In particular, for $f\in L^2(Ω)  igcap L^s(Ω)$ $$\|Δu\|_{2} \leq  egin{cases} c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|
abla \mathbf{A}\|_q^2\|f\|_s, & 	ext{if } 1 < s < d/2,  rac{1}{2}= rac{2}{q}+  rac{1}{s} -  rac{2}{d}\ c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|

papers.title: Rubik's as Galois': the inverse Galois problem for the Rubik's Cube group
papers.abstract: We prove that the Rubik's cube group can be realized as a Galois group over the rationals.

papers.title: Neural numerical homogenization based on Deep Ritz corrections
papers.abstract: Numerical homogenization methods aim at providing appropriate coarse-scale approximations of solutions to (elliptic) partial differential equations that involve highly oscillatory coefficients. The localized orthogonal decomposition (LOD) method is an effective way of dealing with such coefficients, especially if they are non-periodic and non-smooth. It modifies classical finite element basis functions by suitable fine-scale corrections. In this paper, we make use of the structure of the LOD method, but we propose to calculate the corrections based on a Deep Ritz approach involving a parametrization of the coefficients to tackle temporal variations or uncertainties. Numerical examples for a parabolic model problem are presented to assess the performance of the approach.

papers.title: On compact almost automorphic functions: new characterizations, invariance under convolution products and applications
papers.abstract: Let \(\mathcal{G}\) be a non-empty subset of the Euclidean space \(\mathbb{R}^m\) (\(m \geq 1\)). This work is dedicated to further investigating the properties of \(\mathcal{G}\)-multi-almost automorphic functions defined on \(\mathbb{R}^m\) with values in a Banach space \(\X\). Using the theory of \(\mathcal{G}\)-multi-almost automorphic functions, we provide two new characterizations of compact almost automorphic functions. In the first characterization, \(\mathcal{G}\) corresponds to the lattice subgroup \(\mathbb{Z}^m \subset \mathbb{R}^m\), while in the second, \(\mathcal{G}\) is taken to be a dense subset of \(\mathbb{R}^m\). Furthermore, we establish the invariance of the space of bounded and compactly \(\mathcal{G}\)-multi-almost automorphic functions under integral operators with Bi-almost automorphic kernels. Finally, we apply these results to the analysis of the almost automorphic dynamics of Poisson's and heat equations. Specifically, we prove the persistence of compact almost automorphic properties in solutions to these equations assumming that the source or initial data, respectively, is \( \mathcal{G} \)-multi-almost automorphic, where \( \mathcal{G} \) is either the lattice subgroup \( \mathbb{Z}^m \) or a dense subset (subgroup) of \( \mathbb{R}^m \).

papers.title: A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras
papers.abstract: Let $(X,d)$ be a uniformly locally finite metric space, and $T$ an operator in the uniform Roe algebra $C_u^*(X)$ (or uniform quasi-local algebra $C_{ql}^*(X)$). In this paper, we introduce the concept of limit operators of $T$ on galaxies in the nonstandard extension of $X$, and prove that $T$ is a generalized Fredholm operator with respect to the ghost ideal in $C_u^*(X)$ (or $C_{ql}^*(X)$) if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible, and their inverses are uniformly bounded. In particular, if $X$ has Yu's Property A, then $T$ is a Fredholm operator if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible. Using techniques in nonstandard analysis, our result strengthens a work of Špakula--Willett \cite{SpW} on the characterization of Fredholmness by using less limit operators.
papers.comments: This is the accepted version of the following article: Guo, L., Qian, J. and Wang, Q. (2026), A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras. Bull. London Math. Soc., 58: e70534, which has been published in final form at https://doi.org/10.1112/blms.70534. A minor error in the previous version is pointed out by the referee and is corrected (see Remark 1)
papers.journal_ref: Guo, L., Qian, J. and Wang, Q. (2026), A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras. Bull. London Math. Soc., 58: e70534

papers.title: Additive processes on the real line and Loewner chains
papers.abstract: This paper investigates additive processes with respect to several different independences in non-commutative probability in terms of the convolution hemigroups of the distributions of the increments of the processes. In particular, we focus on the relation of monotone convolution hemigroups and Loewner chains, a special kind of family of conformal mappings, on the upper half-plane. Generalizing the celebrated Loewner differential equation, we formulate an integral equation and the concept of ``generator'' for any Loewner chain of reciprocal Cauchy transforms. This generalization enables us to remove the assumption of the absolute continuity of Loewner chains which had been imposed in the literature. The locally uniform convergence of Loewner chains is then equivalent to a suitable convergence of generators. Using generators, we define homeomorphisms between the aforementioned class of Loewner chains, the set of monotone convolution hemigroups, and the set of classical convolution hemigroups on the real line. We also discuss similar homeomorphisms to free, boolean and anti-monotone convolution hemigroups on the real line.
papers.comments: (v1) 67 pages. (v2) 70 pages. Some arguments in Section 4.3 have been changed, and some contents from our another manuscript (arXiv:2301.04361) have been incorporated. (v3) 85 pages. The general case has been added, in which the assumption of finite second moment is removed. (v4) 85 pages. Minor corrections. (v5) only some corrections of typos. To appear in ALEA Lat. Am. J. Probab. Math. Stat

papers.title: On curious properties of the general size-biased distribution
papers.abstract: We offer further results on a general size-biased distribution related to the Riemann xi-function we presented in [9] using the work of Ferrar. Curious properties associated with its expected value are presented, which are related to special functional equations. We also relate our observations to some recent developments related to the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Family Seiberg-Witten equation on Kahler surface and $π_i(\Symp)$ on multiple-point blow ups of Calabi-Yau surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $ω$ be a Kahler form on $M$, which is a torus $T^4$, a $K3$ surface or an Enriques surface, let $M\#n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ be $n-$point Kahler blowup of $M$. Suppose that $κ=[ω]$ satisfies certain irrationality condition. Applying techniques related to deformation of complex objects, we extend the guage-theoretic invariant on closed Kahler suraces developed by Kronheimer\cite{Kronheimer1998} and Smirnov\cite{Smirnov2022}\cite{Smirnov2023}. As a result, we show that even dimensional higher homotopy groups of $\Symp(M\#n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2},ω)$ are infinitely generated.

papers.title: Structures preserved by primitive actions of $S_ω$
papers.abstract: We present a dichotomy for structures $A$ that are preserved by primitive actions of $S_ω = \text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$: such a structure primitively positively constructs all finite structures and the constraint satisfaction problem is NP-complete, or the constraint satisfaction problem for $A$ is in P. To prove our result, we study the first-order reducts of the Johnson graph $J(k)$, for $k \geq 2$, whose automorphism group $G$ equals the action of $\text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$ on the set $V$ of $k$-element subsets of $\mathbb N$. We use the fact that $J(k)$ has a finitely bounded homogeneous Ramsey expansion and that $G$ is a maximal closed subgroup of $\text{Sym}(V)$.
papers.comments: 34 pages plus references; accepted for publication in LMCS

papers.title: Learning to Select Between LP and SDP Relaxations for Nonconvex Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Programs
papers.abstract: Quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQPs) are ubiquitous in optimization: Such problems arise in applications from operations research, power systems, signal processing, chemical engineering, and portfolio theory, among others. Despite their flexibility in modeling real-life situations and the recent effort to understand their properties, nonconvex QCQPs are hard to solve in practice. Most of the approaches in the literature are based on either Linear Programming (LP) or Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations, each of which works very well for some problem subclasses but perform poorly on others. In this paper, we develop a relaxation selection procedure for nonconvex QCQPs that can adaptively decide whether an LP- or SDP-based approach is expected to be more beneficial by considering the instance structure. The proposed methodology relies on utilizing machine learning methods that involve features derived from spectral properties and sparsity patterns of data matrices, and once trained appropriately within a dimension-independent setup, the prediction model applies to any instance with an arbitrary number of variables and constraints. We develop classification and regression models under different feature-design setups, including a dimension-independent representation, and evaluate them on synthetically generated instances and a combined benchmark dataset consisting of MINLPLib and QPLIB instances. We further investigate relaxation selection within a spatial branch-and-bound framework, evaluating the trade-off between lower bound quality and computational time.

papers.title: Black holes in the Dynnikov Coordinate Plane
papers.abstract: This work gives an application of Dynnikov coordinates in geometric group theory. We present a new approach to the study of subgroups of the mapping class group of a disc with $3$ marked points, $\mathbb{D}_3$, using Dynnikov coordinates.

papers.title: Private Minimum Hellinger Distance Estimation via Hellinger Distance Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Objective functions based on Hellinger distance yield robust and efficient estimators of model parameters. Motivated by privacy and regulatory requirements encountered in contemporary applications, we derive in this paper \emph{private minimum Hellinger distance estimators}. The estimators satisfy a new privacy constraint, namely, Hellinger differential privacy, while retaining the robustness and efficiency properties. We demonstrate that Hellinger differential privacy shares several features of standard differential privacy while allowing for sharper inference. Additionally, for computational purposes, we also develop Hellinger differentially private gradient descent and Newton-Raphson algorithms. We illustrate the behavior of our estimators in finite samples using numerical experiments and verify that they retain robustness properties under gross-error contamination.

papers.title: Étude statistique du facteur premier médian, 1 : valeur moyenne
papers.abstract: We establish an asymptotic formula for the mean value of the logarithm of the middle prime factor of an integer, defined with or without multiplicity, with a relative error of size a negative power of $\log x$, thus refining and generalising a recent result of McNew, Pollack, and Singha Roy.

papers.title: A SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method for expectation-constrained nonconvex nonsmooth optimization
papers.abstract: Many real-world problems, such as those with fairness constraints, involve complex expectation constraints and large datasets, necessitating the design of efficient stochastic methods to solve them. Most existing research focuses on cases with no {constraint} or easy-to-project constraints or deterministic constraints. In this paper, we consider nonconvex nonsmooth stochastic optimization problems with expectation constraints, for which we build a novel exact penalty model. We first show the relationship between the penalty model and the original problem. Then on solving the penalty problem, we present a single-loop SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method, which utilizes the subgradients of both the objective and constraint functions, as well as the constraint function value at each iteration. Under certain regularity conditions (weaker than Slater-type constraint qualification or strong feasibility assumed in existing works), we establish an iteration complexity result of $O(ε^{-4})$ to reach a near-$ε$ stationary point of the penalized problem in expectation, matching the lower bound for such tasks. Building on the exact penalization, an $(ε,ε)$-KKT point of the original problem is obtained. For a few scenarios, our complexity of either the {objective} sample subgradient or the constraint sample function values can be lower than the state-of-the-art results by a factor of $ε^{-2}$. Moreover, on solving two fairness-constrained problems and a multi-class Neyman-Pearson classification problem, our method is significantly (up to 466 times) faster than the state-of-the-art algorithms, including switching subgradient method and inexact proximal point methods.

papers.title: Expressing a difference between two Hurwitz zeta functions in terms of the Gauss hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: In the paper, the author expresses the difference $2^m[ζ(-m,λz)-ζ(-m,λz+μ)]$ for $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $\Re(z)>0$ with $λ,μ>0$ in terms of the functions $Γ(j+1){\,}_2F_1(-j,-z;1;2)$ for $0\le j\le m$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$ in the form of matrix equations, where $Γ(z)$, $ζ(z,α)$, and ${}_2F_1(a,b;c;z)$ stand for the classical Euler gamma function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Gauss hypergeometric function, respectively. The case of non-integer $t$ in $2^t[ζ(-t,λz)-ζ(-t,λz+μ)]$ is left open. The coefficients are characterized by matrix formulas and by an explicit recursion; closed-form expressions for them are not obtained. This problem originates from the Landau level quantization in solid state materials.

papers.title: Normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schrödinger equation with mixed dispersion and Sobolev critical growth
papers.abstract: This paper investigates normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schrödinger equation with mixed dispersion and combined nonlinearities involving a lower-power perturbation and a Sobolev critical term. Under a suitable smallness condition on the prescribed mass and in the range \(2<p<2+\frac{4}{N}\), we establish the existence of a local minimizer of the associated energy functional on \(S_r(c)\) and infinitely many pairs of radial normalized solutions by combining the truncation technique, the concentration-compactness principle and genus theory. In particular, our results extend those of Alves et al. (Anal. Appl., (2025), doi: 10.1142/S0219530525500447) by removing the additional assumptions imposed in their work. In the range \(2+\frac{8}{N}<p<4^*\), we prove the existence of bounded radial constrained Palais-Smale sequences at mountain pass levels below the critical Sobolev threshold for sufficiently large \(μ\). We further show that their nonzero weak limits are radial weak solutions, with strong convergence in the derivative norms and in the critical Lebesgue norm. Moreover, under an additional condition \((N)\) ensuring the strict negativity of the limiting Lagrange multiplier, the weak limit preserves the prescribed \(L^2\)-mass, and the Palais-Smale sequence converges strongly in \(H^2(\mathbb R^N)\). These results extend the previous studies of Chang et al. (arXiv preprint, (2023), arXiv: 2305.00327v1) and Bonheure et al. (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., (2019), doi:10.1090/tran/7769).

papers.title: Satisfying sequences for rainbow partite matchings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal F_1,\ldots, \mathcal F_s\subset [n]^k$ be a collection of $s$ families. In this paper, we address the following question: for which sequences $f_1,\ldots, f_s$ do the conditions $|\mathcal F_i|>f_i$ imply that the families contain a rainbow matching, that is, there are pairwise disjoint $F_1\in \mathcal F_1,\ldots, F_s\in \mathcal F_s$? We call such sequences {\em satisfying}. Kiselev and the first author showed that $f_1 = \ldots = f_s=(s-1)n^{k-1}$ is satisfying for $s>470$, verifying the conjecture by Aharoni and Howard. This is the best possible if we insist that the families are of the same size. However, it turns out that much more can be said about asymmetric restrictions. In this paper, we investigate this question in several regimes and in particular answer the questions asked by Kiselev and Kupavskii. We use a variety of methods, including concentration and anticoncentration results, spread approximations, and the Combinatorial Nullstellenzatz.

papers.title: Demystifying 5G Polar and LDPC Codes: A Comprehensive Review and Foundations
papers.abstract: Understanding how 5G networks correct errors is no trivial matter. At the heart of the process lie two sophisticated families of codes: LDPC and polar codes. This paper opens the black box, not only by explaining how these codes are designed, but also by showing how they are encoded and decoded in practice. To describe the research covered in this review, we present a detailed survey of the literature supplemented with insights that are often buried deep within technical standards. These foundations are not just historical footnotes: they remain relevant to research on error correction for future wireless systems. In bringing clarity to these building blocks, we aim to help engineers and researchers navigate what is both a complex and increasingly vital part of wireless communication.

papers.title: Horizontality of partially hyperbolic foliations
papers.abstract: We show exactly which Seifert manifolds support partially hyperbolic dynamical systems. In particular, a circle bundle over a higher-genus surface supports a partially hyperbolic system if and only if it supports an Anosov flow. We also show for these systems that the center-stable and center-unstable foliations can be isotoped so that their leaves are transverse to the circle fibering. As a consequence, every partially hyperbolic system defined on the unit tangent bundle of a higher-genus surface is a collapsed Anosov flow.

papers.title: Smoothing effect for third order operators with variable coefficients
papers.abstract: In this work we study the smoothing effect of some variable coefficient operators of the form $D_t-A$, where $A$ is a Weyl-quantized pseudo-differential operator of order $m=2,3$. The class under consideration includes, among others, KdV-type and ultrahyperbolic Schrödinger operators. We prove homogeneous and inhomogeneous smoothing estimates and use them to get well-posedness results for some NLIVPs with derivative nonlinearities. Finally, we investigate the so called non-trapping property of the bicharacteristic curves of the principal symbol of our operators.

papers.title: On a polygon version of Wiegmann-Zabrodin formula
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a convex polygon in ${\mathbb C}$ and let $Δ_{D, P}$ be the operator of the Dirichlet boundary value problem for the Lapalcian $Δ=-4\partial_z\partial_{\bar z}$ in $P$. We derive a variational formula for the logarithm of the $ζ$-regularized determinant of $Δ_{D, P}$ for arbitrary infinitesimal deformations of the polygon $P$ in the class of polygons (with the same number of vertices). For a simply connected domain with smooth boundary such a formula was recently discovered by Wiegmann and Zabrodin as a non obvious corollary of the Alvarez variational formula, for domains with corners this approach is unavailable (at least for those deformations that do not preserve the corner angles) and we have to develop another one.
papers.comments: Formula (4) is improved (one term was lost in the previous versions). Its proof underwent minor changes

papers.title: Atomic decomposition of Bergman-Orlicz space on the upper complex half-plane
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose an atomic decomposition of the Bergman-Orlicz spaces on the complex upper half-plane. Using this result, we characterize Carleson embeddings with loss between Bergman-Orlicz spaces and certain Orlicz spaces. We also leverage this last result to control the composition operator between two Bergman-Orlicz spaces.

papers.title: Certain Representation of the Rationals With Bounded Partial Quotients
papers.abstract: We define a new representation for a subset of rational numbers and prove that each real number \( x \notin (-1,1) \) can be approximated arbitrarily well by rational numbers which have only \( 2 \)'s and \( 1 \)'s in their representation.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Weiss classes and a rational decomposition of spaces of homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We construct a rational homotopy pullback decomposition for variants of the classifying space of the group of homeomorphisms for a large class of manifolds. This has various applications, including a rational section of the stabilisation map ${\rm Top}(d)\rightarrow {\rm Top}$ of the space of homeomorphisms of ${\bf R}^d$ for $d\ge 6$, or a new method to construct topological bundles and detect characteristic classes thereof. Some steps in the proofs may be of independent interest, such as the construction of a nullhomotopy of the twice-iterated stabilisation map for the space of orientation-preserving derived automorphisms of the rational $E_d$-operad, results on recovering boundaries of manifolds from their interior in the context of embedding calculus, or a treatment of tensor products of truncated $\infty$-operads.
papers.comments: 62 pages, 2 figures, to appear in Duke Mathematical Journal

papers.title: A stochastic epidemic model with memory of the last infection and waning immunity
papers.abstract: We adapt the article of Forien, Pang, Pardoux and Zotsa, on epidemic models with varying infectivity and waning immunity, to incorporate the memory of the last infection. To this end, we introduce a parametric approach and consider a piecewise deterministic Markov process modeling both the evolution of the parameter, also called the trait, and the age of infection of individuals over time. At each new infection, a new trait is randomly chosen for the infected individual according to a Markov kernel, and their age is reset to zero. In the large population limit, we derive a partial differential equation (PDE) that describes the density of traits and ages. The main goal is to study the conditions under which endemic equilibria exist for the deterministic PDE model and to establish an endemicity threshold that depends on the model parameters. The local stability of these equilibria is also analyzed. The endemicity threshold is computed for several examples, including models that incorporate a vaccination policy, and a local stability result is obtained for a memory-free SIS-type model.
papers.comments: Stochastic epidemic model with memory; age-structured model; varying infectivity; varying immunity/susceptibility; endemicity; local stability

papers.title: On the number of components of twisted torus links
papers.abstract: Twisted torus links $T(p,q;r,s)$ generalize torus links by introducing $s$ additional twists on $r$ adjacent strands of the torus link $T(p,q)$. It is well known that the number of components of a torus link $T(p,q)$ is given by the greatest common divisor of $p$ and $q$. However, the number of components of a twisted torus link cannot be determined as straightforwardly from its parameters. In this work, we present a Euclidean algorithm-like procedure for computing the number of components of twisted torus links from their parameters. As a result, we show that the number of components of a twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a multiple of $\gcd(p,q,r,s)$, and in particular, $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot only if $\gcd(p,q,r,s)=1$. We also use our algorithm to determine the number of components for several families of twisted torus links considered in the literature.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 5 figures. Revised version incorporating referee comments and minor corrections and clarifications. Accepted for publication in the Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications

papers.title: Accelerated Gradient Methods Through Variable and Operator Splitting
papers.abstract: This survey develops a variable and operator splitting (VOS) framework for accelerated first-order methods. Operator splitting separates the components of the optimality system, while variable splitting introduces auxiliary dynamics that generate acceleration. The strong Lyapunov property guides the stability analysis, and practical schemes follow from Accelerated Over-Relaxation (AOR) and Extrapolation by Predictor--Corrector (EPC) discretizations. For merely convex problems, a perturbed VOS flow combined with homotopy in the auxiliary scale yields accelerated rates. The framework gives a common derivation and analysis of Nesterov-type, FISTA-type, composite, mirror-descent-type, and bilinear saddle-point accelerated methods. Its main contribution is structural and expository: it organizes these methods within one Lyapunov and splitting template and explains how acceleration survives different splittings and discretizations.

papers.title: Edge-vertex degree based Zagreb index and graph operations
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ consists of two parts, the vertices and edges. The vertices constitute the vertex set $V(G)$ and the edges, the edge set. An edge \( e=xy \), \( ev \)-dominates not only the vertices incident to it but also those adjacent to either \( x \) or \( y \). The edge-vertex degree of $e,$ $deg^{ev}_{G}(e),$ is the number of vertices in the $ev$-dominating set of $e$. In this article, we compute expressions for the $ev$-degree version of the Zagreb index of several unary and binary graph operations.

papers.title: Non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics of two summands
papers.abstract: We prove the non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on a class of compact manifolds arising as double disk bundles, whose principal orbits split into two inequivalent irreducible summands. The proof uses a phase space barrier argument that yields a new obstruction to the existence of closed cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, even when the principal orbits admit homogeneous Einstein metrics.
papers.comments: This submission contains the non-existence result originally part of arXiv:2405.10836v3, now split off for clarity. The artificial condition d2\geq d1 is no longer needed by the main result. The proofs in the Appendix were largely simplified. Proposition 4.10 added for an upcoming preprint

papers.title: A Learning-Based Inexact ADMM for Solving Quadratic Programs
papers.abstract: Convex quadratic programs (QPs) constitute a fundamental computational primitive across diverse domains including financial optimization, control systems, and machine learning. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) has emerged as a preferred first-order approach due to its iteration efficiency - exemplified by the state-of-the-art OSQP solver. Machine learning-enhanced optimization algorithms have recently demonstrated significant success in speeding up the solving process. This work introduces a neural-accelerated ADMM variant that replaces exact subproblem solutions with learned approximations through a parameter-efficient Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. We derive convergence guarantees within the inexact ADMM formalism, establishing that our learning-augmented method maintains primal-dual convergence while satisfying residual thresholds. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior solution accuracy compared to existing learning-based methods while delivering significant computational speedups of up to $7\times$, $28\times$, and $22\times$ over Gurobi, SCS, and OSQP, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed method outperforms other learning-to-optimize methods in terms of solution quality. Detailed performance analysis confirms near-perfect compliance with the theoretical assumptions, consequently ensuring algorithm convergence.

papers.title: Arbitrary orientations of Hamilton cycles in directed graphs of large minimum degree
papers.abstract: In 1960, Ghouila-Houri proved that every strongly connected directed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n$ contains a directed Hamilton cycle. We asymptotically generalize this result by proving the following: every directed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and with minimum degree at least $(1+o(1))n$ contains every orientation of a Hamilton cycle, except for the directed Hamilton cycle in the case when $G$ is not strongly connected. In fact, this minimum degree condition forces every orientation of a cycle in $G$ of every possible length, other than perhaps the directed cycles.
papers.comments: 20 pages (plus 5 page appendix), 3 figures. To appear in Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B

papers.title: Holomorphic disks with boundary on compact Lagrangian surface
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a compact oriented Lagrangian surface in a Kähler surface endowed with a complete Riemannian metric (compatible with the symplectic structure and the complex structure) with bounded sectional curvatures and a positive lower bound on injectivity radius. We show that for every nontrivial class $[γ]$ of the fundamental group $π_1(L)$ such that $γ$ bounds a topological disk in $M$, there exists a holomorphic disk whose boundary belongs to $L$ and is freely homotopic to $γ$ on $L$. This answers a question of Bennequin on existence of $J$-holomorphic disks. Nonexistence of exact Lagrangian embeddings of certain surfaces is established in such Kähler surface if the fundamental form is exact. In the almost Kähler setting, especially, the cotangent bundles of compact manifolds, results on nonexistence of $J$-holomorphic disks and existence of minimizers of the partial energies in the sense of A. Lichnerowicz are obtained.

papers.title: Categorification of $k$-Schur functions and refined Macdonald positivity
papers.abstract: We establish a substantial part of the categorification framework for $k$-Schur functions proposed in Chen's Ph.D.\ thesis, written under the supervision of Mark Haiman. More precisely, we realize $k$-Schur functions as the graded characters of a distinguished family of objects in a certain module category and establish module-theoretic analogues of several foundational properties of $k$-Schur functions. A final part of Chen's framework predicts a homological characterization of modules admitting filtrations by these distinguished objects; we establish this characterization under an additional combinatorial hypothesis. In addition, we unconditionally prove that modules arising in this framework admit filtrations whose subquotients are affine Demazure modules of level $k$. As a consequence, modified Macdonald polynomials expand positively in the characters of affine Demazure modules. This may be viewed as a homological refinement of Macdonald positivity, arising from an intrinsic $\mathrm{ext}$-orthogonality condition on the corresponding Garsia--Haiman modules. We also prove the combinatorial hypothesis for $m \le 2k$ in the appendix and verify it computationally for $m\leq 19$, yielding $k$-Schur positivity of modified Macdonald polynomials in these cases. Our approach builds on our previous work on the algebraic and geometric realization of Catalan symmetric functions, a class encompassing both $k$-Schur and Hall--Littlewood functions.
papers.comments: 69 pages. In v3, the full claim on the k-Schur positivity of Macdonald polynomials was withdrawn due to an error in Section 8 of v2; weaker/restricted results were recorded instead. In v4, corrected the treatment of the $\mathfrak g[z]$-action in Section 5 of v3 and made corresponding revisions. The main statements are unchanged from v3. Other minor corrections

papers.title: Orbit structures on real double flag varieties for the Siegel parabolic subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $ G $ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $ \mathbb{R} $, and $ H $ its symmetric subgroup. For parabolic subgroups $ P_{G} \subset G $ and $ P_{H} \subset H $, the product of flag varieties $ \mathfrak{X} = H/P_H \times G/P_G $ is called a double flag variety, on which $ H $ acts diagonally. Now let $G$ be either $\mathrm{U}(n,n)$ or $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{R})$. We classify the $H$-orbits on $ \mathfrak{X} $ in both cases and show that they admit exactly the same parametrization. Concretely, each orbit corresponds to a signed partial involution, which can be encoded by simple combinatorial graphs. The orbit structure reduces to several families of smaller flag varieties, and we find an intimate relation of the orbit decomposition to Matsuki duality and Matsuki-Oshima's notion of clans. We also compute the Galois cohomology of each orbit, which exhibits another classification of the orbits by explicit matrix representatives.

papers.title: On an Iterative Scheme for the Spinorial Yamabe Equation on Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract: We establish a fixed-point framework for non-linear boundary value problems for first-order elliptic operators on vector bundles, with primary application to the spinorial Yamabe and Brezis--Nirenberg equations. We prove existence and uniqueness of an $H^1$-solution under a smallness condition that is homogeneous under amplitude and operator scaling. The associated iterative scheme converges geometrically in $L^q$ and $H^1$, and the solution depends continuously on the harmonic representative of the boundary datum. Through bootstrapping, we obtain interior $C^{1,α}$-regularity and boundary smoothness under Shapiro--Lopatinski conditions. The method is extended to families of small domains via rescaling to a fixed reference domain.
papers.comments: Updated version: We now work proof our results via Fixed-Point method. We omit fractional Sobolev spaces. New results on well-posedness, specifically the stability and uniqueness of the solution, have been added. The framework has been extended other non-linear BVP, for example the spinorial Brezis--Nirenberg equation. The contraction conditions are now explicit and homogenous in the datum

papers.title: A Study of Fine Selmer Groups Over Function Fields via Greenberg Neighbourhoods
papers.abstract: Greenberg examined the local behaviour of Iwasawa invariants as functions on the set $\mathscr{E}(F)$, the set of all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of a number field $F$. Kleine later extended these ideas to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants in the context of Selmer groups of abelian varieties across different $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of $F$. Let $K$ be a global function field of characteristic $p$. In this article, we examine the relationship between the Iwasawa invariants of fine Selmer groups of an elliptic curve over $K$ as one varies over different $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of $K$, using the methods developed by Kleine. We also study generalised Iwasawa invariants of the fine Selmer groups over a $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$-extension $\mathscr{L}/K$, adapting the techniques used by Kleine, Matar and Sujatha.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra

papers.title: Dispersion models on a circle: universal properties and asymptotic results
papers.abstract: Consider a sequence of masses $m_0,m_1,...$ arriving uniformly at random at some points $u_0,u_1,...$ on the unit circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ (or on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, in the discrete version). Upon arrival, each mass undergoes a relaxation phase during which it is dispersed, possibly also at random. This process can model many physical phenomena, such as the diffusion of liquid in a porous medium. In the discrete case, it can model parking (related to additive coalescence and hashing with linear probing) in which the cars are permitted to follow random displacement policies. The dispersion policies considered in the paper ensure that at time $k$, after the successive dispersions of $m_0,\cdots,m_{k-1}$, the total covered region has Lebesgue measure $m_0+\cdots+m_{k-1}$. Furthermore, during the dispersion of a given mass, the covered domain increases continuously, except when it merges with another covered connected component (CC). We show a very general exchangeability property for the sequence of covered CC. Additionally, we demonstrate a universal spacing property between these CC, and a notable general result: if the $(u_i)$ are independent and rotationally invariant, then the number of free (not covered) CC follows a binomial distribution whose parameters depend solely on the number and total mass of arrived particles. Furthermore, conditional on the number of CC, the sizes of the free CC follow a simple Dirichlet distribution in the continuous case, regardless of the dispersion policy considered and the values of the masses. We also characterize the distribution of the occupied space. In the second part of the paper, we study the total cost associated with these models for various cost models, and establish connections with the additive coalescent. We also provide an asymptotic representation of the limiting covered space as the number of masses goes to infinity.

papers.title: Scalar and Mean Curvature Comparison on Compact Cylinder
papers.abstract: Let $ X $ be a closed, oriented Riemannian manifold. Denote by $ (M = X \times I = X \times [0, 1], \partial M = X \times \lbrace 0 \rbrace \cup X \times \lbrace 1 \rbrace, g) $ a compact cylinder with smooth boundary, $ \dim M \geqslant 3 $. In this article, we address the following question: If $ g $ is a Riemannian metric having (i) positive scalar curvature (PSC metric) on $ M $ and nonnegative mean curvature on $ \partial M $; and (ii) $ χ(X) = 0 $ and $ \dim X \geq 5 $, then there exists a PSC metric on $ X $. This generalizes a result of Gromov and Lawson for $ X = \mathbb{T}^{n} $. Our result also implies an infinite band width consequence complementary to Gromov's band width conjecture, which roughly says no additional obstruction or flexibility for the existence of PSC on $ X $ is gained by passing to $ X \times [0, 1] $. Our result relies on geometric PDE analysis with respect to a new conformal invariance---the $ g $-angle condition between normal vector field along $ \partial M $ and the global vector field tangential to the $ I $-direction.
papers.comments: 18 Pages, all comments are welcome. V2 shows that the same conclusion holds when $ χ(X) = 0 $ and $ \dim X \geq 5 $

papers.title: Partial character tables for $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-spetses
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbb{G}}$ be a simply connected ${\mathbb{Z}}_\ell$-spets, let $q$ be a prime power, prime to $\ell$ and let $S$ be the underlying Sylow $\ell$-subgroup. Firstly, motivated by known formulae for values of Deligne-Lusztig characters of finite reductive groups, we propose a formula for the values of the unipotent characters of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ on the elements of $S$. Using this, we explicitly list the unipotent character values of the ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-spets $G_{24}(q)$ related to the Benson-Solomon fusion system Sol$(q)$, and the Aguadé ${\mathbb{Z}}_5$-spets $G_{29}(q)$. Secondly, when $\ell > 2$ is a very good prime for ${\mathbb{G}}$, the Weyl group $W$ of ${\mathbb{G}}$ has order coprime with $\ell$, and $q\equiv1\pmod\ell$ we introduce a formula for the values of characters in the principal block of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ which extends the Curtis-Schewe type formulae for groups of Lie type, and which we show to satisfy a version of block orthogonality. In both cases we formulate and provide evidence for several conjectures concerning the proposed values.

papers.title: Some applications of the Nygaard filtration and quasisyntomic descent in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This article gives an expository account of quasisyntomic descent and the Nygaard filtration in positive characteristic, complemented by several new applications to $p$-adic cohomology theories. The guiding result is a new approach to Illusie's comparison between fppf cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_p(1)$ coefficients and the slope $1$ part of crystalline cohomology. We follow work of Bhatt-Lurie, but give a more elementary presentation which does not rely on the formalism of $\infty$-categories. We then revisit Ogus' comparison theorem between infinitesimal cohomology and étale cohomology, and give new proofs of several results on fppf cohomology that were previously obtained with the de Rham-Witt complex. We also determine the action of multiplication-by-$n$ on the fppf cohomology of an abelian variety, answering a question of A. Skorobogatov to the author. This is an expanded version of the author's master thesis.
papers.comments: 45 pages. v2: minor corrections and exposition improved based on referee comments

papers.title: Smoothing topological pseudo-isotopies of 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: Given a closed, smooth 4-manifold $X$ and self-diffeomorphism $f$ that is topologically pseudo-isotopic to the identity, we study the question of whether $f$ is moreover smoothly pseudo-isotopic to the identity. If the fundamental group of $X$ lies in a certain class, which includes trivial, free, and finite groups of odd order, we show the answer is always affirmative. On the other hand, we produce the first examples of manifolds $X$ and diffeomorphisms $f$ where the answer is negative. Our investigation is motivated by the question, which remains open, of whether there exists a self-diffeomorphism of a closed 4-manifold that is topologically isotopic to the identity, but not stably smoothly isotopic to the identity.
papers.comments: v2 some small structural changes, corrections and addition of Section 7 after referee comments. To appear in J. Reine Angew. Math

papers.title: A Microlocal Theory for Zariski-Constructible Sheaves on Rigid Analytic Varieties
papers.abstract: We develop a microlocal theory, in the sense of Kashiwara-Schapira, for Zariski-constructible sheaves on rigid analytic varieties. We define and study monodromic sheaves, the monodromic Fourier transform, specialisation, microlocalisation, micro-hom, and singular support in this context. Some questions and conjectures are formulated in the end. The appendix contains infinity-categorical characterisations of monodromic sheaves.
papers.comments: 30 pages. Comments welcome! v2: minor improvements, generalised the theory of monodromic sheaves and specialisation as encouraged by T. Abe

papers.title: On Hypothesis H of Rudnick and Sarnak
papers.abstract: We prove Hypothesis H in full generality for ${\rm GL}_n$ over any number field. This result is a consequence of our stronger effective bound on Euler products involving Rankin--Selberg coefficients at prime ideal powers. The proof rests on a new analytic method, which employs a power sieve over number fields and an iterative argument to bypass the functoriality barrier that had restricted prior results to $n\leq 4$. As applications, we unconditionally establish smoothed $m$-level correlations of zeros of automorphic $L$-functions for a restricted class of test functions, provide an explicit polynomial bound for the strong multiplicity one problem for coefficients, and resolve the Selberg orthogonality conjecture with stronger error terms.

papers.title: On the number of conjugacy classes of subgroups of a finite group
papers.abstract: Let $k'(G)$ and $L(G)$ be the number of conjugacy classes of subgroups and the subgroup lattice of a finite group $G$, respectively. Our objective is to study some aspects related to the ratios $d'(G)=\frac{k'(G)}{|L(G)|}$ and $d^*(G)=\min\{ d'(S) \mid S\text{ is a section of }G\}$ which measure how close $G$ is to being a Dedekind group. We prove that the set containing the values $d'(G)$, as $G$ ranges over the class of nilpotent groups, is dense in $[0, 1]$. A nilpotency criterion is obtained by proving that if $d^*(G)>\frac{2}{3}$, then $G$ is nilpotent and information on its structure is given. We also show that if $d^*(G)>\frac{4}{5}$, then $G$ is an Iwasawa group. Finally, we deduce a result which ensures that a $p$-group of order $p^n$ ($n\geq 3$) is a Dedekind group. This last result can be extended to the class of nilpotent groups and it also highlights the second maximum value of $d^*$ on the class of $p$-groups of order $p^n$.
papers.comments: accepted for publication in Mediterr. J. Math

papers.title: The Root Finding Problem Revisited: Beyond the Robbins-Monro procedure
papers.abstract: We study the sequential root-finding problem with repeated noisy measurements. We propose sequential-test bisection STB, which uses a nonparametric sequential sign test to determine when to move to a new design point. Compared with variants of stochastic approximation, STB offers broader adaptivity and faster convergence. When the regression function satisfies $|f(x)|\geq \textsf{c}_0|x-θ|^γ$ in a neighborhood of $θ$ for constants $\textsf{c}_0,γ>0$ where $θ$ is the root, i.e. $f(θ) = 0$, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees showing that STB, without using the knowledge of $γ$, achieves the minimax adaptive optimal convergence rate $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/(2γ)})$, outperforming Robbins--Monro and related stochastic-approximation methods in convergence rate. Under sub-Gaussian noise, STB provides finite-sample confidence sequences for the root $θ$ without estimating a derivative. In the positive-slope model, we augment STB with {randomized weighted-section and a line fitted to all observations}, leading to asymptotic normality and consistent variance estimation. We formalize the efficiency by a convolution theorem of Hájek-Le Cam type. Furthermore, when the regression function is discontinuous at the root, we show that Robbins--Monro converges at rate $1/n$, whereas STB converges super-polynomially. We extend this construction to multivariate nonparametric level-set estimation by sampling along rays. As a technical byproduct, we establish a new central limit theorem under random stopping, with proof techniques that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Search for a basis of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, using rewriting systems
papers.abstract: We begin by defining Temperley-Lieb algebra, in two different ways: as a presented algebra or as a diagrammatic algebra. Next, we look for a basis algorithmically, using rewriting theory. Finally, we introduce a generalization of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, which is an oriented version of the previous one. This pushes us to employ a more efficient tool, category theory, to use rewriting to easily obtain a basis for the algebra.
papers.comments: 35 pages. This document is an internship report from a bachelor student. It shows a lot of "known" results, except for part 2.1.2, giving the Jones normal form of a diagram; part 2.2.2-3, applying rewriting theory to find the Jones normal forms basis of the Temperley-Lieb algebra; and 4.3-4, applying category theory to find a new basis

papers.title: Radial Epiderivative Based Fritz John and KKT Conditions in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this study, we examine Fritz John (FJ) and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) type optimality conditions for a class of nonsmooth and nonconvex optimization problems with inequality constraints, where the objective and constraint functions all are assumed to be radially epidifferentiable. The concept of the radial epiderivative constitutes a distinct generalization of classical derivative notions, as it replaces the conventional limit operation with an infimum-based construction. This formulation permits the analysis of directional behavior without invoking standard neighborhood-based assumptions and constructions commonly required in generalized differentiation. This leads to one of the key advantages of the radial epiderivative which lies in its applicability even to discrete domains, where classical and generalized derivatives are often inapplicable or undefined. The other advantage of this concept is that it provides a possibility to inverstigate KKT conditions for global minimums. Consequently, this approach necessitates a reformulation of fundamental analytical tools such as gradient vectors, feasible direction sets, constraint qualifications and other concepts which are central to the derivation of optimality conditions in smooth optimization theory. The primary contribution of this paper is the development of a comprehensive theoretical framework for KKT conditions tailored to the radially epidifferentiable setting. We introduce novel definitions of the radial gradient vector, of the set of feasible directions, and examine how classical constraint qualifications may be interpreted and extended within this new framework.
papers.comments: This work contains critical errors that invalidate the main conclusions

papers.title: Genericity of ergodic measures on non-positively curved manifolds with flat strips
papers.abstract: We study the geodesic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive curvature. In the case of surfaces, Coudène and Schapira proved that the existence of a flat strip prevents the set of ergodic measures from being generic in the space of invariant probability measures. We show the existence of a three-dimensional manifold that contains an embedded flat torus and where ergodicity is a generic property. More generally, Coudène and Schapira proved that ergodicity is a generic property within the space of invariant probability measures defined on $Ω_{NF}$, the set of non-wandering vectors whose orbits do not bound a flat strip. We introduce a larger set $\mathcal{R}_w$ where the same property holds, and we illustrate the extent of our findings using a famous example of a rank-one manifold attributed to Gromov.
papers.comments: This article is currently under review for publication in Annales de l'Institut Fourier

papers.title: On F-pure thresholds and quasi-F-purity of hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We show that quasi-$F$-pure but not $F$-pure isolated quasi-homogeneous hypersurface singularities necessarily have $F$-pure threshold $1 - \frac{1}{p}$. This extends work of Bhatt and Singh beyond the Calabi-Yau case. We also classify the (quasi)-$F$-purity of Fermat hypersurfaces.
papers.comments: Updated to include referee feedback; to appear in Nagoya Math Journal. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Pseudo-Anosov Flows: A Plane Approach
papers.abstract: In this text we (re)-tell the theory of pseudo-Anosov flows on 3-manifolds with the orbit space as the central character; via a streamlined framework called {\em Anosov-like group actions}. This brings a simplified and unified perspective, and allows for the import of tools from 1- and 2-dimensional topological dynamics. In so doing, we are able to give a relatively efficient presentation (or re-presentation) of foundational results in the field which appeared over several decades and many papers. We hope that the reader, whether a beginning or more advanced topologist or dynamicist, finds this a welcoming invitation to the rich theory of pseudo-Anosov flows.
papers.comments: v3: replaced all figures by vectorized versions created by Federico Salmoiraghi. Lots of typos, and small errors fixed, sketches or hints added to the exercises. v2: added a new chapter (chapter 3), old section 2.11 incorporated into chapter 3, lots of small modifications following feedback. v1: First complete, public, version. Please don't hesitate to send us comments, including detected typos

papers.title: Two-scale criteria for Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities with applications to Markov chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Given a collection of distributions $\{P_{y}\}$ and a mixing distribution $ρ$ supported over $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we propose new sufficient conditions under which the mixture / joint distribution satisfies a Poincaré or log-Sobolev inequality. We develop these sufficient conditions in a unified manner using the framework of $Φ$-Sobolev inequalities (Chafaï, 2004). The conditions that we develop in this work are satisfied by a variety of Markov chains, and consequently allows us to characterise the evolution of these functional inequalities for iterates generated by simulating these Markov chains. As a result, we obtain an clean error analysis for estimating a broad class of functionals using Markov chain Monte Carlo strategies along these Markov chains.
papers.comments: v3: establish stronger W2 mixing with condition on kernel

papers.title: Planar induced paths via a decomposition into non-crossing ordered graphs
papers.abstract: In any graph, the maximum size of an induced path is bounded by the maximum size of a path. However, in the general case, one cannot find a converse bound, even up to an arbitrary function, as evidenced by the case of cliques. Galvin, Rival and Sands proved in 1982 that, when restricted to weakly sparse graphs, such a converse property actually holds. In this paper, we consider the maximal function $f$ such that any planar graph (and in general, any graph of bounded genus) containing a path on $n$ vertices contains an induced path of size $f(n)$, and prove that $f(n) \in Θ(\log n/\log \log n)$ by providing a lower bound matching the upper bound obtained by Esperet, Lemoine and Maffray, up to a constant factor. We obtain these tight bounds by analyzing graphs ordered along a Hamiltonian path that admit an edge partition into a bounded number of sets without crossing edges. In particular, we prove that the guaranteed size of an induced path when the ordered graph can be partitioned into $2k$, resp. $2k+1$, sets of non-crossing edges, is $Θ_k((\log n/\log \log n)^{1/k})$, resp. $Θ_k((\log n)^{1/(k + 1)})$.

papers.title: Clapping: Removing Per-sample Storage for Pipeline Parallel Distributed Optimization with Communication Compression
papers.abstract: Pipeline-parallel distributed optimization is essential for large-scale machine learning but is challenged by significant communication overhead from transmitting high-dimensional activations and gradients between workers. Existing approaches often depend on impractical unbiased gradient assumptions or incur sample-size memory overhead. This paper introduces Clapping, a Communication compression algorithm with LAzy samPling for Pipeline-parallel learnING. Clapping adopts a lazy sampling strategy that reuses data samples across steps, breaking sample-wise memory barrier and supporting convergence in few-epoch or online regimes. Clapping comprises two variants including Clapping-FC and Clapping-FU, both of which achieve convergence without unbiased assumption for compressed gradient, effectively addressing compression error propagation in multi-worker settings. Numerical experiments validate the performance of Clapping across different tasks.

papers.title: The Derived Auslander--Iyama Correspondence II: Bimodule Calabi--Yau Structures
papers.abstract: Let $d$ be a positive integer. In a previous article we established a bijective correspondence between the following classes of objects, considered up to the appropriate notion of equivalence: differential graded algebras (dg) with finite-dimensional $0$-th cohomology such that the canonical generator of their perfect derived category is a basic $d\ZZ$-cluster tilting object, and basic Frobenius algebras that are twisted $(d+2)$-periodic as bimodules. In this article, we prove a variant of our general correspondence for bimodule right Calabi--Yau dg algebras. A novel ingredient is a new cohomology theory which contains obstructions to the existence and uniqueness of minimal $A_\infty$-bimodule structures on a graded bimodule. As an application of our results, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first example of an algebraic triangulated category with a triangulated Calabi--Yau structure that cannot be lifted to a bimodule right Calabi--Yau structure on any of its dg enhancements.
papers.comments: 103 pages. v2: Corrected several small typos. Added new Section 7.3 on a non-enhanceable triangulated Calabi--Yau structure. v3: Editorial improvements. v4: Enhanced exposition, several small corrections. Subsection 7.3 is now Section 8. v5: Corrected Example 7.14, other minor edits

papers.title: Wave packet decompositions and sharp bilinear estimates for rough Hamiltonian flows
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to prove bilinear $L^p$ estimates for rough dispersive evolutions satisfying non-degeneracy and transversality assumptions. The estimates generalize the sharp Fourier extension estimates for the cone and the paraboloid. We obtain the sharp dependence on transversality and sharp up to endpoints $L^p$ range. To this end, we combine an axiomatic induction-on-scales with the construction of a wave packet parametrix for dispersive equations with $C^{1,1}$-coefficients by using the FBI transform.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds via Brill-Noether theory of curves
papers.abstract: Fix a polarised Calabi-Yau threefold $(X,H)$. We reduce a version of the Bayer-Macrì-Toda conjecture for $(X,H)$, which ensures the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$, to verifying a Brill-Noether-type inequality for curves on $X$. We then prove this inequality for a broad class of Calabi-Yau threefolds, including complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefolds in weighted projective spaces.
papers.comments: 37 pages, comments are very welcome. v3: Final version, to appear in Invent. Math

papers.title: A Generalisation of Sperner's Theorem Using Weighted Chains
papers.abstract: We find the (unique) largest subset of $\{0, 1, 2\}^n$ such that it contains no two elements, one of which is coordinatewise greater than the other, but strictly greater on at most $k$ coordinates. To do so, we decompose the cube into weighted chains. In Appendix B we present a new proof of Sperner's theorem we found while working on this problem.
papers.comments: A new version rewritten to improve the exposition, and with links to AI-generated, human-verified formalisations of proofs

papers.title: Partition Functions of Two-Dimensional Coulomb Gases with Circular Root- and Jump-Type Singularities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the random polynomial $p_n(ρ):=\prod_{j=1}^n (|z_j|-ρ)$, where the points $\{z_j\}_{j=1}^n$ are the eigenvalues of random normal matrices with a radially symmetric potential. We establish precise large $n$ asymptotic expansions for the moment generating function $\mathbb{E}\bigl[{\rm e}^{(u \operatorname{Im}\log p_n(ρ))/π} {\rm e}^{a\operatorname{Re}\log p_n(ρ)}\bigr]$, $u\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>-1$, where $ρ>0$ lies in the bulk of the spectral droplet. The asymptotic expansion is expressed in terms of parabolic cylinder functions, which confirms a conjecture of Byun and Charlier. This also provides the first free energy expansion of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with general circular root- and jump-type singularities. While the $a=0$ case has already been widely studied in the literature due to its relation to counting statistics, we also obtain new results for this special case.

papers.title: Mixed-precision iterative refinement for low-rank Lyapunov equations
papers.abstract: We develop a mixed-precision iterative refinement framework for solving low-rank Lyapunov matrix equations $AX + XA^T + W =0$, where $W=LL^T$ or $W=LSL^T$. Via rounding error analysis of the algorithms we derive sufficient conditions for the attainable normwise residuals in different precision settings and show how the algorithmic parameters should be chosen. These conditions are independent of the choice of inner solver, provided that the prescribed residual accuracy is attained in the inner solves. Using the sign-function Newton iteration as the solver, we demonstrate that reduced precisions, such as half precision with unit roundoff $u_s$, can be used for Lyapunov equations with condition number of order $u_s^{-1}$ without compromising the attainable solution quality. The numerical experiments validate our error analysis, and we establish cost models to quantify the expected speedup for different low-to-high precision timing ratios. This work provides an algorithmic framework towards exploiting native low-precision hardware to accelerate low-rank Lyapunov solvers without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: Catalan Semirings
papers.abstract: We study Catalan semirings, which are additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups belong to a natural family of transformation monoids known as Catalan monoids. There are two kinds of Catalan semirings, whose properties differ substantially. We address the Finite Basis Problem for individual Catalan semirings of each kind and their representations by Boolean triangular matrices. Furthermore, we characterize the varieties and pseudovarieties generated by all Catalan semirings of each kind.
papers.comments: 40 pages, 6 illustrations. The text of version 2 constitutes Section 2 of the present version

papers.title: Continuation of Dirichlet series I
papers.abstract: We study Dirichlet series arising as linear functionals on an inner product space of meromorphic functions and establish a relation between the discontinuities of the former on the boundary and the poles and zeros of the latter on the imaginary axis. As an example application of Delange's Tauberian theorem, it is shown that the conjectured asymptotic in the additive divisor problem follows conditionally on the non-vanishing of certain meromorphic functions on the imaginary axis.
papers.comments: A uniform lower bound for the norm on the r.h.s. of (3.17) has not been given. This is crucial, and requires an additional argument

papers.title: Derivation of the fourth-order DLSS equation with nonlinear mobility via chemical reactions
papers.abstract: We provide a derivation of the one-dimensional fourth-order DLSS equation based on an interpretation as a chemical reaction network. We consider the rate equation on the discretized circle for a process in which pairs of particles occupying the same site simultaneously jump to the two neighboring sites; the reverse process involves pairs of particles at adjacent sites simultaneously jumping back to the site located between them. Depending on the rates, in the vanishing-mesh-size limit we obtain either the classical DLSS equation or a variant with nonlinear mobility of power type. Via EDP convergence, we identify the limiting gradient structure to be driven by entropy with respect to a generalization of diffusive transport with nonlinear mobility.
