Interestingly, the DLSS equation with power-type mobility shares qualitative similarities with the fast diffusion and porous medium equation, since we find traveling wave solutions with algebraic tails or compactly supported polynomials, respectively.
papers.comments: 38 pages, 2 figure. Accepted version. Comments welcome

papers.title: General Chen's first inequality and applications for Riemannian maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose \textit{general Chen's first inequality} for Riemannian maps between Riemannian manifolds and demonstrate its equality and sharpness via non-trivial examples. We also utilize this general inequality by establishing Chen's first inequalities when the target spaces are generalized complex and generalized Sasakian space forms, including real, complex, real Kähler, Sasakian, Kenmotsu, cosymplectic, and almost $C(α)$ space forms. In addition, we estimate $δ$-invariants under various hypotheses on these space forms. Finally, we validate our new approach by comparing particular results with those of existing approaches.
papers.comments: Received 28 January 2026; received in revised form 17 September 2026; accepted 20 October 2026

papers.title: A family of nonlocal energies whose minimizers are supported on two intervals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the one-dimensional interaction energy $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(W*ρ)(x)dρ(x) + \int_{\mathbb{R}}U(x)dρ(x)$ where the interaction potential $W(x)= -\frac{|x|^b}{b},\,1\le b \le 2$ and the external potential $U(x)=\frac{|x|^4}{4}$, and $ρ$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the real line. Our main result shows that the minimizer is supported on two intervals when $1<b<2$, showing in particular how the support of the minimizer transits from an interval (when $b=1$) to two points (when $b=2$) as $b$ increases. As a crucial part of the proof, we develop a new version of the iterated balayage algorithm, the original version of which was designed by Benko, Damelin, Dragnev and Kuijlaars for logarithmic potentials in one dimension. We expect the methodology in this paper can be generalized to study minimizers of interaction energies in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose support is possibly an annulus.

papers.title: On the Structure of Stationary Solutions to McKean-Vlasov Equations with Applications to Noisy Transformers
papers.abstract: We study stationary solutions of McKean-Vlasov equations on the circle. We establish an exact equivalence between solutions of the stationary McKean-Vlasov equation and an infinite-dimensional quadratic system of equations over Fourier coefficients, allowing explicit characterization of stationary states in a sequence space rather than a function space. This framework provides a transparent description of local bifurcations, their periodicity and resonance structures, while accommodating singular potentials. We derive analytic expressions for the emergence, form and shape (supercritical, critical, subcritical or transcritical) of bifurcations involving possibly multiple Fourier modes and connect them with discontinuous phase transitions. We also characterize, under suitable assumptions, the detailed structure of the stationary bifurcating solutions through leading small-amplitude coefficients for arbitrarily many fixed Fourier modes. At the global level, we establish regularity and concavity properties of the free energy landscape, proving existence, compactness, and coexistence of globally minimizing stationary measures, and identifying discontinuous phase transitions with points of non-differentiability of the minimum free energy map. We apply the theory to the Noisy Mean-Field Transformer model, where we show how changing the inverse temperature $β$ affects the geometry of the infinitely many bifurcations from the uniform measure. We also discuss how increasing $β$ motivates the study of approximate multi-mode stationary profiles as candidates for a separate metastability analysis; persistence times require additional dynamical estimates. Moreover, we determine the exact threshold $β_0\simeq2.447$ separating continuous and discontinuous phase transitions in this model. The same threshold marks the change of the first bifurcation from supercritical to subcritical.

papers.title: An explicit formula for the limit of the heat kernel measures on the spheres embedded in $\mathbb {R}^\infty$
papers.abstract: We show that the heat kernel measures based at the north pole of the spheres $S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)$, with a properly scaled radius $\sqrt N$ and adjusted center, in the sense of finite-dimensional marginals, to a Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^\infty$. In particular, in the direction of the base point, the variance of this limiting measure is $1-e^{-t}-te^{-t}$, and in the orthogonal directions, the variance is $1-e^{-t}$.

papers.title: Linear decay of the beta-plane equation near Couette flow on the plane
papers.abstract: We prove new time decay estimates for the linearized $β$-plane equation near the Couette flow on the plane that combine inviscid damping and the dispersion of Rossby waves. Specifically, we show that the profiles of the velocity field components (i.e. $u(t,x+ty,y)$) decay pointwise on any compact set with polynomial rates. While mixing dominates for streamwise frequencies that are $O(1)$, dispersive effects need to be extracted for low streamwise frequencies that appear along a critical ray in frequency space.

papers.title: Monadic Second-Order Logic of Permutations
papers.abstract: Permutations can be viewed as pairs of linear orders, or more formally as models over a signature consisting of two binary relation symbols. This approach was adopted by Albert, Bouvel and Féray, who studied the expressibility of first-order logic in this setting. We focus our attention on monadic second-order logic. Our results go in two directions. First, we investigate the expressive power of monadic second-order logic. We exhibit natural properties of permutations that can be expressed in monadic second-order logic but not in first-order logic. Additionally, we show that the property of having a fixed point is inexpressible even in monadic second-order logic. Secondly, we focus on the complexity of monadic second-order model checking. We show that there is an algorithm deciding if a permutation $π$ satisfies a given monadic second-order sentence $\varphi$ in time $f(|\varphi|, \operatorname{tw}(π)) \cdot n$ for some computable function $f$ where $n = |π|$ and $\operatorname{tw}(π)$ is the tree-width of $π$. On the other hand, we prove that the problem remains hard even when we restrict the permutation $π$ to a fixed hereditary class $\mathcal{C}$ with mild assumptions on $\mathcal{C}$.
papers.comments: Accepted to Advances in Applied Mathematics

papers.title: Stability of Homogeneous minimal hypersurfaces in the Page space and $Y^{p,q}$ Sasaki-Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability of homogeneous minimal submanifolds in two families of closed Einstein manifolds, the Page space $\mathbb{CP}^2 \# \overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ and the Sasaki-Einstein spaces $Y^{p,q}$, which are equipped with cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics admitting the isometric action of $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and $U(1) \times U(1) \times SU(2)$ respectively. We determine all the homogeneous, minimal hypersurfaces and explicitly compute the spectrum of their associated stability operators and determine their index.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 1 figure; v2 (agrees with published version): 15 pages, 4 figures, substantial improvements and statement of Theorem 1.2 corrected

papers.title: From Kinetic Nonequilibrium to Deviatoric Stress: An Operator Formulation of the First-Order Chapman--Enskog Transport Map
papers.abstract: The Chapman--Enskog procedure provides the classical asymptotic connection between kinetic nonequilibrium and macroscopic viscous stress. The present work isolates its first-order kinetic-to-stress step as an explicit operator composition. The construction separates the leading-order streaming source, the collisional kinetic response, and the deviatoric second-moment projection into a single transport map. Under explicit solvability, coercivity and bounded-inverse, regularity, and controlled-remainder assumptions, this map is well defined and bounded; hypocoercive estimates may additionally be used in closing the conditional remainder bound. In particular, a nonzero first-order deviatoric stress requires a nonzero first-order kinetic correction, although the converse is not asserted. The result is not a new derivation of the Navier--Stokes constitutive law or viscosity coefficient; its contribution is to make the kinetic-to-macroscopic transport map and its analytic conditions explicit. A BGK example recovers the classical Newtonian constitutive relation.

papers.title: Stabilization and control of the semilinear hinged plate equation
papers.abstract: In this article we prove semiglobal stabilization and exact controllability results for semilinear plate equations with hinged boundary conditions and analytic nonlinearity, when the damping or control acts on a region where the linear Schrödinger equation is observable. At the core of these results lies a new unique continuation property for the nonlinear plate equation, which significantly relaxes the geometric conditions required for such a property to hold. This property is obtained by combining recent results on propagation of analyticity in time and unique continuation for linear plate operators. More broadly, our approach exploits the linear observability of the plate equation to establish both stabilization and control results. First, we prove exponential decay of the nonlinear energy under a defocusing assumption on the nonlinearity. Second, under a weaker asymptotic assumption on the nonlinearity, we prove semiglobal exact control by analyzing control properties inside the compact attractor provided by the dynamics of the damped equation.
papers.comments: v2: Introduction re-written to better position the results within the literature. Section 2 better organizes preliminaries and Corollary 2.7 corrected (previously Corollary 2.6). Section 4.2 added comment on convergence toward equilibria. Several minor corrections and clarifications added (analyticity hypothesis, proof of Theorem 1.1 and various passages of Section 5)

papers.title: A modified Consensus-Based Optimization model: consensus formation and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos
papers.abstract: We introduce a modified CBO model based on a regularized Gibbs weight. For each fixed temperature and regularization parameter, the regularized weight yields a configuration-independent lower bound on the denominator of the consensus map, thus a quantitative analysis without an upper bound on the objective function or cutoff in the noise. We first prove large-time consensus for the finite-particle system: above an explicit stability threshold, every particle converges exponentially to a common random limit. This consensus mechanism does not require the $C^2$ condition used in the direct weighted-energy argument. We next prove uniform-in-time propagation of chaos: we derive quantitative bounds for the finite-particle consensus point from finite-time concentration estimates for the mean-field law, with explicit approximation and large-time tail errors. The synchronous-coupling estimate also gives a quantitative comparison between the random particle consensus point and the deterministic mean-field consensus point. We also quantify the regularization error in the quantitative Laplace principle, making the effect of the additive regularization explicit. A direct weighted-energy estimate is obtained under stronger $C^2$ assumptions. Furthermore, we give a stopped quadratic stability estimate with the actual Gibbs denominator. Under the weak-landscape condition, full support of the initial law, and local nondegeneracy of the minimizer, we prove a high-probability finite-particle global-optimization theorem for any fixed $λ>σ^2$. The proof combines an affine-flow local-mass estimate, finite-time mean-field entrance, ordinary finite-horizon propagation of chaos, and an $α$-independent convex trapping energy near the minimizer.
papers.comments: The abstract/structure of the paper has been revised, and a probabilistic finite-particle result has been added under an additional set of assumptions

papers.title: Estimates for convolution operators on Hardy spaces associated with ball quasi-Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: Let $0 \leq α< n$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $X$ and $Y$ be ball quasi-Banach function spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We consider operators $T_α$ defined by convolution with kernels of type $(α, N)$. Assuming that the powered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator satisfies a Fefferman-Stein vector-valued maximal inequality on $X$ and is bounded on the associated space, we prove that, for $α= 0$, $T_0$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to X$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n)$; and for $0 < α< n$, under certain additional assumptions on $X$ and $Y$, $T_α$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to Y$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{Y}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. In particular, these results yield the corresponding estimates for singular integral operators and Riesz potentials. We also provide an off-diagonal Fefferman-Stein vector-valued inequality for the fractional maximal operator on the $p$-convexification of ball quasi-Banach function spaces.

papers.title: Peng's Maximum Principle for Stochastic Delay Differential Equations of Mean-Field Type
papers.abstract: We extend Peng's maximum principle to the case of stochastic delay differential equations of mean-field type. More precisely, the coefficients of our control problem depend on the state, on the past trajectory and on its expected value. Moreover, the control enters the noise coefficient and the control domain may be non-convex. Our approach is based on a lifting of the state equation to an infinite dimensional Hilbert space that removes the explicit delay in the state equation. The main ingredient in the proof of the maximum principle is a precise asymptotic for the expectation of the first order variational process, which allows us to neglect the corresponding second order terms in the expansion of the cost functional.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in Appl. Math. Optim

papers.title: Teichmüller spaces and normal forms associated to wandering domains
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical Teichmüller space ${\mathcal T}(U,f)$ associated to a wandering domain $U$ of an entire function $f$. We show that a discrete grand orbit relation in $U$ forces ${\mathcal T}(U,f)$ to be infinite dimensional, thereby answering a question of Fagella--Henriksen. We further describe the geometry of these spaces by developing normal forms for the dynamics on wandering domains, yielding global linearising coordinates in the discrete case and power-type dynamics between annuli in the indiscrete case.
papers.comments: 22 pages. V2: Author accepted manuscript. To appear in IMRN

papers.title: Convergence rate of empirical measures in the subspace robust Wasserstein distance
papers.abstract: We obtain an estimate for the expected subspace robust 2-Wasserstein distance between any probability measure with a finite q-th moment (q>2) defined on a separable Hilbert space, and its empirical distribution from $n$ i.i.d. samples.
papers.comments: v2: main theorem extended to probability measures with bounded q-th moment and general k; lower bound sharpened; refinements under spectral decay added

papers.title: Midpoints and critical points
papers.abstract: For a degree $5$ real polynomial with roots $x_1\leq \cdots \leq x_5$ and roots $ξ_1\leq \cdots \leq ξ_4$ of its derivative, we set $z_j:=(x_j+x_{j+1})/2$, $1\leq j\leq 4$. We prove that one cannot have at the same time $\min_{1\leq j\leq 3}(z_{j+1}-z_j)\geq \min_{1\leq j\leq 3}(ξ_{j+1}-ξ_j)$ and $\max_{1\leq j\leq 3}(z_{j+1}-z_j)\geq \max_{1\leq j\leq 3}(ξ_{j+1}-ξ_j)$. The result settles a general question about midpoints and critical points of hyperbolic polynomials.

papers.title: Groupoid graded rings and their categories of graded modules
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a groupoid acting on a set $X$ and let $R$ be a $G$-graded ring with graded local units. We study the main properties of the category $gr-(R,G,X)$ of $X$-graded $R$-modules and adjoint functors between categories of this kind. We characterize the latter in terms of tensor-like and hom-like functors. As an application we obtain a characterization of equivalences between such categories in the spirit of Morita theory. Then we introduce restriction and induction functors between categories of type $gr-(R,G,X)$ and show that many functors between such categories can be realized naturally as a restriction or induction functor. This includes the forgetful functor, the functor associating a $G$ graded $R$-module with the $H$-graded module formed by the sum of the homogeneous components of degree in subgroupoid $H$, and the one associating it with the collapsing of homogeneous components in cosets modulo $H$ for $H$ a wide subgrupoid. We characterize when a restriction or induction functor is an equivalence of categories. Finally, we prove that $gr-(R,G,X)$ is always equivalent to the category of modules over a ring with local units and, generalizing a result of Menini and Năstăsescu, we characterize when $gr-(R,G,X)$ is equivalent to the category of modules over a unital ring.
papers.comments: 26 pages. We corrected some mistakes and fixed typos

papers.title: On a bound of $p$-ranks of Iwasawa modules of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over a quartic CM-field
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number. If a number field $k$ has at least one complex place, there are infinitely many $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over $k$, and some authors studied the behavior of Iwasawa invariants of these $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In particular, Fujii studied the case where $k$ is an imaginary quadratic field and obtained some results on the boundedness of Iwasawa $λ$-invariants in a certain infinite family of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In the present article, we give analogous theorems in the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field. One of our main theorems determines all the Iwasawa invariants, including the $ν$-invariants, of a certain infinite family of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over a quartic CM-field.

papers.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
papers.abstract: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.

papers.title: Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs
papers.abstract: Uniqueness for stochastic PDEs with drift in differential form is a main open problem in the recent literature on regularisation by noise. This paper establishes a self-contained theory in the framework of stochastic evolution equations on separable Hilbert spaces and provides a first result to address such an issue, in the direction of both pathwise and weak uniqueness, as well as continuous dependence on the initial data. The singularity of the drift allows to achieve novel uniqueness results for several classes of examples, ranging from fluid-dynamics to phase-separation models.

papers.title: Totient-based Identities for Integer Pairs with Equal Divisor Sums
papers.abstract: A pair of integers is called amicable if each number equals the sum of the proper divisors of the other. In this paper, we investigate a broader class of integer pairs $(A, B)$ that satisfy the weaker condition $σ(A) = σ(B)$, where $σ$ is the sum-of-divisors function. We focus on pairs whose greatest common divisor is a power of two and analyze their distinct prime factorizations. Specifically, we consider configurations of the forms $(A=2^n ab,\ B=2^n cd)$, $(A=2^n abc,\ B=2^n de)$, and $(A=2^n abc,\ B=2^n def)$, where the factors are odd primes. For each configuration, we derive explicit symmetric identities that must be satisfied. These identities relate the odd prime factors of $A$ and $B$ to the quantity $\varphi(A)+\varphi(B)$, where $\varphi$ denotes Euler's totient function. As a consequence, these relations provide necessary structural constraints for amicable pairs of these specific forms, while also revealing an underlying algebraic symmetry for any pair with equal divisor sums.

papers.title: Derivation of a nonlinear, history-dependent tissue-level current law for an electropermeabilization model via homogenization
papers.abstract: We study a phenomenological electropermeabilization model in a periodic medium representing biological tissue. Starting from a cell-level model describing the electric potential and the degree of poration, we perform dimensional analysis to identify a relevant scaling in terms of a small parameter $\varepsilon$ - the ratio between the cell and the tissue size. The electric potential satisfies electrostatic equations in the extra- and intracellular domains, while its jump across the cell membrane evolves according to a nonlinear law coupled with an ordinary differential equation for the poration degree. We prove the well-posedness of the microscopic problem, derive a priori estimates, obtain formal asymptotics, and rigorously justify the expansion by combining two-scale convergence with monotonicity arguments. The resulting macroscopic model exhibits memory effects and a nonlinear, time-dependent effective current. It captures the nontrivial evolution of effective conductivity, including a characteristic drop reflecting the capacitive behavior of the lipid bilayer, in agreement with experimental data. Numerical computations of the effective conductivity confirm that, although the intracellular and extracellular bulk conductivities are constant, tissue conductivity varies nonlinearly with electric field strength, showing a sigmoid trend.

papers.title: On Diophantine exponents of lattices
papers.abstract: We describe the spectrum of ordinary Diophantine exponents for $d$-dimensional lattices. The result reduces the problem to two-dimensional case and uses argument of metric theory.
papers.comments: Minor AI suggested corrections of inaccuracies in the final version of the manuscript

papers.title: Probabilistic Hanna Neumann Conjectures
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of polymatroids on Stallings core graphs, and prove a gap theorem. As special cases of it, we prove the gap conjecture of Ernst-West, Puder, Seidel and the author on the stable $K$-primitivity rank (using a forthcoming result of Ernst-West and Puder); prove Reiter's conjecture on word-random subgroups of finite groups; improve Bowen's bounds on the $f$-invariant for p.m.p. actions of free groups in which a generating partition has a non-cyclic stabilizer, deducing coalescence; and extend the proof of Wise's $w$-cycle conjecture by Louder and Wilton to not-necessarily-cyclic subgroups, which gives a new proof of this special case of the Friedman-Mineyev theorem (i.e. the Hanna Neumann conjecture). Louder and Wilton further improved the bound in Wise's conjecture via their "dependence theorem"; in an appendix joint with Noam Ta Shma, we extend this improvement too to not-necessarily-cyclic subgroups, again as a special case of the main gap theorem. We also compute the exact decay rate of the expected number of invariant subsets, respectively subspaces, for word-random subgroups of $S_n$, respectively $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$.
papers.comments: 56 pages. v2: substantially revised and extended, with a new abstract: new applications to Bowen's f-invariant and to the dependence theorem of Louder and Wilton (in an appendix joint with Noam Ta Shma). Appendices contributed by Doron Puder and Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain

papers.title: Inverse Iterations for Phase-Invariant Nonlinear Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: We study the local convergence of nonlinear inverse iterations for eigenvalue problems arising from variational energies that are invariant under global phase rotations. This symmetry introduces an inherent degeneracy of the target eigenvalue, preventing the direct application of existing convergence results that require a simple eigenvalue. Within an abstract variational framework, we investigate a shifted Jacobian-based inverse iteration, known as the J-method, and establish its local convergence to quasi-isolated ground states. Our analysis shows that the target eigenvalue of the J-operator has algebraic and geometric multiplicity exactly two. By introducing an auxiliary iteration that fixes the global phase, we prove local linear convergence of the iterates modulo phase rotations and derive sharp convergence rates in terms of the spectrum of the J-operator. In particular, these rates can be improved through spectral shifting. We apply the abstract theory to a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation that models spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates, verify the relevant structural assumptions and numerically examine the quasi-isolation of the computed ground states. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the shifted J-method, particularly in regimes with slowly converging conventional inverse iterations.

papers.title: Chip-firing on the Lattice of Nonnegative Integer Points
papers.abstract: Chip-firing on a directed graph is a game in which chips, a discrete commodity, are placed on the vertices of the graph and are transferred between vertices. In this paper, we study a chip-firing game on the lattice of nonnegative integer points on the $x$-$y$ plane, where we start with $2^n$ chips at the origin. When we fire a vertex $v$, we send one chip to each out-neighbor. We fire until we reach a stable configuration, a distribution of chips where no vertex can fire. We study the intermediate firing configuration: a table that assigns to each vertex the total number of chips that reach it. We prove that the nonzero entries of the stable configuration correspond to the odd entries of the intermediate firing configuration. The intermediate firing configuration consists of three parts: the top triangle, the midsection, and the bottom triangle. We describe properties of each part. We study properties of each row and the number of rows of the intermediate firing configuration. We also explore properties of the difference tables, which are tables of first differences of each row of the intermediate firing configuration.
papers.comments: 22 pages, 11 figures, revisions were made throughout the paper

papers.title: A note on toric periods in unramified families
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the algebra $\mathbf{C}[X_1^{\pm 1},X_2^{\pm 1}]$ and $Q(A)$ its quotient field. In this short article we exhibit the correct normalization for the toric period on the parabolically induced unramified family over $Q(A)$, so that it behaves optimally under restriction to the parabolically induced unramified family over $A$. Finally, we explicitly describe the structure of the $A$-module given by the image of this normalized period. These results answer questions raised by D. Prasad, and point towards potential generalizations to a broader unramified Gan-Gross-Prasad setting.
papers.comments: Revised version, to appear in Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. (Math. Sci.)

papers.title: iCanonical basis arising from quasi-split rank one iquantum group
papers.abstract: We compute icanonical basis of the quasi-split rank one modified iquantum group, by obtaining explicit transition matrices among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and standardized canonical basis; all these bases can be naturally categorified. These transition matrices follow from their counterparts computed in this paper among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and canonical basis on simple finite-dimensional modules of quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$.
papers.comments: v2: 43 pages, major revision, formulated uniform transition formulas between monomial and icanonical bases including previously separate boundary cases b=a+c (the old boundary case formulas were incorrect due to sign error in results in the literature); full transition formula from icanonical to canonical bases

papers.title: Partial Linearity: Diagolinear Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce and study diagolinear categories. These are pointed categories equipped with sum-like and product-like monoidal structures, where diagonal matrices of morphisms between two sequences of objects are (uniquely) realizable as morphisms from the sum of the first sequence to the product of the second sequence. We formulate and prove the coherence theorem for diagolinear categories and study the universal construction that realizes also the non-diagonal matrices (equivalently, turns the two monoidal structures into actual categorical sum and product). We also compare diagolinear categories with duoidal categories.
papers.comments: We have renamed "prelinear" to "diagolinear" to reflect that diagonal matrices realize morphisms here. In this version we have isolated this part of the project and included new results on a reflection to bicartesian categories and a number of examples. In follow-up papers, we will include the other topics presented in the original paper: partially linear categories and centrality in that context

papers.title: On the dimension drop for harmonic measure on uniformly non-flat Ahlfors-David regular boundaries
papers.abstract: We extend earlier results of Azzam on the dimension drop of the harmonic measure for a domain $Ω\subset \R^{n}$ with $n\geq 3$, with dimensional Ahlfors regular boundary $\partialΩ$ of dimension $s$ with $n-1-δ_0 \leq s\leq n-1$, that is uniformly non flat. Here $δ_0$ is a small positive constant dependent on the parameters of the problem. Our novel construction relies on elementary geometric and potential theoretic considerations. We avoid the use of Riesz transforms and compactness arguments, and also give quantitative bounds on the $δ_0$ parameter.

papers.title: On noncontinuous bisymmetric strictly monotone operations
papers.abstract: We construct bisymmetric, partially strictly increasing binary operations on real intervals which are not continuous. This shows that continuity cannot be removed from the classical characterization of bisymmetric quasi-sums due to Aczél and Dhombres. Our examples are operations of the form \[ F(x,y)=f^{-1}(αf(x)+βf(y)), \] where $α,β>0$ and $α+β\neq1$. The generating map $f$ is chosen as a strictly increasing bijection from an interval onto a two-component subset of $\mathbb{R}$ separated by a gap. The range is directly invariant under the relevant weighted sums, while the gap produces a jump of $f$ and hence discontinuity of every one-variable section. As a consequence, we obtain discontinuous associative and strictly increasing operations on intervals, and we extend the construction to the multivariate case. In the opposite direction, we prove that if a symmetric bisymmetric strictly increasing operation is reflexive at two points of an interval, then it is automatically continuous on the segment between them and coincides there with a quasi-arithmetic mean.

papers.title: Twisted scalar curvature as a moment map
papers.abstract: We develop the moment map theory of the twisted scalar curvature of a Kähler metric. Primarily, we introduce a coupled system of equations on a holomorphic submersion intertwining the twisted scalar curvature of a Kähler metric on the base and the fibrewise scalar curvature of a relatively Kähler metric on the total space. This resulting system can be viewed as producing the natural coupled metric geometry of holomorphic submersions, and we show that this system appears canonically as a moment map. The approach generalises to foliations, where we prove similar results.
papers.comments: v2. Minor edits. To appear in Math. Zeit

papers.title: Derived graded modules
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the $\infty$-category of (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over a $G$-graded ring $R$ for a torsion-free abelian group $G$, and we study its foundational properties. Moreover, we prove a categorical equivalence between (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over $R$ and derived (formal) comodules over a certain comonad constructed from the group ring $R[G]$ of $G$ over $R$.
papers.comments: 42 pages; Lemma 5.1 in v2 is false, which required major revision. The revised material appears in Sections 5 and 6 of this version

papers.title: Normalized solutions for a critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg equation: the effect of the weights on the coupling range
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions of $-\mathrm{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) = λ|x|^{-2a}u + β|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u + |x|^{-b2^\sharp}|u|^{2^\sharp-2}u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx = ρ^2$, where $0 < a < \frac{N-2}{2}$, $a < b < a+1$, $2 < q < 2^\sharp$, and $2^\sharp$ is the critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg exponent. Let $q_c$ denote the mass-critical exponent. For $2 < q < q_c$ and small $β> 0$, we obtain two positive radial solutions: a local minimizer with negative energy and a solution of mountain-pass type. For $q_c \le q < 2^\sharp$, there is a number $β_0 \ge 0$, defined through the energy level below which compactness holds, such that a positive radial ground state exists for every $β> β_0$. In the mass-critical case $q = q_c$, this holds for $β_0 < β< β^*$, where $β^*$ is explicit, and for $β\ge β^*$ the ground state level is zero and is not attained. Our main result is a necessary and sufficient condition on $N$, $a$, $b$ and $q$ for $β_0 > 0$. The condition holds only when $a$ is close to $\frac{N-2}{2}$, and it fails in the formal unweighted limit $a = b = 0$. When $β_0 > 0$, the ground state level is not attained for $0 < β< β_0$, and every normalized solution has energy above the compactness level. When $β_0 = 0$, we describe the behavior of ground states as $β\to 0$. The proofs combine the Pohozaev constraint, sharp estimates for the extremals of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, and a blow-up analysis in Emden-Fowler variables.

papers.title: Transversal gates for quantum CSS codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we focus on the problem of computing the set of diagonal transversal gates fixing a CSS code. We determine the logical actions of these gates and characterize the subgroups that induce tensor products of single-qubit logical gates and logical identities. We describe these groups through explicit linear equations given by componentwise products of basis vectors of the underlying classical codes, which is the key difference from previous approaches. We compute the complete set of diagonal transversal gates fixing the code, and of transversal logical gates, for any CSS code arising from monomial codes, a family that includes decreasing monomial codes and polar codes. As a consequence, we recover and extend some results in the literature on CSS-T codes, triorthogonal codes, and divisible codes. We also extend these results to diagonal gates acting transversally on several code blocks and use them to characterize addressable gates.

papers.title: Gradient-based collective and structured nonlinear dimension reduction with quadratic surrogates
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the approximation of continuously differentiable functions with high-dimensional input by a composition of two functions: a feature map that extracts few features from the input space, and a profile function that approximates the target function taking the features as its low-dimensional input. We focus on the construction of structured nonlinear feature maps, that extract features on separate groups of variables, using a recently introduced gradient-based method that leverages Poincaré inequalities on nonlinear manifolds. This method consists in minimizing a non-convex loss functional, which can be a challenging task, especially for small training samples. We first investigate a collective setting, in which we construct a feature map suitable to a parametrized family of high-dimensional functions. In this setting we introduce a new quadratic surrogate to the non-convex loss function and show an upper bound on the latter. We then investigate a grouped setting, in which we construct separate feature maps for separate groups of inputs, and we show that this setting is almost equivalent to multiple collective settings, one for each group of variables.

papers.title: Taylor-Accelerated Neural Network Interpolation Operators on Irregular Grids: Higher-Order Approximation and Derivative-Informed Field Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, a new class of Taylor-accelerated neural-network interpolation operators is introduced for quasi-uniform, irregularly distributed grids to reconstruct derivative-informed physical fields in both univariate and multivariate settings. The framework incorporates Taylor expansions within the neural network operators framework, allowing operators to efficiently utilize the smoothness of the target function. We determine the analytical properties of the proposed operators, including well-posedness, uniform boundedness, and exact interpolation at the sampling nodes. Additionally, we establish polynomial reproduction to a specified degree and provide Jackson-type error estimates based on higher-order moduli of smoothness, thereby improving convergence rates on quasi-uniform, irregular grids. The applicability of the method is demonstrated by reconstructing physical fields such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and fluid properties, including pressure and velocity. The numerical results show that the proposed operators provide reliable, accurate estimates in the presence of noise and irregular sampling. The enhanced accuracy of the proposed method is validated by comparing it with current interpolation systems on irregular grids, including Lagrange-type methods.

papers.title: Minimum $\mathcal{F}$-covers: the supersolvable and metabelian cases
papers.abstract: Given a set $\mathcal{F}$ of finite groups, it is said that a group $G$ is an $\mathcal{F}$-cover if every group in $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $G$. Moreover, $G$ is a minimum $\mathcal{F}$-cover if there is no $\mathcal{F}$-cover whose order is less than $|G|$. In [Cameron P. J., et al., Minimal cover groups, J. Algebra 660 (2024)], the authors pose the following question: For which classes $\mathcal{X}$ of groups, closed under taking subgroups and direct products, is it true that, if $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of $\mathcal{X}$-groups, then there is a minimum $\mathcal{F}$-cover which is an $\mathcal{X}$-group? In this paper, we give a negative answer in two cases: $\mathcal{X}\in \{``supersolvable", ``metabelian"\}.$
papers.comments: accepted for publication in The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics

papers.title: On some problems regarding $LCM$-groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and denote by $o(g)$ the order of an element $g\in G$. We say that $G$ is an $LCM$-group if $o(x^ny)$ is a divisor of the least common multiple of $o(x^n)$ and $o(y)$ for all $x, y\in G$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This paper extends some existing results on $LCM$-groups, such as the structure of a minimal non-$LCM$-group, and establishes criteria for $G$ to be an $LCM$-group or a nilpotent group. We also prove that, in general, a minimum cover of a finite set of $LCM$-groups is not an $LCM$-group, and we answer two questions posed by M. Amiri.
papers.comments: accepted for publication in Comm. Algebra

papers.title: Constructions of contractibility in finite subset spaces
papers.abstract: The space of all finite non-empty subsets of a topological space $X$, also known as the Ran space of $X$, is weakly contractible for $X$ path connected. We consider subspaces $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ of the Ran space given by all subsets of $X$ of size at most $n$, and their first homotopy groups. These groups are known to be trivial for $n\geqslant 3$, though the proofs are not constructive. We draw an explicit contraction in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 3}(S^1)$ of the generator of $π_1(S^1)$, which we then use to conclude that the induced maps $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 2n+1}(X))$ and $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n+2}(X))$ are trivial for all positive integers $n$. Pathological maps with infinitely many strata changes in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ are resolved via locally contractible neighbourhoods and exit paths. From this we conclude the triviality of $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X))$, for all $n\geqslant 3$.
papers.comments: Major revision, simpler construction, stronger results. Comments welcome

papers.title: Base Change Of Fundamental Group Schemes
papers.abstract: Let $K/k$ be a field extension, $X$ a connected quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over $k$ with a rational point $x$, $p:X_K\to X$ the natural projection, $\mathcal{C}_X$ and $\mathcal{C}_{X_K}$ the Tannakian categories whose objects consist of vector bundles on $X$ and $X_K$ respectively. We give criteria for the natural homomorphism $π(\mathcal C_{X_K},x_K)\toπ(\mathcal C_X,x)_K$ to be an isomorphism. Suppose further $X$ is geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$. As applications, we prove base change isomorphisms for $π^{\acute{e}t},π^{E\acute{e}t}$ under arbitrary extensions and for $π^S,π^N,π^{EN}$ under arbitrary algebraic extensions; a cuspidal cubic curve example shows that it can fail for purely transcendental extensions. In positive characteristic, base change isomorphism holds for $π^{Loc}$ and $π^{ELoc}$ under separable algebraic extensions; an elliptic curve example shows that it can fail for finite purely inseparable extensions.

papers.title: On Fujita's conjecture for a general hyperkähler manifold in the standard series of examples
papers.abstract: For the moduli spaces $\mathcal{V}(K3)_{d,t}^n$ and $\mathcal{V}(\text{Kum})_{d,t}^n$ of polarized hyperkähler manifolds of $\text{Hilb}^n(K3)$-type and $\text{Kum}^n$-type respectively, with polarization with square $2d$ and divisibility $t$, we study general base point freeness and very ampleness of the polarization. We provide conditions, in terms of $n, d, t$ that guarantee that the general polarization, in any connected component of these moduli spaces, to be base point free or very ample.
papers.comments: Improved main results to work also in the case the moduli space is not connected, giving lower bounds on d which are linear in terms if n, and, at worst, quadratic in term of t. 23 pages; no figures. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Constrained Mean Field Games with Grushin type dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to a class of finite horizon deterministic mean field games with Grushin type dynamics, state constraints and nonlocal coupling. First, we consider the optimal control problem that each agent aims to solve when the evolution of the population is given and we establish some properties as: the existence of an optimal trajectory for any starting point $(x,t)$, the closed graph property for the multivalued map which associates to each point $(x,t)$ the set of optimal trajectories starting from that point, endowed with a suitable notion of convergence, the continuity of the value function. The main issue to overcome is due to the local interplay at boundary points between the set of state constraints and the degenerate dynamics. To this end, we shall point out two different sets of assumptions which are both sufficient for these properties. Afterwards, we tackle the mean field games; taking advantage of the aforementioned properties, we prove the existence of a relaxed equilibrium (which describes the evolution of the game in terms of a probability on the set of admissible trajectories) and derive the existence of a mild solution (which is a couple formed by the value function for the generic player and a family of time dependent measures on the state).

papers.title: On the triple product property for subgroups of finite groups of nilpotency class $2$
papers.abstract: Some non-trivial upper bounds are proved relating to the triple product property (TPP) for subgroups of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ using elementary group theory. The TPP is the property defined for three non-empty subsets $S, T, U$ of a group $G$ that the group equation $s's^{-1}t't^{-1}u'u^{-1} = 1$, over pairs of elements $s', s \in S$, $t', t \in T$, $u', u \in U$, is satisfied if and only if $s' = s$, $t' = t$, $u' = u$. When $G$ is finite, and the parameter $ρ_0(G)$, called \emph{subgroup TPP ratio}, is defined as $ρ_0(G) := \max\frac{|S||T||U|}{|G|}$, where the maximum is over the collection of all triples of subgroups $S, T, U$ of $G$ satisfying the TPP, this paper proves that \textup{(1)} $ρ_0(G) < \sqrt{G:Z(G)}$} for (all) groups of nilpotency class $2$, \textup{(2)} $ρ_0(G) \leq p$ for $p$-groups with a cyclic commutator subgroup of order $p$, \textup{(3)} $ρ_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with a "large" centre such that either $G/Z(G)$ is isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p$ or $C_{p^2} \times C_p$, \textup{(4)} and $ρ_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with "small" (irreducible, complex) character degrees of $1$ or $p$ where $G/Z(G)$ is not isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p \times C_p$.
papers.comments: 23 pages, including abstract, references and an appendix with three tables. This version contains corrections, as well as additional detail and preliminary results, for the results on extraspecial groups. The title has been updated for clarity, and the subject classifications have also been updated (removal of 68R05, addition of 20D15)

papers.title: An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting
papers.abstract: We collect open problems in permutation patterns on four themes: rank-unimodality in the permutation pattern poset and log-convexity of principal classes, Wilf-equivalence and shape-Wilf-equivalence, the enumeration of derangements in permutation classes, and sorting by stacks in series, generalized stacks, and restricted containers (C-machines).

papers.title: On problems of Erdős and Baumann-Briggs on minimising the density of $s$-cliques in graphs with forbidden subgraphs
papers.abstract: Using flag algebras, we prove that the minimum density of $8$-cliques in a large graph without an independent set of size $3$ is $491411/268435456+o(1)$, thus resolving a new case of an old problem of Erdős [Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. 7 (1962) 459-464]. Also, we establish some other results of this type; for example, we show that the minimum $s$-clique density in a large graph with no independent set of size 3 nor an induced 5-cycle is $2^{1-s}+o(1)$ when $s=4,5,6$. For each of these results, we also describe the structure of all extremal and almost extremal graphs of large order $n$. These results are applied to give an asymptotic solution to a number of cases of the problem of Baumann and Briggs [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025) P1.22] which asks for the minimum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph in which every $k$-set spans a $t$-clique.

papers.title: Approximation of invariant measures for stochastic functional differential equations with infinite delay via an explicit finite-memory scheme
papers.abstract: Owing to the intrinsic computational limitation that infinite memory cannot be stored numerically, the approximation of invariant probability measures (IPMs) for stochastic functional differential equations (SFDEs) with infinite delay remains an open problem. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an explicit finite-memory truncated Euler-Maruyama scheme that combines memory and state truncation for such SFDEs. We establish strong convergence of the numerical segment process over any finite time horizon and obtain a convergence order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. We further prove that this numerical segment process admits a unique IPM and that its IPM converges to the exact counterpart under the $L^2$-Wasserstein metric as the step size vanishes, with an explicit convergence rate. The framework applies to both linear and superlinear coefficients.

papers.title: Design of Hierarchical Excitable Networks
papers.abstract: We provide a method to systematically construct vector fields for which the dynamics display transitions corresponding to a desired hierarchical connection structure. This structure is given as a finite set of directed graphs $\mathbf{G}_1,\dotsc,\mathbf{G}_N$ (the lower level), together with another digraph $\mathbfΓ$ on $N$ vertices (the top level). The dynamic realizations of $\mathbf{G}_1,\dotsc,\mathbf{G}_N$ are heteroclinic networks and they can be thought of as individual connection patterns on a given set of states. Edges in $\mathbfΓ$ correspond to transitions between these different patterns. In our construction, the connections given through $\mathbfΓ$ are not heteroclinic, but excitable with zero threshold. This describes a dynamical transition between two invariant sets where every $δ$-neighborhood of the first set contains an initial condition with $ω$-limit in the second set. Thus, we prove a theorem that allows the systematic creation of hierarchical networks that are excitable on the top level, and heteroclinic on the lower level. Our results modify and extend the simplex realization method by Ashwin & Postlethwaite.

papers.title: Dimension of the singular set in the parabolic obstacle problem
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the singular set in the parabolic obstacle problem for general obstacles $\varphi \in C^{2,1}$, with $Δ\varphi < 0$. We prove that the singular set has parabolic Hausdorff dimension at most $n-1$. Prior to our result, this was only known when $Δ\varphi \equiv -1$. Our approach combines a truncated parabolic frequency formula and monotonicity estimates with an iterative argument showing that the frequency is saturated for all values of the truncation parameter between $2$ and $3$.

papers.title: The mathematical landscape of partial information decomposition: A comprehensive review of properties and measures
papers.abstract: Partial Information Decomposition (PID) has become one of the most prominent information-theoretic frameworks for describing the structure and quality of information in complex systems. Despite its widespread utility, there exists no unique solution constraining precisely how a PID should be constructed, leading to a multiverse of different formalisms with different mathematical commitments. In this work, we provide a comprehensive overview of the mathematical landscape of PID. By integrating existing PID measures into a common language, we systematically examine all major approaches to the PID framework that have emerged so far, determining for each measure whether or not each known property holds. In addition, we derive a web of all known theorems mapping the relationships and incompatibilities between these properties, before also revealing some novel interdependency results. In doing so, we chart a brief history of the framework, promote a unified perspective for its discussions, and offer a path towards both theoretical refinement and informed empirical applications for the future of this powerful method.

papers.title: Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton Method for Efficient Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Computing exact optimal transport (OT) distances at large scale remains computationally challenging. Entropy-regularized OT can be solved efficiently, but its solution is biased toward the regularized problem, and small regularization parameters often lead to slow convergence and numerical instability. In this paper, we propose \emph{Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton} (IBSN), an efficient method for high-accuracy computation of the original OT problem. Building on a verifiable inexact Bregman proximal framework, IBSN develops a sparse Newton inner solver tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which yields a lower-dimensional Newton system. To accelerate the inner subproblem solves, we introduce a Hessian sparsification strategy tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which reduces the cost of Newton direction computation while preserving key spectral properties. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting algorithm, including convergence of the inner sparse Newton iterations and global convergence of the overall method to an optimal OT solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that IBSN is effective in high-accuracy regimes and compares favorably with representative first-order and second-order OT solvers.

papers.title: A Known M-Curve of Degree 8 in OSCAR
papers.abstract: We show how the computer algebra system OSCAR can be used to retrace geometric constructions of plane algebraic curves and provide topologically correct and visually pleasing drawings. The approach is illustrated on Shustin's construction from 1987 of a particular M-curve of degree eight. We arrive at an explicit homogeneous trivariate polynomial with rational coefficients, and we provide a computational proof of all claimed properties of Shustin's original article.

papers.title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin and has the origin in the interior of its support, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a gauge on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a reduction to a two-dimensional inequality derived from Prékopa's theorem, which may be of independent interest. As a consequence of this extension, we resolve a nearly 30-year-old question of Richard Gardner and Gaoyong Zhang in the affirmative. In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_p K$ of a convex body $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for $p>-1$. Furthermore, they established that $R_p K$ is convex for $p\geq 0$, but the convexity of $R_p K$ for $p\in (-1,0)$ remained open. We prove that $R_p K$ is convex for all $p>-1$.
papers.comments: 23 pages. Substantially simplified presentation by assuming g in LC satisfies max g = g(0) and the origin lies in the interior of its support. Earlier versions treated the boundary case with lengthy proofs and approximation arguments that diluted the main results and proof ideas. These cases will be revisited in future work. Minor technical improvements throughout

papers.title: Discrete Gaussian Free Field via Hadamard's formula
papers.abstract: We establish a discrete Hadamard variational formula for Green operators on weighted graphs along an increasing family of subgraphs. The increment of the Green operator factors through harmonic extension from the newly added layer and the positive square root of its boundary Green operator. This gives a dimension-free decomposition of the Green kernel and an associated isometric Hadamard operator. As an application, the discrete Gaussian free field is constructed by successively adding independent harmonically extended Gaussian contributions. The formulation uses only the graph structure and its conductances, without smoothness assumptions. For nested square-lattice approximations of smooth planar domains, we also prove convergence of the growing fields in finite-dimensional distributions and convergence of the integrated Hadamard increments as Green-operator forms.

papers.title: On uniform large genus asymptotics of Witten's intersection numbers
papers.abstract: Following ideas from [14], we give a uniform large genus asymptotics for primitive psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of stable algebraic curves, and extend this result including insertions of zeros in a certain uniform way. Application to a particular formal solution of the Painlevé I equation is given. We also use a method from [14] to give a new proof of the polynomiality conjecture on large genus asymptotic expansions of psi-class intersection numbers.
papers.comments: We corrected an error in the statement of Theorem 2, and updated its proof. We also corrected a few typos. 23 pages

papers.title: A Simple Categorical Calculus of Interacting Processes
papers.abstract: We present a calculus that models a simple sort of process interaction. Our calculus consists of a collection of terms together with a rewrite relation, parameterised by an arbitrary multicategory whose morphisms we understand as non-interactive processes. We show that our calculus is confluent and terminating, and that terms modulo the induced convertibility relation form a virtual double category. We relate our calculus to the free cornering of a monoidal category, which is a double-categorical model of process interaction that is similar in spirit to the calculus presented herein. Precisely, we construct a functor from the virtual double category given by our calculus into the underlying virtual double category of the free cornering of the free monoidal category on the multicategory of non-interacting processes. If we think of the terms of our calculus as programs and the rewriting system as an operational semantics for these programs, this functor gives a sound denotational semantics for our calculus in terms of the free cornering.
papers.comments: To appear in the post-proceedings of MFPS 2026

papers.title: A Mathematical Framework for Linear Response Theory for Nonautonomous Systems
papers.abstract: Linear Response theory aims to predict how added forcing alters the statistical properties of a system. This has been predominantly studied for autonomous dynamical systems, yet many systems in the physical, natural, and social sciences are inherently nonautonomous. In such settings, one would like to understand how the system's time-dependent statistical properties change when additional infinitesimal forcings are applied. This question is of clear practical relevance, but from a rigorous mathematical viewpoint it has been addressed only for a few specific classes of systems and perturbations. Here we provide a rigorous linear response theory for a rather general class of deterministic and random nonautonomous systems satisfying a specific set of assumptions that are the counterpart of the standard assumptions used in the autonomous setting. A central ingredient is rapid loss of memory along the nonautonomous evolution. Our main strategy is to reformulate the sequential dynamics as a fixed-point problem for a global transfer operator acting on an extended sequence space of measures. This yields explicit and readily implementable causal response formulas for predicting the effect of small perturbations on time-dependent statistical states. We illustrate the theory on two representative classes: sequential compositions of expanding maps and sequential compositions of noisy random maps. We also establish linear response for reflected Euler-Maruyama discretizations of dissipative nonautonomous stochastic differential equations with nondegenerate additive Gaussian noise, on fixed compact domains. As a physical application, we study the response of a Ghil-Sellers climate energy balance model, discretized in latitude and time to a time-dependent perturbation of the greenhouse parameter.
papers.comments: Further revision. We enriched the introduction and simplified the applications to Euler-Maruyama dicretizations of SDE and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance model

papers.title: Fixed-Point Delayed Subgradient Methods for Nonsmooth Convex Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the nonsmooth convex optimization problems over the fixed point constraint sets of firmly nonexpansive operators. To find an optimal solution of the problem, we present an iterative method based on the hybrid steepest descent method and the idea of a delayed subgradient scheme in which allows the use of staled subgradients from the earlier iteration when updating the next iteration. We start the convergence part by deriving an upper bound for the difference of the best-achieved function values and the optimal value. After that, to ensure the convergence in iterations, we prove that there exists a subsequence of the generated sequence by the proposed method which converges to an optimal solution. Moreover, we subsequently show that the whole generated sequence converges to an optimal solution when the strict convexity of the objective function is imposed. Further, we extend the presented results to the inexact version and the centralized network system consisting of a finite number of workers and a central server. Finally, we apply the proposed method to image inpainting problems. The numerical results describe the effect of delay in many cases of objective functions.

papers.title: From cut sets to cube complexes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain an action on a cube complex from an action on a path-connected topological space with a system of divisions. In the settings of hyperbolic groups or relatively hyperbolic groups with no peripheral splittings, our result provides an alternate route to Sageev's construction of a cube complex action from a collection of (relatively) quasiconvex subgroups of a (relatively) hyperbolic group.
papers.comments: v2: 29 pages, better discussion of related work

papers.title: Residual Recombination Methods as Anderson-like Acceleration: An Algebraic Interpretation of BoostConv
papers.abstract: BoostConv has been introduced in earlier works as an effective acceleration technique for nonlinear iterative processes and has been successfully employed in a variety of applications to enhance convergence rates or to compute unstable fixed points that are otherwise inaccessible through standard approaches. Despite its demonstrated practical effectiveness, the theoretical properties of the method have not yet been fully characterized. In this work, we present a more robust formulation of the BoostConv algorithm and, for the first time, provide a rigorous proof of its local convergence. The proposed analysis places BoostConv within a precise mathematical framework, clarifying its interpretation as a nonlinear convergence accelerator and establishing sufficient conditions under which convergence to a fixed point is guaranteed. The theoretical findings are illustrated through several numerical examples, spanning from a linear problem to a low-dimensional benchmark and a large-scale incompressible Navier-Stokes simulation. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical relevance of the proposed method and bridge the gap between empirical performance and rigorous analysis, paving the way for further developments and applications to complex nonlinear problems.

papers.title: $p$-Ordinary Part of Hyperbolic Cycles on Modular Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study hyperbolic cycles in the first homology group of congruence subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with local coefficients. We prove that, for any prime number $p$, the $p$-ordinary part of the first homology group is generated by hyperbolic cycles.

papers.title: Piecewise M-Stationarity and Convergence of a Bounding Algorithm for Mathematical Programs with Complementarity Constraints
papers.abstract: This study explores B-stationarity condition for mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCCs) and convergence of a Bounding Algorithm we proposed in [33]. Special attention is given to the cases with biactive complementarity constraints. First, we introduce the concept of piecewise M-stationarity and prove its equivalence to B-stationarity under MPCC-GCQ. Then, this concept is employed to propose a simplified B-stationarity verifica- tion. Finally, we investigate improved convergence properties of the Bounding Algorithm in [33]. Limit points of this method are shown to be C-stationary, based on the stationarity of an approaching sequence; moreover, they are piece-wise M-stationary (and therefore B-stationary), if an additional second-order condition is satisfied by the sequence.

papers.title: On a stable partnership problem with integer choice functions
papers.abstract: We consider a far generalization of the well-known stable roommates and non-bipartite stable allocation problems. In its setting, one is given a finite non-bipartite graph $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative integer edge capacities $b(e)\in{\mathbb Z}_+$, $e\in E$, in which for each vertex (``agent'') $v\in V$, the preferences on the set $E_v$ of its incident edges are given via a choice function $C_v$ acting on the vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_+^{E_v}$ bounded by the capacities and obeying the standard axioms of substitutability and size monotonicity. We refer to the related stability problem as the stable partnership problem with integer choice functions, or SPPIC for short. Extending well-known results for particular cases, we give a solvability criterion for SPPIC and develop an algorithm of finding a stable solution, called a stable partnership, or establishing that there is none. Moreover, in general the algorithm constructs a pair $(x,{\cal K})$ such that $x\in {\mathbb Z}_+^E$ and ${\cal K}$ is a set of pairwise edge-disjoint odd cycles in $G$ satisfying the following properties: if ${\cal K}=\emptyset$, then $x$ is a stable partnership, whereas if ${\cal K}$ is nonempty, then a stable partnership does not exist, and in this case, the set ${\cal K}$ is determined canonically. Our constructions essentially use earlier author's results on the corresponding bipartite counterpart of SPPIC. Keywords: stable marriage problem, stable roommates problem, stable partition, stable allocation, choice function
papers.journal_ref: Discrete Applied Math., Vol.397, 2026, pp.345-359. Free share link until Dec.15, 2026: https://authors.elsevier.com/a/1n-qk_,OC1pQzC

papers.title: New Characterizations of Nonsmooth Convex Functions via Generalized Derivatives
papers.abstract: This paper studies the convexity properties of nonsmooth extended-real-valued weakly convex functions, a class of functions that is central to modern optimization and its applications. We establish new characterizations of convexity using second-order generalized derivative tools, including subgradient graphical derivatives, second subderivatives, and second-order subdifferentials. These tools allow us to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for convexity in the nonsmooth framework.

papers.title: Galois representation of the product of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the adelic Galois representations attached to products of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic. As a function-field analogue of Serre's open image theorem for products of elliptic curves, we show that the image of the joint adelic representation is commensurable with the subgroup defined by the natural determinant compatibility conditions if and only if at least one of the two Drinfeld modules has potential complex multiplication, or the two modules are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist. Our proof combines Pink's theory of minimal quasi-models, explicit reciprocity laws from global class field theory, and an analysis of residual Galois representations. As an arithmetic application, we prove a torsion finiteness result: if one of the Drinfeld modules has no potential complex multiplication and the two are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist, then that Drinfeld module has only finitely many torsion points over the compositum of the maximal abelian extension of the base field and the torsion field of the other module. This is an analogue of the classical results of Ribet and Zarhin for abelian varieties.
papers.comments: Compared with v3, this 40-page version removes the strong supersingular reduction condition from the main theorem, making the adelic open image result unconditional. We also prove a stronger torsion-finiteness result. The manuscript has been thoroughly revised for clarity; comments are welcome

papers.title: Minimizing the Age of Incorrect Information of Discrete-Time Markov Sources With Hybrid ARQ
papers.abstract: This work introduces a framework for analyzing the Age of Incorrect Information (AoII) in a real-time monitoring system with a generic discrete-time Markov source. We study a noisy communication system employing a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) protocol, subject to a transmission rate constraint. The optimization problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP), and it is shown that there exists an optimal policy that is a randomized mixture of two stationary policies. To overcome the intractability of computing the optimal stationary policies, we develop a multiple-threshold policy class where thresholds depend on the source, the receiver, and the packet count. By establishing a Markov renewal structure induced by threshold policies, we derive closed-form expressions for the long-term average AoII and transmission rate. The proposed policy is constructed via a relative value iteration algorithm that leverages the threshold structure to skip computations, combined with a bisection search to satisfy the rate constraint. To accommodate scenarios requiring lower computational complexity, we adapt the same technique to produce a simpler single-threshold policy that trades optimality for efficiency. Numerical experiments exhibit that both thresholdbased policies outperform periodic scheduling, with the multiplethreshold approach matching the performance of the globally optimal policy.

papers.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
papers.abstract: Given a strict partial order $Δ$ on a set $Λ$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(Δ)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(Δ)$, where $Δ$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(Δ)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$Δ$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(Δ)/G(Γ)\cong G(Δ\setminusΓ)$, where $Γ$ is a normal subset of $Δ$, and $G(Γ)$ and $G(Δ\setminusΓ)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.

papers.title: Transmission permutations and Demazure products in Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
papers.abstract: A line bundle on a curve with two marked points can be special in many ways, as measured by the global sections of all of its twists by these points. All of this information is conveniently packaged into a permutation, which we call the transmission permutation. We prove that when twice-marked curves are chained together, these permutations are composed via the Demazure product; in reverse, bundles with given permutation can be enumerated via reduced decompositions of a permutation. This paper demonstrates the utility of transmission permutations by giving a short derivation of the basic dimension bounds of both classical Brill--Noether theory and Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory in a unified framework. The difference between the two cases derives from taking permutations in either symmetric groups or affine symmetric groups.
papers.comments: 17 pages. v2: minor corrections and improvements

papers.title: Exact solution of the ruin problem in the Cramér--Lundberg with proportional investments and the limits of applicability of the power-law asymptotics
papers.abstract: The Cramér-Lundberg model with exponential claims and proportional investment is solved exactly: the integro-differential equation for the survival probability reduces to a doubly confluent Heun equation, yielding an explicit solution in terms of Heun functions, a verification theorem, and a qualitative analysis of ruin probability versus investment share.

papers.title: Semiprojective Banach lattices
papers.abstract: We study a norm-controlled notion of semiprojectivity for Banach lattices, testing sequential quotient towers in separable ambient lattices and requiring arbitrarily small norm loss at a fixed stage. For a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space $X$, we prove that $C_0(X)$ is semiprojective if and only if $X$ is compact and an absolute neighbourhood retract. Finite $\ell_1$-sums preserve semiprojectivity, and arbitrary $\ell_1$-sums of $1^+$-projective lattices are semiprojective without any order-unit assumption. By contrast, $\mathbb{R} \oplus_\infty \ell_1$ fails to be semiprojective, showing that neither semiprojectivity nor $1^+$-projectivity is preserved by finite $\ell_\infty$-sums, extensions, or pullbacks over a projective base. Every separable semiprojective lattice is $λ$-projective for some finite $λ$, and its scalar-valued lattice homomorphisms separate points. Consequently, a separable reflexive Banach lattice is semiprojective precisely when it is finite-dimensional, and no nonzero separable atomless order-continuous lattice is semiprojective. We also characterise $\ell$-openness as $1^+$-projectivity relative to separable ambient lattices; for separable domains this is ordinary $1^+$-projectivity. The restriction to separable ambient lattices is redundant for separable domains but affects the nonseparable examples.

papers.title: The Huang Algebra Ideal and the Diagonal Shift Property
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a grading-restricted vertex algebra and let $A^\infty(V )=U^\infty(V)/Q^\infty(V)$ be the associative algebra constructed by Huang, where $U^\infty(V)$ is the space of column-finite infinite matrices with entries in $V$ and $Q^\infty(V)$ is an ideal of a (nonassociative) algebra structure on $U^\infty(V)$ defined by Huang. Huang introduced families of elements in $Q^\infty(V)$ and conjectured that these elements generate $Q^\infty(V)$. We introduce the ``diagonal shift property" and prove that the elements that Huang conjectured as a generating set for $Q^\infty(V)$ satisfy this property. On the other hand, in the case that $V$ is the rank one Heisenberg vertex operator algebra, we construct infinitely many linearly independent elements in $Q^\infty(V)$ that do not satisfy the diagonal shift property. As a corollary, we disprove Huang's conjecture.
papers.comments: Final version, to appear in the Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\), without imposing finiteness conditions on \(Λ^!\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, thereby closing a gap left open in the work of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: Flat Lorentzian Lie groups: A complete description
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a complete structural description of flat Lorentzian Lie groups, i.e., Lie groups endowed with a flat left invariant Lorentzian metric, thereby resolving a long-standing open problem in the theory of pseudo-Riemannian Lie groups. Our main result shows that any flat Lorentzian Lie group either admits a timelike parallel left-invariant vector field or is of Kundt type, and that in both cases the underlying Lie algebra falls into one of six explicit classes. A key ingredient of the proof is a refined analysis of the double extension process, which reveals that all flat Lorentzian Lie algebras arise - directly or in a generalized sense - from flat Euclidean ones. As a consequence, we obtain easily a complete classification in dimensions three and four, recovering and unifying several previously known partial results.
papers.comments: 65 pages, 8 Tables, third version, many typos an errors corrected. Submitted

papers.title: Generalized Howe curves of genus 4, 5, and 6 with completely decomposable Jacobians
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves are important objects in number theory and algebraic geometry, and the existence of such a curve of genus $g \geq 4$ is an open problem, for general characteristics $p > 0$. As a computational approach to this problem, Kudo-Harashita-Howe (2020) showed that a superspecial curve of genus 4 exists in each characteristic $p$ with $7 < p < 20000$. Their method restricted attention to a specific class of curves, known as Howe curves, for which superspeciality is reduced to those of curves of genus at most 2. In this paper, we focus on a more specific class of curves, namely Howe curves whose Jacobians decompose into a product of four elliptic curves. By restricting our attention to such curves, the superspeciality reduces to the supersingularity of elliptic curves, which enables us to construct a superspecial curve of genus 4 more efficiently than Kudo-Harashita-Howe's method.
