As our first main result, we confirmed by computer the existence of such superspecial curves of genus 4 in characteristics $p$ with $20000 < p < 10^6$. Using a similar approach, we also propose constructions of superspecial curves of genera 5 and 6 from only supersingular elliptic curves. Furthermore, computational experiments establish the existence of superspecial curves of genus 5 (resp. genus 6) in characteristics $p$ with $13 < p < 10^5$ (resp. $7 < p < 10^5$).

papers.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.
papers.comments: 14 pages. v2: fixed a few typos

papers.title: Uniqueness and Mixing in the Low-Temperature Random-Cluster Model on Trees and Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the random-cluster model on trees and treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p\in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q\in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, approximately sampling from this model on graphs of degree at most $Δ$ is computationally hard. At parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf{u}}(q,Δ)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all bounded degree graphs. On typical graphs (e.g., random regular graphs), the same is predicted at $p > p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$, where $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $Δ$-regular wired tree. Our first result establishes this non-uniqueness/uniqueness phase transition at $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ for all $q$ on the infinite $Δ$-regular wired tree, resolving a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m (1996). For this, we establish weak spatial mixing at $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ under sufficiently wired boundary conditions. We use this understanding of decay of correlations to show that on the wired tree on $n$ vertices, whenever $q>1$ and $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$, the mixing time of random-cluster Glauber dynamics is a near-optimal $n^{1+o(1)}$. We then extend these results on spatial and temporal mixing from the tree to treelike geometries with mostly wired boundaries and use them to show that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix rapidly on the random $Δ$-regular graph for all $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ as long as $q \ge C \log Δ$, providing an efficient sampling algorithm for both the random-cluster and Potts models in this context.

papers.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $δ_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ of the minimum distance function $δ_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $δ_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$. We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.

papers.title: Global Hopf bifurcation and symmetric periodic solutions in multi-agent systems with pseudoneutral memory
papers.abstract: We study the emergence of symmetric oscillatory behavior in multi-agent systems where each agent incorporates distributed memory of past states and feedback from changes in its response over a finite time window. The latter admits a neutral-form presentation but reduces to a finite difference of delayed states. The closed-loop dynamics are therefore described by a system of nonlinear retarded functional differential equations with a high degree of symmetry, arising from a network of homogeneous agents. By reformulating the problem as a fixed point operator equation, we apply equivariant degree theory to establish rigorous conditions for unbounded global Hopf bifurcation from the consensus equilibrium. Our main results provide sufficient conditions for the local asymptotic stability of consensus and for the existence of unbounded global branches of non-constant periodic solutions with prescribed spatio-temporal symmetries. The question of whether such periodic solutions are stable (and therefore constitute periodic multiconsensus) is not resolved by the degree method; we address it in an illustrative example via numerical simulations. The example, which models eight coupled asset markets with chartist traders and fundamentalists, demonstrates how memory-driven instability can generate periodic boom-bust cycles across clusters of assets. The numerical example illustrates the predicted two-cluster pattern, and Floquet computations provide numerical evidence of local orbital asymptotic stability at sampled parameter values.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Quantum Groups Revisited
papers.abstract: We present the RLL-realization of extended orthosymplectic quantum supergroups for any parity sequence, with R-matrices evaluated in the earlier work [Lett. Math. Phys. 116 (2026), 55, 97 pages, arXiv:2408.16720]. Our isomorphism is compatible with the internal structure of generalized doubles. We also relate different sign conventions through 2-cocycle twists.

papers.title: Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the variational problems associated with the $L^2$-norms of the normal and tangent curvature tensors for submanifolds immersed in a unit sphere. We define the critical points of these functionals under normal variations as Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds, for which we explicitly establish the Euler-Lagrange equations in terms of the second fundamental form. Furthermore, by investigating the focal submanifolds of OT-FKM isoparametric hypersurfaces, we construct infinitely many non-trivial examples of both Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds. Notably, the curvature tensors of these examples generally do not satisfy the classical Yang-Mills equations.
papers.comments: 34 pages; corrected a sign in the definition of $\mathcal{H}^{T}$; revised the expression for $\mathcal{H}^{N}$ and corrected Theorem 1.6(1), with a complete treatment of the remaining cases; all other conclusions remain unchanged

papers.title: Continuum-marginal optimal transport: a mesh-free kernel method
papers.abstract: In this paper we study continuum-marginal optimal transport. Given a time-continuous family of probability marginals, the problem is to recover the minimum-energy velocity field whose flow reproduces every marginal. This problem is the continuum limit of the classical two-marginal Benamou-Brenier formulation, and also the deterministic limit of the Nelson problem of stochastic optimal transport. We propose a practical mesh-free solver for this problem. The weak continuity equation is embedded in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, yielding a sample-only objective that requires no spatial discretization. The velocity is parametrized by any linear-in-parameters dictionary or neural network, and is optimized by mini-batch stochastic methods. Synthetic experiments confirm that the method achieves accurate drift recovery and marginal consistency. The same computational framework also applies to the Nelson problem.
papers.comments: Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (10/2026). Reviewed on OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=1bzgCxWYpr. 48 pages, 16 figures, 14 tables

papers.title: Capacity-Aware Multi-UE Handover Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks Using Dueling DDQN
papers.abstract: Frequent handovers and finite satellite capacity make multi-user mobility management challenging in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks. This paper develops a capacity-aware multi-user handover framework based on a double deep Q-network (DDQN) with a dueling architecture. Both training and evaluation employ sequential user equipment (UE) processing with shared satellite occupancy, while action masking excludes invisible or capacity-infeasible satellites. The state incorporates satellite visibility, achievable link quality, remaining capacity, previous association, short-term visibility, and time information. A fixed multi-criteria reward balances throughput, blocking, handover cost, connection persistence, and short-term visibility, while expert trajectories are used only for replay-buffer initialization. Simulations under different UE densities and satellite capacities show that the proposed framework maintains high average throughput per UE and low blocking rates with moderate handover frequency. Ablation results show that removing the remaining-capacity vector has only a limited effect on performance when sequential occupancy tracking and feasible-action masking are retained.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC) 2027

papers.title: Lengths as intersections on surfaces
papers.abstract: Geodesic currents on closed orientable hyperbolic surfaces are measures on the unit tangent bundle invariant under geodesic flow and orientation reversal. Every geodesic current induces a kind of ``length'', namely the dual functional on curves defined by the geometric intersection pairing with the current. It is natural to ask which other ``lengths'' or curve functionals arise this way. In this paper we give a purely axiomatic and combinatorial characterization of curve functionals on closed orientable hyperbolic surfaces that are dual to geodesic currents. This yields a new definition of geodesic currents as curve functionals or, equivalently, as functions on surface groups, without reference to measures or flows. More precisely, we show that a functional on curves arises as the geometric intersection pairing with a geodesic current if and only if it is additive under disjoint union and satisfies a simple \emph{smoothing} property: it is non-increasing under surgery of essential crossings. As applications, we obtain new axiomatic characterizations of measured laminations and hyperbolic length functionals, and new descriptions of surface group actions on real trees dual to measured laminations, including a streamlined proof of a classical theorem of Skora. We also provide a unified framework for dual geodesic currents arising from metric structures and generalized cross-ratios, including those associated with certain Anosov representations. Our approach subsumes all previously known constructions of dual geodesic currents for closed surfaces and yields broad new families of examples.
papers.comments: Title changed. Improved multiple sections: rewrote some parts of the introduction, revised and taxonomized examples in Section 2. Reordering in Sections 6, 7. Sections 8, 9 substantially revised, in particular fixed a gap in Lemma 9.11

papers.title: Muon with Nesterov Momentum: Heavy-Tailed Noise and (Randomized) Inexact Polar Decomposition
papers.abstract: Most first-order optimizers treat matrix-valued parameters as vectors, ignoring the intrinsic geometry of hidden-layer weights in neural networks. Muon addresses this mismatch by updating along the polar factor of a momentum matrix, but its theoretical understanding has lagged behind practice. In particular, practical implementations incorporate Nesterov momentum, compute the polar factor only approximately, and operate with stochastic gradients that may be heavy-tailed. We close this gap by developing a convergence theory for Muon with Nesterov momentum and inexact polar decomposition in non-convex matrix optimization under heavy-tailed noise. Our analysis builds on a unified framework for inexact polar decomposition that captures practical iterative approximations such as Newton-Schulz and quantifies how their errors propagate through the optimization dynamics. Under uniform bounds on polar errors, we establish an optimal iteration and sample complexity of $O \left(\varepsilon^{\frac{-(3α-2)}{(α-1)}} \right)$ for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, where $α\in(1,2]$~denotes the heavy-tail index. For the inexact-polar setting with $σ_1=0$, we also provide guarantees that do not require prior knowledge of $α$. We analyze a randomized low-rank polar decomposition that is substantially more efficient than full-space methods while remaining compatible with our theory. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed inexact and randomized~variants.

papers.title: On Enhancing the Dissipative Behavior of Active Flux Advection Schemes
papers.abstract: In this work, the traditional third-order Active Flux advection scheme is modified by reformulating the method and introducing four additional parameters R, S, T, and U that allow the numerical dissipation and dispersion of the scheme to be adjusted. The influence of these parameters is studied using Fourier analysis and parameter choices that lead to schemes with improved dissipative properties are identified. These improvements are validated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves: from tents to houses
papers.abstract: One of the classical results of mathematical population genetics states that the frequency of a beneficial mutant's offspring, on its way to fixation in a large population, looks like a logistic curve. A logarithmic scaling (both in height and time) of these selective sweep curves leads (in the case of strong selection) to a tent-like shape in the large population limit: First the logarithmic frequency of the mutant increases linearly from 0 to 1, then that of the former resident decreases from 1 to 0. For moderate selection the logarithmic frequencies develop (in the large population limit) a jump at the beginning/the end of the sweep, which takes the shape of the tent into that of a house. Our main result (proved for the Moran model) assesses the regularity of this convergence in the large population limit: It is uniform in the house's roof (phases of linear growth and decline) and "Skorokhod $M_1$" in the house's walls (closely around the jumps). Apart from interest in its own right, we anticipate that this result and the proof techniques will be instrumental for extending the description of clonal interference by Poissonian interacting trajectories (as it was done in Hermann et al. (2024) for strong selection) also to moderate selection.

papers.title: On the asymptotic behavior at the kinetic time of a weakly interacting Fermi gas
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the dynamics of a weakly interacting Fermi gas at the kinetic time regime $t\sim λ^{-2}$ where $λ\ll 1$ is the strength of the interaction potential. We prove that if the initial state is close to equilibrium, then the two-point time correlation function of the many-body quantum dynamics can be computed effectively. In fact, we show that its leading order behavior is determined completely by the collisional frequency of the Boltzmann-Nordheim collision operator at equilibrium. This settles a prediction by Lukkarinen-Spohn, and thus gives a justification of the quantum Boltzmann equation from many-body quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Khayyam's Choices of Conics
papers.abstract: In the late eleventh century, Omar Khayyam gave a systematic classification of, and solutions to, cubic equations by means of intersecting conic sections. His work is often retold in modern Cartesian language, where each cubic is reduced to equations of certain curves whose intersection determines solutions in the Cartesian plane. In this paper, we retain the first part of the standard modern treatment of Khayyam: translating his verbal algebra into modern symbolic algebra. But instead of interpreting the resulting equations as curves in a Cartesian plane, we interpret them as Khayyam himself did, as relations between positive geometrical magnitudes represented by conics in the Apollonian sense. On this basis, and using a purpose-designed colour scheme, we reconstruct, in a compact treatment, his solutions to all the cubic equations treated by Khayyam. The reconstruction brings to light a hidden feature of the treatise and draws a sharp line between the geometrization of algebra as practised by Khayyam, on the one hand, and the geometrization of algebra developed by Fermat and Descartes, on the other.
papers.comments: v2: substantially revised and retitled; all constructions redrawn as exact TikZ figures

papers.title: Robustly transitive behavior in symplectic dynamics
papers.abstract: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic deformations of this system display large robustly transitive sets. As a corollary of our construction we also obtain new open sets of real-analytic symplectomorphisms which are topologically mixing but not uniformly hyperbolic. To establish these results we develop perturbation techniques to create blender horseshoes in the real-analytic setting and import ideas from control theory which show that, typically, these objects have a large domain of influence.

papers.title: A dual-field structure-preserving mixed finite element discretization for incompressible Hall MHD equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-field structure-preserving mixed finite element discretization for the incompressible Hall magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations is introduced. It preserves pointwise mass conservation, magnetic Gauss law, and conservation of current density. It also satisfies a discrete energy law that exactly captures the correct energy dissipation rate in the dissipative regime and recovers energy conservation in the ideal limit. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the temporal and spatial accuracy and to illustrate the structure-preserving properties of the scheme.

papers.title: Excursion-dependent inverse-subordinator time changes of regenerative processes: Excursion structure and multiscale occupation-time limits
papers.abstract: We study an excursion-dependent generalization of inverse-subordinator time changes for recurrent regenerative processes. Subordinators from an independent family are assigned to measurable classes of excursions and to the distinguished state at which the process is regenerative, and the random clock is constructed from the corresponding occupation times. Although the time-changed process is not necessarily regenerative or Markovian, we show that its transformed excursion point process is again Poisson and is obtained from the original excursion point process by a marking-and-mapping procedure. We also identify the transformed stagnancy component, on the original local-time scale, as a subordinator independent of this point process. We use this representation to study occupation- and waiting-time asymptotics. Under regular variation assumptions on the tails of the Lévy measures of the cumulative excursion lifetimes and stagnancy components, we prove a multiscale joint occupation-time limit theorem, including generalized arcsine laws and Darling--Kac-type limits. We further obtain joint scaling limits for the last and next visit times to the distinguished state.

papers.title: Lifted Schrödinger Bridges for Gaussian Mixture Endpoints: Projection Gaps and Path-Space Obstructions
papers.abstract: We study stochastic density control between Gaussian-mixture endpoint distributions under Brownian prior dynamics. Since the direct Schrödinger bridge between Gaussian mixtures is generally not available in closed form, we introduce a lifted path-space construction in which each trajectory is augmented with a source--target component label. Consequently, the problem decomposes into Gaussian component-to-component Schrödinger bridges with explicit marginal, drift, and cost formulas, while the mixture-level assignment reduces to a finite-dimensional entropic coupling problem with a Sinkhorn scaling form. We then analyze the projection obtained by discarding or forgetting the label. By construction, the projected law satisfies the original Gaussian-mixture endpoint constraints, but its relative entropy generally differs from the lifted relative entropy by a nonnegative conditional label-information gap. This gap reveals a path-space obstruction: the lifted optimizer cannot, in general, be identified with the direct unlabeled Schrödinger bridge after projection. We also derive the posterior-averaged Markov drift associated with the projected marginal flow, prove a kinetic-energy upper bound, and identify a common path-potential condition under which the projection gap vanishes. Several numerical illustrations showing density and shape control are recorded for a self-contained exposition.
papers.comments: 37 pages; revised version of a journal submission with a new section on duality certificates

papers.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, sta- ble log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out con- secutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

papers.title: Integer points close to a transcendental curve: an algorithmic approach
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose an algorithmic approach to determine the integer points located near a transcendental curve. This approach is closely related to a celebrated work by Bombieri and Pila and to the so-called Coppersmith's method. We establish the underlying theoretical foundations, prove the algorithms, study their complexity and present practical experiments; we also compare our approach with previously existing ones. From a practical point of view, we focus on an instance of our general problem, called the Table Maker's Dilemma, whose solving makes it possible to evaluate a given function with correct rounding. Our experiments show a significant speedup. In particular, our results show that the development of a correctly rounded mathematical library for the binary128 format is now possible at a much smaller cost than with previously existing approaches.

papers.title: An inverse source problem for a fully nonlinear elliptic equation
papers.abstract: We study an inverse source problem for fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form \[ F(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } Ω. \] The question is whether the source term can be recovered from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. In two dimensions, the first linearization does not immediately give uniqueness: it leaves a natural conformal ambiguity in the linearized coefficients. For homogeneous nonlinearities $F$ with injective differential $DF$, we show that this ambiguity has a precise meaning at the level of the equation itself, namely that the source is determined up to an explicit scalar factor. The main point of the paper is to show how this remaining factor can be removed. We use the second linearization to extract information which is invisible at first order, and combine it with an algebraic nondegeneracy condition on the nonlinearity. Under this condition, the residual ambiguity is forced to be trivial, and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map uniquely determines the source. The result applies, in particular, to homogeneous admissible Hessian equations of Monge--Ampère type and related examples.

papers.title: Stable Initial-State Recovery from Dynamical Samples using Nagy-Type and Pollard-Hilding-Type Frame Perturbations
papers.abstract: Stimulated by Aldroubi and his collaborator's recent work on dynamical sampling, we consider a homogeneous discrete dynamical system of the form $f_n = A f_{n-1}= A^{n}f, \quad f_0 = f$, where A is a bounded linear operator on a separable Hilbert space H, which is known as the evolution operator, and $f_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ is the unknown initial state. The associated dynamical samples are given by the collection $\{\langle A^n f, g\rangle: g \in \mathcal{G, 0 \leq n < n < L(g)}\}$, where $\mathcal{G} \subset H$, is a finite or countable sampling set and $L$ is a function $L: G \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \bigcup \{\infty\}$. We analyze the stability of perturbed dynamical sampling systems in the sense of Nagy and Pollard-Hilding. More precisely, we establish sufficient conditions for the stable recovery of an initial state from perturbed dynamical samples obtained by changing the sampling vector, the evolution operator, ro simultaneously both, within the framework of Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type perturbation of frames.

papers.title: The partial data Calderón problem in dimension three
papers.abstract: We consider an inverse boundary value problem for the time-independent Schrödinger equation in dimension three. We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined near a boundary point uniquely determines the potential in a neighborhood of the boundary point in the interior. In particular, we show that the uniqueness question can be reduced to the injectivity of a weighted X-ray transform, which links inverse boundary value problems to integral geometry.
papers.comments: The asymptotic expansion (4.20) does not hold since there is a cancellation

papers.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
papers.abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.

papers.title: Limits of Finite-Sample Dependence Measures under Data Processing Inequality
papers.abstract: We study dependence measures between two discrete random variables. The measures vanish at independence and satisfy the data processing inequality (DPI): stochastic post-processing of one variable cannot increase dependence. We ask which such measures admit an exactly unbiased estimator from a fixed finite number of i.i.d. samples, a property equivalent to being polynomial in the joint probabilities. We distinguish fixed-alphabet DPI, which preserves the alphabet size of the variable being processed, from dimension-changing DPI. Under one-sided fixed-alphabet DPI, every measure with a continuously differentiable extension to a neighborhood of the closed probability simplex vanishes whenever one processed state has zero probability. If the processed alphabet is larger than the other alphabet, the measure is identically zero. If it has $n$ states and the other alphabet has at least $n$, every nonzero polynomial measure has degree at least $2n$ and requires at least $2n$ samples for unbiased estimation. Both bounds are attained by the Gram determinant. Under one-sided dimension-changing DPI, every family with the same boundary regularity is identically zero. These results yield sharp task bounds for multi-task peer prediction. For two agents with $n$ signals each, $2n$ tasks are necessary and sufficient for nontrivial expected payments that vanish for independent reports and cannot increase under memoryless stochastic garbling. Under these requirements, unequal signal-space sizes force the larger-alphabet agent's expected payment to vanish identically for any finite number of tasks.

papers.title: The existence of invariant sublinear expectations for $G$-SDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of invariant sublinear expectations of Markovian semigroups on sublinear expectation spaces. To achieve this, we establish a complete metric space of sublinear expectations, on which we extend Harris' method to the nonlinear setting on the convergence of sublinear semigroups. We then explore two cases of $G\text{-}$diffusions by studying the Lyapunov function and the local Doeblin condition. One is the $G\text{-}$Brownian motion on the unit circle which is the case studied in Feng and Zhao(2021), but with the new method. Another is the multidimensional $G\text{-}$SDEs on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$. We establish, for the first time in the literature, the existence of the invariant sublinear expectation for $G\text{-}$SDEs under the non-degenerate and weakly dissipative assumption. For this, we prove that for a class of $G\text{-}$SDEs, the $G\text{-}$expectation can be represented as the supremum of the semigroup of a family of SDEs, of which the regularity is obtained by considering { oscillations and coupling of the nonlinear Markovian semigroup,} and the Denis-Hu-Peng representation for the distribution of $G\text{-}$Brownian motions.
papers.comments: 35 pages, this work has been accepted by the SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis

papers.title: The functoriality of moves on graphs and extended path homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Combinatorics of graphs is a very powerful tool to unravel various properties of graph algebras. In particular, isomorphisms between graph algebras are often implemented by moves between their graphs. In this paper, we make these combinatorial methods functorial. Our categorical approach not only reveals the relationship between moves, but also leads to unexpected extensions of known moves (shifts and reductions) and the characterization of out-splits as admissible epimorphisms admitting a lifting of the source map. The former allowed us to go beyond isomorphisms and Morita equivalences, and the latter yielded a factorization lemma for out-splits. Better still, the functorial understanding of maximal out-splits permitted combining them with the derived-graph construction, which resulted in computing new proper endomorphisms of Cuntz algebras. Finally, the functorial implementation of balanced in-splits required the construction of a new category of graphs, where morphisms are given as homomorphisms of graph inverse semigroups. Thus, the combinatorics of moves brought a new tool to the realm of noncommutative topology where directed graphs are viewed as quantum spaces.

papers.title: Divided differences and complex variations of multiple zeta-star values
papers.abstract: Motivated by the known derived set $[1,+\infty)$ of multiple zeta-star values, we study finite multiple star harmonic sums and their infinite-depth limits. Divided differences give a cube-integral representation of their holomorphic interpolation on $\mathrm{Re}(s)>0$, which agrees with the Kawashima functions after reversal of the index. The finite-depth interpolations converge locally uniformly in $s$ as the depth tends to infinity, uniformly over all positive integer index sequences on compact subsets. For real $s>1$, these limits define a bijection from the infinite positive integer indices onto $(1,s]$. For each admissible infinite index, they tend to the corresponding multiple zeta-star limit as $\mathrm{Re}(s)\to+\infty$ with bounded imaginary part. For $\mathrm{Re}(s)>1$, we prove strict separation of every ordered pair of finite indices and of every ordered pair of infinite indices: either the difference or the difference divided by $s$ has positive real part throughout this half-plane, with the choice fixed by the pair. In particular, both index maps are injective. The proof uses a summation principle for functions with positive real part, established through positive integral representations and explicit kernel estimates.

papers.title: Well-balanced second-order approximation of the compressible atmospheric Euler equations
papers.abstract: We introduce a second-order approximation to the compressible atmospheric Euler equations with gravity that is invariant domain preserving and well-balanced with respect to stratified rest states, including isentropic and isothermal equilibria. The approximation is built upon discrete auxiliary states derived from a hydrostatic reconstruction of the density and potential temperature. These auxiliary states, together with an affine shift of the numerical state, provide local bounds needed for maintaining well-balancing and invariant domain preserving properties of the method. The numerical method is then verified and validated with analytic solutions, well-balancing tests, and typical benchmark problems for atmospheric flows.

papers.title: The five vertex model on a rectangle
papers.abstract: We derive a determinantal expression for the inhomogeneous asymmetric five vertex model in a rectangular geometry with arbitrary boundary conditions at the bottom and top. Standard non-intersecting lattice path, or free fermion, approaches are not applicable and the determinantal form thus is not immediate.

papers.title: Magnetic cotangent groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce magnetic cotangent groupoids on the cotangent bundle of a Lie groupoid using normalized cocycles, and characterize when magnetic symplectic forms are multiplicative on these groupoids. We show that $\mathbb{S}^1$-central extensions of Lie groupoids yield such structures via symplectic reduction. For a Kac--Moody extension, the resulting deformation connects the coadjoint and gauge action groupoids, which are not Morita equivalent.

papers.title: On finiteness properties of the unramified Iwasawa module of a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension with restricted ramification
papers.abstract: In the present article, we consider $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions defined by restrictions on ramification at $p$-adic primes. We study the finiteness, the existence of non-trivial finite submodules, and the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of these $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In addition, we give a new sufficient condition for Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture with some non-trivial concrete examples.

papers.title: Partial Observation of Linear Systems with the Mori-Zwanzig Formalism
papers.abstract: The Mori-Zwanzig formalism provides a systematic framework for deriving reduced-order model of dynamical systems when only part of the state is observed, but its practical use is often limited by the complexity of the resulting computations. This paper develops an explicit formulation of the Mori-Zwanzig equation for linear time-invariant systems under partially observed observables. By expressing the dynamics in terms of observables, the Koopman generator, and projections onto resolved and unresolved components, we derive closed-form representations of the Markovian, noise, and memory contributions that arise in the Mori-Zwanzig identity. For the linear setting, the resulting formulas recover the reduced dynamics obtained from the variation-of-constants formula while retaining the operator-based structure of the Mori-Zwanzig approach. This makes the derivation a transparent reference case for reduced-order modelling with memory and clarifies how unresolved variables influence the observed dynamics through history-dependent terms. The analysis also identifies the ingredients needed for extensions to nonlinear systems and more general projections, including spectral filtering and data-driven approximations of memory effects. Analytical and numerical examples involving the harmonic oscillator and wave equations illustrate the construction and demonstrate how the formalism can be used to obtain interpretable reduced-order models for partially observed systems.

papers.title: Cost of one-relator groups
papers.abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $Γ=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(Γ)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $β^{(2)}_1(Γ)=\mathrm{cost}(Γ) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.

papers.title: Tropical Regularity
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of tropical regularity as a generalization of tropical smoothness and present a geometric classification conjecture for tropical regular cycles. Roughly, the conjecture predicts that every regular tuple either forms a regular fibration or descends via a lattice projection to one of finitely many minimal-model cycles. Our main results establish this conjecture in three fundamental cases:unmixed regular tuples $(T,\ldots,T,[F])$ with $L(T)=\{0\}$ and $[F]$ spanning its ambient space; regular tropicalizations of complete intersections with generic coefficients; and regular tropical $2$-cycles satisfying the Hodge index inequality and spanning their ambient space.

papers.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We show that random linear codes (RLCs) possess nearly optimal discrepancy-type properties in a broad range of settings. Our main results are two general discrepancy theorems: one controls all translates of a fixed test, and the other controls large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating examples follow: First, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. More precisely, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1 - \frac{1}{n}\log_q|B_ρ| + \varepsilon$, where $|B_ρ|$ is the volume of a radius-$ρ$ Hamming ball in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, satisfies $|C \cap B| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot |B|}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all radius-$ρ$ Hamming balls $B$ with high probability. This significantly strengthens the best prior results, which follow from work by Blinovsky (1987, 1990) and Levitin (1988) on the covering properties of RLCs. Second, over prime fields, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for zero-error list-recovery, and list-recovery from erasures, above capacity. More precisely, for a prime $q>2$ and input list size $2\leq \ell\leq q-1$, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1-\log_q \ell+\varepsilon$ will satisfy $|C \cap S| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot \ell^n}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all combinatorial rectangles $S=S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_n$, where $|S_i|=\ell$ for all $i$, with high probability. An analogous result also holds when we can bound $|S_i|$ only for some of the $i$'s. We use this to show the abundance of locally leakage-resilient $n$-party linear ramp secret sharing schemes with any linear reconstruction threshold and sublinear threshold gap $O(n/\log n)$ over fields of polynomial size $q=Θ(n^γ)$ for a constant $γ\in(0,1/5)$. Prior work was stuck at reconstruction thresholds above $n/2$ for both threshold and ramp schemes.
papers.comments: 66 pages. Updated discussion of related work

papers.title: A new perspective in linear Cauchy Elasticity: variational minimum principles for statics, dynamics, and heterogeneous materials
papers.abstract: A variational minimum principle for linear elastodynamics of a possibly heterogeneous material without a stored energy function is developed. It involves a change of variables to dual fields, and results in a degenerate elliptic Euler-Lagrange system, even when the primal elastodynamics is hyperbolic. Uniqueness assertions for the dual dynamic and static problems and implications of the degenerate ellipticity are sketched. Some implications pertaining to heterogeneous materials and ones with indefinite elastic moduli are discussed.
papers.comments: This preprint was suggested as a submissiion for math.AP by arxiv - there is no separate category on arxiv for theoretical Solid Mechanics

papers.title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the necessary framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $θ$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehatθ$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.
papers.comments: 16 pages. v2: Corrections and additions. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: The Calderón problem for near-Euclidean metrics
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the anisotropic Calderón problem of determining the potential from boundary measurements of the time-independent Schrödinger equation on compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We prove a global uniqueness theorem for small perturbations of the Euclidean metric.
papers.comments: The asymptotic expansion (4.23) does not hold since there is a cancellation

papers.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.

papers.title: Korovkin type theorems for operators acting on functions of polynomial and exponential growth on $[0,\infty)$
papers.abstract: We establish two Korovkin-type approximation theorems for sequences of positive linear operators acting on continuous functions on $[0,\infty)$. The first result shows that pointwise convergence on all polynomial test functions implies pointwise convergence for every function in the domain that is dominated by a polynomial. The second result provides an analogous criterion for functions of exponential growth, where the test functions are the exponentials $e^{λx}$, $λ\in\mathbb{R}$. The results are applied to several classical and modified positive linear operators, including Baskakov, Szász--Mirakjan, Phillips, Post--Widder, Gamma, and Durrmeyer-type operators. Further applications are given to operators associated with modified Bessel functions and hyperbolic functions. The approach provides a unified framework for deriving pointwise convergence on unbounded intervals from convergence on suitable test functions.

papers.title: Lumping of reaction networks: Generic and critical parameters
papers.abstract: We investigate linear lumping for parameter-dependent mass action reaction networks, distinguishing between generic and critical parameter regimes. For generic parameters -- those ranging in some non-empty open subset of parameter space -- we prove that exact linear lumping yields only "obvious" reductions: elimination of non-reactant species or projections along stoichiometric first integrals. This characterization extends to reaction networks with product-form kinetics, including Michaelis-Menten and Hill-type rate laws. For mass action systems we proceed to develop an algorithmic approach to identify critical parameter sets -- algebraic subvarieties in parameter space where non-trivial lumpings become available. This procedure reduces the determination of lumping maps to a system of finitely many polynomial equations. It also applies to constrained lumping scenarios (which are frequently motivated by chemical considerations). We then review and extend results about proper lumpings. Finally, we discuss lumpings of a self-replicator system, and of a two-pathway enzyme mechanism, to document the viability of our methods in relevant scenarios. Our results clarify the relationship between structural (parameter-independent) and fine-tuned (parameter-dependent) reductions, with implications for approximate lumping when system parameters lie near critical values

papers.title: Periodicity in Banach algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider operators that are compositions of an isometric isomorphism and a left multiplier on a Banach algebra, and we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for these operators to have a dense set of periodic elements. As an application of this result, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over C*-algebra of compact operators on a separable Hilbert space. As another application, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over commutative non-unital C*-algebra. Finally, in the last section of the paper, we provide extensions of these results from the case of a sequence generated by powers of a single operator to families of operators indexed over a countable set.

papers.title: Inequalities between Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues in large dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ be a bounded domain in $R^d$. Denote by $λ_k$ (resp. $μ_k$) the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator in $Ω$ with Dirichlet (resp. Neumann) boundary conditions. Denote by $Ψ= Ψ(d,k,Ω)$ the shift of indices in the inequality $μ_{k+Ψ} \le λ_k$. We are interested to describe the behaviour of $Ψ$ for large $d$. We prove that a) $Ψ(d,1,Ω) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all domains $Ω$; and b) $Ψ(d,k,Ω) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all $k$ and all convex domains $Ω$.

papers.title: Antenna Orientation Optimization for Rotatable Antenna-Enabled ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Non-fixed flexible antenna architectures, such as fluid antenna system (FAS), movable antenna (MA), and pinching antenna, have garnered significant interest in recent years. In this paper, we deploy a rotatable antenna (RA) array at the base station (BS) to improve the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) performance by exploiting the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) introduced by antenna rotation. To enhance the sensing performance over an extended region containing a potential target while meeting the communication requirements of multiple users, we aim to maximize the minimum echo signal power within the sensing region, subject to required minimum communication rates of the users. For the special case of a single user and a point target, we develop a tractable approximation of the original problem, leading to independent per-RA subproblems. We characterize the geometric structure of these subproblems and derive closed-form solutions. Under the far-field approximation, the per-RA subproblems become approximately identical, allowing a common pointing vector to be adopted for all RAs. For the general multi-user and regional sensing case, we propose an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that alternately optimizes the transmit beamforming for communication, the covariance matrix of the probing signal, and the pointing vectors of the RAs in an iterative manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RA-enabled ISAC system significantly outperforms various benchmark schemes with restricted antenna-orientation flexibility, while the evaluation of the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) further verifies its benefits for target-position estimation accuracy.
papers.comments: 16 pages, submitted to IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: L2-L2-gain bounds for quadratic output systems
papers.abstract: We derive an explicit bound for the L2-L2-gain of linear time-invariant systems whose output is a quadratic function of the state and the input. Such systems appear naturally in many areas, for example for port-Hamiltonian systems, optimal-control, and stochastic problems. In case the output is purely quadratic in the state, the bound is determined by the supremum over $ω\in\mathbb R$ of the L2-norms of the bivariate transfer function restricted to the anti-diagonals $\{(s,\, iω-s)\mid s\in i\mathbb R\}$ of the frequency domain $i\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R $. Further, we show how the bound can be computed by solving linear matrix equations. This result provides a practical tool for assessing and reducing quadratic-output models.

papers.title: Mean Field Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms for Mean Field Control
papers.abstract: This monograph provides an introduction to mean field reinforcement learning through the lens of Markov decision processes arising from large-population stochastic control with mean field interactions and common noise. Starting from the connection between multi-agent reinforcement learning and mean field control, it develops the probabilistic, mathematical, and control-theoretic framework needed to formulate representative-agent learning problems, analyze their relationship with finite-population systems, and study both general and linear-quadratic models. The presentation includes dynamic programming principles, propagation-of-chaos limits, and theoretical analyses of tabular Q-learning and policy-gradient methods. It also discusses numerical implementations, including tabular schemes and deep reinforcement learning methods such as deep deterministic policy gradient. The goal is to give readers a coherent bridge between mean field control theory and reinforcement learning methodology, emphasizing the mathematical structure of the problems and the design of tractable learning approaches for large stochastic populations.

papers.title: How to approximate the flat spectral triple of a quantum torus by fuzzy tori : a twisted tale
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical and the quantum flat torus can be rigorously approximated at a differential level by finite-dimensional fuzzy tori within the framework of the spectral propinquity, a distance up to unitary equivalence which we extend in this paper to the space of twisted, metric spectral triples. Standard attempts to establish this convergence are traditionally obstructed by the intrinsic non-locality of discrete calculus and the subsequent failure of the Leibniz rule. While contemporary alternatives such as spectral truncations circumvent this issue by abandoning $C^*$-algebras in favor of operator systems, our approximations instead remain within the $C^*$-algebraic category, generalizing the commutator formula used to define the Lipschitz seminorm induced by spectral triples. To this end, we introduce a relaxed notion of a twisted spectral triple where the twist is a linear map acting as a discretized Riesz transform that encapsulates the non-locality of the discrete world. Self-adjointness is obtained by adjoining the backward difference to the forward difference and representing this doubled calculus with the creation and annihilation operators of the CAR algebra. The maximum of the norm of the twisted commutator and norm of the displacement of the twist from the identity becomes our Lipschitz seminorm, from which the quantum metric structure of quantum compact metric spaces (QCMS) on fuzzy tori is constructed. Our proposal to connect twisted spectral triples with QCMS recovers the usual connection between metric spectral triples and QCMS. By extending the spectral propinquity to this generalized setting of twisted spectral triples with possibly unbounded twists, we prove that fuzzy tori equipped with their natural two-sided discrete calculus converge to an amplification of the standard flat Dirac triple, while the underlying twists converge to the identity.
papers.comments: 50 pages. Minor misprints corrections, improved introduction, per referee report. Previous version correction: The definition of the twist is relaxed somewhat, without needing any change in the proofs, but to make it compatible with a subsequent paper on C*-crossed products which uses this technique

papers.title: Fluctuations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy at critical temperature
papers.abstract: We consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model at the critical inverse temperature $β= 1$ with zero external field. We prove that the free energy $F_N = F_{N,β=1}$ of this model has variance \[ \mathrm{Var}(F_N) = \frac16 \log N + O(1)\,, \] confirming a physics prediction of Aspelmeier \cite{aspelmeier2008free}, and that the centered and scaled $F_N$ satisfies a Gaussian CLT. We also identify the critical two-replica overlap scale, proving \[ \mathbb{E} \langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle \asymp N^{-2/3}\,, \] as conjectured by Talagrand \cite{talagrand2011mean2}, together with a uniform exponential moment bound for $N^{1/3} |R_{1,2}|$. The key input is a critical reweighted moment method, in the spirit of the ``small subgraph conditioning'' technique from probabilistic combinatorics, but capable of capturing diverging fluctuations. Through this reweighting, we relate the critical SK model to the BBP critical edge, which determines the overlap and fluctuation scales.
papers.comments: 41 pages. v3: updated introduction and overview

papers.title: A note on ultrahomogeneous unary algebras
papers.abstract: In a recent paper \cite{q}, Quinn-Gregson fully classified ultrahomogeneous mono-unary algebras of arbitrary cardinalities. In particular, he proved that every 1-ultrahomogeneous mono-unary algebra is ultrahomogeneous, and every locally finite mono-unary algebra with finitely many 1-orbits is $ω$-categorical. It is also known that every 1-homomorphism homogeneous mono-unary algebra is homomorphism-homogeneous \cite{ed}. Very naturally, Quinn-Gregson asked if these three results can be generalized to unary algebras. This short note answers the first and the third question negatively by providing two simple counterexamples. We also show that the second question has a positive answer in ``tree-like" cases which covers his result to mono-unary algebras and has a small combinatorial implication.
papers.comments: Add a counterexample to a new question in Quinn-Gregson's updated version

papers.title: Symmetric Spectral Reciprocity for $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Uniform Subconvexity
papers.abstract: We establish an explicit symmetric spectral reciprocity formula for twisted fourth moments of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}$ $L$-functions over an arbitrary number field. A Rankin--Selberg kernel gives a new analytic regularization of the formal Petersson identity for products of Eisenstein series, based on the rank decomposition $4=2+2$. The formula preserves the nonnegativity of the amplified fourth-moment spectral side at general levels. We further identify a new \emph{square-level concentration phenomenon}: after amplification, the dominant off-diagonal contribution comes from representations whose conductor is the square of a product of two distinct primes. Using square-level local test functions in the relative trace formula, we prove new hybrid subconvexity bounds for twisted $L$-functions. Combining these bounds with symmetric spectral reciprocity and amplification, we obtain the uniform estimate \begin{align*} L(1/2,π)\ll_{F,\varepsilon} C(π)^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{120}+\varepsilon} \end{align*} for every unitary cuspidal automorphic representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}/F$ with arbitrary central character. We also obtain stronger bounds for fixed central characters, a prime-level fifth-moment estimate, and applications to Rankin--Selberg and ring class $L$-functions.

papers.title: Steady Euler flows with contact discontinuities in infinitely long nozzles with general upstream data
papers.abstract: We investigate steady compressible Euler flows in two-dimensional infinitely long nozzles, where the piecewise smooth upstream data admit a contact discontinuity. Except for the subsonicity condition, no additional constraints are imposed on the data. We establish existence and uniqueness on the maximal interval of wall amplitudes containing the straight-nozzle configuration, and show that the contact discontinuity curve is of class $C^{2,α}$. An Euler--Lagrange transformation reduces the problem to a scalar elliptic equation in divergence form on a fixed strip, with discontinuous coefficients and the contact discontinuity conditions incorporated into the weak formulation. We further investigate the downstream asymptotic behavior and show that the convergence rate of the flow matches that of the nozzle walls.

papers.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
papers.abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.
papers.comments: 25 pages, few minor improvements. To appear in the Schiermonnikoog volume "Moduli Spaces and Modular Forms" edited by EMS Press

papers.title: Three classes of few-weight self-orthogonal projective codes and their applications for LCD codes
papers.abstract: Since self-orthogonal codes, few-weight codes and linear complementary dual codes(LCD codes, for short) have nice applications in coding theory and cryptography, they have received continuous attention. In 2024, by introducing the notion of the augment code, Heng et al.[16] constructed several classes of few-weight self-orthogonal codes basing on defining sets, which are introduced by Ding et al.[7] in 2007. In this manuscript, for two classes of defining sets, we consider the corresponding augmented codes, construct three classes of four-weight self-orthogonal projective codes and determine the parameters of their dual codes. And then, we construct three classes of LCD codes. In particular, we prove that there exists a class of these LCD codes whose dual codes are almost optimal LCD codes according to the sphere packing bound.

papers.title: Polish spaces of separable Banach lattices
papers.abstract: We compare two Polish presentations of separable real Banach lattices: closed sublattices of a universal lattice and closed ideals of $\operatorname{FBL}[\ell_1]$. We construct translations preserving lattice isometry in both directions, continuous and injective from sublattices to ideals and Borel in the reverse direction. Natural generation and Fremlin tensor operations are $\boldsymbolΣ^0_2$-measurable with $G_δ$ graphs. Isometric lattice isomorphism in either universal coding is Borel bireducible with a complete orbit equivalence relation of Polish-group actions. Uniform monotonicity and order uniform smoothness are $\boldsymbolΠ^0_3$-complete in both codings, whereas strict monotonicity, order smoothness, and order continuity are coanalytic. Abstract $L_p$ and AM-spaces form closed classes of sublattice codes. We also give explicit Borel bounds for atom counts, compact order intervals, and the lattice-isometry classes of $L_p[0,1]$, $\ell_p$, and $c_0$.

papers.title: Combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of fence posets
papers.abstract: Given a fence poset P , we define a new statistic on permutations, denoted by blP, that provides a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of P , answering a question of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova (2025). Using the fact that the base polytope of a lattice path matroid can be decomposed into order polytopes of fence posets, we also obtain a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of the base polytope of Schubert matroids, answering a question of Stanley (1999). As an application of this statistic, we establish the first nontrivial lower bound for the linear coefficient of the Ehrhart polynomial of an order polytope. Finally, we conjecture generalizations of this statistic to skew-shape posets and circular fence posets.

papers.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
papers.abstract: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.
papers.comments: 49 pages, LaTeX, 5 figures, many smaller improvements

papers.title: Propagation dynamics of an acid-mediated invasion model with degenerate tumor diffusion
papers.abstract: We investigate traveling wave fronts for an acid-mediated tumor invasion model with density-dependent degenerate diffusion. The model is a partially diffusive PDE--ODE system of Gatenby--Gawlinski type, in which the tumor diffusion coefficient $D(U)$ is allowed to be a general decreasing function satisfying $D(1)=0$. This degeneracy causes the traveling wave equation for the tumor component to lose uniform ellipticity near the healthy state, and hence standard arguments for nondegenerate reaction diffusion systems are not directly applicable. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a nonlinear change of variables which removes the degeneracy from the highest-order term of the tumor equation. For each fixed admissible tumor profile, the acid profile is represented by a Green kernel, while the healthy-tissue profile is obtained from an explicit integral formula. The transformed tumor profile is then constructed as the stationary limit of a uniformly parabolic auxiliary problem. By combining comparison principles, local Schauder estimates, carefully chosen super- and sub-solutions, and the Schauder fixed-point theorem, we prove the existence of traveling wave fronts for every wave speed $θ\ge 2\sqrt{rD(0)}$. The resulting wave connects the tumor-dominant state $(0,1,1)$ at $z=-\infty$ to the healthy state $(1,0,0)$ at $z=+\infty$. We further establish strict pointwise bounds, monotonicity of all wave components, and one-sided exponential asymptotic estimates in both the transformed variable and the original traveling-wave variable.

papers.title: On the diffusive-mean field limit of a kinetic weakly interacting particle system
papers.abstract: We study the joint diffusive-mean field limit for a system of weakly interacting kinetic Langevin dynamics, extending the results of Delgadino, Gvalani and Pavliotis (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2021) to the hypoelliptic/hypocoercive case. We show that, in the absence of phase transitions, the two limits commute, and we calculate the covariance matrix of the limiting Brownian motion using the Green-Kubo/Kipnis-Varadhan formula. However, at low temperatures, and in the presence of phase transitions, the two limits may not commute. We demonstrate our findings by providing a detailed analysis of the diffusive-mean field limit for the $O(2)$ model in a magnetic field. Our analysis is based on the systematic use of recently developed hypocoercivity techniques, together with an appropriate linearization of the mean field McKean-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck partial differential equation.

papers.title: A Direct Approach to Hermite Interpolation
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of polynomials satisfying the natural duality relations for Hermite interpolation, analogous to the classical Lagrange interpolation polynomials. They yield an explicit closed formula for the Hermite interpolant with arbitrary multiplicities, without recourse to divided differences, recursive corrections, or auxiliary Bézout identities. We also give a detailed account of Hermite's original approach to the problem, based on an integral formula, which he used both to derive the interpolating polynomial and to estimate the interpolation error for holomorphic data.(To appear in L'Enseignement Mathématique.)

papers.title: Generalised flip order on the faces of nestohedra
papers.abstract: Tamari lattices and weak Bruhat order are classical posets on the vertices of associahedra and permutohedra. These posets are particular instances of the \emph{flip order} on the vertices of graph associahedra. We present here a generalisation of the flip order to all the faces of nestohedra, encoded in terms of hypergraphs. For right-filled hypergraphs, we characterise our order in terms of generalised inversions. As an application, we describe shuffle products on faces of suitable nestohedra as sums over intervals in this order.

papers.title: A Direct Polynomial Approach to Spectral Decomposition
papers.abstract: We give a direct construction of the spectral projectors of a complex square matrix, based on explicit interpolation polynomials previously introduced. This yields a spectral resolution $A=\sum_{i=1}^r(λ_iP_i+N_i)$ from which the Primary Decomposition Theorem, the Cayley--Hamilton theorem, criteria for diagonalizability, and the spectral theorem for normal matrices are proved by short formal arguments. A weaker form of the construction, extends to any perfect fields via a Galois invariance argument and produces the Jordan--Chevalley decomposition.

papers.title: Densities of arithmetic Hecke triangle group orbits
papers.abstract: We give new proofs computing the asymptotic densities for orbits of the arithmetic Hecke triangle groups $Γ_q$ when $q=4$ and $q=6$. We use elementary number theory techniques along with basic properties of the Möbius function and Riemann zeta function with additional congruence conditions. This note actually came about by observing that, in the $q=4$ case, the underlying congruence condition partitions the set of coprime integer pairs into three classes of equal density.

papers.title: Weight-constrained universal sequences
papers.abstract: In 2011/12, Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams showed that a binary universal sequence can be constructed containing all $n$-tuples of Hamming weight either $r$ or $r+1$ for every possible $r$, and no others. In this paper we examine extensions of this result that require choosing a weight-like function applying to $n$-tuples with symbols taken from an alphabet of arbitrary (finite) size. We consider three possible such weight functions, and in each case establish an analogous result to that of Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams.
papers.comments: A number of errors and omissions have been rectified

papers.title: A multi-player optimal stopping game based on a spider Brownian motion
papers.abstract: This paper studies a multi-player non-zero-sum optimal stopping game driven by a spider Brownian motion. We study a specific, tractable family of games and the focus is on the existence and uniqueness of subgame-perfect Nash equilibria (SPNE). We begin by analyzing the two-player setting, in which the underlying process is a skew Brownian motion, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE. We then derive sufficient conditions for the uniqueness of the SPNE in the symmetric case, (where the skew Brownian motion reduces to a standard Brownian motion and both players have the same payoff structures). We also give examples which show that there can be multiple SPNE or no SPNE. We then extend the framework to the multi-player setting and provide sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE in this more general setting with a spider Brownian motion.

papers.title: The first chiral homology group in higher genus
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of the first chiral homology group of vertex algebras, developed by van Ekeren and Heluani for elliptic curves, to compact Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus. Our approach realizes a genus $g$ surface by iterated self-sewing of $g$ handles onto the Riemann sphere, each governed by a sewing parameter $ρ_i$ in a punctured disc. We construct an explicit complex computing the chiral homology groups $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_0$ and $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1$ of a vertex algebra $V$ on a genus $g$ surface with $n$ marked points, and equip it with a projectively flat connection, with an explicit central-charge anomaly, over the $g$-dimensional space of sewing parameters. We prove a genus $g$ Fourier-space Borcherds identity for the associated modified vertex operators. We show that two finiteness assumptions 1) finite dimensionality of the first Poisson homology $\HP_1(R_V)$ of the Zhu $C_2$-algebra, and 2) finite generation of a certain Koszul homology of the associated graded algebra, imply finite dimensionality of $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1(X,V)$ for every genus $g$ and every vertex algebra $V$. Using the degeneration $ρ_i \to 0$ together with the factorization theorem of Damiolini-Gibney-Tarasca, we relate the totally degenerate limit of $H_1^{\mathrm{ch}}$ to the Hochschild homology of an iterated construction on the Zhu algebra, and deduce vanishing of the first chiral homology group in every genus for rational vertex algebras.

papers.title: On Riemannian Geometry in Elastic Diffeology
papers.abstract: Blohmann's tangent functor makes the category of elastic diffeological spaces a Cartesian tangent category in the sense of Cockett and Cruttwell. We use this structure to develop Riemannian geometry on elastic diffeological spaces. Following Cockett and Cruttwell, with additional axioms for scalar multiplication, we introduce connections, covariant derivatives and curvature; for a Riemannian metric we prove a Koszul formula and the uniqueness of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative. Our main result is a variational characterization of geodesics: if a full connection whose vertical part is Levi-Civita admits a geodesic flow fixing the zero section, then the critical paths of the energy functional are exactly the paths satisfying the geodesic equation, and regular length-minimizing paths are geodesics after constant-speed reparametrization. On elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, completeness of the geodesic spray yields such a flow and uniqueness of geodesics. The results apply to quotients of complete Riemannian manifolds by free isometric actions of countable groups, such as irrational tori, and, under a tangent-commuting hypothesis, to mapping spaces from a closed manifold into elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, including free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.
papers.comments: 32 pages. v3: Substantially revised; preliminaries reorganized, assumptions for the variational characterization weakened, and applications to quotient and mapping spaces added

papers.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $Σ/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichmüller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(ψ)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlevé I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the upper bound $12.566563\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$.

papers.title: Generalizations of the groups $G_{n}^{k}$: graphs, moduli spaces, algebraic geometry, spherical braids
papers.abstract: In this work, we construct a generalization of the $G_n^k$-theory to the case of an arbitrary hypergraph. The case of spherical braids is considered separately, using the stratification of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_n(S^2)$ and the hypergraph $Γ_n^{\mathrm{sph}}$ encoding projective constraints. In contrast to the original $G_{n}^{k}$ theory, where codimension-one properties are determined by exactly $k$ particles, the present work considers various cases corresponding to strata of codimension~$1$. These groups admit nice maps to free products of cyclic groups. Among unsolved problems, we emphasize the question how the above construction works for abelian varieties and, in particular, for elliptic curves.
papers.comments: 9 pages; referee's remarks taken into account; some formulations justified

papers.title: Pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebras
papers.abstract: A pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebra $\mathcal{A}$ is a left-symmetric algebra endowed with a nondegenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form $ω$ such that all left multiplication operators are symmetric with respect to $ω$. In this setting, the underlying subadjacent Lie algebra $(\mathcal{A}^{-},ω)$ forms a flat $T$-symplectic Lie algebra. This paper provides a systematic investigation into the structural properties of pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebras. In particular, we introduce a distinguished subclass termed \emph{Milnor pre-symplectic algebras}, and prove that any pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebra whose commutator ideal is nondegenerate necessarily belongs to this subclass. Next, we investigate the Levi-Civita product associated with symplectic Lie algebras. We show that this product always yields a right-symmetric algebra, and we prove that it forms a left-symmetric algebra if and only if it is associative. Furthermore, we provide a characterization of symplectic Lie algebras in terms of representations of left-symmetric algebras, and conclude by establishing a construction method for these structures known as the $T^*$-extension. Furthermore, we develop a double extension procedure for pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebras by means of commutative associative algebras. We show that every such algebra with a degenerate commutator ideal can be reconstructed via this extension process. More generally, we show that any pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebra is either a Milnor pre-symplectic algebra or can be obtained through a finite sequence of successive double extensions starting from a Milnor pre-symplectic algebra. As a concrete application of these structural results, we provide a complete classification of pre-symplectic left-symmetric algebras of dimension less than or equal to $4$.

papers.title: Qualitative Analysis of a Two-Compartment Pharmacokinetic Model for Human Ethanol Metabolism and Its Generalization
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit a continuous-time two-compartment pharmacokinetic model of human ethanol metabolism originally proposed by Levitt and Levitt. We first establish the positivity of the solutions, investigate the existence and uniqueness of a positive equilibrium, and analyze its local and global asymptotic stability. As a result, the global dynamics of the original ethanol metabolism model is characterized, thereby complementing and extending the analytical results reported in the original study. Second, building upon the foundational two-compartment model of Levitt and Levitt, we replace the Michaelis--Menten metabolism rate with a general class of nonlinear functions, including both monotone and nonmonotone forms. This generalization allows us to examine a wider range of physiologically motivated scenarios and reveals richer dynamical behavior. We then establish the positivity of the solutions, study the existence and asymptotic stability of equilibria, and analyze the long-term dynamics under different ethanol input conditions. In particular, for a specific nonmonotone family, we establish the occurrence of a nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcation through center-manifold analysis. Furthermore, we prove the absence of nonconstant periodic orbits in the generalized model without assuming monotonicity of the metabolic rate functions. These findings extend the qualitative analysis beyond equilibrium stability and provide further insights into the complex dynamics of human ethanol metabolism. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to illustrate the theoretical findings. The numerical results provide further support for the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Partial Path Interception in Derivation DAGs: Structural Complexity, Parameterized Algorithms, and Approximation
