papers.abstract: Partial path interception (PPI) asks for a minimum-cost vertex set whose removal from a directed acyclic graph leaves at most a prescribed number of designated terminals able to reach a protected sink. We study how costs, depth, and fan-out affect its complexity. Unit-cost PPI is NP-complete at depth two with exactly two paths per terminal. Unique-path and individual-coverage instances admit polynomial-time algorithms, and bounded treewidth yields fixed-parameter tractability. Parameterized by the terminal threshold, weighted PPI is in XP and W-one-hard already at depth two, with no subexponential-time algorithm in that threshold under ETH. At depth two, undeletable terminals with bounded fan-out admit an FPT algorithm parameterized by the terminal threshold plus the fan-out bound. For unit costs, a dual-gammoid rank identity characterizes the optimum. Unit-cost depth-two instances with intermediate in-degree at most two are solvable in polynomial time for every terminal threshold, whereas depth-three instances are W-one-hard even with terminal out-degree one. On general directed acyclic graphs, minimum cuts and submodular optimization give a randomized approximation whose factor is the smaller of the coverage demand and roughly the square root of the number of initially exposed terminals, up to logarithmic factors. Reductions from smallest specified-edge subgraph, densest subgraph, and minimum union transfer conditional approximation lower bounds. PPI also gives an exact formulation of proof-valid caching under conjunctive derivation semantics: under independent premise erasures, the recovery probability equals one minus the erasure rate raised to the number of exposed premises. We extend this formulation to shared workloads, derive a sorting-based optimum under exact module routing, and give an AND-OR reliability envelope and a separate coded payload-recovery benchmark.

papers.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve risk functional minimization problems with general losses in Banach spaces within the framework of stochastic approximation. We introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD). Specifically, using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ to balance approximation and optimization errors. We solve each SMD subproblem over the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic subgradient onto its dual space. This yields closed-form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the uniform convexity of the underlying Banach space using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we show that the risk functional values converge to the minimum at a rate of $\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates under suitable regularity conditions. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.

papers.title: Extending Goldberg's Exact Sequence to Braid Groups of Graphs and Simplicial Complexes
papers.abstract: For a finite connected simplicial complex $X$, the strand map $ι_\ast$, from $\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ to $\prod_{i=1}^nπ_1(X,x_i^0)$, sends a pure braid to the homotopy classes of its strands. A theorem of Goldberg (1973) computes its kernel when $X$ is a closed surface other than $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$: the kernel is the normal closure of the pure braids supported in an embedded disc. We extend this picture to arbitrary finite connected simplicial complexes. Call $X$ $\textit{weakly Goldberg}$ if some contractible subcomplex $X_0\subseteq X$ realises Goldberg's description, $\kerι_\ast=\left\langle \operatorname{im}(\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)) \right\rangle$, and $\textit{Goldberg}$ if $X_0$ can moreover be chosen so that $\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ is injective. We prove that the strand map is surjective if and only if $X\not\cong S^1$; that $X$ is weakly Goldberg if and only if its free part is a forest; and that $X$ is Goldberg if and only if it admits an $\textit{admissible tree}$ -- a maximal tree of a scaffold, compatible with the boundary and interior types of the attachments of the free part to the thick components. We also classify the complexes for which the kernel is trivial, settle the exceptional surfaces $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$, and obtain complete answers for manifolds and for graphs. The main tools are a graph-of-spaces decomposition of the configuration space at a point of $X$ and a resolution procedure reducing an arbitrary complex to a simple model.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal annuli in convex balls
papers.abstract: We construct a $4$-parameter family of properly embedded genus-zero surfaces with at most two boundary components in a Riemannian $3$-ball. The construction is a free boundary analog of the canonical $5$-parameter family of surfaces on the $3$-sphere by Marques-Neves in the proof of Willmore conjecture. In the Euclidean unit ball, this family realizes the critical catenoid as a Simon-Smith min-max limit. As applications, we give an upper bound of Almgren-Pitts $4$-width $ω_4(\mathbb{B}^3)$ by the area of the critical catenoid. Moreover, we prove the existence of at least three free boundary minimal annuli in any compact $3$-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature and strictly convex boundary.
papers.comments: 52 pages, 1 figure, submitted version, comments are welcome!

papers.title: Dimension-Free Lipschitz Bounds for Brenier Maps to Compact Log-Concave Targets
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq1$, $Λ>0$, and $ρ\in\mathbb{R}$, let $μ=\mathcal{N}(0,Λ^{-1}\mathrm{Id})$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, where $\mathrm{Id}$ is the identity matrix, and let $ν$ be a probability measure whose support is a convex body $K$ of diameter $D=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and whose density is proportional to $e^{-W}$, where $\mathrm{D}^{2}W\succeq-ρ\mathrm{Id}$. We prove that the Brenier map $T$ from $μ$ to $ν$ has Lipschitz constant $\operatorname{Lip}(T)\leq\sqrt{Λ/(2π)}\int_{-D/2}^{D/2}e^{ρt^{2}/2}\,\mathrm{d}t$, which is sharp in every fixed dimension. For log-concave targets, the optimal coefficient of $\sqrtΛ\,D$ is $1/\sqrt{2π}$. For sources with finite second moment and density proportional to $e^{-V}$ for which $x\mapsto\frac12\langle Qx,x\rangle-V(x)$ is convex, where $Q$ is symmetric positive definite, and log-concave targets with compact support $K$, the Brenier potential $Φ$ satisfies $\partial_{vv}Φ\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\langle Qv,v\rangle}\,w_{K}(v)$ in the sense of distributions, where $w_{K}(v):=\sup_{y\in K}\langle y,v\rangle-\inf_{y\in K}\langle y,v\rangle$ is the width of $K$ along $v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $C_{1}<0.463$. This removes Kolesnikov's $\sqrt d$ loss. For log-concave sources with $\mathrm{D}^{2}V\preceqΛ\mathrm{Id}$ and the target $ν$, the Brenier map $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Lip}(T)^{2}\leqΛ\int_{0}^{D^{2}/4}e^{ρt}\,\mathrm{d}t$, so $\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ has the optimal exponential rate $1/8$ in $ρD^{2}$.
papers.comments: This is a fully revised and shorter version of the paper

papers.title: A classification of nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals
papers.abstract: We classify nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals over an arbitrary field. In dimension zero, we compute the canonical trace ideal using a graph on the socle monomials. In positive dimension, we prove a dimension bound under unmixedness and a connectedness condition, with weaker assumptions on the canonical trace ideal.
papers.comments: 16 pages. Substantially revised, with a new title. The nearly Gorenstein classification has been extended to arbitrary monomial ideals

papers.title: On the Local Linear Convergence of Operator Splitting Methods for Conic Programming
papers.abstract: Operator-splitting methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG) and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) often exhibit linear convergence on conic programs, although general theory guarantees only sublinear rates. We identify two geometric conditions -- strict complementarity and quadratic facial violation -- that explain this local behavior: under these conditions, PDHG and ADMM converge linearly to an optimal solution when initialized sufficiently close to the converging strictly complementary solution. We establish this result through a unified and verifiable primal-dual error-bound framework. First, we show that strict complementarity, together with a quadratic facial-violation property of the associated complementary faces, implies uniform quadratic growth of both the primal and dual augmented Lagrangians near a strictly complementary solution. Second, we prove the local equivalence of three regularity conditions: uniform quadratic growth of the augmented Lagrangians, quadratic growth of a localized smoothed primal-dual gap, and metric subregularity of the saddle-point mapping. This equivalence clarifies the relationship among previously proposed conditions for local linear convergence. Third, using a unified formulation, we give a concise analysis showing that these equivalent conditions yield local linear convergence of PDHG and ADMM. We verify the quadratic facial-violation property for standard polyhedral and symmetric cones, as well as relevant faces of exponential and power cones, and show that it is preserved under Cartesian products. We also obtain an improved local rate using a restarted Halpern scheme. Finally, we extend the framework to convex composite optimization through a quadratic subdifferential-violation condition, which generalizes the quadratic facial-violation.

papers.title: Pointwise function spaces over compacta are not weak Banach spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space. We prove that there is no continuous bijection $h\colon C_p(K)\to E_w$ whose inverse is continuous at $h(0)$. Consequently, $C_p(K)$ and $C_w(L)$ are not homeomorphic for any infinite compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ and $L$. This settles Krupski's problem and its two-space version due to Krupski and Marciszewski, and answers a question of Kąkol, Leiderman, and Michalak concerning $C_p([0,1])$ and weak Banach spaces.

papers.title: Carleson measures, Volterra integral operators and multipliers for $Q_K$ spaces
papers.abstract: We study embeddings and operators on the Möbius-invariant spaces $Q_K$ using two dyadic capacities. One capacity is defined by analytic packets; the other is defined by domination of positive semidefinite matrices. We prove that they are equivalent. They give criteria for bounded and compact embeddings $Q_K\to L^2(μ)$, bounded and compact Volterra operators, and pointwise multipliers. For the weights $K(t)=t^p/\log^β(e/t)$, $0<p<1$ and $β\ge1$, we prove $\mathcal M(Q_K)\subsetneq H^\infty\cap Q_K^{\log}.$ This disproves the logarithmic multiplier conjecture recorded in Bao and Wulan's 2021 survey.

papers.title: On the horizon problem over the product of self-similar fractals
papers.abstract: In this article, we first investigate the box dimension results for the graphs of continuous functions defined on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, where $\mathfrak{F}$ is the self-similar fractal generated by an iterated function system (IFS) exhibiting the open set condition (OSC). Following this, we manifest the existence of a prevalent surface, defined by a continuous function on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, that satisfies the horizon property in relation to the box dimension, i.e., the box dimension of the prevalent surface is greater than that of its horizon up to a constant $η$, where $η$ is the box dimension of the self-similar fractal $\mathfrak{F}$. Finally, we provide an example consolidating that the OSC on the underlying IFS of $\mathfrak{F}$ cannot be dropped.

papers.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
papers.abstract: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.

papers.title: A Two-regime Khintchine Inequality and an Improved Bound on the Degree-1 Fourier Weight for Linear Threshold Functions
papers.abstract: The Khintchine inequality provides a lower bound on the expected absolute value of a weighted sum of independent Rademacher random variables. In the classical setting, when the coefficient vector has unit Euclidean norm, this lower bound is a constant, with equality attained only by a simple family of extremal configurations. A refinement due to De, Diakonikolas, and Servedio, referred to as the \emph{linear Khintchine inequality} in this work, strengthens this estimate by establishing a lower bound that depends linearly on the distance of the coefficient vector from the extremal set. In this paper, we present a refined analysis of this dependence on the weight vector. Our results reveal a phase transition in the rate of improvement: when the dimension exceeds six, the lower bound undergoes an abrupt change as the weight vector deviates from the minimizer. Additionally, we improve the slope constant in linear Khintchine inequality. As a consequence, we establish an improved lower bound on the degree-1 Fourier weight for linear threshold functions $\mathbf W^{\leq1}[f]\geq0.55100929$, marking progress towards a conjecture of Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm.

papers.title: Density of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum
papers.abstract: The Lagrange spectrum is a classical object in number theory, defined as the set of values of $\liminf_{q\to\infty} q\, \mathrm{dist}(qα,\mathbb{Z})$ where $α$ runs through irrational numbers. It has a complicated structure, with the discrete part, Hall's ray, and a transitional part in between. One can similarly define Lagrange spectrum in the multidimensional set-up, and until now not much has been understood about it. In this paper we prove that, unlike in the one-dimensional case, the closure of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum is equal to the interval between $0$ and its supremum. The proof relies on a correspondence between Diophantine approximation and dynamics on the space of unimodular lattices and proceeds by studying a dynamical counterpart of the Lagrange spectrum that we call dynamical Lagrange spectrum. The latter is shown to be equal to the interval between $0$ and its maximum by means of an argument utilizing the higher rank nature of the set-up. A passage from full dynamical spectrum to the density of the Diophantine spectrum is achieved by applying equidistribution of expanding translates of horospheres in the space of lattices.
papers.comments: 13 pages; several results from the previous version generalized, references updated

papers.title: Permutative lifts of strictly ergodic subshifts
papers.abstract: Permutative sliding block codes - in the sense of Hedlund - give rise to finite-to- one extensions of subshifts. We provide criteria under which minimality and unique ergodicity are preserved by this 'lifting procedure'. These findings are illustrated by means of some nat- ural example families, which we use to obtain strictly ergodic finite-to-one extensions of sub- stitution subshifts (including the case of Fibonacci, Tribonacci, silver mean and noble means substitutions). We further study the interplay between permutative sliding block codes and Toeplitz flows. In particular, we find examples which demonstrate that a permutative lift of a strictly ergodic subshift may be minimal, but not uniquely ergodic - a phenomenon which cannot occur for primitive substitution subshifts.

papers.title: Proof of the generalized Chui conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Chui's conjecture on sums of Cauchy kernels. It states that among all configurations of Cauchy kernels on the unit disk, the equispaced one minimizes $L^1$ norm of the sum in the unit disk. Moreover, we obtain a generalization to a wider set of functionals, including weighted $L^p$ norms for $p > 1$ with radially symmetric weights.

papers.title: On multiply induced characters
papers.abstract: We investigate finite group structures that yield complex irreducible characters induced simultaneously from two or more distinct subgroups. When such a group is realized as the Galois group of a Galois extension of number fields, this phenomenon implies that multiple subfields share the same Artin $L$-function.
papers.comments: 20 pages. We have corrected errors and typos
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 2026, Article 108430

papers.title: Removable matchings in $2$-connected graphs
papers.abstract: A matching $M$ of a $2$-connected graph $G$ is \emph{removable} if $G-M$ is $2$-connected. We prove that, for every integer $d\ge4$, every $2$-connected graph with at least $2d$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$ has a removable matching of size $d$. This improves the previously known lower bound $d-2$ for $d\ge5$ to the optimal value $d$, answering a question of Li, Zhou, Fujita, and Mao. We also show that a $2$-connected graph on at least six vertices with minimum degree at least $3$ has a removable matching of size $3$ if and only if it is not a wheel. Our proofs use edge contraction and the structure of \emph{minimal non-removable matchings}.

papers.title: Multicolor Ramsey numbers of ordered matchings
papers.abstract: For an ordered graph $H$ and an integer $q\geq2$, let $r_{<}(H;q)$ denote the $q$-color ordered Ramsey number of $H$. Conlon, Fox, Lee and Sudakov asked whether, for every $q\geq3$, there is a constant $c_q$ such that $r_{<}(M;q)\leq n^{c_q\log n}$ for every ordered matching $M$ on $n$ vertices. We answer this negatively in a strong form: for every $q\geq2$, there is $c_q>0$ such that almost every perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$ satisfies $$r_{<}(M;q)>2^{c_q(\log n)^q/(\log\log n)^{q-1}}.$$ This matches the general upper bound up to a factor of $(\log\log n)^{q-1}$ in the exponent. We also give two applications. First, we prove a lower bound conjectured by Fox, He and Wigderson for multicolor Ramsey numbers of acyclic digraphs. Second, we strengthen a result of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt by giving a superquasipolynomial lower bound on the maximum chromatic number of $M$-free ordered graphs, for almost every perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$.
papers.comments: 6 pages, no figures. Minor revisions to exposition, notation and references. Main results unchanged

papers.title: Proximity Gaps for Gabidulin Codes and Applications
papers.abstract: Proximity gaps are central to the soundness of interactive oracle proofs of proximity (IOPPs) and polynomial commitment schemes (PCSs). An $[n,k,d]$ linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb F^n$ has a $δ$-proximity gap with error $ε$ if, for every $u_0,u_1\in\mathbb F^n$, either all points on $\ell_{u_0,u_1}=\{u_0+αu_1:α\in\mathbb F\}$ are $δ$-close to $C$, or at most an $ε$ fraction are. Although proximity gaps for Hamming-metric codes are well understood, their rank-metric counterparts remain largely unexplored despite their applications in coding theory and cryptography. In this work, we study proximity gaps for linear rank-metric codes and their cryptographic applications. First, we show that every $[n,k,d]$ linear rank-metric code $C$ over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$ admits a proximity gap for every $δ\le(d-1)/(3n)$, with error at most $q^{e+1}/q^m$, where $e=\lfloorδn\rfloor$. For Gabidulin codes, we improve the gap to $(d-1)/(2n)$ with error $10q^{n-1}/q^m$. These two proximity gaps match those for general linear Hamming-metric codes and Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, respectively. We prove the $(d-1)/(2n)$ bound is tight by constructing an infinite family of constant-rate Gabidulin codes and affine lines $\ell_{u_0,u_1}$ on which a $1-o(1)$ fraction of points are $d/(2n)$-close to the code, while $u_1$ is at least $3d/(4n)$-far from it. At $δ=(d-1)/(2n)$, a further counterexample gives a lower bound of order $q^{n-1}/q^m$ on $\varepsilon$, matching our upper bound up to a constant factor. As applications, we construct an IOPP for interleaved Gabidulin codes by adapting the Ligero IOPP for interleaved RS codes. We then adapt the Ligero-based PCS for ordinary polynomials to obtain a $q$-linearized polynomial commitment scheme. To our knowledge, this is the first PCS framework based on rank-metric error-correcting codes.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $ε$)-approximate solutions for $ε$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: Cumulative angular cancellation in Maz'ya's endpoint inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish domain criteria for critical homogeneous potential inequalities in the plane. Assuming signed plane cancellation, uniform absolute summability of frozen annular moments at each boundary centre implies the nonlinear endpoint estimate on arbitrary bounded open sets. For the Newton kernel and trace-free quadratic integrands, uniform boundedness of signed cumulative moments over all source centres and truncation radii is necessary and sufficient; testing all translates and dilates of one fixed radial unit-mass mollifier suffices. Tangent-cone cancellation on finitely cornered Dini domains follows as a geometric corollary. On one explicit strictly convex, non-Dini $C^1$ domain, the estimate holds for $2ξ_1ξ_2$ and fails for $ξ_1^2-ξ_2^2$ with $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$ divergence. A Laplacian-measure extension transfers density estimates to PDE inequalities on the Dini class and on strictly convex $C^1$ domains. We also classify quadratic cancellation on polygons. The signed necessary-and-sufficient criterion is restricted to quadratic integrands.
papers.comments: 38 pages, 2 figures. Substantially revised and retitled. Added a boundary atomic-sum sufficient criterion and an exact quadratic cumulative criterion on arbitrary bounded planar open sets, together with contrasting endpoint estimates on one strictly convex non-Dini $C^1$ domain. Extended the Laplacian-measure construction to strictly convex $C^1$ domains

papers.title: Conifold Gap for the Quintic Threefold
papers.abstract: We prove the all-genus conifold gap conjecture for the Gromov--Witten (GW) theories of the quintic threefold, other smooth Fermat Calabi--Yau threefold hypersurfaces, and local $\mathbb P^2$, as well as for the FJRW theories associated with these hypersurfaces. Our proof uses Mixed Spin P-field (MSP) theory and analogous master-space constructions. The central object is the \emph{cone-vertex theory}. We express this theory as a translation of the point CohFT via a formal Laplace transform and prove a universal conifold gap theorem for the resulting translated theories. The master-space construction then transfers the gap from the cone-vertex theory to the GW and FJRW theories.
papers.comments: 29 pages. Improved the proof of the universal cone-vertex gap theorem and added a family of examples

papers.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
papers.abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $κ$-barrelled and $ω$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $ω$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $σ$-compact, $ω$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_κ$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $ω$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.

papers.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers I. Analytic Rigidity
papers.abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked whether a transcendental entire function can map the set of Liouville numbers $\mathscr{L}$ into itself. We answer this question in the negative by proving a local rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. More precisely, if $U\subset\mathbb{R}$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr{L}\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr{L}$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb{R}(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $τ>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $ξ\in V\cap\mathscr{L}$ satisfying $μ(f(ξ))\leqτ$ contains a Cantor set. The proof combines a two-height counting estimate near analytic graphs with a nested-interval construction.
papers.comments: 29 pages. Retitled as Part I of a two-part work. Includes a Lean 4 formalization

papers.title: Strong Solutions and Long-Time Behavior for One-Dimensional Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Thermodynamically Compatible Pressure Laws
papers.abstract: Motivated in part by non-ideal equations of state such as the van der Waals law, we study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant positive viscosity and heat conductivity and general thermodynamically compatible pressure and internal-energy functions. Assuming $e_θ>0$, we obtain local $H^1(\mathbb R)$ strong solutions for initial data with positive specific volume and temperature, without sign conditions on the pressure derivatives. Near an equilibrium satisfying $p_v(\bar v,\barθ)<0$, sufficiently small $H^1(\mathbb R)$ perturbations generate global strong solutions with uniform thermodynamic bounds and time-integrable dissipation. For the full constitutive class, all first spatial derivatives decay in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ and the perturbation converges to zero in $L^p(\mathbb R)$ for every $2<p\le\infty$. We also identify a locally entropy-affine subclass of constitutive laws for which a Fourier--Duhamel argument establishes convergence to equilibrium in $H^1(\mathbb R)$. For more general thermodynamically compatible constitutive laws, we establish a conditional criterion for convergence in $H^1(\mathbb R)$, based on the space-time integrability of the nonlinear pressure remainder in entropy variables.
papers.comments: This version substantially extends the previous manuscript, which established local well-posedness and global existence. It adds long-time stability results, including decay of spatial gradients, conditional nonlinear H^1 convergence, and full H^1 stabilization for locally affine pressure laws in entropy coordinates. The title and author list have also been updated

papers.title: The Distance Between the Adjacency Spectral Center and the Characteristic Set of a Tree
papers.abstract: Let $S(T)$ denote the adjacency spectral center of a tree $T$, and let $C(T)$ be its characteristic set. We determine the maximum possible distance $Δ_n:=\max_{|V(T)|=n}\operatorname{dist}_T(S(T),C(T))$ for every $n\ge 3$. It turns out that $Δ_n=0$ for $3\le n\le 11$, that $Δ_{12}=1$, and that $Δ_n=\left\lfloor\frac{n-11}{2}\right\rfloor (n\ge 13)$. More generally, if the two sets are at distance $d\ge 2$, then the branch issuing from a closest vertex of $S(T)$ in the direction of $C(T)$ contains at least $2d+5$ vertices, while the complementary part of the tree contains at least $6$. We also establish structural restrictions in the equality case and completely classify the extremal trees of every odd order $n\ge 17$: there are exactly four nonisomorphic extremal trees, consisting of two brooms and two double brooms. Our proofs exploit the opposite extremal behaviour of paths for the adjacency spectral radius and for the bottleneck Perron value.
papers.comments: V2: Strengthened the separation theorem with sharper branch-size bounds, characterized the equality case, and classified all extremal trees of odd order $n \geq 17$. Proofs and exposition have also been revised

papers.title: Surjectivity of the Enots Wolley Sequence
papers.abstract: We prove that the Enots-Wolley sequence, a greedy sequence defined by local divisibility and coprimality conditions, contains every positive integer with at least two distinct prime divisors. This resolves an open conjecture by Shannon and Sloane. The only analytic number-theoretic inputs are the prime number theorem and Mertens' estimate for reciprocal primes.
papers.comments: Revised exposition, abstract, and proof outline; simplified an arithmetic estimate. Main results unchanged

papers.title: A new family of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$ and integer $n\ge1$, we give a single Kummer equation defining an $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $\mathcal X_{q,n}$. The family recovers the Hermitian curves for $n=1,2$, the Giulietti--Korchmáros curve for $n=3$, and the Beelen--Montanucci curves for odd $n\ge5$. For $q>2$ and even $n\ge4$, it gives new maximal curves of genus $(q^2-1)q^n/2$ that are not covered by the Hermitian curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$. We compute the genus for both parities of $n$ and give a uniform proof of maximality by counting rational places. For $q>2$ and odd $n\ge5$, we remove the Galois hypothesis from the known non-covering results for the Beelen--Montanucci and Garcia--Güneri--Stichtenoth curves. For even $n\ge4$, we determine the full automorphism group,of order $(q^n+1)q(q^2-1)$, and give explicit equations and genera for all Galois quotients, with closed-form equations for several classes of subgroups.

papers.title: The Face Lattice of any Simplicial Polytope is Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We show that the cover graph of the face lattice of every simplicial polytope admits a Hamilton cycle. Moreover, any two distinct facets can be prescribed as the neighbors of the full polytope on this cycle. By duality, the face lattice of every simple polytope is Hamiltonian as well. This proves the simplicial and simple cases of a conjecture of Behrooznia, Brenner, Merino, Mütze, Rieck, and Verciani (SODA26). The proof uses a line shelling in both directions. The forward shelling partitions the faces into Boolean intervals, whose cover graphs are cubes. The reverse shelling gives a second partition, on which we construct a perfect matching by adding or removing a fixed vertex in each interval. This matching connects the cubes of the first partition. A theorem of Gregor then completes it to a Hamilton cycle using only edges within these cubes. The same argument applies to shellable simplicial spheres, although without the prescribed neighbors of the full complex in this case. Using Chari's shelling construction of perfect matchings, we also obtain Hamiltonicity for polytopes with at most one facet that is not a simplex.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism and multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps. We establish a conditional variational principle and prove the real analyticity and strict monotonicity of the Birkhoff spectrum, as well as the existence and uniqueness of the measure attaining the supremum in the conditional variational principle, on a certain region. To this end, we prove the existence and uniqueness of an expanding equilibrium measure and the real analyticity of the pressure function on a suitable domain. For parabolic systems, our approach using thermodynamic formalism provides a unified framework for establishing the conditional variational principle and investigating finer properties of the Birkhoff spectrum, including its real analyticity, strict monotonicity, and the existence and uniqueness of a measure attaining the supremum on a certain region.

papers.title: Four collinear points or six visible points
papers.abstract: Every finite planar set of at least $880$ points contains four collinear points or six pairwise visible points.
papers.comments: 4 pages, 2 figures. Revision based on feedback through xsci.com

papers.title: Exponentially Larger Deletion-Correcting Codes and Constant-List-Decodable Insertion-Deletion Codes
papers.abstract: We establish improved asymptotic rate bounds for adversarial insertion--deletion codes. For binary unique-deletion correction in the linear-deletion regime, we strictly improve Levenshtein's classical lower-bound expression. At deletion fraction $δ=0.1$, our achievable rate increases from $0.162009$ to $0.194890$, a relative gain of approximately $20.30\%$. For list decoding with any prescribed finite list size $L$, we obtain new achievable-rate bounds for binary deletion and insertion codes. Our approach combines the Lovász local lemma with refined counting of common subsequences and supersequences, using generating functions and run-restricted sampling. We also establish a combinatorial reduction that trades $L$ units of insertion budget for one unit of deletion budget without changing the code or increasing the list size. It transfers insertion lower bounds at $γ+Lδ$ and deletion upper bounds at $δ+γ/L$ to mixed errors. We also derive a run-counting Levenshtein-type list-decoding upper bound and a higher-order Elias-type upper bound. The latter recovers Yasunaga's asymptotic unique-decoding bound at $L=1$ and strictly improves the Haeupler--Shahrasbi--Sudan insertion upper bound for every fixed $L$ and $0<γ<q-1$. Numerical comparisons quantify the gains and the remaining gaps.

papers.title: Admissible qx+1 Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $q\geq3$ be odd and put $m_r=\lfloor r\log_2q\rfloor$. We count parity sequences with exactly $r$ entries equal to $1$ for which the coefficient in the $qx+1$ iteration first drops below $1$ at step $m_r+1$. Their number $a_q(r)$ also counts the corresponding residue classes modulo $2^{m_r+1}$. By classifying increasing integer sequences according to the first index at which they exceed a prescribed bound, we obtain a recurrence which, for $q=3$, establishes the five- or six-term block pattern conjectured in 2015, allowing a shorter final block. We establish the sharp inequalities \[ \frac1r\binom{m_r-1}{r-1}\leq a_q(r)\leq\frac1r\binom{m_r}{r-1} \] Equality in the lower (respectively upper) bound occurs exactly when $\{r\log_2q\}$ is smaller (respectively larger) than all preceding fractional parts $\{j\log_2q\}$, $1\leq j<r$. These indices are characterized by denominators of convergents and semiconvergents from below and above; at these indices $r\geq2$, the values $a_q(r)$ are rational Catalan numbers. We also characterize the dependence on $q$ and prove, for each fixed odd $q\geq3$, that $a_q(r)=Θ_q(r^{-3/2}B_q^r)$, where $B_q=(\log_2q)^{\log_2q}/(\log_2q-1)^{\log_2q-1}$. For $q=3$, this proves Hikawa's conjectured polynomial factor for the number of finite binary words of given weight for which the length of every nonempty prefix is smaller than $\log_2 3$ times the number of its ones.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 2 tables. The author thanks the editors of the Journal of Integer Sequences for comments on an earlier version, particularly for noting that Proposition 6 holds for every nondecreasing bound

papers.title: Domain-decomposed Evolutional Deep Neural Network with Random Features for Transient Pressure Diffusion with Discontinuous and High-Contrast Coefficients
papers.abstract: Transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media becomes difficult to resolve efficiently when permeability is discontinuous and spans several orders of magnitude. In this paper, we develop a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network (DD RF-EDNN) that separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution. Permeability-informed random features are compressed into an orthonormal pressure space, and a conservative finite-volume operator is projected onto this space so that only the reduced coordinates are advanced in time. This formulation retains the dissipative structure of the discrete flow problem without repeated neural-network optimization. The analysis quantifies dictionary and singular-value truncation errors, proves contractivity under an energy-consistent dissipativity correction, and derives a conditional grid-level estimate for homogeneous dynamics and time-independent data admitting a steady lifting. Numerical experiments on low-permeability inclusions, high-conductivity blocks and channels, and three-dimensional grids assess the accuracy of the method across distinct coefficient configurations. The method reaches a final-time relative $L^2$ error of $9.54\times10^{-4}$ in the principal benchmark and maintains errors on the order of $10^{-2}$ at a permeability contrast of $10^3$. Numerical diagnostics further show that the observed error balance and temporal convergence are consistent with the analysis. These results support DD RF-EDNN as a structure-preserving and interpretable reduced formulation for transient simulations on prescribed heterogeneous media.

papers.title: The category of nominal sets is locally monoidal closed
papers.abstract: The category Nom of nominal sets was proposed by Pitts and Gabbay as a setting for the semantics of abstract syntax with variable bindings. It is well-known that Nom is a topos, also known as the Schanuel topos, and in particular it follows that Nom is locally closed, i.e., every slice category Nom/X is cartesian-closed. In this paper, we show that Nom has a much stronger property: every monoidal (closed) structure on Nom induces a monoidal (closed) structure on all slice categories Nom/X. One monoidal closed structure of particular interest on Nom is the separated product A * B, whose right adjoint A -* B is called the separated function space. In particular, it follows that Nom is locally separatedly closed.

papers.title: The lattice covering density of the regular octahedron
papers.abstract: We prove that the lattice covering density of the regular octahedron is $9/8$, establishing the optimality of the classical body-centered cubic covering. A hypothetical lattice covering of smaller density would yield a lattice basis whose six Kuhn tetrahedra each fit in a translate of the octahedron. A sharp determinant bound then gives a contradiction. As a consequence, the maximum order of an undirected Abelian Cayley graph with three generators and their inverses and diameter at most $k$ is $\frac{32}{27}k^3+O(k^2)$ as $k\to\infty$.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Freeness of Wigner Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, within the framework of real infinitesimal free probability introduced by Cébron and the second author, we compute the real infinitesimal free cumulants of independent complex Wigner matrices. Our approach relies on establishing a combinatorial relation between annular non-crossing partitions and families of directed graphs. As a consequence, we demonstrate that independent complex Wigner matrices are asymptotically real infinitesimally free. In particular, we show (under mild conditions) that a complex Wigner matrix is asymptotically infinitesimally free from its transpose.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 11 figures, added a reference and Remark 6.2

papers.title: Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras from Ševera bicomplexes
papers.abstract: A Ševera bicomplex is a bicomplex $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ whose differentials $d_{i}$ are Grothendieck differential operators of order $\leq i$ with respect to a given $A$-module structure on $M$, where $A$ is a graded commutative algebra. One also requires that $(M,d_{0})$ admits a contracting homotopy $K$ that is a differential operator of the same order as $d_{0}$. Under suitable assumptions, the differential $d_{2}$ of the second page of the spectral sequence associated with $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ is a Batalin-Vilkovisky operator on $E_{2}$, so that when $E_{2}$ is a free rank 1 $A$-module, the graded commutative algebra structure of $A$ is enhanced to a Gerstenhaber algebra structure, and the choice of a $d_{2}$-closed basis element for $E_{2}$ further enhances this to a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra structure. The prototypical example of this construction is Ševera's description of the Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structure on the algebra of smooth functions of an odd symplectic manifold. Throughout the whole article we look at Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras through the lenses of Cartan calculus. Indications of a generalization to derived Cartan calculus are briefly discussed in the concluding section.
papers.comments: Version 2: Example 5.12, Remark 6.23 and Appendix on Xu modules added, some minor typos fixed. 33 pages

papers.title: Infinitely Many Binomial Coefficients of Deficiency One
papers.abstract: A binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ is good if all its prime divisors exceed $k$, and its deficiency is the number of $k$-smooth integers in $(n-k,n]$. A short constructive proof of the existence of infinitely many good binomial coefficients with deficiency exactly one is given, which provides an answer to a problem of Erdős, Lacampagne, and Selfridge.
papers.comments: The main result, Theorem 1.1, dose not hold. An error is the reversal of the no-carry condition: the correct condition is $a_j+b_j\leq p-1$, not $b_j\geq a_j$

papers.title: Uniqueness for the inverse Schrödinger problem in the plane with $L^p$ potentials, $p>1$
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain. We prove that the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-Δ+V$ uniquely determines every complex-valued potential $V\in L^p(Ω)$, $p>1$, provided that zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue. This extends the previously known range $p>4/3$ to all $p>1$. The proof uses Bukhgeim's quadratic-phase solutions and an average of Alessandrini's identity over the phase center. After separating the Neumann-series tails, we show that each remaining Born term tends to zero. The fixed-order estimates combine bounds for the absolute kernels with oscillatory cancellation and a duality argument for the product of the two Cauchy transforms.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $α$ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_α^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.

papers.title: Disproving Conjectures on the Davenport and Narkiewicz Constants
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is a classical invariant arising from the arithmetic of ideal class groups of number fields. Closely related to the Davenport constant is the first Narkiewicz constant $\Nark_1(G)$, which arises in the quantitative study of algebraic integers and their factorizations. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured in 2006 that $\DD(G)\leq \sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ while Narkiewicz and Śliwa conjectured in 1982 that $\Nark_1(G)=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ where $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ are the invariant factors of $G$. Both are central conjectures concerning arithmetic invariants arising from the theory of number fields. In this paper, we disprove both conjectures. Moreover, we show that, for every fixed $r\geq5$, both $\DD(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ and $\Nark_1(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ are unbounded over finite abelian groups of rank $r$. We develop a probabilistic representation technique to establish a uniform upper bound for the Davenport constant: $$ \DD(G)\leq\frac{16}{5}\,\rr(G)\exp(G). $$ Our bound gives the first improvement of the classical van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk estimate: $\DD(G)\leq\exp(G) \left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \leq\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$, by removing the logarithmic dependence on the exponent from this classical estimate, replacing it with the absolute constant $16/5$. Their bound stood unimproved since its establishment in 1969. The existence of $C=16/5$ also brings us closer to the most challenging conjecture on the Davenport constant, namely the Emde Boas--Kruyswijk Conjecture in 1969, which predicts that $\DD(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1.$ As a further application of our results, we disprove a conjecture of Girard in 2008 concerning cross numbers, an invariant with deep roots in the arithmetic of number fields and Krull monoids.

papers.title: Excitation and Identifiability in the 2D Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: Convergence in parameter estimation classically requires ``persistency of excitation," which is a non-degeneracy condition on a trajectory-dependent signal. To the best of our knowledge, this paper develops the first such excitation theory for a nonlinear PDE. In the context of identifying the unknown viscosity from spectral observations in the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations for incompressible fluids, our excitation condition is computable, verifiable a priori, and sharp with respect to scaling. Our approach employs a data assimilation methodology to account for an unknown initial state and select candidate viscosities by minimizing the loss between the observed low-modes of the fluid velocity and low-modes of a nudging-based filter assimilating these observations. The main novelty of our framework is to distinguish a new functional, $\mathsf{W}$, representing the work done by the filter's associated sensitivity variable on the enstrophy, around which our entire analysis is centered. We show that $\mathsf{W}$ is explicitly comparable to the observability Gramian of the associated Gauss--Newton iteration, and subsequently establish the following dichotomy at every critical point of the observational loss: either $\mathsf{W}$ exceeds a minimal excitation threshold, in which case the candidate viscosity obeys an explicit error estimate that depends inversely on $\mathsf{W}$ and the observational density $N$, but directly on the error between initial conditions, or else the observations are quantitatively insensitive to parameter updates in a way that is detectable to the user. Our approach is energy-based, and therefore expected to be adaptable to many other nonlinear dissipative systems.
papers.comments: 48 pages, several discussions and remarks streamlined, references added

papers.title: The Hilbert Basis Theorem for Non-Associative Skew Power Series Rings and Non-Associative Skew Laurent Series Rings over a Non-Associative Coefficient Ring
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give conditions on a unital non-associative ring $R$ and additive map $σ: R\longrightarrow R$ so that the non-associative skew power series ring, denoted by $R[[X;σ]]$ and the non-associative skew Laurent series ring denoted by $R((X;σ))$ are left (resp. right) Noetherian, respectively. Consequently, we establish versions of Hilbert Basis Theorem of $R[[X;σ]]$ and $R((X;σ))$, respectively, for left (resp. right) Noetherianity . We also give a counterexample showing that the Hilbert Basis Theorem does not hold in general in the non-associative case. In establishing the Hilbert Basis Theorems for $R[[X;σ]]$ and $R((X;σ))$, we introduce and utilize the right (resp. left) quasi-associative property of $R$, which is equivalent to $rR$ (resp. $Rc$) being one-sided ideals for all $r\in R$ (resp. $c\in R$).

papers.title: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
papers.abstract: We study three particles on the two-dimensional square lattice with contact interactions of infinite strength, in every sector of total quasimomentum, for three statistics: identical bosons, two identical fermions with a distinguishable third particle, and two identical bosons with a distinguishable third particle. The atom-dimer sector associated with the infinitely degenerate eigenvalue of the pair-contact operator is analysed on the whole Brillouin zone. A Feshbach-Schur reduction gives explicit effective Hamiltonians built from the Dirichlet Laplacian and a rank-four exchange operator, and a spectral transfer theorem with explicit error bounds identifies the atom-dimer threshold of the three-body operator with that of the effective one; the eigenvalue counting function below the threshold is squeezed between those of the effective operator, so that the number of atom-dimer states bound uniformly in the coupling equals the number of bound states of the effective Hamiltonian. The threshold problem reduces to a four-by-four Hermitian matrix whose zero-energy limit is built from the two-point resistances of the square lattice and hence to a quartic polynomial. This yields the complete atom-dimer zones in closed form; the critical hopping ratio as an explicit function on the whole Brillouin zone with two-sided bounds and closed forms at all symmetry points; at most two atom-dimer states per sector with an explicit second threshold; exact onset laws of infinite order at the corner point and linear-over-logarithmic in the pure p-wave channel; and two exact dualities relating a change of statistics to a shift of quasimomentum by half a reciprocal-lattice vector. The reduction of the three-body eigenvalue problem to the lattice Skornyakov-Ter-Martirosyan equation is proved with an explicit isomorphism of eigenspaces.
papers.comments: Version 2: major revision. Added spectral transfer theorem with explicit constants, analysis of critical parameters, proof of the lattice Skornyakov-Ter-Martirosyan reduction, first-principles derivation of lattice constants, and corrected remainder constant for the 2+1 bosonic mixture. Response to referee report.37 pages with Supplementary, 8 figures

papers.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
papers.abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.
papers.comments: 43 pages. Dedicated to the memory of Lev Genrikhovich Shnirelman (1905--1938)

papers.title: A quasipolynomial inverse theorem for the $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ norm in the high characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove an inverse theorem for the Gowers uniformity norm $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ with quasipolynomial bounds in the case when $p \geq k$. The inverse theorem follows from a quasipolynomial structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms, which are a natural generalization of Freiman homomorphisms to maps of several variables. The proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is the central result of the paper and rests on three main ingredients: algebraic regularity method, abstract Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem and the theory of multilinear maps defined on multilinear varieties. The last ingredient originates from an earlier work of Gowers and the author, and is significantly expanded in this paper. In particular, once the theory of such maps is in place, the proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is relatively short, especially compared to the previous quantitative results in the inverse theory of Gowers norms.
papers.comments: 65 pages; corrected a couple of inaccuracies and improved the presentation of some arguments

papers.title: Matching algebras and their Dunkl subalgebras
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$, we consider the quotient algebra $\mathcal M(G)$ of the polynomial ring in the variables $u_e$ (for $e \in E$) by the ideal generated by all products $u_e u_f$ for non-disjoint edges $e$ and $f$ (including all squares $u_e^2$). This quotient is called the matching algebra of $G$, since it has a basis indexed by the matchings of $G$. In this quotient, we define a subalgebra $\mathcal D(G)$ generated by the signed incidence sums $θ_v=\sum_{e=(v,w)}u_e-\sum_{e=(w,v)}u_e$ for all $v \in V$ (where all edges of $G$ are oriented arbitrarily); we call this the Dunkl matching algebra. We show that, as a graded vector space, $\mathcal D(G)$ is dual to the span of all polynomials $p_M = \prod_{(i,j) \in M} (x_i - x_j)$, where $M$ ranges over all matchings of $G$. For the complete graph $K_n$, the latter span is a direct sum of two-row Specht modules (one in each degree); thus its Hilbert series is that of the Catalan triangle, and, in characteristic zero, the Dunkl matching algebra can be presented by linear and quadratic relations. For arbitrary graphs, we formulate the saturation problem of deciding when the selected matching Specht generators $p_M$ in a given degree $k$ span the full two-row Specht module $S^{(n-k,k)}$. We show that saturation in degree $k$ forces $k$-connectivity, that saturation in degree $2$ is equivalent to $2$-connectivity, and that $k$-linked graphs are saturated in degree $k$. We also prove saturation in every possible degree whenever the complement of $G$ is a matching. We show that the Dunkl matching algebra equals the full matching algebra exactly for forests, and give an explicit Hilbert series formula for unicyclic graphs.
papers.comments: 32 pages. Produced using GPT-5.6 based on third author's notes; significantly edited and fully proofread. v3 simplifies (and details) some proofs in Section 5 (no more ear-decomposition) and improves references in Section 4. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: Determination of all diffeomorphism invariant tensor fields on the space of smooth positive densities on a compact manifold with corners
papers.abstract: It was proved in [3] that on a closed manifold of dimension greater than one, every smooth weak Riemannian metric on the space of smooth positive probability densities that is invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group is a multiple of the Fisher--Rao metric. Here we describe all purely covariant tensor fields of arbitrary order on the space of positive densities of a compact manifold with corners which are invariant under the action of the connected component of the diffeomorphism group. Finally, we classify the considerably fewer purely contravariant invariant tensor fields, describe the basic mixed contraction, and indicate the expected form of general invariant tensor fields.

papers.title: Noncommutative Maximal Averages over Submanifolds and Variable Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish noncommutative maximal inequalities for averages over submanifolds in the $L^p$-spaces associated with semifinite von Neumann algebras. For every $1<p\leq\infty$, we prove local maximal bounds for smooth submanifolds of finite type at the parameter origin, and global bounds over all positive scales for polynomial parametrizations, without a finite-type assumption and with constants depending only on $p$, the degree and the dimensions. For variable hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq3$, satisfying a uniform rotational curvature condition, we obtain local maximal bounds for $p>n/(n-1)$. To our knowledge, these are the first such noncommutative inequalities for general lower-dimensional submanifolds and polynomial images. The key step is a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for a regularized auxiliary family adapted to non-isotropic dilations. The geometric kernels need not satisfy the pointwise smoothness or $L^2$-Dini conditions required by existing noncommutative Calderón--Zygmund theories. We combine a Calderón--Zygmund decomposition based on Cuculescu projections with integral regularity estimates, a non-isotropic Littlewood--Paley decomposition and Fourier decay to prove this endpoint estimate. Marcinkiewicz interpolation yields maximal $L^p$ bounds for the regularized averages, and interpolation with Fourier-based $L^2$ bounds recovers the original averages. The variable-hypersurface result uses oscillatory $TT^*$ estimates and localization. As applications, we obtain maximal ergodic inequalities for trace-preserving actions of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and, under additional assumptions, bilaterally almost uniform convergence results for the associated normalized averages.
papers.comments: 92 pages. The main content of the paper is unchanged. The abstract and introduction have been revised, and typographical errors elsewhere have been corrected

papers.title: Local stability of direct Mach configurations
papers.abstract: We investigate the local stability of direct Mach configurations for the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations. Given a piecewise constant direct Mach configuration with subsonic flow behind both the reflected shock and the Mach stem, we prove that under a transversality condition on the shock polar loops and a suitable condition on the truncation segment, every sufficiently small perturbation of the incoming flow gives rise to a Mach configuration that is a small perturbation of the background one, in the sense that the reflected shock, the Mach stem and the slip line, together with the downstream subsonic flow, stay close to their background counterparts. The triple point is fixed at the origin, and the domain is truncated at a finite distance. Euler--Lagrange coordinates are employed to transform the unknown contact discontinuity curve (slip line) into a fixed boundary and to write the full Euler system as a first-order elliptic system for the flow direction and pressure coupled to transport equations for the Bernoulli and entropy quantities. The key idea in dealing with the contact discontinuity is to solve a mixed boundary value problem, in divergence form with discontinuous coefficients, for a single elliptic equation, so that continuity of the scalar unknown and its conormal flux allows reconstruction of the flow direction and pressure with the required contact discontinuity conditions.

papers.title: Real-rootedness and ultra log-concavity of rank-two matroid Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial of a rank-two matroid with exactly three parallel classes is real-rooted whenever its smallest parallel class has size at most three. This bound is sharp: the loopless rank-two matroids with parallel-class sizes $(4,561,600)$ and $(4,a,a+29)$, for all sufficiently large integers $a$, have $h^*$-polynomials that are not real-rooted. By matroid duality, these examples disprove Ferroni's real-rootedness conjecture even for cycle matroids of theta graphs. Nevertheless, every matroid of rank two or corank two has a positive $h^*$-coefficient sequence that is ultra log-concave of order equal to the polynomial's degree. In particular, the unimodality conjecture holds in both cases.

papers.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
papers.abstract: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.
papers.comments: Updated reference list. Added concluding examples. 43 Pages

papers.title: On the asymptotics of the Erdős-Rogers function
papers.abstract: The Erdős-Rogers function $f_{\ell,s}(n)$ is the largest order of a $K_\ell$-free induced subgraph guaranteed to exist in every $K_s$-free graph on $n$ vertices. While this function is well understood for $s=\ell+1$, the case where $s$ is much larger than $\ell$ has remained wide open. A long-standing lower bound of Sudakov states that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\geq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$, while a recent result of Bradač shows that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell-1}{s-1}+o(1)}$. In this paper, we close this gap asymptotically by proving that $f_{\ell,s}(n)= n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$. More precisely, we prove that for all $2\leq \ell<s$, we have $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s-\ell}+o(1)}$. Our proof builds on Bradač's recent tight construction for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, which can be viewed as the $\ell=2$ case of our result.
papers.comments: 30 pages, added an appendix to the previous version

papers.title: Strong Artin Conjecture for Generalized Octahedral Representations in $\mathrm{GL}_3$
papers.abstract: We prove the strong Artin conjecture for the largest solvable Artin representations in three dimensions, whose projective image is isomorphic to the affine special linear group $C_3^2\rtimes \mathrm{SL}(2, 3)$. It is also the last solvable case in three dimensions. This is achieved with a new case of base change and automorphic induction for non-Galois quartic extensions with no intermediate fields. We additionally deduce the strong Artin conjecture for all 6-dimensional primitive solvable Artin representations.
papers.comments: 20 pages, minor improvements and typo fixes

papers.title: Stanley-Reisner Theory in Mixed Characteristic
papers.abstract: We discuss a class of mixed characteristic rings defined analogously to Stanley-Reisner rings by replacing one variable with a uniformizing parameter for a discrete valuation ring. We adapt Hochster's formula for Tor and Ext modules, Hochster's formula for local cohomology, and Terai's criterion for Serre conditions to this new setting; one of the tools needed is cellular sheaf cohomology, for which we give a brief treatment.
papers.comments: This version differs from the orignal posting only in that an error in the statemnt of one result is corrected. The proof is unaffected

papers.title: Dynamic Coded Distributed Computing with Joint File Placement and Reduce Function Reassignment
papers.abstract: Coded distributed computing (CDC) mitigates the Shuffle communication bottleneck through coded multicast, but existing schemes with predetermined worker populations do not directly adapt to worker arrivals and disconnections. To address these dynamics, we propose a dynamic CDC scheme that preserves surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while exploiting the storage brought by arriving clusters. The model accommodates general MapReduce tasks under a placement that is partly fixed and partly new. The scheme uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays (PDAs) for file placement. A delivery-aware greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions, and a Communication Array allows workers with no Reduce function to serve as coded transmitters. For arbitrary feasible disconnections, the scheme's exact communication load is derived. A converse bound under one-shot communication shows that, in the absence of disconnections, the scheme lies within a factor of 2 of the lower bound under these assumptions when new clusters arrive, and within a factor of 4 otherwise.

papers.title: Smooth perturbation theory and generic Cantor spectrum for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic operators
papers.abstract: We consider multi-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with monotone sawtooth-type potentials in the perturbative localization regime. We prove that a given gap is closed iff a corresponding (via a natural gap labeling) eigenfunction vanishes at the origin. Using this, we show that for a generic choice of the sampling function $f$, the spectrum of such an operator is a Cantor set, with all possible gaps being open. We also provide a class of functions $f$ for which some gaps are closed. Finally, we observe that certain gaps are more difficult to close than the others.
papers.comments: Fixed an error in Example 4.12 in the previous version: condition (4.16) is not possible due to monotonicity of $f$, which leads to Corollary 4.12 and a separate class of gaps (semi-principal gaps). Added Examples 4.13 and 4.14 for further illustration

papers.title: Upper bounds on the Turán density of projective hypergraphs over a finite field
papers.abstract: For a prime power $q\geq2$ and an integer $m\geq2$, let $PG(m,q)$ denote the $m-$dimensional projective hypergraph over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Employing the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method and using the incidence structure, we establish the Turán density of $PG(m,q)$ \begin{equation*} π(PG(m,q))\leq\begin{cases} \left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{q}} & \text{ if } m=2, \left(1-\frac{1}{(q+1)|E(PG(m-1,q))|}\right)^{\frac{1}{1+q^{m-1}}} & \text{ if } m\geq3. \end{cases} \end{equation*} The previously known upper bound on its Turán density was $1-\binom{q^m}{q}^{-1}$. As a consequence of our estimate, this upper bound is improved for each prime power $q\geq3$ and for each dimension index $m\geq2$. For a positive integer $t$, let $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ be the $(q+1)-$graph formed by taking $t$ copies of the $PG(2,q)$ that shares a common edge. Using the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method, we establish that the upper bound of the Turán density of $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ is $\left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{qt}}$.
papers.comments: $r-$graph, Turán density, projective plane and hyperplane, $\mathsf{L}^{p}-$method

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Stochastic First-Order Algorithms with Variance Reduction in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We establish complexity lower bounds for stochastic first-order algorithms in nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, allowing algorithms to use variance reduction. Our main contribution is a lower bound for a zero-respecting algorithm class that permits variance reduction, extending beyond the algorithmic restrictions imposed by some existing lower bounds. We consider objectives with an $L$-Lipschitz continuous joint gradient, a compact convex dual domain of Euclidean radius at most $D_Y$, and a primal value function, defined by maximizing the objective over the dual variable, with initial suboptimality at most $Δ$. The target accuracy $\varepsilon$ is measured by the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope of the constrained primal value function with parameter $1/(2L)$. Under an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle with variance at most $σ^2$ and mean-squared smoothness, we prove the lower bound $Ω\!\left(L^2D_YΔ\varepsilon^{-3}+L^3D_Y^2Δσ^2\varepsilon^{-6}\right)$. This result quantifies the dependence on accuracy, dual-domain radius, and oracle noise even when variance reduction is allowed. We also establish complementary lower bounds for nonconvex--strongly-concave minimax optimization. With dual strong-concavity parameter $μ>0$ and condition number $κ:=L/μ$, we obtain $Ω\!\left(LΔ\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon^{-2}+LΔκσ^2\varepsilon^{-4}\right)$ under the bounded-variance oracle model. Under the additional mean-squared smoothness condition with constant $\bar L$, we obtain $Ω\!\left(LΔ\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon^{-2}+Δ\bar Lσκ^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-3}\right)$. Together, these results identify complexity barriers across the concave and strongly concave regimes, with the main nonconvex--concave bound remaining valid for algorithms that use variance reduction.

papers.title: Fast Stochastic Post-Fault Replanning for Launch Vehicles under Persistent Parametric Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Post-fault ascent replanning for launch vehicles requires rapid joint trajectory-guidance replanning under uncertainty to maintain closed-loop constraint satisfaction. In particular, propulsion performance cannot be promptly and fully identified after a fault, leaving persistent parametric uncertainty throughout the remaining flight. A fast stochastic ascent replanning method is developed to address this problem. To efficiently account for the cross-time correlation induced by persistent parametric uncertainty, a fast system level synthesis formulation is developed with a Riccati-based solution structure. The resulting feedback synthesis is complemented by a task-oriented terminal weighting method that shapes terminal covariance according to post-injection correction demand. These components are integrated with nominal trajectory replanning, chance-constraint tightening, and online feedback realization to establish a real-time joint stochastic trajectory-guidance replanning framework for launch vehicles. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the proposed method effectively suppresses the influence of persistent parametric uncertainty and maintains stable convergence and high injection accuracy across parameter sweeps, with subsecond solution times. Compared with conventional ascent guidance, the empirical constraint-violation rate is substantially reduced.

papers.title: Randomization Beyond Deterministic Adaptivity in Parallel Sampling
papers.abstract: Parallel samplers, including masked diffusion models, generate several coordinates per round from conditional marginals, and their accuracy depends on which coordinates are revealed together. A schedule can be improved in two natural ways: adaptively, by choosing later batches from the values already generated, or by randomization, by drawing the schedule at random. We show that randomization is strictly more powerful. For every $r \geq 1$ we construct a full-support distribution on $9r$ binary coordinates such that every deterministic three-round sampler, even with value-dependent batches and arbitrary product kernels, has forward Kullback-Leibler divergence at least $γr - \log 4$ with $γ\approx 0.0966$, whereas drawing one of four fixed schedules with two fair bits drives the divergence below $18 r β^r$ with $β\approx 0.966$. Both samplers query conditionals of the same target. The separation holds for every fixed number of rounds $T \geq 2$, a strict advantage survives perturbations of the target and errors in the conditional predictor, and exact rational arithmetic certifies the gap at nine coordinates, where trained neural predictors preserve it. The mechanism is a hidden mixture: each schedule preserves the dependence pattern of one component, while no deterministic first batch can serve them all.

papers.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
papers.abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.

papers.title: Analyticity and tautness of smooth Dupin submanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth immersed Euclidean submanifold is locally Nash if it satisfies the Dupin condition on the regular part of its unit normal bundle. This condition is equivalent to the Morse-Bott property of all squared distance functions and, for compact connected embedded submanifolds, to tautness over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. No local finiteness assumption on the regular locus, or regularity assumption on its complement, is required. We also prove that, in each fixed Euclidean space, every compact connected smooth taut submanifold can be joined to one of finitely many representatives by a Nash isotopy through taut embedded submanifolds. In each fixed intrinsic dimension, we also obtain only finitely many diffeomorphism types admitting taut embeddings in Euclidean spaces. We first treat hypersurfaces by combining a dimension-dependent degree bound on proper Dupin pieces with a continuation argument using finite jets and resultants. An analytic Hessian criterion then gives the Morse-Bott property, and small tubes extend the conclusions to arbitrary codimension. The degree bound also provides uniform semialgebraic complexity. Together with the semialgebraicity of tautness in parameter families and Nash triviality, this yields the finiteness and deformation results. Classical classification theorems give further topological restrictions.
papers.comments: 29 pages. Substantially revised and reorganized, with expanded proofs. The Morse-Bott characterization of the regular Dupin condition is made explicit. The analytic Hessian criterion is strengthened to a necessary and sufficient condition. Title and abstract updated

papers.title: Dunkl--BMO functions representable in terms of generalized balayage of Carleson measures and an application
papers.abstract: We characterize compactly supported functions $f$ in Dunkl--BMO spaces as those that can be written as \begin{equation*} f=g+\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}, \end{equation*} the sum of some bounded function $g$ and the generalized balayage $\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}$ of a Carleson measure on $\mathbb{R}^{N}\times(0,\infty)$ associated with the Dunkl--Poisson semigroup. As a direct application of this representation of Dunkl--BMO functions, we establish a new characterization of the Hardy space in the Dunkl setting via a principal value integral related to $\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}$. Moreover, analogous conclusions hold for the Dunkl--heat semigroup as well.

papers.title: Measuring the roughness of a signal
papers.abstract: We study the non-parametric estimation of the roughness of a path from discretely sampled observations. Our approach is based on the concept of normalized power variation of a path. The estimator identifies a variation index by comparing coarse increments with local sums of fine increments. We prove pathwise consistency under Hölder regularity, nondegenerate coarse critical power sums, uniform local bounds on fine critical power sums, and separation of the two sampling scales and obtain a convergence rate for the estimator. Neither convergence of critical variation nor monotonicity of the finite-sample statistic is required. The result applies to fractional Brownian motion under dyadic sampling and to Schauder series with bounded coefficients bounded away from zero.
