For signed Takagi--Landsberg functions we obtain a uniform asymptotic formula and a quantitative bound for every root of the estimating equation in a fixed parameter interval. For fractional Brownian motion, we obtain asymptotic uniqueness of the estimating root and a polynomial almost-sure error bound. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments for Takagi-Landsberg functions, fractional Brownian motion and the stochastic heat equation.

papers.title: Improved dimension bounds for Falconer's distance problem in the plane
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^2$ be analytic with $t=\dim_{\mathrm H}E>1$. We prove $\dim_{\mathrm H}ΔE\ge 4/5+η_0$ for an absolute, non-explicit constant $η_0>0$, and \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}ΔE\ge \frac{t^2-2t+5}{2t^2-7t+10} \quad\text{for }1<t\le\frac{11-\sqrt{41}}{4}, \] which reaches $7/8$ at the right endpoint. For pinned distances, $\dim_{\mathrm H}Δ_xE\ge q_*=0.7813\ldots$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^2$ outside an exceptional set of Hausdorff dimension at most one, with stronger bounds depending on $t$ and further exceptional-set estimates. If $E$ is compact and supports an $s$-Frostman measure $μ$, $s>1$, then \[ \underline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}Δ_xE\ge \max\left\{\frac45+η_0,\min\left\{\frac{3s+1}{5},\frac78\right\}\right\} \] for $μ$-almost every $x$. The same bound holds for pinned Hausdorff dimension under a common dyadic mass law, allowing oscillation with scale. We retain information about both endpoints in the Kolmogorov complexity estimates of Stull and Fiedler--Stull. Applying the partition estimates with the endpoints reversed yields $4/5$ and the rational bound. Equality forces both information profiles to have excess information on a common interval of scales. Encoding one source measure for all pins converts this constraint into a configuration of points and circles with many rich perpendicular bisectors. Lower bounds of Katz--Tardos and Ren--Wang contradict the upper bound of Fu--Gan--Ren; compactness then gives $η_0>0$. This rigidity argument has a precedent in the work of Héra, Shmerkin and Yavicoli on Furstenberg sets, using Bourgain's projection theorem. A separate finite-scale selection proves the pinned lower box bound.

papers.title: Hodge and Hodge-Witt polygons under specialization
papers.abstract: We show that, in equal characteristic $p$, the Hodge-Witt polygon can only move down and domino numbers can only increase under specialization in smooth proper families. We also show that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal{O}_C$ lies on or above the Hodge-Witt polygon of its special fiber, where $C$ is a complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We further show that, in this mixed-characteristic setting, if the crystalline cohomology of the special fiber is torsion-free in degrees $n$ and $n+1$, then the degree-$n$ Hodge polygon of the generic fiber lies on or below the abstract Hodge polygon of the special fiber. We illustrate these comparisons with explicit examples.

papers.title: Diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts: Varadhan asymptotics and path-law singularity
papers.abstract: We study the Euclidean Varadhan formula (EVF) and path laws for diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts in dimension $d\geq2$. For drifts given by smooth bounded skew-symmetric stream matrices, we prove a quantitative lower bound under a sector condition with a lower-order term. Its constants depend only on the dimension and the sector condition data. By approximation, the locally uniform Euclidean lower bound holds for all divergence-free $L^\infty_t{\rm BMO}^{-1}_x$ drifts. However, a time-dependent counterexample shows that EVF can fail even for a drift in $L^\infty_tL^d_x$. A complementary upper bound is given under a structural decomposition condition. In particular, for every time-independent $L^{d,\infty}$ drift (without any smallness assumption), and the decoupled diffusion associated with the two-dimensional vorticity equation, the EVF holds. Finally, we construct a time-independent $L^d$ drift whose SDE has a unique strong solution from the origin and whose path law is mutually singular with the corresponding driftless Brownian law. The same diffusion satisfies EVF, showing that Brownian short-time endpoint costs can persist despite singularity of the path law.

papers.title: Quantitative Stability Of Aggregation-Diffusion Under Local Attraction
papers.abstract: In this note, we establish quantitative stability of aggregation-diffusion energy for compactly supported data. Our consideration focuses on the degenerate diffusion with local attraction that are asymptotically flat at infinity, such as Riesz kernels. We characterize the spectral gap of the Wasserstein Hessian at steady states.

papers.title: Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent type
papers.abstract: We study the Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent types and its application to the representation theory of the (mixed, small, and Lusztig) quantum supergroups. Using local and global models and SW-Zastava spaces, we construct factorization functors and compare the Iwahori Gaiotto category with the category $O$ of the mixed quantum supergroup. We then study the images of intersection cohomology sheaves and the metaplectic Hecke action. In type A, we describe the finite and affine monodromic categories, the corresponding Yokonuma--Hecke actions, and their role in the Kazhdan--Lusztig algorithm. The last section treats the pointwise purity.

papers.title: Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations and Mixed-Type Chebyshev Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
papers.abstract: We characterize when a semi-infinite banded totally positive matrix admits a positive bidiagonal factorization, without assuming boundedness, and establish criteria for stability under perturbations. These criteria distinguish whether the initial factor entries are fixed or allowed to vary. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, such factorizations always exist; a factorization can be chosen to depend analytically on all sufficiently small perturbations within the same band if and only if the polynomial symbol has distinct roots. Explicit root formulas determine the associated mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials and their matrix of positive measures. They also yield scalar linear forms independent of the chosen factorization, from which we obtain asymptotic zero spacing and sine-kernel limits. We further treat finite boundary modifications and limiting zero distributions for matrices with convergent diagonals.

papers.title: Terminal Blocks of Primes in Pisot Numeration Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a prime number theorem for fixed terminal block words in a family of Pisot integer numeration systems defined by canonical block expansions. Suppose that the dominant root $\varphi$ is a Pisot number and that the characteristic polynomial $P_h$ is its minimal polynomial. Then every terminal block word of total digit-length $m$ occurs among the primes with asymptotic frequency $\varphi^{-m}$. The result recovers the known Zeckendorf and generalized Fibonacci cases and extends the terminal-prime problem to irreducible Pisot-unit systems without assuming that the recurrence coefficients are monotone, that the canonical expansions are greedy, or that the finiteness property (F) holds. Explicit non-$β$ families and Pisot units failing (F) illustrate this extension. The main structural ingredient is a canonical block language whose expansion of the companion substitution fixed word records the corresponding integer expansions in natural order. This connects terminal conditions with Rauzy cylinder windows and then with a linear orbit on a compact torus. The required multiplicity-one geometry follows from Barge's pure-discreteness theorem after reversal of the substitution words. The same toral model yields prime genericity for finite factors of the substitution fixed word, polynomial sampling laws, asymptotic independence from fixed congruence classes, fixed-shift correlation formulas, and Möbius orthogonality. Combined with established prime theorems, it also gives a terminal refinement of Chebotarev and arithmetic progressions inside fixed terminal prime classes.

papers.title: Making Every Number from 1 to N Under a Fixed Cycle of $+$, $\times$, $-$, $÷$
papers.abstract: Start with the number $2$. At each move, combine two numbers already made, but the operations must be used in the fixed repeating order $+,\times,-,÷$. We ask for the fewest moves needed to make every integer from $1$ to $N$. Since $2$ is already one of the numbers we want and each move makes at most one new number, at least $N-1$ moves are needed. We show that $N-1$ moves are also enough for every $N\ge 9$. Conventional induction cannot work, because a division that comes right after a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ produces numbers already made. Instead we extend a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ to $\{1,\dots,3P\}$ all at once, which counting shows is the smallest multiplicative extension $P\to kP$ that can work, and then adjust the last few moves to reach every other $N$. For $9\le N\le 33$ we give explicit sequences, found by computer search.

papers.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
papers.abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.

papers.title: Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature
papers.abstract: We systematically explore the relationship between edge-connectivity and Lin--Lu--Yau curvature for graphs. The intuition is that a connected graph with large Lin--Lu--Yau curvature should also have large edge-connectivity, and vice versa under suitable conditions. We prove that the edge-connectivity of a connected graph is bounded lower by the product of its minimum degree, its Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and the constant $\frac{3}{2}$. We also provide two lower bounds on the edge-connectivity of a graph that guarantee positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature, and discuss the sharpness of these bounds.

papers.title: Infinite Girth, Finite Quotients, and Nielsen Connectivity in Groups
papers.abstract: We develop new methods for studying infinite girth in finitely generated residually finite groups, particularly those containing no non-abelian free subgroups and satisfying no non-trivial group law. Our main contribution is a probabilistic Nielsen-component lifting principle, based on product replacement graphs, which provides a criterion for transferring suitable generation and word-avoidance properties of finite quotients to the ambient group. As an application, we prove that every finitely generated group admitting infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic non-abelian finite simple quotients has infinite girth, with extensions to quasisimple and, under additional hypotheses, almost-simple quotients. We further establish infinite girth for the B. H. Neumann group and the Bou-Rabee-Seward group, obtaining new results on the occurrence of non-abelian finite simple quotients and sections. By a different construction, we also prove that Alt_fin(Z) semidirect Z has infinite girth. Finally, we establish a marked finite-quotient characterization of infinite girth for finitely generated residually finite groups and prove that, for linear groups over fields of characteristic zero, large marked girth can be realized in congruence quotients. We conclude with several open questions and remarks arising from our results.
papers.comments: Many new results were added to the current version (e.g. Theorem A, Corollary B & Corollary C), and many structural changes were made. The Question 1.1 is completely resolved now. Question 1.2 was added and also resolved. Section 5.3, 6.1, and 6.2 are added to the last question and remark section

papers.title: Statistics of divisor functions over function fields
papers.abstract: Extending recent works on the restricted divisor function over integers, we consider an analogue of this function over the function field. We provide some exact and asymptotic formulas related to this function.

papers.title: A rank bound for bases and circuits in binary matroids
papers.abstract: Let \(b(M)\), \(d(M)\), and \(r(M)\) denote the number of bases, the number of circuits, and the rank of a matroid \(M\), respectively. Using a weighted count of fundamental circuits, we prove that every nonempty simple binary matroid \(M\) with no coloops satisfies \[ 2b(M)\ge(r(M)+1)d(M), \] with equality if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to the Fano matroid. This settles a conjecture recorded by Oxley in 1983. For every \(e\in E(M)\), we also establish the deletion bound \(b(M\backslash e)\ge d(M)\) and characterize its equality cases. The deletion bound yields a sharp linear lower bound for basis growth under successive series extensions. Finally, under a circuit-size exclusion condition, every pair \((C,e)\) with \(C\) a circuit of a prescribed size and \(e\in C\) can be assigned a distinct basis containing \(C-e\).

papers.title: A Kinetic Concentration criterion for Large-data Boltzmann Dynamics
papers.abstract: We establish a conditional theory of genuinely non-perturbative global dynamics for the cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials on the three-dimensional torus. We prove that any global mild solution satisfying \[ \sup_{t\ge0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}W(v)\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3}F(t,x,v)\,dv<\infty, \] for a suitable stretched-exponential weight \(W\), enjoys uniform weighted \(L^\infty\) control, is unique in the dissipative mild class, and converges exponentially to the global Maxwellian. In particular, these conclusions hold for arbitrary-amplitude solutions admitting a uniform stretched-exponential velocity upper bound. The key mechanism is a *tail-to-coercivity principle*: uniform velocity-tail control generates positive lower bounds for the local density and nonlinear collision frequency, without imposing macroscopic coercivity a priori. A double-Duhamel positivity argument also generates a Gaussian lower bound at arbitrarily short positive times, allowing initial data with local vacuum. We establish a polynomially weighted counterpart under an additional spatially uniform lower velocity profile, obtaining analogous weighted \(L^\infty\) bounds, uniqueness, and exponential relaxation. Our results provide a low-regularity alternative to conditional theories requiring smoothness and pointwise macroscopic bounds. They reveal how a single velocity-tail condition controls large-data Boltzmann dynamics and suggest a route toward problems with physical boundary conditions.
papers.comments: Revised version for journal submission, including the new Theorem 1.18. 131 pages,

papers.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
papers.abstract: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $Σ_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(Σ_m)\to 4π^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.
papers.comments: 65 pages, 7 figures. v2: Substantially revised exposition; routine computations in Riemannian geometry moved to the appendices. All comments are welcome!

papers.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
papers.abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.

papers.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k \geq 2$, there are integers $M_k$ and $P_k$ so that for all $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$, with $p>P_k$, and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding, by way of an involved algebraic argument. Reasonable bounds are provided for $P_k$ and $M_k$.
papers.comments: 35 pages. The paper is formalized, up to twos admit for the inverse Theorem 1.4, and a Theorem of Dimitrov at this URL https://github.com/lacey-gatech/restricted-polynomials-lean

papers.title: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

papers.title: Additive complements to the primes and large gaps between Romanoff numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erdős Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive. As an application, we obtain $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X$ for the longest block in $[1,X]$ containing no Romanoff number $p+2^n$, improving the bound $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X/\log\log\log X$ of Kalmynin and Konyagin. The argument also applies to $p+a^n$ for every fixed integer $a\ge2$. The key step is a lemma on large shifts, proved using truncated products of divisor sums and the removal of auxiliary primes dividing differences of shifts.
papers.comments: 32 pages. Substantially revised and expanded version of "A lower bound for additive complements to the primes", with a new title. Includes a detailed proof of a large-shift lemma and new results on gaps between Romanoff numbers

papers.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
papers.comments: 39 pages; a lemma simplified; AI statement enlarged;

papers.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
papers.abstract: A quasiconformal uniformization theorem of Rickman from 1966 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipschitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.

papers.title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
papers.abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. It has been a long-standing open question whether there exists an index-symmetric division ring that is infinite-dimensional over its center. We give the first such examples: using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. This applies to the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, to the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero, to quantum skew fields, to the quotient division rings of noetherian AS-regular Hopf domains, and to the quotient and degree-zero division rings of three- and four-dimensional elliptic Sklyanin algebras, which we show to be twisted Calabi--Yau. In particular, every division ring on Artin's list of noncommutative surfaces is index-symmetric.
papers.comments: 17 pages. v2: list of examples extended; minor corrections

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We study weighted Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we introduce a more refined trilinear estimate. We obtain this estimate by applying weighted bilinear restriction on half-scale cubes and combining tube traversal with trilinear Kakeya to sum the local packet energies. Together with Lorentz rescaling, it yields improved weighted extension estimates.

papers.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
papers.abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's \(L^1\) space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight phi, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence, and make the relationship with the order convergence results of Chetcuti et al. explicit. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local phi-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and \(\|h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}\|_1\to0\) for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming \(σ\)-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.
papers.comments: Revision with new appendix, and some extra results and shortenings, etc

papers.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
papers.abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.

papers.title: Global Extendability of Local Atoms in Sparse Moment Relaxations
papers.abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while their moment matrices can also carry information about solutions. We study whether atomic candidates extracted from clique blocks reveal part of a global minimizer in moment relaxations with correlative sparsity. We give sufficient conditions for global extendability. If the relaxation is value-exact and the moment matrix of a selected clique has maximum rank over the optimal face and satisfies simplicial regularity, then at least one of its atomic candidates is globally extendable. When this maximum rank is one, we derive a direct certificate for global extendability. Further examples demonstrate the necessity of value exactness for global extendability. Numerical experiments on unicycle trajectory optimization successfully yield near-optimal solutions through progressive extraction and fixing, demonstrating the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $γ: \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $Ω$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(γ(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ of $T_γM$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $Ω$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabré et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^Ω\subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^Ω:= \mathscr{W}^Ω\cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ via a foliation in the case $Ω$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.

papers.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. More unexpectedly, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite groups, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

papers.title: Near-boundary rigidity and strict maximum modulus for Neumann eigenfunctions on convex planar domains
papers.abstract: We develop a near-boundary rigidity theorem for arbitrary nonzero Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded convex planar domains. Precisely, if an eigenfunction $u$ with positive eigenvalue $μ$ has an interior maximum-modulus point $p$ satisfying $\sqrtμ\,\text{dist}(p,\partialΩ)\leπ/\sqrt3$, then $Ω$ must be a rectangle and $u$ must be a cosine of one coordinate, and $μ\ge4μ_2(Ω)$, with the factor $4$ being sharp. This shows that a scale-invariant distance condition at just one maximum-modulus point determines the geometry of the entire domain and the explicit form of the eigenfunction. We further prove that the maximum modulus of every second Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded convex planar domain is attained only on the boundary, without assuming boundary smoothness or eigenvalue simplicity. Moreover, we also prove strict boundary maximum modulus for higher Neumann eigenfunctions under suitable conditions, including all third Neumann eigenfunctions on arbitrary triangles.

papers.title: Disproving two conjectures on the cospectrality of complete tripartite graphs
papers.abstract: The spectral distance between two non-isomorphic graphs of the same order is the lp-distance between their ordered adjacency spectra, and the cospectrality of a graph G on a family Gn is the minimum such distance from G to another graph in Gn. Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that, for every n >= 4 and for p in {1, 2}, the cospectrality of the complete tripartite graph Kn,n,n among all graphs on 3n vertices is attained exactly at Kn-1,n,n+1. We disprove both conjectures for every n >= 4. As a counterexample we use the graph Hn = (n - 1)K1 nabla (K1 union Kn,n), whose spectrum we determine. It yields cs(1)(Kn,n,n) <= 1 + o(1) and cs(2)(Kn,n,n) <= 1/2 + o(1) as n -> infinity, contrary to the conjectured values. We also study the cospectrality of Kn,n,n for p = 2, asymptotically, among complete multipartite graphs with possibly added isolated vertices. We conclude the paper by posing a conjecture that Hn is the unique graph nearest to Kn,n,n for p in {1, 2} and every n >= 3, and a problem asking whether every connected graph H with sigma(2)(Kn,n,n,H) < 2/3 has an adjacency matrix of rank at most 5.

papers.title: Graph and Hypergraph Counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation Conjecture Beyond $n^{k-1}$
papers.abstract: For a fixed $k$-graph $F$, let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\text{ex}(n,F)+q$ edges. Let $c(n,F)$ be the minimum number created by adding one edge to an extremal $F$-free $k$-graph. We construct stable counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for every $k\ge2$. The ratio $h_F(n,q)/(q c(n,F))$ tends to zero over ranges extending beyond $n^{k-1}$. For graphs, we give examples of every chromatic number at least three. In particular, there is a graph $F$ for which this ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{4/3})$. For $k\ge3$, we use connected linear expansions of $G=(M_a\cup K_{1,b}\cup I_h)\vee K_{m_1,\ldots,m_{k-1}}$. Under explicit parameter conditions, the ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{k-1+(b-1)/(a+b-1)})$ when $b\ge k+1$. We prove the exact Turán theorems for both constructions and determine their unique extremal graphs and hypergraphs. Keywords: supersaturation; extremal graph; linear hypergraph; graph expansion; stability.

papers.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
papers.abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.
papers.comments: v2: revised and extended version with a new title. Main text 20 pages, 3 figures; Supplementary Information (41 pages) appended. Data, certificates and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23841282

papers.title: Stationary Unit Roots and Inference in Softplus INGARCH Models
papers.abstract: A unit root makes linear count time series models such as the Poisson INGARCH(1,1) nonstationary. We show that a softplus link changes this. Weiß, Zhu and Hoshiyar (2022) introduced softplus INGARCH models and gave a sufficient condition for stationarity. For Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related versions of these models, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition, which allows a unit root. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail, and the observations can have infinite variance or long memory. To our knowledge, this is the first stationary unit root established for an INGARCH-type count model. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is asymptotically normal both below and at the unit root, including cases with infinite variance. Two applications show that unit-root conclusions can depend on the softplus scale.

papers.title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

papers.title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
papers.abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler--Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by n converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative sets of assumptions allowing less regular drifts, based on small-jump integrability or smoothing estimates for Lévy semigroups. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
papers.abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

papers.title: Gaps between roots in ballistic deposition on a strip: linear variance, Gaussian limits and a Poisson regime
papers.abstract: Mansour, Rastegar and Roitershtein studied the \emph{roots} of ballistic deposition on a cyclic strip of $K$ sites, namely the sites that receive a particle at height one, and the number $D_{i,K}$ of pairs of consecutive roots at distance $i+1$. They computed the first two moments of $D_{i,K}$ for $i\le7$. They conjectured that for every $i$ the mean and the variance are exactly linear in $K$, that $D_{i,K}$ satisfies a central limit theorem, and that the standardized vector $(D_{i,K})_{i\ge1}$ converges to a Gaussian process. We prove these conjectures. The key observation is that the roots are exactly the valleys of a uniformly random circular arrangement, so that $D_{i,K}$ counts occurrences of a family of consecutive patterns. We determine sizes from which the moments are exactly linear; the size for the mean is sharp for every $i$, and those for the second moments cannot be lowered in any case we checked. We give closed forms for the variance constants and for the limiting covariance; the mean constants agree with a known distribution of distances between surface peaks. The reduction and the exact moment formulas are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib. We also prove a Wasserstein bound of order $(\mathbb{E} D_{i,K})^{-1/2}$ that is uniform in $i$, and a local limit theorem. Finally we describe the limit completely when $i$ grows with $K$: it is degenerate, Poisson or Gaussian according as $\mathbb{E} D_{i,K}$ tends to zero, to a positive constant, or to infinity.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of Kähler geometry: the classical Kähler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Ampère energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics.
papers.comments: comments are welcome. v2: exposition slightly improved

papers.title: Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients
papers.abstract: The elliptic regularity theory with $W^{1,n}$ coefficients dates back to Miranda, who established $W^{2,2}$ estimates for elliptic equations in divergence and non-divergence forms. For any such fixed operator, the $L^p$ estimates for all $1<p<\infty$ follow from the theory of VMO coefficients developed since the 1990s. However, the VMO theory does not yield constants in the estimates uniformly controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the VMO modulus. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems with coefficients in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, allowing an unbounded spatially skew-symmetric part. The constants in the estimates depend quantitatively on the critical Sobolev norms, and we show that they are sharp for scalar equations when $p>n$ and for systems when $p\neq 2$.
papers.comments: Sharpness of the estimate and Hajłasz-space version included; exposition refined

papers.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
papers.abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing the steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansions of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose monodromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddles. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstrate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package \href{https://github.com/jfeldbrugge/IntegralResurgence.jl}{\texttt{IntegralResurgence.jl}}.

papers.title: A Criterion for Finite Hypergeometric Reductions of Lauricella's $F_C$ with Arguments Related by Cube Roots of Unity
papers.abstract: We consider the germ at the origin of Lauricella's function $F_C^{(3)}(a,b;c_0,c_1,c_2;κ,ωκ,ω^2κ)$, where $ω=\exp(2π\sqrt{-1}/3)$. We assume that $a,b,c_0,c_1,c_2$ avoid nonpositive integers and that $c_0,c_1,c_2$ also avoid half-integers. We consider finite linear combinations of ordinary generalized hypergeometric series with arguments $ακ^3$, where $α$ is a nonzero complex constant that may vary between summands, each multiplied by a nonnegative integer power of $κ$. Every target series has lower parameters outside the nonpositive integers and converges near the origin or terminates. We prove that such a representation exists if and only if, for each $j=0,1,2$, either $c_j-c_0$ or $c_j+c_0$ is an integer, and construct finite sums of ordinary ${}_9F_8$ functions when this condition holds. We prove necessity from irreducible differential equations of order $24$ for the generating functions of the three coefficient subsequences and from their formal solutions at infinity.

papers.title: On the residual polynilpotence of tree products of groups with locally cyclic edge subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a non-empty class of nilpotent groups closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, finite direct products, and unrestricted direct powers of the form $\prod_{x \in X}Y_{x}$, where $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $Y_{x}$ ($x \in X$) are isomorphic copies of a group $Y \in \mathcal{N}$. Suppose also that $T$ is a tree product of $n$ groups ($2 \leqslant n < \infty$) with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ is the class of all torsion-free $\mathcal{N}$-groups, and the symbol $\mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ ($k \geqslant 1$) denotes the class of polynilpotent groups such that $X \in \mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ if and only if $X$ has a subnormal series of length at most $k$ whose factors belong to $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$. We prove that if all free and all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n+1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. We prove also that if all vertex groups lie in $\mathcal{N}$, then $T$ has a homomorphism onto a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n-1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group acting injectively on all edge subgroups. By assuming that $\mathcal{N}$ is the class of all nilpotent groups, we get a stronger result: if all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. It follows that all cyclically-pinched one-relator groups are residually finitely generated $(\mathit{Poly}_{2}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-groups.
papers.comments: Corollary was strengthened; some comments were added below its statement. In English and Russian

papers.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
papers.abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

papers.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
papers.abstract: For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that integrating one coordinate of the truncated correlation of order $k$ for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF) gives $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. The integral converges absolutely, and the identity holds pointwise, including at coincident fixed coordinates by continuous extension. This answers the marginal-identity part of Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran's question for the planar GEF. We also prove a general criterion for simple point processes: under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions, the identities hold almost everywhere if there are compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one, eventually equal to one on each compact set, whose linear statistics have variances tending to zero. For GEF zeros, strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions. The proof combines a mixed-cumulant estimate with the partition formula for ordinary and factorial cumulants.

papers.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
papers.abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith--Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $\mathcal E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that this dg algebra fits into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer--Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg $\mathcal E_M$-modules and the derived category of \mbox{$D$-modules} on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra $\mathcal E_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

papers.title: A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fréchet Means on Real Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fréchet mean is their standard sample mean [12,10,16,24]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fréchet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [19]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $δ$ of the mean has volume $O(δ)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fréchet Hessian vanishes.

papers.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\C$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold
papers.abstract: We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper $q$-colorings on sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$. We prove that, whenever $q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d$, Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. This improves the previous bound $q = (α^* + o_d(1))d$ where $α^* = 1.7632...$ is the unique solution of $x = \exp(1/x)$ on $[1, \infty)$ by Efthymiou, Hayes, Štefankovič, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bezáková, Galanis, Goldberg, and Štefankovič (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.

papers.title: On the stabilizing effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with a vanishing normal component, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

papers.title: From Inverse Vandermonde Matrices to the Shift Structure of the Dirichlet Eta and Beta Functions
papers.abstract: We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the inverse of Vandermonde matrices with nodes drawn from the quadratic sequences $u\_n = n^2$ and $u\_n = (n -1/2 )^2$. We derive new limiting formulas for the entries of the inverses, expressed through the even and odd central factorial numbers. These formulas are then used to study the asymptotic behavior of a ratio of determinants involving a modified Vandermonde matrix. For each node sequence, the corresponding determinant ratio converges uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane to an explicit expression involving the Dirichlet eta or beta function. We then study a family of related functions and, using an inversion theorem, exhibit their shift structure: the shifted values of the eta and beta functions are recovered as finite linear combinations of the family, which yields an integral form of these values as integrals of polynomials related to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials against generalized (half-)Clausen functions. A unified form of the shift representation, valid for an arbitrary base point z with Re(z) > 0, brings the eta and beta families under a single theorem. On the critical line the representation is unitary and the values on the two sides are complex conjugates.

papers.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $dγ_n=π^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12Δ+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_γ=DL^{-1/2}Π_0$, where $Π_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_γ$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(γ_n)$ and $a>\int F\,dγ_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/π$ for complex-valued inputs.
papers.comments: 33 pages. A Lean 4 formalization of the results of this paper is available at https://github.com/na0b/gaussianriesz-lean and at https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000009&version=1

papers.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
papers.abstract: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, relative to arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and rank-$n$ degenerate maps $L(A)=Ψ(u^TA)$, subject to explicit cone and matrix-pencil conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are precisely the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which consist of maps of rank three outside product form.

papers.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
papers.abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit smooth vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $Diff_0(S^n)$. By deleting one gradient component from the second generator, we obtain two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $SDiff_0(S^n)$. In both cases two generators are minimal. The proof first generates the divergence-free vector fields using rotations, a linearly modulated rotational shear, and transverse vector spherical harmonics. On $S^2$ this reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; for $n\ge4$ irreducibility of the transverse harmonic spaces completes the degree-raising argument, while $S^3$ requires a separate treatment of its two curl eigenspaces. Adding one gradient field and using the divergence map then generates all smooth vector fields. Finally, a Casimir operator for a recovered copy of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ separates the components of the generating fields and compresses the natural finite generating families to two.

papers.title: Trace Inverse Estimates and Kernel-based Meshfree Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Interface Problems
papers.abstract: Kernel Galerkin methods allow meshfree trial spaces to be generated independently in each material subdomain and refined through their center sets, without generating an approximation mesh. We establish trace inverse estimates for products of Sobolev-kernel spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche discretizations of linear elliptic interface problems. The estimates control gradient traces on subdomain boundaries by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form supplies the flux control required for stability directly from the kernel and center assumptions, without a separate discrete flux hypothesis. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{s-1}$ and $h^s$ for piecewise $H^s$ solutions, $2\le s\le m$, where $h$ is the maximum subdomain fill distance and $m$ is the kernel Sobolev order. The $L^2$ bound additionally requires piecewise $H^2$ regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For kernels $Φ_m(\varepsilon\,\cdot)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, we derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis and an $O(h^{-2})$ bound in an $L^2$-orthonormal basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and kernel scaling, while a three-dimensional heat-conduction problem in a curved composite illustrates the method.

papers.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.

papers.title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
papers.abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine the original definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve asymptotic time-uniform coverage even for independent and identically distributed settings. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation. In time-series settings, this relaxation can substantially ease restrictions on bandwidth and kernel selection. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

papers.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.
papers.comments: 23 pages. Proposition 1.10 from v1 removed, will appear elsewhere

papers.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.
papers.comments: 35 pages; exposition revised and references updated

papers.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.
papers.comments: v2: a reference to the companion paper arXiv:2610.39228 added; 27 pages, 6 tables

papers.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
papers.abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schrödinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{itΔ}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.
papers.comments: 35 pages, Corrected minor typographical errors; the results are unchanged

papers.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
papers.abstract: Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from \(2\), and let \(V\) have dimension four over \(K\). The Drinfeld upper half-spaces of \(V\) and \(Λ^2V\) define compatible open analytic subsets of \(\Pp(V)\), \(\Gr(2,V)\), and \(\Flag(1,2;V)\). Both restricted incidence projections are smooth and surjective. For every torsion-free discrete subgroup of \(\PGL(V)(K)\), the three actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the incidence correspondence descends to smooth analytic quotients. These domains contain an explicit flag defined over an unramified extension of degree seven. A symplectic form on \(V\) equips the projective domain with a contact structure and places the Grassmannian domain in \(\Sp_4/(\Sp_2\times\Sp_2)\). For torsion-free discrete symplectic groups, this contact structure descends to the quotient. Free discrete symplectic groups of every finite rank at least two give contact threefolds whose underlying Berkovich spaces have the homotopy type of a bouquet of circles. Every quotient of the projective domain by a torsion-free discrete group preserving the contact distribution is noncompact. For every torsion-free discrete projective linear group, the flag quotient and all fibers of its two incidence projections are noncompact; both projections are nonproper.
papers.comments: 17 pages. v2: new sections on torus-stable domains and on noncompactness of the quotients; corrections and revised exposition

papers.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,ω_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, in characteristic zero, for $X$ a smooth projective Poisson surface with a smooth or empty anticanonical divisor and $ρ>0$ (positive leaf rank), the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$.

papers.title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
papers.abstract: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $χ(S^n_{R}) \leq (ξ_R + o(1))^n$, where $ξ_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-\frac{1}{4R^2}) $ and $χ(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.

papers.title: Who pays for urban environment management? The role of the third-party service provider
papers.abstract: The dominant contemporary paradigm of direct state-led urban environmental regulation entails significant risks, including high administrative burden, frequent conflicts with polluting entities, and economic vulnerabilities for those sources. To address these deficiencies, this paper integrates third-party service provider (TPSP) into China's existing management framework as a beneficial extension beyond conventional government intervention. Utilizing an evolutionary game approach, we compare two distinct institutional settings, a non-integration management mode and an integration management mode, and scrutinize the evolutionary dynamics across both two- and three-dimensional systems. To enhance system robustness, we embed a strategic behavior-based dynamic punishment mechanism that effectively eliminates the perturbing effects of varied penalty rules, thereby steering all stakeholders toward an ideal stable state. This comparative institutional analysis isolates the marginal contribution of third-party intermediation, specifies when outsourcing environmental services outperforms direct government enforcement, and reframes evolutionary game theory as a design device for institutional self-correction. Furthermore, a predefined variable importance analysis is conducted to highlight critical factors warranting attention in practical policy implementation. Extensive simulation experiments, carried out under diverse system-level and parameter-level conditions, validate the theoretical properties of our model. The findings offer concrete managerial insights to inform the formulation of more effective urban environmental supervision regulations.

papers.title: Finite comparison and countable injective hulls
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to the unrestricted product version of Bergman's finite-comparison theorem, even when all factors have finite length. Finite comparison does hold for quasi-injective common modules under finite cogeneration. We also prove a semidirect-product case of Bergman's Question 3.2. For a semiprimary right self-injective ring, failure of the quasi-Frobenius conclusion produces a cyclic module with simple top and countably infinite homogeneous socle inside a fixed countable injective hull. We identify its extension class and an associated opposite-side extension obstruction. Over the square-zero algebra $k\oplus k^{(\mathbb N)}$, we compute the countable hull quotient as endomorphisms modulo finite-rank maps. This quotient also describes the socle-radical quotient of the regular product, yields a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors, and detects splitting of specified simple submodules. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.

papers.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
papers.abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

papers.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
papers.abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defects and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection. Suitable variational regularizations are also proposed to deal with the motion of singular defect lines.
papers.comments: Second version. Largely expanded. Comments welcome

papers.title: Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels
papers.abstract: Let $0<σ<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$.
