We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[ \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-Δ)^{σ/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $σ>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $σ=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.

papers.title: The sharp leading asymptotics of the self-energy of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model
papers.abstract: We study the self-energy $E_0(α,Λ)$ of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $Λ$, retaining the vacuum contribution of the $A^2$ term (no normal ordering); $α=e^2/4π$ is the fine structure constant. Lieb and Loss proved lower and upper bounds of orders $α^{1/2}Λ^{3/2}$ and $α^{2/7}Λ^{12/7}$ for large $Λ$ and suggested that the upper bound, which comes from product states, gives the correct order. We prove that, for every fixed $α>0$, $E_0(α,Λ)=(1+o(1))\,c_α\,α^{2/7}Λ^{12/7}$, with an explicit constant $c_α=0.99338\ldots$, as $Λ\to\infty$. The same asymptotics hold uniformly in the joint limit $Λ/α\to\infty$, $α^{5/2}Λ\to\infty$, provided $\log(2+α)=o((Λ/α)^{1/21})$. The infimum of the energy over product states has the same leading asymptotics. The upper bound follows from a coherent state bound for the field energy in a fixed electron density. For the lower bound we combine a periodization of the field, a blockwise Born-Oppenheimer bound, and a lower bound on the magnetic Neumann Laplacian on a cube for band-limited fields. The magnetic estimate follows from a non-concentration bound for the vorticity of band-limited fields satisfying a weighted gradient condition.
papers.comments: 38 pages. First paper of a series on the Pauli-Fierz model in the ultraviolet limit. v2: main results unchanged; exposition revised and comparison with Bach-Hach expanded. Ancillary file: interval arithmetic script for the explicit constants

papers.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
papers.abstract: We study the effective mass of a spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field (the Pauli-Fierz model without external potential), with bare mass $m$, fine structure constant $α=e^2/4π$ and a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $Λ$. We define $1/(2m_{\rm eff}):=\limsup_{P\to0}(E(P)-E(0))/|P|^2$ for the fiber ground state energy $E(P)$; this agrees with the curvature mass whenever $E$ is twice differentiable at zero. By scaling, $h=m_{\rm eff}/m$ depends only on $α$ and $λ=Λ/m$. For all $α>0$ and $λ\ge1$ we prove $h\ge1+0.3441\,α/(1+0.2985\sqrtα+0.1252\,α)$, a bound independent of the cutoff; with the band extended to the cutoff, its first order coefficient in $α$ is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. At fixed $α>0$ we further prove $h\geλ^{8/7-ε}$ for every $ε>0$ and all sufficiently large $λ$. Hence $ι_{\rm PF}(α):=\inf_{λ>0}h/λ>0$: at fixed coupling, a bare mass reproducing a prescribed physical mass $m_{\rm phys}$ can exist only if $Λ\le m_{\rm phys}/ι_{\rm PF}(α)$. This proves the obstruction to mass renormalization at fixed physical mass anticipated by Lieb and Loss (2002). The first bound uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state. The second uses the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and a position estimator constructed from the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud.
papers.comments: 64 pages. Second paper of a series on the Pauli-Fierz model in the ultraviolet limit; Part II uses results of the companion paper arXiv:2610.34122. v2: gap in the proof of Lemma 8.2 repaired, exponent budget added, other corrections; main results unchanged. Ancillary file: interval arithmetic script for the constants of Part I

papers.title: Spectral localizer for unbounded topological Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: In a series of joint papers with Loring, it was shown how index parings of $K$-theory classes with Fredholm modules can be computed as the half-signature of a suitably constructed finite-dimensional matrix, called the spectral localizer. After offering a novel perspective on earlier results, it is shown how the framework can be extended to unbounded gapped Hamiltonians given as second-order linear differential operators (in particular, matrix-valued Schrödinger and regularized Dirac operators). Important insights are the coercive phase space localization and discretizations by means of wavelets.

papers.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
papers.abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincaré class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 8 figures. v2: proofs of Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.1(a) corrected (constants and cell scales); one volume formula in Section 5 restricted to its range of validity; numerical statements aligned with the recorded results

papers.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing \(R=|X_1|\), the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass exactly when \(\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty\); otherwise they converge to zero. Radial and Fourier--radial approximations have distinct sharp \(L^q\) convergence criteria at each \(0<q<1\); convergence at every such order holds for both families exactly when \(\mathbb{E}e^{sR}<\infty\) for every \(0<s<2\). In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors multiplied by \((\log n)^{1/4}\) and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. A uniformly bounded input family gives uncountably many coefficient-limit laws inequivalent under nonzero deterministic complex rescaling. We distinguish these laws using exact weighted tails under \(\mathbb{E}I_0(2R)<\infty\), where \(I_0\) is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments. For \(\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-λu^α\), \(0<α<1\) and \(λ>0\), the normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, while every positive limit moment diverges; we determine the logarithmic tails. Finite limiting moments need not imply convergence of the original coefficient moments. In the positive-limit class, coefficient periodograms recover the critical measure and energy normalization gives Gaussian limits. Hardy nonmembership holds under finite variance alone; the positive-limit class has sharp weighted Bergman criteria for \(0<p\le2\) and boundary Sobolev threshold \(s=-1/2\).

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: Forcing square with small conditions
papers.abstract: We show that if $κ^{<κ} = κ$, then there is a $κ$-strategically closed, $κ^+$-c.c. partial order that forces $\square_κ$. We discuss consequences for generic large cardinals.

papers.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
papers.abstract: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. The quadratic response at uniform equilibrium is studied in this work, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), the quadratic final-state map on a family of delayed controls that return the linearized state to zero is reduced to a scalar expression associated with a planar curve. A constant-level curve gives the return, and a tangential variation yields an explicit right inverse of the derivative of the quadratic final-state map. This inverse acts on all missing modes and maps mean-zero periodic $H^r$ targets to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only, while nonlinear controllability at this time remains open. Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.

papers.title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
papers.abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We introduce a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

papers.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $γ_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/γ_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We prove that the conjectured equality fails for all $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.

papers.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
papers.abstract: We study compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds endowed with an automorphism group acting with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, provided that the Bismut connection is not flat. In the first case, we explicitly describe all these structures up to homothety and biholomorphic isometry. We also construct explicit families of complete non-compact examples. The resulting non-Bismut-flat threefolds have non-constant scalar curvature and restricted Bismut holonomy $T^1\subset \mathrm{SU}(3)$, and include examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and complete examples on $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$. Finally, we construct a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Bismut-flat Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures whose complex structures are not compatible with any Bismut-flat metric.
papers.comments: v2: several improvements including full classification in the compact case when the group is covered by T^3 X SU(2) and proof that the restricted Bismut holonomy is one dimensional

papers.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2016. The proof combines a local pairing argument based on the lopsided Lovász local lemma with cycle decompositions of random graphs.

papers.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Structural Reductions, Transverse Products, and Fixed-Codimension Stability
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, product constructions, and fixed-codimension stability. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument yield an explicit bound \[ \mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}. \] For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two configuration splits off a common linear factor, so $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities. We further prove that for every fixed codimension $c$, the sequence $\mathcal{N}(k,k+c)$ is eventually constant. In codimension three, a sharper normal-span argument gives \[ \mathcal{N}(k,k+3)=\mathcal{N}(7,10)\qquad(k\geqslant7), \] where the numerical threshold uses the computer-assisted theorem $\mathcal{N}(1,3)=7$. The structural and stability results are otherwise independent of that numerical input.

papers.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=τ(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $ν_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p\nmid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. In particular, $n$ is matchable, meaning that $D(n)$ can be matched with the primitive progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$, if and only if $\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. The proofs combine a Vandermonde determinant with a partition into shorter progressions. If $E(x)$ counts the matchable non-$M$-numbers up to $x$, then, as $x\to\infty$, $$ E(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x} \sum_{r\ge1}\frac{(\log\log x)^{r-1}}{(r-1)!\,q_r^{q_r}}, $$ where $q_r$ is the least prime greater than $2^r$. This also gives a second term in the asymptotic formula for the count of all matchable integers up to $x$.

papers.title: Residual-based Adaptive Refinement of hp-Variational PINNs for elliptic PDEs with geometric singularities and localized features
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks approximate the solution of boundary value problems by minimizing the strong-form residual, their accuracy is often limited near corner and crack singularities, sharp layers and localized features and the enforcement of Neumann boundary conditions remains challenging. In hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks, the problem is formulated in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing the differentiation order applied to the neural network, while boundary constraints are imposed through penalty terms. The variational residual is evaluated using fixed Gauss quadrature points and the strong-form residual on a fixed collocation set, which may fail to capture regions of rapid variation. To address this issue, we integrate hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual-based Adaptive Refinement. During training, the strong-form residual is computed on a dense candidate pool and points with the largest residuals are added adaptively to the collocation set. Since the weak formulation is defined in $H^{1}(Ω)$, it avoids the $H^{2}(Ω)$ regularity requirement that fails on cracked and non-convex domains. The proposed method is validated on four two-dimensional elliptic problems and consistently achieves substantial reductions in relative $L^{2}$, absolute $L^{\infty}$ and relative $H^{1}$ semi-norm errors through adaptive residual-driven point placement.
papers.comments: This submission is withdrawn because it duplicates the authors' work "Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions" (arXiv:2610.26458). Please refer to that work instead

papers.title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
papers.abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.
papers.comments: 186 pages; to appear in Acta Numerica; v2: fixes to bibliography

papers.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
papers.abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector, in which one species is an obligate consumer as the definition allows, the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs, which reduces the question to a smaller, stable face. The failure is robust. It persists under small perturbations, including weak additional interactions, so every sign pattern that satisfies (C1) and (C2) and contains ours is a counterexample, and it occurs for an open cone of growth vectors. For $n\ge 6$ there are also counterexamples in which every species grows when alone. Finally, we announce that the conjecture holds for $n=4$ and that, for $n=5$, four minimal sign patterns characterise its failure.
papers.comments: 22 pages, 3 figures. Ancillary files: four verification scripts (Julia, standard library only)

papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and prove that every vector bundle of rank at least three admits smooth connected simply branched spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.
papers.comments: 86 pages; v2 adds a projective-geometric existence proof (Proposition 2.1) based on a suggestion by Anand Patel, and a general existence theorem for non-Higgs spectral structures (Proposition 4.4)

papers.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
papers.abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Companion to arXiv:2610.41555. Code and data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23730750. v2: adds Corollary 5.2 (Murnaghan-Nakayama inequalities), a remark on the dual e-positive picture and a remark that proofs for new shapes must leave class functions; credits Haiman 1993 for the inclusion C_KL in C_J; other numbering unchanged

papers.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge 2$. We characterize the nonzero additive maps on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction, assuming surjectivity only in infinite dimension. These maps are precisely those of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is unitary or antiunitary, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar for $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and a nonzero real scalar for $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$.
papers.comments: 16 pages. The surjectivity assumption has been removed in the finite-dimensional case

papers.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.
papers.comments: v2: added Example 2.23 (YB-solutions associated to a field); 17 pages

papers.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
papers.abstract: For every bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$T(Ω)\ge\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_Ω\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)^2\,\mathrm{d} x,$$ where $T(Ω)=4\int\limits_Ωu\,\mathrm{d} x$ and $-Δu=1$ in $Ω$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)$. Equality holds for balls.
papers.comments: 4 pages, minor revisions to the introduction and references

papers.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
papers.abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $(N-1)(k-1)+1$, and this bound $N$ for the second Dirichlet eigenvalue is sharp.

papers.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
papers.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

papers.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
papers.abstract: Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

papers.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
papers.abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) classifying pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal under the appropriate pullback. The proof uses a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. For left-invariant metrics on step 2 Carnot groups, this tuple is the growth of the osculating flags of the Jacobi curves of generic normal extremals, i.e., the lengths of the columns of their Young diagrams starting from the second column. The compatible graphs are used where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations extend by continuity, so our classification requires no local constancy of the tuple.
papers.comments: 82 pages, 1 table. Based on the PhD thesis of the first author, written under the supervision of the second author and defended at Texas A&M University in September 2026. v2: exposition of Subsection 1.4 and Section 4 improved (new Definition 4.1; Section 4 renumbered), matching edits in Sections 8 and 9, and a sentence on Jacobi curves added to the abstract

papers.title: Existence and stability of Weyl points
papers.abstract: Weyl points are quasimomentum-energy pairs in the band structure of three-dimensional periodic media at which two dispersion surfaces touch conically. They first arose in a model introduced by H. Weyl in 1929, but were first observed only recently in condensed matter physics and photonics experiments. Weyl points have been explored theoretically via numerical computation and via tight binding (discrete) models. In this article we present the first analytical treatment of Weyl points in a continuum PDE-type model. Starting with a Schrödinger operator whose electric potential is periodic with respect to the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, we introduce a small BCC-periodic magnetic vector potential that is equivariant with respect to a specific abelian group of symmetries. For magnetic Schrödinger operators of this type, we prove (i) that a pair of Weyl points bifurcates from a threefold degeneracy in the band structure of the underlying non-magnetic operator, and (ii) that these Weyl points are stable against small self-adjoint BCC-periodic perturbations of both the electric and magnetic vector potentials.

papers.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant Γ_{1,4} = 8
papers.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants Γ_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(μ)$ associated to a partition $μ=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for signatures \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups
papers.abstract: We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is at least a constant multiple of the logarithm of the order of the group and small compared with every positive power of it. This holds for both undirected and directed Cayley graphs, in discrete and continuous time, and the lower bound on the number of generators is best possible, up to the value of the constant. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
papers.comments: 22 pages; extended to directed Cayley graphs and discrete time

papers.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
papers.abstract: Haiman conjectured that for every partition $λ\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{λ,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings. Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_μ$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.
papers.comments: 25 pages. Companion to arXiv:2610.39021. Code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23730750; data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23532289. v2: credits Haiman 1993 for the inclusion C_KL in C_J and the values at w_0(mu); results and numbering unchanged

papers.title: A Finite-Range, Translation-Invariant Counterexample to Weak Gibbsianity
papers.abstract: We construct a finite-range, translation-invariant counterexample to the Weak Gibbsianity property for quantum spin systems on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The proof relies on showing how a local potential can induce macroscopically large deviations from an equilibrium configuration after a perturbation is introduced at the boundary of the lattice.

papers.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
papers.abstract: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $Γ$. Ordering the orbit $Γ\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\inΓ\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $φ$. Previously this was known either when $Γ=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $φ$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}λ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}χ(n)e^{2πi n^2 x}/n^s$.

papers.title: Abelianization and moment maps
papers.abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $μ$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $μ$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.

papers.title: Multipliers and weighted d-bar estimates
papers.abstract: We study some size estimates for the solution of the equation d-bar u=f in one variable. The new ingredient is the use of holomorphic functions with precise growth restrictions in the construction of explicit solutions to the equation.
papers.comments: This is a corrected version produced after formalizing in Lean the published version. There was a missing weight in the estimate of Theorem 3 and minor typos. The formalized version is in https://github.com/joaquimortega/MR1949832

papers.title: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole -approaching a sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström background fast enough at infinity- in presence of a massive and charged scalar field, motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in that setting : 1. Stability : We prove that spherically symmetric characteristic initial data to the Einstein-Maxwell- Klein-Gordon equations approaching a Reissner-Nordström background with a sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon in a neighbourhood of time-like infinity. Moreover if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. This generalizes the celebrated stability result of Dafermos for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. 2. Instability : We prove that for the class of space-times considered in the stability part, whose scalar field in addition obeys a polynomial averaged-L^2 (consistent) lower bound on the event horizon, the scalar field obeys an integrated lower bound transversally to the Cauchy horizon. As a consequence we prove that the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. This generalizes an instability result due to Luk and Oh for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. This instability of the black hole interior can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.
papers.comments: Correction of the instability argument, which requires an additional assumption on the event horizon. This additional assumption, like the previous ones, is conjectured to hold for generic exterior perturbations

papers.title: Mass inflation and the $C^2$-inextendibility of spherically symmetric charged scalar field dynamical black holes
papers.abstract: It has long been suggested that the Cauchy horizon of dynamical black holes is subject to a weak null singularity, under the mass inflation scenario. We study in spherical symmetry the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations and \textit{while we do not directly show mass inflation}, we obtain a "mass inflation/ridigity" dichotomy. More precisely, we prove assuming (sufficiently slow) decay of the charged scalar field on the event horizon, that the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}= \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$ for two (possibly empty) disjoint connected sets $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{S}$ such that: _$\mathcal{D}$ (the dynamical set) is a past set on which the Hawking mass blows up (mass inflation scenario). _$\mathcal{S}$ (the static set) is a future set isometric to a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon i.e.\ the radiation is zero on $\mathcal{S}$. As a consequence, we establish a novel classification of Cauchy horizons into three types: dynamical ($\mathcal{S}=\emptyset$), static ($\mathcal{D}=\emptyset$) or mixed, and prove that $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}$ is globally $C^2$-inextendible. Our main motivation is the $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture for a realistic model of spherical collapse in which charged matter emulates the repulsive role of angular momentum: in our case the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon system on one-ended space-times. As a result, we prove in spherical symmetry that: - two-ended asymptotically flat space-times are $C^2$-future-inextendible i.e. $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship is true for Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon, assuming the decay of the scalar field on the event horizon at the expected rate. - In the one-ended case, the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $C^2$-inextendible. This result suppresses the main obstruction to $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship in spherical collapse.
papers.comments: Strengthened the event-horizon assumptions to account for the correction to the instability argument in arXiv:1704.05790

papers.title: Beating the average: how to generate profit by exploiting the inefficiencies of soccer betting
papers.abstract: In economy, markets are denoted as efficient when it is impossible to systematically generate profits which outperform the average. In the past years, the concept has been tested in other domains such as the growing sports betting market. Surprisingly, despite its large size and its level of maturity, sports betting shows traits of inefficiency. The anomalies indicate the existence of strategies which shift betting from a game of chance towards a game of skill. This article shows an example for an inefficiency detected in the German soccer betting TOTO 13er Wette, which is operated by state-run lottery agencies. Gamblers have to guess the outcome (win, draw, loss) of 13 soccer matches listed on a lottery tip. Applying stochastic methods, a recipe is presented to determine hit rates for single match outcomes. More important, the recipe provides the number of lottery tips required to achieve a specific number of strikes (number of correct match forecasts per lottery tip) for any given level of safety. An approximation is derived to cope with large numbers in hypergeometric distributions, valid under certain constraints. Overall, the strategy does lead to returns exceeding the aggregated lottery fees, resulting in moderate, but consistent profits. It is briefly discussed if lessons learned from soccer betting can be transferred back to financial markets, because gamblers and retail investors face similar challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: A Tribute to S. Deser: Conserved Quantities in Generic Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: I describe parts of my joint work with S. Deser [March 19, 1931 - April 21, 2023] which started when I was working as a post-doc at Brandeis University in 2001. Our work was mostly, but not exclusively, on conserved charges of higher curvature theories of gravity. I also describe some recent developments, such as expressing the conserved charges in terms of the linearized Riemann tensor; I expound upon the computations. I also reminisce about our interaction for over two decades that went beyond our scientific collaboration. The physics part of this review is intended for graduate students and researchers interested in extended theories of gravity, especially about the conserved quantities and perturbative techniques in these theories.
papers.comments: 1 figure, 39 pages. The section containing the author's reminiscence of S. Deser was published in "The Supersymmetric World: The Beginnings of the Theory", 2nd ed., edited by G. Kane and M. Shifman (World Scientific, Singapore, 2025)

papers.title: Enumerating Complexity Revisited
papers.abstract: We study the relation between deterministic and randomized $\textit{enumerating}$ Kolmogorov complexity of sets $S\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Let $D(S)$ be the length of a shortest input on which a fixed optimal deterministic machine enumerates $S$, and let $ R(S) $ be the probability that a fixed optimal randomized machine enumerates $S$. It is easy to see that $-\log R(S) \le D(S)+O(\log D(S))$ for every $S$; the converse direction is much harder. Solovay proved $D(S)\le -3\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for all $S$, while for finite sets the sharper bound with the constant $2$ is known. We show that the case of infinite sets carries no extra cost: $\textit{any}$ inequality of the form $D(F)\le -α\log R(F)+O(\log\log\frac{1}{R(F)})$ with a computable $α$, valid for all finite $F$, automatically extends to all sets. More generally, we prove a single dichotomy from which such transfer results follow for an arbitrary computable non-decreasing bound, and which also shows that every c.e. set $S$ has a finite subset $F$ such that $F$ has at least as large deterministic complexity as $S$ but randomized one approximately the same or lower. Our result makes qualitative progress on a problem studied by Solovay in 1977 by showing that the search for the optimal constant can be reduced to a purely combinatorial question about a game played with finite sets. In particular, our result yields $D(S)\le-2\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for every $S$, improving Solovay's constant $3$ to $2$.

papers.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
papers.abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.
papers.comments: 46 pages, 5 figures, clarifications and corrections added

papers.title: Achieving Exponential Asymptotic Optimality in Average-Reward Restless Bandits without Global Attractor Assumption
papers.abstract: We consider the infinite-horizon average-reward restless bandit problem. We propose a novel two-set policy that maintains two dynamic subsets of arms: one subset of arms has a nearly optimal state distribution and takes actions according to an LP-Priority routine; the other subset of arms is driven towards the optimal state distribution and gradually merged into the first subset. We show that our two-set policy is asymptotically optimal with an $O(\exp(-C N))$ optimality gap for an $N$-armed problem, under the assumptions of aperiodic-unichain, non-degeneracy, and local stability. Our policy is the first to achieve exponential asymptotic optimality under the above set of easy-to-verify assumptions, whereas prior work either requires a global attractor assumption or only achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. We further discuss obstacles in weakening the assumptions by demonstrating examples where exponential asymptotic optimality is not achievable when any of the three assumptions is violated. Notably, we prove a lower bound for a large class of locally unstable restless bandits, showing that local stability is particularly fundamental for exponential asymptotic optimality. Finally, we use simulations to demonstrate that the two-set policy outperforms previous policies on certain restless bandit problems and performs competitively overall.
papers.comments: 63 pages, 4 figures. Reorganized the proof of Theorem 1 for clarity, with additional corrections and improvements to other arguments

papers.title: Effective eigenvalue approximation from moments for self-adjoint trace-class operators
papers.abstract: Spectral properties of bounded linear operators play a crucial role in several areas of mathematics and physics. For each self-adjoint, trace-class operator $O$ we define a set $Λ_n\subset \mathbb{R}$, and we show that it converges to the spectrum of $O$ in the Hausdorff metric under mild conditions. Our set $Λ_n$ only depends on the first $n$ moments of $O$. We show that it can be effectively calculated for physically relevant operators, and it approximates the spectrum well without diagonalization. We prove that using the above method we can converge to the minimal and maximal eigenvalues with super-exponential speed. We also construct monotone increasing lower bounds $q_n$ for the minimal eigenvalue (or decreasing upper bounds for the maximal eigenvalue). This sequence only depends on the moments of $O$ and a concrete upper estimate of its $1$-norm; we also demonstrate that $q_n$ can be effectively calculated for a large class of physically relevant operators. This rigorous lower bound $q_n$ tends to the minimal eigenvalue with super-exponential speed provided that $O$ is not positive semidefinite. As a by-product, we obtain computable upper bounds for the $1$-norm of $O$, too. Numerical examples demonstrate the relevance of our approximation in estimating entropy and negativity, which is useful, among others, in quantum optical and in open quantum system models. The results can be directly applicable to problems in quantum information, statistical mechanics, and quantum thermodynamics, where using traditional techniques based on diagonalization is impractical.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Added two appendices, and made minor revisions. Accepted for publication in PTEP

papers.title: An Efficient Frequency-Based Approach for Maximal Square Detection in Binary Matrices
papers.abstract: We present FreqBased, a frequency-based algorithm for the maximal square problem in binary matrices. The algorithm maintains a vertical run-length array and a horizontal counter to validate candidate squares, matching the standard single-array dynamic programming algorithm in O(mn) time and O(n) space while reducing the amount of work performed during execution. Experiments on synthetic random binary matrices reveal a clear density-dependent performance transition: FreqBased consistently outperforms the dynamic programming baseline on moderate- and high-density inputs across Intel and AMD processors, achieving peak speedups of 1.175x and 1.277x, respectively, while executing up to 2.08x fewer instructions. On 180 real aerial image masks from the INRIA dataset, FreqBased outperforms the baseline on every instance with speedups of up to 4.63x, confirming that the instruction-count advantage observed on synthetic inputs extends to real binary matrices with spatial structure. Hardware performance counter analysis shows that the performance advantage arises primarily from reduced instruction count despite lower execution efficiency, demonstrating that algorithms with identical asymptotic complexity can exhibit substantially different practical performance depending on input characteristics.

papers.title: A Generalized Tangent Approximation based Variational Inference Framework for Strongly Super-Gaussian Likelihoods
papers.abstract: Variational inference, as an alternative to Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, has played a transformative role in enabling scalable computation for complex Bayesian models. Nevertheless, existing approaches often depend on either rigid model-specific formulations or stochastic black-box optimization routines. Tangent approximation is a principled class of structured variational methods that exploit the geometry of the underlying probability model. However, its utility has largely been confined to logistic regression and related modeling regimes. In this article, we propose a novel variational framework based on tangent transformation for a broad class of probability models characterized by strongly super-Gaussian likelihoods. Our method leverages convex duality to construct tangent minorants of the log-likelihood, thereby inducing conjugacy with Gaussian priors over model parameters in an otherwise intractable setup. Under mild assumptions on the data-generating mechanism, we establish algorithmic convergence guarantees, a contribution that stands in contrast to the limited theoretical assurances typically available for black-box variational methods. Additionally, we derive near-parametric variational risk bounds. Superior performance of our proposed methodology is illustrated on simulated and real-data scenarios that challenge state-of-the-art variational algorithms in terms of scalability and their ability to consistently capture complex underlying data structure.
papers.comments: 145 pages (35-page main paper + 110-page supplementary material), 51 figures, 14 tables. Accepted in the Journal of the American Statistical Association (Theory & Methods)

papers.title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization with Flexible Sample Queries
papers.abstract: Group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) aims to learn models that perform well across $m$ distributions simultaneously. Existing methods either (i) query $m$ samples per round, which imposes strict implementation requirements, or (ii) query only a single sample per round, which requires many rounds to converge and therefore leads to long runtime. To avoid these limitations, we introduce a novel setting called \emph{flexible sample queries} (FSQ), which allows the number of samples that can be queried to vary across rounds. Under the FSQ setting, we cast GDRO as a two-player game: one performs non-oblivious online convex optimization, while the other tackles a non-oblivious prediction with limited advice (PLA) problem. In this game, the first player updates its decision using follow-the-regularized-leader with stochastic gradients. For the second player, we develop a new PLA method equipped with an adaptive exploration strategy that can leverage an arbitrary per-round sample size. We then establish the \emph{first} high-probability regret bound for non-oblivious PLA. By integrating these components, we develop an anytime GDRO algorithm that supports FSQ, and derive a high-probability optimization error bound of $O\left(\frac{1}{t}\sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^t \frac{m}{r_j}\log m}\right)$, where $r_j$ is the sample size at round $j$. This result demonstrates that the optimization error decreases as the per-round sample sizes increase, and implies the same near-optimal sample complexity of $O(m\log (m)/ε^2)$ for any fixed sample size $r\in[m]$.

papers.title: DRO: A Python Library for Distributionally Robust Optimization in Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce dro, an open-source Python library for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for regression and classification problems. The library implements 15 DRO formulations and 9 backbone models, enabling 85 distinct DRO methods. Furthermore, dro is compatible with both scikit-learn and PyTorch through a unified interface, and uses approximation techniques to reduce runtime for some computationally demanding formulations. Comprehensive documentation is available at https://python-dro.org.

papers.title: Competing Bandits in Matching Markets via Super Stability
papers.abstract: We study bandit learning in matching markets with two-sided reward uncertainty, extending prior research primarily focused on single-sided uncertainty. Building on Irving's (1994) concept of super-stability and the partial-order proposal algorithm of Cseh and Juhos (2021), we use a simultaneous Extended Gale-Shapley procedure to certify stable matchings from incomplete preference information. By employing this procedure, our centralized algorithm attains logarithmic pessimal stable regret dependent on an instance-dependent admissible gap parameter. This algorithm is further adapted to a decentralized setting with a time-independent additive $O(N^3K)$ regret increase under the stated shared-flag communication model. Finally, we establish a centralized instance-dependent lower bound for binary stable regret on strict interior Bernoulli instances, elucidating the roles of admissible partial ranks and super-stable matching in characterizing the complexity of stable matching with bandit feedback.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares for Robust Subspace Recovery
papers.abstract: Robust subspace estimation is fundamental to many machine learning and data analysis tasks. Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS) is an elegant and empirically effective approach to this problem, yet its theoretical properties remain poorly understood. This paper establishes that, under deterministic conditions, a variant of IRLS with dynamic smoothing regularization converges linearly to the underlying subspace from any initialization. We extend these guarantees to affine subspace estimation, a setting that lacks prior recovery theory. Additionally, we illustrate the practical benefits of IRLS through an application to low-dimensional neural network training. Our results provide the first global convergence guarantees for IRLS in robust subspace recovery and, more broadly, for nonconvex IRLS on a Riemannian manifold.

papers.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
papers.abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
papers.comments: 36 pages, 14 figures, Revised version addressing referee comments, with clarifications to the discussion, improved notation, and corrections of minor errors and typos

papers.title: Domain size asymptotics for Markov logic networks
papers.abstract: A Markov logic network (MLN) $\mathbb{M}$ determines a probability distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ on the set $\mathbf{W}_n$ of structures, or ``possible worlds'', with domain $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. We study the properties of such distributions as $n$ tends to infinity. We show that with mild assumptions on an MLN $\mathbb{M}$ with one soft constraint with an arbitrary positive weight the distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ will behave quite differently from the uniform distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^{uni}$ on $\mathbf{W}_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For a language with only one relation symbol $R$ which has arity 1 we give an almost complete characterization of the possible asymptotic behaviours of $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathbb{M}$ may be any MLN for this language. The asymptotic behaviour depends on the soft constraints and weights of the MLN. This characterization is used to show that if the language under consideration contains at least one relation symbol of arity 1 then the following holds: (a) There is an MLN $\mathbb{M}$ such that for every lifted Bayesian network (LBN) $\mathbb{G}$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\mathbb{M}$ and $\mathbb{G}$ determine different distributions on $\mathbf{W}_n$. (b) There is an LBN $\mathbb{G}$ such that for every MLN $\mathbb{M}$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\mathbb{G}$ and $\mathbb{M}$ determine different distributions on $\mathbf{W}_n$. We also show that, in the limit, the weight dimension and the domain size dimension may behave completely differently.

papers.title: Free mutual information and higher-point OTOCs
papers.abstract: We introduce a quantity called the free mutual information (FMI), adapted from concepts in free probability theory, as a new physical measure of quantum chaos. This quantity captures the spreading of a time-evolved operator in the space of all possible operators on the Hilbert space, which is doubly exponential in the number of degrees of freedom. It thus provides a finer notion of operator spreading than the well-understood phenomenon of operator growth in physical space. We derive two central results which apply in any physical system: first, an explicit "Coulomb gas" formula for the FMI of two observables $A(t)$ and $B$ in terms of the eigenvalues of the product operator $A(t)B$; and second, a general relation expressing the FMI as a weighted sum of all higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). This second result provides a precise information-theoretic interpretation for the higher-point OTOCs as collectively quantifying operator ergodicity and the approach to freeness. This physical interpretation is particularly useful in light of recent progress in experimentally measuring higher-point OTOCs. We identify universal behaviours of the FMI and higher-point OTOCs across a variety of chaotic systems, including random unitary circuits and chaotic spin chains, which indicate that spreading in the doubly exponential operator space is a generic feature of quantum many-body chaos. At the same time, the non-generic behavior of the FMI in various non-chaotic systems, including certain unitary designs, shows that there are cases where an operator spreads in physical space but remains localized in operator space. The FMI is thus a sharper diagnostic of chaos than the standard 4-point OTOC.
papers.comments: 92 pages, 24 figures. Comments are welcome!;v2: published version, minor revisions

papers.title: Der Stern von Bethlehem -- Einige Theorien und Hintergruende: Von der altorientalischen Astrologie ueber Kepler zu Newton
papers.abstract: Many have have taken in hand to write a treatise on the Star of Bethlehem, particularly on Kepler's explanation as a stellar birth, triggered by Mars joining a great conjunction (a meeting of Jupiter and Saturn), as he observed it in October 1604. It is the aim of my short treatise to introduce, at a hopefully well digestible level, into underlying antiquity's concepts of physics, astrology, and astronomy around the time of Christ's birth and to demonstrate their essential developments up to the early modern period. In the latter, Kepler played a significant role. His contributions enabled him to calculate back to the year 7 BC with astonishing precision, locating a triple great conjunction in Pisces, which was then complemented by Mars. This is confirmed by both Babylonian tradition and modern astronomy. The following background provided may be specifically helpful for a more theologically oriented audience, also because the controversy surrounding "geocentric" and "heliocentric" world systems (Copernicus) is touched upon. And, because the overall context raises questions for theology, with which the epilogue concludes.

papers.title: Morita Rigidity for Kleene Algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce Morita equivalence to the study of Kleene algebras and modules. Classical characterizations of Morita-equivalent semirings such as having equivalent categories of modules and one semiring being a full idempotent corner of a finite matrix semiring over the other transfer easily to this new context. We also observe that Morita equivalence can be applied to extending and restricting scalars in Lindenbaum--Tarski algebras of propositional dynamic logics, and that an appropriately-defined category of generalized finite automata satisfies the property that when the underlying Kleene algebras are Morita equivalent then the corresponding categories of generalized automata are equivalent. But the signature results which we obtain relate to rigidity of Kleene algebras in this context. Specifically, every semiring that is Morita-equivalent to the semiring reduct of a Kleene algebra has a unique expansion to a Kleene algebra, and semiring bimodules witnessing Morita-equivalence of semirings which are reducts of Kleene algebras are already Kleene bimodules.
papers.comments: 29 pages; corrects issues found by LLM

papers.title: Distributed Adaptive Estimation with ISS Guarantees for Sensor Networks with Partially Unknown Source Dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper studies distributed adaptive estimation over sensor networks with partially unknown source dynamics. We present parallel continuous-time and discrete-time designs in which each node runs a local adaptive observer and exchanges information over a directed graph. For both time scales, we establish stability of the network coupling operators, prove boundedness of all internal signals, and show convergence of each node's estimate to the source despite model uncertainty and disturbances. We further derive input-to-state stability (ISS) bounds that quantify robustness to bounded process noise. A key distinction is that the discrete-time design uses constant adaptive gains and per-step regressor normalization to handle sampling effects, whereas the continuous-time design does not. A unified Lyapunov framework links local observer dynamics with graph topology. Simulations on star, cyclic, and path networks corroborate the analysis, demonstrating accurate tracking, robustness, and scalability with the number of sensing nodes.
papers.comments: This version is accepted for publication in the 2026 IFAC World Conference

papers.title: Robust Cauchy-Based Methods for Predictive Regressions
papers.abstract: This paper develops robust inference methods for predictive regressions that address key challenges posed by endogenously persistent or heavy-tailed regressors, as well as persistent volatility in errors. Building on the Cauchy estimation framework, we propose two novel tests: one based on $t$-statistic group inference and the other employing a hybrid approach that combines Cauchy and OLS estimation. These methods effectively mitigate size distortions that commonly arise in standard inference procedures under endogeneity, near nonstationarity, heavy tails, and persistent volatility. The proposed tests are simple to implement and applicable to both continuous- and discrete-time models. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate favorable finite-sample performance across a range of realistic settings. An empirical application examines the predictability of excess stock returns using the dividend-price and earnings-price ratios as predictors. The results suggest that the dividend-price ratio possesses predictive power, whereas the earnings-price ratio does not significantly forecast returns.

papers.title: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
papers.abstract: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply $p$-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.

papers.title: $k$-path graphs: experiments and conjectures about algebraic connectivity and $α$-index
papers.abstract: This work presents conjectures about eigenvalues of matrices associated with $k$-path graphs, the algebraic connectivity, defined as the second smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix, and the $α$-index, as the largest eigenvalue of the $A_α$-matrix. For this purpose, a process based on [Discrete Applied Mathematics 164 (2014) 297-303] is presented to generate lists of $k$-path graphs containing all non-isomorphic 2-paths, 3-paths, and 4-paths of order $n$, for $6 \leq n \leq 26, 8 \leq n \leq 19$, and $10 \leq n \leq 18$, respectively. Using these lists, exhaustive searches for extremal graphs of fixed order for the mentioned eigenvalues were performed. Based on the empirical results, conjectures are suggested about the structure of extremal $k$-path graphs for these eigenvalues.

papers.title: Structural and Spectral Properties of Strictly Interval Graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with a subclass of chordal graphs, which are simultaneously strictly chordal and interval, the strictly interval graphs. We present a new characterization of the class that leads to a simple linear recognition algorithm. Next we introduce a new subclass of strictly interval graphs, the $SI$-core graphs, that are non-split and non-cograph graphs and show that several elements of the new class are Laplacian integral

papers.title: Measures and Models of Non-Monotonic Dependence
papers.abstract: A margin-free measure of bivariate association generalizing Spearman's rho to the case of non-monotonic dependence is defined in terms of two square integrable functions on the unit interval. Properties of generalized Spearman correlation are investigated when the functions are piecewise continuous and strictly monotonic, with particular focus on the special cases where the functions are drawn from orthonormal bases defined by Legendre polynomials and cosine functions. For continuous random variables, generalized Spearman correlation is treated as a copula-based measure and shown to depend on a pair of uniform-distribution-preserving (udp) transformations determined by the underlying functions. Bounds for generalized Spearman correlation are derived and a novel technique referred to as stochastic inversion of udp transformations is used to construct singular copulas that attain the bounds and parametric copulas with densities that interpolate between the bounds and model different degrees of non-monotonic dependence. Sample analogues of generalized Spearman correlation are proposed and their asymptotic properties are investigated. Potential applications of the theory are demonstrated including: exploratory analyses of the dependence structures of datasets and their symmetries; elicitation of functions maximizing generalized Spearman correlation via expansions in orthonormal basis functions; and construction of tractable probability densities to model a wide variety of non-monotonic dependencies.
