papers.title: Behavioral patterns and mean-field games in epidemiological models
papers.abstract: We introduce a new type of Mean Field Game epidemiological models, in which subpopulations have different behavioral patterns: some people exhibit a type of ``rational'' self interested behavior by choosing Nash-equilibrium long-term strategies while others follow pre-specified ``non-rational'' patterns (e.g., either sticking to their usual habits or trying to mimic those around them). Our new B-MFG models allow for occasional behavioral switches, which rational individuals also take into account when formulating their Nash-equilibrium strategies. Although this modeling approach is general, here we develop it for individuals choosing their ``contact rates'' within a particular Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Susceptible-Dead (SIRSD) epidemic model. The latter is based on a frequency-based force of infection with proportionate mixing and the mortality rate that rapidly increases once the proportion of infected individuals exceeds some prescribed threshold, resulting in a strain on medical resources. Numerical tests illustrate the properties of our model and highlight the ways in which additional/non-rational behavioral patterns and behavioral switching increase the impact of infectious diseases. The paper aims to build a bridge between two distinct communities of epidemiological modelers and to promote the consideration of behavioral patterns in broader Mean Field Games literature.

papers.title: Decoupled Kemeny quasi-likelihoods for rank-based generalised linear models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a unified profile quasi-likelihood framework for generalised linear models built on a topologically complete extension to Kendall's $τ$ with finite sample power and Type-I error rates. By establishing equivalence between continuous $L^2$ profile estimators and discrete Generalized Gibbs exponential families, we prove local asymptotic minimax efficiency over the copula tangent space. The framework yields monotone-affine invariant inference, sub-Gaussian concentration bounds, and exact finite-sample $t$-pivot tail majorization under arbitrary tie configurations. We illustrate the methodology through three canonical applications: bivariate rank correlation, paired testing, and intraclass correlation.

papers.title: Inference-Time Alignment for Diffusion Models via Variationally Stable Doob's Matching
papers.abstract: Inference-time alignment for diffusion models aims to adapt a pre-trained reference diffusion model toward a target distribution without retraining the reference score network, thereby preserving the generative capacity of the reference model while enforcing desired properties at inference time. A central mechanism for achieving such alignment is guidance, which modifies the sampling dynamics through an additional drift term. In this work, we introduce variationally stable Doob's matching, a novel framework for provable guidance estimation grounded in Doob's $h$-transform. Our approach formulates guidance as the gradient of the logarithm of an underlying Doob's $h$-function and employs gradient-regularized regression to simultaneously estimate both the $h$-function and its gradient, resulting in a consistent estimator of the guidance. Theoretically, we establish non-asymptotic convergence rates for the estimated guidance. Moreover, we analyze the resulting controllable diffusion processes and prove non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for the generated distributions in the Wasserstein-2 distance. Finally, we show that variationally stable guidance estimators are adaptive to unknown low dimensionality, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality under low-dimensional linear subspace assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method and show the advantages compared to the baselines.

papers.title: Finite-sample Valid Permutation Inference under Multi-way Clustering
papers.abstract: Econometric applications with multi-way clustering often feature a small number of effective clusters or heavy-tailed data, making standard cluster-robust and bootstrap inference unreliable in finite samples. In this paper, we develop a framework for finite-sample valid permutation inference in linear regression with multi-way clustering under an assumption of conditional exchangeability of the errors. Our assumption is closely related to the notion of separate exchangeability studied in earlier work, but can be more realistic in many economic settings as it imposes minimal restrictions on the covariate distribution. We construct permutation tests of significance that are valid in finite samples and establish theoretical power guarantees, in contrast to existing methods that are justified only asymptotically. While our main presentation is under exchangeable errors, our framework encompasses invariance-based tests that remain valid under general forms of heteroskedastic errors. We also extend our methodology to settings with missing data and derive power results that reveal phase transitions in detectability. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate that the proposed tests maintain correct size and competitive power, while standard cluster-robust and bootstrap procedures can exhibit substantial size distortions.

papers.title: Starfield: Demand-Aware Satellite Topology Design for Low-Earth Orbit Mega Constellations
papers.abstract: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations are emerging as high-capacity backbones for next-generation Internet. Deployment of laser terminals enables high-bandwidth, low-latency inter-satellite links (ISLs); however, their limited number, slow acquisition, and instability make forming a stable satellite topology difficult. Existing patterns like +Grid and Motif ignore regional traffic, ground station placement, and constellation geometry. Given sparse population distribution on Earth and the isolation of rural areas, traffic patterns are inherently non-uniform, providing an opportunity to orient inter-satellite links (ISLs) according to these traffic patterns. In this paper, we propose Starfield, a novel demand-aware satellite topology design heuristic algorithm supported by mathematical analysis. We first formulate a vector field on the constellation's shell according to traffic flows and define a corresponding Riemannian metric on the spherical manifold of the shell. The metric, combined with the spatial geometry, is used to assign a distance to each potential ISL, which we then aggregate over all demand flows to generate a score for each satellite's link selection. Inspired by +Grid, each satellite selects the link with the minimum Riemannian distance along with its corresponding angular links. To evaluate Starfield, we developed a custom, link-aware, and link-configurable packet-level simulator, comparing it against LAMP, +Grid, Motif, and Random topologies. For the Phase 1 Starlink, simulation results show up to a 30% reduction in hop count and a 15% improvement in stretch factor across multiple traffic distributions. Moreover, static Starfield, an inter-orbital link matching modification of Starfield, achieves a 15% improvement in stretch factor under realistic traffic patterns compared to +Grid. Experiments demonstrate Starfield's robustness under traffic demand perturbations.

papers.title: Madelung hydrodynamics of spin-orbit coupling: action principles, currents, and correlations
papers.abstract: We exploit the variational and Hamiltonian structures of quantum hydrodynamics with spin to unfold the correlation and torque mechanisms accompanying spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in electronic motion. Using Hamilton's action principle for the Pauli equation, we isolate SOC-induced quantum forces that act on the orbital Madelung--Bohm trajectories and complement the usual force terms known to appear in quantum hydrodynamics with spin. While the latter spin-hydrodynamic forces relate to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), SOC-induced orbital forces originate from a particular current operator that contributes prominently to the spin current. This distinction between force terms reveals two fundamentally different mechanisms generating quantum spin-orbit correlations. Leveraging the Hamiltonian structure of the hydrodynamic system, we also elucidate spin transport features such as the correlation-induced quantum torques and the current shift in the spin Hall effect. This Hall shift leads to a new definition of the transport spin current thereby addressing an open question in spintronics. Finally, we illustrate the framework via the Madelung--Rashba equations for planar SOC configurations and propose a particle closure for possible numerical implementations.
papers.comments: Slightly expanded version. 28 pages. Comments welcome

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
papers.abstract: In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling. We show that, using a carefully designed \blue{end-point adapted} time-discretization scheme and with sufficiently accurate drift estimates, the RF sampler enjoys an iteration complexity of order $O(k/\varepsilon)$ (up to log factors), where $\varepsilon$ is the precision in total variation distance and $k$ is the intrinsic dimension of the target distribution. In addition, we show that the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) procedure is equivalent to a stochastic version of RF by establishing a novel connection between these processes and stochastic localization. Building on this connection, we further design a stochastic RF sampler that also adapts to the low-dimensionality of the target distribution under mild requirements on the accuracy of the drift estimates, and also with a specific time schedule. We illustrate the efficacy of newly designed time-discretization schedules with simulations on the synthetic data and text-to-image (T2I) data experiments.

papers.title: Spectral Codes: A Geometric Formalism for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: We present a new geometric perspective on quantum error correction based on spectral triples in noncommutative geometry. In this approach, quantum error correcting codes are reformulated as low energy spectral projections of Dirac type operators that separate global logical degrees of freedom from local, correctable errors. Locality, code distance, and the Knill Laflamme condition acquire a unified spectral and geometric interpretation in terms of the induced metric and spectrum of the Dirac operator. Within this framework, a wide range of known error correcting codes including classical linear codes, stabilizer codes, GKP type codes, and topological codes are recovered from a single construction. This demonstrates that classical and quantum codes can be organized within a common geometric language. A central advantage of the spectral triple perspective is that the performance of error correction can be directly related to spectral properties. We show that leakage out of the code space is controlled by the spectral gap of the Dirac operator, and that code preserving internal perturbations can systematically increase this gap without altering the encoded logical subspace. This yields a geometric mechanism for enhancing error correction thresholds, which we illustrate explicitly for a stabilizer code. We further interpret Berezin Toeplitz quantization as a mixed spectral code and briefly discuss implications for holographic quantum error correction. Overall, our results suggest that quantum error correction can be viewed as a universal low energy phenomenon governed by spectral geometry.

papers.title: Entanglement in quantum spin chains is strictly finite at any temperature
papers.abstract: Entanglement is the hallmark of quantum physics, yet its characterization in interacting many-body systems at thermal equilibrium remains one of the most important challenges in quantum statistical physics. We prove that the Gibbs state of any quantum spin chain can be exactly decomposed into a mixture of matrix product states with a bond dimension that is independent of the system size, at any nonzero temperature. As a consequence, the Schmidt number, arguably the most stringent measure of bipartite entanglement, is strictly finite for thermal states, even in the thermodynamic limit. Our decomposition is explicit and is accompanied by an efficient classical algorithm to sample the resulting matrix product states.

papers.title: Zero Variance Portfolio
papers.abstract: When the number of assets is larger than the sample size, the minimum variance portfolio interpolates the training data, delivering pathological zero in-sample variance. We show that if the weights of the zero variance portfolio are learned by a novel ``Ridgelet'' estimator, in a new test data this portfolio enjoys out-of-sample generalizability. It exhibits the double descent phenomenon and can achieve optimal risk in the overparametrized regime when the number of assets dominates the sample size. In contrast, a ``Ridgeless'' estimator which invokes the pseudoinverse fails in-sample interpolation and diverges away from out-of-sample optimality. Extensive simulations and empirical studies demonstrate that the Ridgelet method performs competitively in high-dimensional portfolio optimization.

papers.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.

papers.title: Monoidal categories graded by partial commutative monoids
papers.abstract: Effectful categories have two classes of morphisms: pure morphisms, which form a monoidal category; and effectful morphisms, which can only be combined monoidally with central morphisms (such as the pure ones), forming a premonoidal category. This suggests seeing morphisms of an effectful category as carrying a grade that combines under the monoidal product in a partially defined manner. We axiomatize this idea with the notion of monoidal category graded by a partial commutative monoid (PCM). Monoidal categories arise as the special case of grading by the singleton PCM, and effectful categories arise from grading by a two-element PCM. Further examples include grading by powerset PCMs, modelling non-interfering parallelism for programs accessing shared resources, and grading by intervals, modelling bounded resource usage. We show that effectful categories form a coreflective subcategory of PCM-graded monoidal categories; introduce cartesian structure, recovering Freyd categories; and describe PCM-graded monoidal categories as monoids by viewing a PCM as a thin promonoidal category.

papers.title: Stone Duality for Monads
papers.abstract: We introduce a contravariant idempotent adjunction between (i) the category of ranked monads on $\mathsf{Set}$; and (ii) the category of internal categories and internal retrofunctors in the category of locales. The left adjoint takes a monad $T$-viewed as a notion of computation, following Moggi-to its localic behaviour category $\mathsf{LB}T$. This behaviour category is understood as "the universal transition system" for interacting with $T$: its "objects" are states and the "morphisms" are transitions. On the other hand, the right adjoint takes a localic category $\mathsf{LC}$-similarly understood as a transition system-to the monad $Γ\mathsf{LC}$ where $(Γ\mathsf{LC})A$ is the set of $A$-indexed families of local sections to the source map which jointly partition the locale of objects. The fixed points of this adjunction consist of (i) hyperaffine-unary monads, i.e., those monads where term $t$ admits a read-only operation $\bar{t}$ predicting the output of $t$; and (ii) ample localic categories, i.e., whose source maps are local homeomorphisms and whose locale of objects are strongly zero-dimensional. The hyperaffine-unary monads arise in earlier works by Johnstone and Garner as a syntactic characterization of those monads with Cartesian closed Eilenberg-Moore categories. This equivalence is the Stone duality for monads; so-called because it further restricts to the classical Stone duality by viewing a Boolean algebra $B$ as a monad of $B$-partitions and the corresponding Stone space as a localic category with only identity morphisms.
papers.comments: 19 pages without appendix, 35 pages total, to appear in final proceedings of MFPS2026

papers.title: On the Reliability Limits of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Planning
papers.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent planning delegates operational decisions to specialists that communicate through finite reports. In this research, we study its reliability limits when a coordinator can revisit source records before completing a resource-constrained plan. A useful report can support an immediate decision or direct later reading, so its value depends on how these stages communicate. We derive exact communication and access tradeoffs and prove that two report forms suffice for a broad class of allocation requirements, one favoring immediate resource identification and the other distinguishing absence from unnamed availability. For shared capacity, this reduction permits joint optimization of reporting roles and adaptive reads for a fixed number of source types with unequal workloads and reading costs. Identical specialists can optimally report different facts, and maximizing immediate completion can impose an unbounded recovery cost penalty even with full-record access. We also conduct numerical experiments to quantify the benefits of the proposed joint optimization and show how source access improves language-agent decisions that already use their reports optimally. In particular, an exhaustive evaluation of 207,632 report designs on small allocation instances recovers the predicted joint optima. Our analysis suggests that reliable agent communication should be evaluated by the complete decisions it supports and the cost of finishing its unresolved cases, instead of solely by report length, local prediction accuracy, or immediate task completion, as is often the case in current practice.
papers.comments: 36 pages, including appendices; 2 figures. Substantially revised

papers.title: Empirical Ciphertext Distinguishability Testing of KEMs and Hybrid Encryption via Deep Learning
papers.abstract: We model indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack (IND-CPA) games as binary classification tasks for deep neural networks (DNNs). We apply this methodology to the public-key encryption (PKE) schemes used to construct PQC key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) such as ML-KEM and HQC, and to cascaded symmetric algorithms, demonstrating methodological generality. Moreover, we present a novel extension of this approach to empirical distinguishability testing of hybrid KEMs. For IND-CPA-secure schemes and their combinations, no DNN achieves accuracy significantly different from random guessing (measured via Bonferroni-corrected binomial tests), consistent with theoretical security guarantees. For insecure schemes, such as plain RSA, AES-CTR and AES-CBC with IV or counter reuse, or RC4, the DNNs classify the ciphertexts better than random guessing. Thus, this framework is shown to serve as a practical, scheme-agnostic tool for flagging distinguishable ciphertexts in both individual and composed constructions.

papers.title: A Linear Temporal Logic of Frequencies on Series of Events
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LTLFS, a linear temporal logic for reasoning about frequencies in finite series of probabilistic events. The logic conservatively extends linear temporal logic over finite traces with measure-sensitive operators that compare the empirical distribution observed at any point in a series with an independently specified target distribution. Its semantics integrates the actual sequence of events, the probability distribution governing individual outcomes, and the set of finite assignments compatible with the target frequency. This supports two complementary tasks: verifying whether an observed partial distribution is compatible with the benchmark, and predicting whether and with what probability the completed series can still satisfy it. The language can express observed and attainable frequencies, the probability of realizing a desired final distribution, and conditional probabilities for subsequent outcomes under the assumption that the benchmark is met. We establish formal properties of the operators and characterize their interaction with the temporal structure. A running example concerning representational fairness in sequential outputs from a generative AI system illustrates how the framework can distinguish temporary deviations from irrecoverable violations and support early, logically interpretable intervention. LTLFS thereby provides a symbolic foundation for runtime monitoring of evolving quantitative requirements, with applications to explainable and responsible AI.

papers.title: Wave number dynamics in the real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the large-scale dynamics of the one-dimensional real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations using a scalar equation for the local wave number derived by a Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) expansion. For the real equation, the reduction has a conserved gradient structure. With higher-order regularization, we obtain families of exact stationary solutions and show that all nonuniform steady states are linearly unstable. These include localized holes distinct from the classical Langer-Ambegaokar hole. In the Eckhaus-unstable regime, the reduced equation develops finite-time singularities associated with phase slips. We derive a universal self-similar description of this process, with parameter-independent scaling exponents in good agreement with direct numerical simulations. The similarity profile satisfies a nonlinear fourth-order boundary-value problem admitting multiple numerically identified solutions. For the complex equation with nearly real coefficients, an additional Burgers-type nonlinearity produces wave steepening and traveling shocks connecting plane waves of different wave numbers. We derive the shock profile exactly and show numerically that the full complex Ginzburg-Landau equation converges to this prediction in the appropriate asymptotic limit. Outside this regime, the wave number profile becomes nonmonotonic, as explained in terms of spatial dynamics. These shocks differ qualitatively from classical Nozaki-Bekki solutions. The reduced equation thus unifies stationary holes, self-similar collapse toward phase slips, and propagating shocks within a common description of pattern-forming systems.

papers.title: A Thin Sheet Volume Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: A thin-sheet (TS) volume integral equation (VIE) formulation incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is represented as an equivalent thin sheet, with its constitutive tensors derived from the GSTC susceptibility tensors. Invoking the thin-sheet approximation, the governing VIEs are reduced to surface integral equations (SIEs), in which tangential and normal flux density components are treated as distinct sets of unknowns and discretized using Rao-Wilton-Glisson and pulse basis functions, respectively. In contrast to conventional GSTC approaches based on conventional SIEs, which represent only tangential fields, the proposed framework rigorously enforces the bianisotropic GSTCs, including normal field interactions, while retaining the flux-based VIE character of the formulation. Numerical examples, including a comparison with an SIE-GSTC solver that neglects the normal susceptibility components, demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed TS-VIE-GSTC solver for polarization rotation on planar and curved sheets, perfect reflection, beam steering with spatially varying susceptibilities, multi-directional attenuation, and oblique phase-shift transformation.

papers.title: Identification to Subclasses of Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: An identification of two vertices \(u\) and \(v\) in a graph replaces them with a new vertex that is made adjacent to every vertex of \(N(u)\cup N(v)\setminus \{u,v\}\). We study the \(\mathcal{H}\)-Identification problem, which is to decide whether a given graph \(G\) can be transformed (``identified'') to a graph in \(\mathcal{H}\) by applying at most \(k\) vertex identifications. We determine the classical and parameterized complexity of this problem for various subclasses \(\mathcal{H}\) of chordal graphs, obtaining an almost complete picture for two parameters: \(k\) and \(n-k\). We also consider the Identification problem, which is to test, for two given graphs \(G\) and \(H\), whether \(G\) can be identified to \(H\). We determine the parameterized complexity of this problem when \(H\) is a graph from one of our testbed classes, taking the number of simplicial vertices of \(H\) as the parameter.
papers.comments: A preliminary version of this paper appeared in the proceedings of IPEC 2026. Minor mistakes and inconsistencies have been corrected in this version

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Markov Risk Measures and Multipattern Risk Approximation
papers.abstract: For a risk-averse finite-horizon Markov Decision Process, we introduce a special class of Markov coherent risk measures, called mini-batch measures. We also define the class of multipattern risk-averse problems that reduce to linear MDPs in the risk-neutral case. We use both concepts in a feature-based $Q$-learning method with multipattern $Q$-factor approximation and we prove a high-probability regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(d^{3/2}HN^{H-1}\sqrt{K}\big)$, where $d$ is the number of features, $H$ is the horizon, $N\ge2$ is the mini-batch size, $K$ is the number of episodes, and $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}$ hides logarithmic factors. We also propose an economical version of the $Q$-learning method that streamlines the policy evaluation (backward) step. The theoretical results are illustrated on a stochastic assignment problem and a short-horizon multi-armed bandit problem.

papers.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Picard-Type Operator Learning in Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs
papers.abstract: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) aims to learn solution operators on infinite-dimensional function spaces from finite-resolution data. In this setting, it is important for the learned model to be discretization-invariant, or resolution-robust, and to reflect PDE-specific structure. It is therefore natural to ask how such structure should be encoded in the model architecture, hypothesis class, or learning procedure. In this paper, we study operator learning for solution operators of nonlinear parabolic PDEs based on Duhamel--Picard iteration. We formulate Picard iteration as an abstract state-transition model and present a theoretical framework for Picard-type operator learning. We derive implementation-agnostic generalization error bounds that separate the implementation error from the estimation error associated with the abstract state-transition model induced by Picard iteration. A key consequence is that increasing the Picard depth reduces the Picard truncation error without causing an unbounded growth of the entropy-based estimation error. We also extend the analysis to long-time prediction by rolling out the same learned local model over successive time blocks. Finally, we illustrate the theory for nonlinear heat equations on the torus using a Picard-type Fourier neural operator as a concrete implementation.

papers.title: Kernel-Gradient Drifting Models
papers.abstract: We propose kernel-gradient drifting, a one-step generative modeling framework that replaces the fixed Euclidean displacement direction in drifting models with directions induced by the kernel itself. Standard drifting is attractive because it enables fast, high-quality generation without distilling a large pretrained diffusion model, but its theory is currently understood mainly for Gaussian kernels, where the drift coincides with smoothed score matching and is identifiable. Our gradient-based reformulation exposes this score-based structure for general kernels: the resulting drift is the score difference between kernel-smoothed data and model distributions, yielding identifiability for characteristic kernels and a smoothed-KL descent interpretation of the smoothed drifting dynamics. Since kernel gradients are intrinsic tangent vectors, the same construction extends naturally to Riemannian manifolds and to discrete data via the Fisher-Rao geometry of the probability simplex. Across spherical geospatial data, promoter DNA and molecule generation, kernel-gradient drifting enables state-of-the-art one-step generation beyond the Euclidean setting without distillation. Code is available \href{https://github.com/jcarrascopollo/kgd_thesis}{here}.

papers.title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps
papers.abstract: We develop a quantitative statistical theory of transformers in the large-context regime by adopting the abstraction of contextual flow maps (CFMs): dynamical systems that evolve a distinguished token in the presence of a contextual measure across a stack of attention blocks. Within this framework, the finite-context model approximates an idealized infinite-context system in which the contextual measure is replaced by its underlying population, so that the context length $n$ becomes a statistical resource. Exploiting the McKean--Vlasov structure of the dynamics and the classical machinery of propagation of chaos, we establish a forward bound controlling the deviation between the finite- and infinite-context CFMs uniformly along depth, and a backward bound controlling the deviation between the corresponding training trajectories uniformly across iterations of online gradient descent. Both bounds achieve the optimal Wasserstein rate $n^{-1/d}$ for general CFMs and parametric rate $n^{-1/2}$ for a restricted class of CFMs that includes transformers as a special case. The analysis rests on a new Eulerian adjoint formulation of the loss gradient and stability estimates for the resulting forward--adjoint system, both of which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Multicategorical Semantics for Untyped Effects
papers.abstract: Completeness proofs in categorical semantics usually proceed by building a syntactic category whose composition is given by substitution. For untyped effectful Call-by-Value languages, this runs into a basic obstacle: there is no canonical notion of simultaneous substitution of computations, since evaluation order is semantically meaningful. We address this by taking single computation substitutions, that is, binding steps, as primitive, and representing computation substitution by finite sequential lists composed by concatenation. We formalize this idea in a one-object Freyd-multicategorical setting. We introduce Freyd operads, separating a cartesian operad of values from a symmetric Ren-cartesian preoperad of computations, connected by a Freyd functor, and from any Freyd operad we construct a corresponding Freyd PROP of substitutions. We prove that this construction is representable and, in the strict one-object setting, left adjoint to restriction to codomain 1. Using the induced term model, we interpret untyped computational lambda-calculus with procedures and higher-order functions in weakly closed Freyd operads, and prove soundness, initiality, and completeness. This yields a categorical semantics tailored to untyped effectful computation and broad enough to encompass realizability-oriented models such as monadic combinatory algebras.

papers.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
papers.abstract: We study local coordination on finite graphs, equivalently, the ability of randomized local protocols with independent private randomness to produce highly correlated outputs at neighboring vertices. Hutchcroft, Rospuskova, and Tamuz (2026) showed that if such local coordination can be achieved with low cost, then the graph admits a low-cost leader profile, or equivalently an appropriate bounded-radius decomposition, with a square-root loss in the cost. We substantially improve this bound for unbiased binary outputs. If the average disagreement is $\varepsilon$, we construct a leader profile of cost $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The key ingredient is an information-theoretic influence measure: after fixing an ordering of the independent information sources, we assign to each binary output the increments of mutual information revealed along that ordering. For two outputs that disagree with probability $p$, the corresponding measures are within binary entropy $h(p)$ in total variation. Combined with a grand coupling theorem, this yields the improved bound. We also show that a universal linear bound is impossible. We construct graphs with binary local profiles of cost $O(\varepsilon)$ for which every leader profile has cost $$ Ω\!\left(\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right). $$ The construction uses weighted majority functions and can be implemented as an action-symmetric Nash equilibrium, giving a negative answer to the question of HRT whether leader equilibria are always optimal up to a constant factor. Finally, we show that the binary assumption is essential: for general real-valued outputs, the square-root dependence of the HRT theorem is sharp up to a universal constant.

papers.title: Semi-analytical representation of the Gaunt-modified Landau-Lifshitz equation in a plane wave
papers.abstract: We analyze electron dynamics in a plane electromagnetic wave using the Landau-Lifshitz equation with a quantum radiation reaction correction modelled by a Gaunt factor. In this geometry, the quantum parameter $χ$ depends solely on the lightfront momentum, allowing the modified equation of motion to retain the integrable structure of the classical problem. We derive a semi-analytical solution for the energy evolution and the four-velocity, which reduces to the known classical result in the appropriate limit. The results provide an analytical and deterministic description of semiclassical radiation reaction in plane-wave fields.

papers.title: On spherically symmetric Berwald vacuum solutions in Finsler gravity
papers.abstract: Berwald-Finsler spacetimes are Finsler spacetimes that are closest to pseudo-Riemannian geometry, as their canonical nonlinear connection defines an affine connection on spacetime. In this paper, we find the first exact, non-Ricci flat, $SO(3)$-symmetric Berwald solutions to the Finsler gravity vacuum equation. To this aim, we first select from all spherically symmetric Berwald spacetimes, the only class that admits flat Finsler spacetime structures, making it particularly suitable for future investigations of asymptotic flatness. Then, for this class, we completely solve the Finsler gravity vacuum equation, and find three families of solutions. In particular, we show that in Finsler geometry there exist $SO(3)$-symmetric, vacuum solutions that are not Ricci-flat. These solutions are promising candidates to model the gravitational field around compact objects, beyond their Riemannian description.
papers.comments: This version corrects a misprint in equation (114) of the previous one

papers.title: Temporal Conductance and Bounds on the Voter Model for Dynamic Networks
papers.abstract: The voter model is a classical stochastic process that models how opinions might spread through a network: at each step, every node lazily adopts the opinion of a random neighbour; eventually all nodes share the same opinion (consensus). Stronger connectivity should yield faster consensus. Berenbrink, Giakkoupis, Kermarrec, and Mallmann-Trenn (ICALP 2016) make this precise via the network's conductance: if the network has $m$ edges, minimum degree $d_{\min}$, and conductance at least $φ$, then the voter model reaches consensus in expected $O(m/(d_{\min}φ))$ steps. Their results extend to dynamic networks with fixed vertex degrees by considering the network's conductance at each time step. We introduce temporal conductance $Φ$, a more general connectivity measure for dynamic networks. Unlike static conductance, which collapses to $0$ whenever some snapshot is disconnected, $Φ$ captures connectivity through edges that appear at different times. We generalise the results of Berenbrink et al. from static conductance to temporal conductance, showing that the expected consensus time of the standard voter model is at most $O(m/(d_{\min}Φ))$. Moreover, we prove that this bound is tight up to constant factors. We expect temporal conductance to be a useful primitive for analysing other dynamics on temporal networks, and potentially time-inhomogeneous Markov chains more generally.

papers.title: Functional Principal Component Analysis for Manifold-Indexed Data
papers.abstract: Functional principal component analysis has traditionally focused on processes indexed by Euclidean domains, although functional observations increasingly arise on curved domains. We develop functional principal component analysis for real-valued processes observed at discrete locations on a general Riemannian manifold. We estimate the mean and covariance functions using intrinsic kernel smoothing based on geodesic distance and a normal-coordinate volume correction, with a general weighting scheme accommodating unequal numbers of observations across subjects. We establish $L^2$ and uniform convergence rates for these estimators and derive corresponding error bounds for the estimated eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. These results quantify how manifold dimension, sampling frequency and the weighting scheme affect estimation accuracy and characterize the phase transition between sparse and dense sampling regimes. Simulation studies on the circle and sphere, together with real-data applications, illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed methodology.

papers.title: A Single Physical Principle Determines Quantum Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Why does quantum relative entropy occupy such a privileged role among measures of distinguishability? We show that a single operational principle determines it. If one pair of states can be distinguished at least as successfully as another for every prior, when both are assisted by the same auxiliary pair, acting as a catalyst, a distinguishability measure should assign it no smaller value. Remarkably, for a normalized measure, this requirement singles out Umegaki relative entropy under mild classical continuity and expansibility on uniform distributions: adding impossible outcomes leaves their associated entropy unchanged. Qubit catalysts already suffice. No additivity or quantum continuity is assumed. We also prove that, without auxiliary assistance, respecting binary discrimination dominance uniquely determines the quantum extension of every regular classical divergence, including the Hirche--Tomamichel extensions of classical $f$-divergences. For additive classical divergences, these extensions respect classical catalysis; allowing noncommuting qubit catalysts is what singles out Umegaki relative entropy.
papers.comments: Major revision with a substantially stronger uniqueness theorem: catalytic Lorenz monotonicity characterizes Umegaki relative entropy without assuming additivity; full-rank qubit catalysts suffice. Includes a new proof and results distinguishing classical from quantum catalysis

papers.title: Compatibility of Martensitic Microstructures in Polycrystals
papers.abstract: The paper studies martensitic microstructures in polycrystals, focussing on their compatibility across grain boundaries. After a reduction to the case of a planar grain boundary, the case when the grain boundary separates two constant gradients of zero energy is considered. It is shown that for cubic-to tetragonal transformations such a configuration can occur when the relative grain rotation is not in the cubic group. Then the case when the grain boundary separates two simple laminates of zero energy is considered, it being shown using a computer-assisted symbolic calculation that in the cubic-to-tetragonal case compatibility is only possible for a closed set of measure zero in the manifold of grain boundary normals and relative grain rotations, and that a similar slightly weaker result holds for cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations. The results suggest why higher-order laminates are often observed for such transformations. The Taylor set of deformation gradients is defined and studied, this set having the property that any deformation whose gradient belongs to it corresponds to a zero-energy microstructure for the polycrystal independent of grain geometry and grain rotations. New upper bounds for the Taylor set are proved for cubic-to-tetragonal and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations, generalizing those of Bhattacharya and Kohn using the geometrically linearized theory. We give a simple proof of a related result of Peigney characterizing the positive diagonal matrices in the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells for cubic-to-tetragonal transformations.
papers.comments: 29 pages. Revised. To appear in Journal of Elasticity

papers.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
papers.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3213 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.4813e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic numbers. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 1 figure. v2: the witness of v1 was found not to survive exact arithmetic and is replaced by a certified one; adds the width and the lower edge of the ribbon, a second configuration with a wide window, and the semialgebraic structure. Code, data and certificates: https://github.com/avnerkantor/one-shot-twenty-one-balls (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23816267)

papers.title: Quantum error-correcting codes from aperiodic monotiles: the Hat and the Spectre
papers.abstract: Li and Boyle showed that the Penrose tiling defines a quantum error-correcting code: superpositions of tilings over isometry orbits protect quantum information against erasure of any bounded region. We extend the construction to the aperiodic monotiles discovered by Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss. For the Hat, we prove strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings, and we prove local recoverability unconditionally for all nonsingular Hat tilings via the torus parametrization of the underlying cut-and-project scheme. The remaining singular case reduces to one sharply posed geometric question -- can a region that is a union of hats be retiled a second way? -- which we verify computationally has no counterexample up to a substantial scale: a certified $2490$-tile patch admits precisely one tiling by hats, so all $2^{2490}$ of its tile-subregions retile uniquely. Unlike the Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and Fibonacci tilings, both monotiles form two local-indistinguishability classes, so their code spaces split into two erasure-correcting sectors carrying a superselected classical label. Whether the label survives depends on which isometries are gauged: the Spectre's classes are exchanged by a $30^{\circ}$ rotation and merge once all proper isometries are gauged, whereas the Hat's are exchanged only by reflections. Under the physically natural gauge group $SE(2)$, the Hat code therefore stores one robust classical bit -- the handedness of its long-range order, readable in any bounded window with separation $Δ= |K|\sqrt{5}/3$ -- alongside its protected quantum sectors. It is the reflexible monotile, not the chiral one, that carries the chirality bit. We give the exact Perron-Frobenius data of both codes, including the per-class reflected-Hat frequencies $(3\mp\sqrt{5})/6$ and the Spectre orientation-class frequencies $(5\pm\sqrt{15})/10$.

papers.title: Random unitary circuits with constant spectral gap
papers.abstract: We prove constant lower bounds for the spectral gap of the following random walks on unitary groups $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ on $n$ qubits. (i) Random Pauli Rotation: choose an $n$-qubit Pauli operator $P$ and an angle $θ\in [0,2π)$, both uniformly at random, and apply $e^{\mathrm i θP}$. (ii) Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit: choose $n-1$ unitaries $U_{i}$ uniformly at random from $\mathsf{SU}(4)$ (including central phases of the parent group) independently, and apply $U_{2j-1}$ on two qubits $2j-1, 2j$ and then $U_{2j}$ on two qubits $2j, 2j+1$. Importantly, the gap bounds are independent of $n$ and apply for all finite dimensional unitary representations of $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ uniformly. Our results immediately imply that the Random Pauli Rotation and Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit converge to approximate unitary $t$-designs after $\mathcal{O}(nt)$ steps. As a consequence, we improve implications for the complexity growth of random unitary circuits as a function of the depth. The existing argument can be applied almost verbatim, but previously the depth had to be $\mathcal{O}(2^{cn})$ for some $c < 1$. Our unconditional constant spectral gap removes this restriction. We prove analogous constant-gap results for orthogonal and Clifford groups; the latter is indispensable for our result on the Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit. The former implies convergence to approximate orthogonal $t$-designs. In this case, the implied mixing time with respect to a constant additive and multiplicative error is optimal (up to an absolute constant factor) for $t=2$.
papers.comments: 34 pages. 1 figure. Julia and Mathematica code (v3) added proof ideas and clarified local groups to include central phases

papers.title: Kernel Ridge Regression over Hölder Classes: Function and Derivative Losses
papers.abstract: We study ordinary kernel ridge regression over full Hölder-Zygmund balls, measuring errors in Sobolev norms and in pointwise and uniform losses for mixed derivatives. For targets of smoothness $s$, every RKHS norm equivalent to $H^{s+d/2}$ gives the optimal $H^r$ risk for $0\le r<s$; integer choices of $r$ include integrated squared derivative losses. Pointwise and uniform guarantees require additional kernel structure. A localized wavelet kernel attains the sharp derivative rates with the same regularization orders as for function estimation, whereas equivalent changes of the RKHS norm can destroy the population bias rates. For the ordinary Gaussian kernel with a shrinking bandwidth, we prove a uniform derivative risk bound with the optimal polynomial rate and an explicit, unoptimized logarithmic factor. The results allow bounded measurable design densities bounded away from zero and conditionally sub-Gaussian noise.

papers.title: Derivative Computation in PINNs: Automatic Differentiation, Finite Differences and Beyond
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate finite-difference (FD) derivative computation in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) as an alternative to automatic differentiation (AD). On three benchmark PDEs we show that, with a properly calibrated step size, FD matches AD in accuracy on every problem while running faster across the full tested batch-size range and using substantially less GPU memory, and that a stochastic variant we propose outperforms AD on a stationary problem. We further show that for neural architectures with inter-sample dependencies (e.g. BatchNorm, self-attention) the standard PyTorch autograd idiom is silently incorrect; the correct per-sample alternative is computationally infeasible at PINN-relevant batch sizes, while FD provides a forward-only approximation that is empirically an order of magnitude closer to the true per-sample derivative.
papers.comments: v2: journal version under review; 22 pages, 12 figures

papers.title: Is the Quantum-Entangled Universe a Small World?
papers.abstract: Partial entanglement may provide enough connections in the universe to satisfy the definition of a small world. To investigate this possibility, we define a network of particles on a given space-like hyper-surface with a long-range link between any two particles that are connected by a chain of exchanged particles involving a limited number of interactions. Considering the mean free paths of particles in different regions of space and the resulting probability distributions of entanglement connections vs. distance, we find evidence of small-world or random network structure on all but the smallest scales - corresponding to stars and planets - on which other types of connections would need to be added to complete the small world picture.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 3 figures, error in Eq. (3) corrected, with consequent changes to Eqs. (5), (6), and Fig. 2, but no effect on conclusions

papers.title: A Probability Model for Pentagonal Prism Dice Rolls
papers.abstract: In the realm of probability theory and game design, the study of dice probabilities plays a crucial role. The featured dice are usually fair, so their probabilities can be predicted without rolling the dice. Pentagonal prismatic dice are not fair. Hence, the probabilities are more complicated. Our mathematical model is naturally derived from both the geometric properties of the dice and empirical evidence. Dice of varying sizes but with constant volume were designed. Using a 3D printer with 100 percent infill, the dice were printed and prepared. A machine that simulates dropping dice through a dice tower onto a hard surface was used to obtain about 41,000 results. From these data, a statistical model was constructed that gives probabilities of dice with varying height-to-radius ratios. The formula for the model is based on the centroid solid angle, but with two adjustment parameters due to varying energy and other requirements to transition between different resting aspects. Within the range of height-to-radius ratios tested, the data are within reasonable statistical error of the model.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 7 figures. Revised methods and statistical reporting; original 41,068 outcomes retained. Parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit calibration and ancillary data/code added

papers.title: Minimax Rate for Diffusion-Guided Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation based on Fokker-Planck Equation
papers.abstract: Diffusion-guided methods have recently emerged as effective tools for probing the intrinsic geometry of high-dimensional data. Understanding their accuracy requires quantifying both (i) finite-scale approximation error relative to the true local intrinsic dimension (LID) and (ii) estimation error from finite samples. We address these two questions for the FLIPD field (Kamkari et al., 2024; arXiv:2406.03537), defined at the population level through the logarithmic scale derivative of a Gaussian-smoothed density and admitting a Fokker--Planck representation. For $α$-smooth densities on a regular $d$-dimensional manifold, we establish a uniform $O(σ^2)$ approximation bound relative to the manifold dimension $d$. Under expected integrated squared loss, we prove a minimax lower bound of order $(nσ^d)^{-1}$ for estimating the FLIPD field from $n$ observations when $n^{-1/(2α+d)}\leσ\leσ_0$. A plug-in FLIPD estimator based on the empirical denoising score matching (DSM) solution attains a matching upper bound. Thus the minimax rate is of order $(nσ^d)^{-1}$ and it becomes $n^{-2α/(2α+d)}$ at its smallest scale.

papers.title: Spatial Mixing and Deterministic Approximate Counting of Multi-spin Systems beyond Bounded Degree Graphs
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for deterministic approximate counting of multi-spin systems beyond bounded-degree graphs. The algorithm recursively constructs rational polytopes containing the true marginal vectors and uses linear-fractional programming to obtain certified bounds on marginal ratios. For positive interactions on graphs of polynomial connective constant $D$, we establish strong spatial mixing whenever $Dc<1$, where $c$ bounds the Birkhoff contraction coefficients of the interactions. Under the same condition, we also give a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (\textbf{FPTAS}) for the partition function. We further extend the framework to proper colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs using recursion on permissive blocks. For every fixed $η\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large fixed $d$, and fixed integer $q\ge(2+η)d$, we obtain an \textbf{FPTAS} for counting proper $q$-colorings of $G\sim\mathcal G(n,d/n)$ with high probability over $G$. This improves the leading constant $3$ in the earlier counting guarantee of Yin and Zhang (APPROX/RANDOM, 2016) to $2$, and asymptotically matches the spatial mixing regime established by Yin (ICALP, 2014).

papers.title: Low-Rank Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
papers.abstract: A shortest-path decision is often made from edge costs that are only observed through noisy samples, such as the average of $m$ simulation replications. When the mean cost vectors of different instances lie near a $k$-dimensional subspace, projecting the averaged sample onto that subspace should remove noise. We make this precise. The mean squared error of any projection estimator splits exactly into a variance term and a bias term. The best projector is the positive eigenspace of $Σ_c - D/m$, where $Σ_c$ is the covariance of the true costs and $D$ is the noise covariance. For a rank-$k$ signal, the projection has the error of a sample mean with a factor $d/(μk)$ more replications, where $d$ is the number of edges and $μ$ is an incoherence constant. For a signal that is only approximately low-rank, every rank-$k$ projection has an error floor, and the plain average wins beyond an explicit replication count. A margin bound shows that the chance of choosing a suboptimal path falls at the same improved rate. A projector learned from $n$ noisy instances loses at most an $O(d/n)$ term.

papers.title: Characteristic Mapping Method for Vlasov-Poisson with BGK-collisions
papers.abstract: This work presents the first steps for simulating kinetic plasmas with collisions using the characteristic mapping method (CMM). The CMM is a semi-Lagrangian method that uses the group structure of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms to efficiently represent the flow-maps of transport problems. Individual submaps can be composed to follow the flow backward in time to its initial foot point, numerically establishing the back-to-label symmetry. The novelty of the presented work is the handling of the source term by storing the Duhamel integrals of each time sub-interval, allowing efficient temporal-integration. Furthermore, we use the Lagrangian structure to avoid implicit time-stepping in the hydrodynamic regime, which is known to be stiff. We benchmark our method on the Boltzmann-BGK and Vlasov-Poisson-BGK equations and consider different test cases, the Sod shock tube problem and nonlinear Landau damping for different Knudsen numbers. We show third-order spatial and temporal convergence and illustrate the fine-scale zoom property of CMM for the bump-on-tail instability.

papers.title: A Quaternary Legendre Pair of Length 64
papers.abstract: A quaternary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ is a pair of sequences over $\{\pm 1, \pm \mathrm{i}\}$ whose periodic autocorrelations sum to $-2$ at every nonzero shift. We give a quaternary Legendre pair of length $64$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported construction at this length.

papers.title: Topological Geometry of Neutrino Mass and Mixing
papers.abstract: This work presents an analytical, parameter-free derivation of the lepton mixing matrix and active neutrino mass spectrum from an icosahedral $A_5$ flavor manifold coupled to the three-generation Iwahori-Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$. Partitioning the icosahedral vertex curvature across the six fundamental Weyl chambers of $H_3(q)$ fixes an elementary angular defect $Δ_{AD} = π/18$, unifying ultra-high-energy mass generation and low-energy flavor mixing as dual realizations of a single geometric invariant. At the topological braiding threshold $μ\sim M_0$, the right-handed Majorana scale $M_0$ breaks scale invariance and drives the five-dimensional Temperley-Lieb quotient into its hyperbolic regime with loop modulus $d'_{AD} = 2\coshΔ_{AD}$, where Quantum Yang-Baxter Baxterization projects the algebraic roots onto a hierarchical heavy spectrum $M_1 > M_2 > M_3 > 0$. Integrating out and inverting these states via a flavor-isotropic Seesaw mechanism Type-I locks in the normal mass hierarchy with $m_1 \approx 3.64$ meV, $\sum_i m_i \approx 63.5$ meV, and $m_β\approx 9.45$ meV. Simultaneously, probability conservation requires analytic continuation onto the compact unitary circle, factorizing the mixing matrix into the $A_5$ Golden Ratio baseline, a unitary boundary twist generated by the longest Coxeter involution, and a discrete Majorana parity matrix. This geometry yields $θ_{13} = 8.49^\circ$, $θ_{12} = 32.11^\circ$, $θ_{23} = 45^\circ$, and maximal Dirac CP violation, $δ_{CP} = \pm π/2$, while discrete $SO(3)$ parities quantize the relative Majorana phases, $α_{13} = -π, α_{23} = 0$, preventing $0νββ$ decay cancellation, $m_{ββ} \approx 1.14$ meV, and suppressing renormalization group drift to $\dotθ_{ij} \sim 10^{-7}$ rad.
papers.comments: 29 pages (main text) plus four Appendices. Improves the underlying algebra, updates the main results accordingly, and corrects typos from the previous version

papers.title: Nonparametric In-Context Learning under Growing Geometric Complexity: Minimax Optimality and Local Geometry-Adaptivity of Transformers
papers.abstract: Transformers have become a central architecture for in-context learning (ICL), particularly through their state-of-the-art performance in large language models. This success motivates understanding how transformers exploit intrinsic geometry of real-world data. However, existing nonparametric ICL theory has largely focused on simplified settings, such as Euclidean domains or single manifold models, failing to fully explain its phenomenal empirical success in complex tasks. To address this gap, we study the prediction problem under unknown heterogeneous geometry, modeled by sample size-dependent mixtures of manifolds with heterogeneous dimensions, smoothness, and sampling masses. Under the growing geometric complexity model, we establish a minimax lower bound capturing the aggregate difficulty of the components and construct an oracle tangent local polynomial estimator with a matching upper bound. This estimator is connected to a structure-informed, two-stage softmax transformer with a geometric preconditioner and local polynomial solvers. The transformer achieves negligible approximation error relative to the minimax rate with logarithmic depth and polynomial size. Finally, we derive an in-context generalization bound for near empirical risk minimizers (ERM) over this class. Together, these results identify conditions under which the resulting predictor exploits local geometry and attains minimax rate.

papers.title: Algebraic-Geometric Parvaresh--Vardy Subspace Designs and Rank Condensers
papers.abstract: A subspace design is a collection of subspaces $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ of $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ with the property that no low-dimensional subspace $W$ intersects the collection "too much". Subspace designs and related objects in linear-algebraic pseudorandomness have found a broad range of applications, ranging from list decoding to derandomizing algorithms. We construct explicit strong subspace designs over every finite field. In the extremal case where the co-dimension $t$ of each $H_i$ is equal to the dimension of $W$, for every constant field size our construction attains $n=Ω(k)$ and matches the probabilistic intersection bound up to a constant factor. All previous constructions required the field size to grow with $t$ (or $k$). Our subspace designs also imply new constructions of rank condensers over arbitrary finite fields. This result is the first to achieve an optimal dependence on $k$ while maintaining both a constant output entropy rate and a constant field size. As an application, we construct lossless rank extractors for linear sources of rank $r$, for all $r < q$, with parameters matching those of Guo, Raj, Shangguan and Zhang (FOCS '26), thereby generalizing their result to prime fields and smaller field sizes. Our construction is based on an algebraic-geometric version of the Parvaresh--Vardy codes (Parvaresh--Vardy FOCS '05, Guruswami ECCC '05), extending the framework underlying the condensers of Guruswami, Umans and Vadhan (JACM '09). We view our construction as a linear-algebraic analysis -- tailored to affine sources -- of the GUV construction, generalized to functions over algebraic curves. More specifically, inspired by Ta-Shma and Umans (CCC '12) we develop a two-level evaluation scheme, where we first evaluate a function on a curve at extension-field points, and then evaluate a corresponding affine-linear polynomial to obtain outputs over the base field.

papers.title: Short-Length Code Designs for Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Deep Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables joint communication and sensing using a shared waveform, but its signal design is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between the two objectives, particularly in the short blocklength regime. This paper proposes an autoencoder (AE)-based framework for ISAC waveform design in noncoherent settings. We derive a modified Cramér-Rao bound for multi-target delay estimation and analyze the maximum-likelihood decoding rule for noncoherent communication under correlated fading. These results reveal structural connections and trade-offs between communication and sensing objectives in waveform design. Based on this analysis, the AE learns waveform representations that jointly optimize both functionalities, with a tunable parameter controlling the trade-off. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms conventional schemes in both communication reliability and sensing accuracy, especially under short blocklength and fading conditions.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 5 figures, preprint of a journal paper. Removed a part of a sentence that should have been deleted, but remained in the manuscript by mistake

papers.title: Proofs Without Nominals: Gödel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
papers.abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzmüller and Scott's Notes on Gödel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, or, more cheaply and for all results at once, by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language, 294 of them explicit. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what it flags are terms a prover introduced. A soundness theorem over general models closed under the object language, and a sentence of that language the embedding proves but which fails in such a model, fix what the certificate says. The Notes' three open questions are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. Generalised to Gödel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of Gödel's footnote, and settles them again without nominals. In effect only the empty conjunction is excluded; the singleton comes back with the other axioms. In one variant the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to Gödel's essence. Every theorem here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4, the separating model in its propositional part; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.
papers.comments: 51 pages. New in v5: the witness criterion and the whole-term condition come apart (a proof with the nominal in a context alone); three open questions answered by Bjoern Lindheim's harness, cited; both detectors read schema positions off the rule, the Isabelle/HOL one every rule, with a whole-term mode; 114 facts of the Notes replayed in Isar. Ancillary: sources, sessions, detectors, reports

papers.title: Concurrent Strategies as Street Fibrations
papers.abstract: Concurrent games and strategies based on event structures are an established and expressive model of interactive computation. In this paper we revisit the problem of equipping this model with symmetry. Symmetry is essential for many applications, but it is also a source of mathematical complexity, not least because strategies with symmetry can be compared up to several distinct notions of equivalence. Our first contribution is a complete characterization of two classes of strategies for which composition admits an identity. For these two classes the identity laws hold, respectively, up to a "weak" and a "strong" notion of equivalence. The main result is that the weak class of strategies corresponds precisely to those inducing Street fibrations over the game. We also show how the established "thin" approach to symmetry also fits in this general framework. A second contribution is a formal connection between games and setoid-valued profunctors. This follows a long tradition of relating games and relational models, but here additionally includes a very general model of symmetries. Our characterization of strategies as Street fibrations makes the connection to profunctors significantly easier to establish.

papers.title: Sublinear Markov Semigroups Beyond Uniqueness
papers.abstract: To what extent does a local operator on smooth test functions determine a sub-Markov semigroup and its underlying structure of laws? Many existing approaches work with Feller semigroups on the space \(C_b\) of bounded continuous functions and rely on uniqueness, often established through a comparison principle for the associated evolution equation. However, even when the local operator is linear, uniqueness may fail and a \(C_b\)-Feller restriction may exclude the associated canonical semigroup. We discover that the space \(\operatorname{USC}_b\) of bounded upper semicontinuous functions offers a natural setting for this study. Within this framework, a complete description of the relationships among sublinear local operators, sublinear sub-Markov semigroups, and their underlying structures of laws is achieved without assuming uniqueness. Under suitable regularity and Lyapunov conditions, we construct the greatest semigroup compatible with a prescribed sublinear local operator and obtain a stochastic representation in terms of a Markov process under sublinear expectations. We characterize all sublinear sub-Markov semigroups dominated by this greatest semigroup in two ways: through a one-to-one correspondence with stable subfamilies of its representing laws, and through an order relation between their infinitesimal generators and the prescribed local operator. We further characterize the greatest semigroup via the greatest viscosity subsolution of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation. These results clarify what information about global stochastic evolution can be recovered from local infinitesimal descriptions and what freedom remains in the absence of uniqueness. The resulting characterizations are new even when the local operator is linear.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling inspired by the analysis of Kac's walk, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(π_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

papers.title: Residual correction for accelerating dual-time-stepping lattice Boltzmann methods
papers.abstract: For lattice Boltzmann simulations of unsteady flows at low Reynolds numbers, dual-time stepping decouples the physical time step from lattice streaming, yet conserved-moment iteration errors decay slowly at large steps. We develop a residual correction method based on the conserved-moment structure of the collision operator. With fixed step histories and both relaxation rates equal to unity, post-collision populations depend on incoming populations only through reconstructed conserved moments, so one collision eliminates local perturbations with zero conserved moments. Periodic rest-state linearization shows that, at large physical steps, the contraction factor of the uniform conserved mode approaches unity, while its moment residual scales inversely with the step relative to macroscopic error. On periodic domains, combining this scaling with linearized acoustic propagation and viscous diffusion yields a macroscopic auxiliary system driven by the conserved-moment residual and solved in Fourier space for low-wavenumber errors. For solid walls, reference-state linearization of the complete sweep, including executed bounce-back updates, yields a sparse kinetic correction. Both auxiliary systems compute increments from the full nonlinear residual, and we prove fixed-point equivalence with the original discrete system, preserving unsteady and nonlinear convective effects. Refining the time step on fixed grids verifies second-order temporal self-convergence of slowly varying periodic velocity fields in two and three dimensions. Under fixed physical steps and tolerances, mean inner sweeps per step drop from hundreds in three-dimensional periodic flow and thousands in a two-dimensional cavity to a few.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables (main text), plus 10-page Supplementary Materials (29 pages total); v2: restructured manuscript with expanded discrete defect analysis, fixed-point equivalence proof, and extended verification details

papers.title: Invariant Shape Analysis of Surfaces with Spherical Topology
papers.abstract: Every real spherical harmonic of even degree is congruent to its mirror image. We prove that a real spherical harmonic of odd degree $n\ge3$ with distinct Maxwell axes is congruent to its mirror image if and only if the hyperelliptic curve of genus $n-1$ defined by its binary form has a reduced automorphism of even order whose lift acts on the form by $-1$. We then determine the locus of these curves: it is the locus of curves with an extra involution if and only if $n-1$ is a power of two, and otherwise it also contains, for each even divisor $k$ of $n-1$ with odd cofactor $d\ge3$, an irreducible family $y^2=x K(x^{2k})$, $°K=d$, with generic reduced automorphism group $\Z/2k$. For $n=3$ the condition is the vanishing of the skew invariant of the binary sextic. As an application, the invariants of the truncated spherical harmonic expansion of a genus-zero surface, in a conformal parameterization normalized by its conformal barycenter, give a descriptor that is exactly invariant under parameterization, position and scale, records handedness, and is stable in the orbit distance.

papers.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
papers.abstract: We introduce a technique for studying state preparation complexity in the quantum $p$-spin model on $n$ qubits, a disordered quantum spin system with random interactions on every set of $p$ qubits. We reduce the task of proving state preparation lower bounds to bounding the local profile complexity of the class, a quantity derived from the metric entropy of the set of vectors recording each state's expectation values against all weight-$p$ Pauli strings. We show that, for sufficiently large fixed $p$, any class with local profile complexity $O(n^2)$ remains separated from the ground-state energy by $Ω(\sqrt n)$, a gap on the leading energy scale. When the profile complexity is $o(n^2)$, we prove the stronger conclusion that the class cannot outperform a benchmark class of simpler states at leading order. Product states always provide such a benchmark. Our framework strengthens known bounds and covers classes beyond the reach of previous methods. These include examples where circuit lightcones extend across the entire system, preventing an application of standard arguments. We obtain an $Ω(n^2/\log n)$ gate lower bound for preparing near-ground states and depth--width tradeoffs, allowing arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and arbitrarily many discardable ancillas. We also derive lower bounds on entanglement depth and matrix product state bond dimension, and energy obstructions for forward and reverse magic at every fixed level of Parham's magic hierarchy (arXiv:2504.19966). For Clifford circuits doped with $T$-gates, we obtain sharper energy comparisons using product stabilizer states as a more restrictive benchmark. The proof combines an adaptation of a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem (arXiv:1810.12197) with metric-entropy bounds for the Gaussian process indexed by the local profiles of states in the class.

papers.title: Sharp Convergence and Sample Complexity of Policy Mirror Descent for Average-Reward MDPs
papers.abstract: Policy mirror descent (PMD) has a mature finite-time theory in discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs), but less is known in the average-reward setting, a more natural objective for many control applications. We give a finite-time, finite-sample analysis of PMD in ergodic average-reward MDPs built around a single master recursion that governs convergence for any critic, without external regularization. Its specializations yield linear rates for exact, inexact-tabular, and linear function approximation (LFA) updates. For exact PMD, the rate is tight in the worst case, and convergence can become superlinear. We complement these convergence results with critics whose end-to-end sample complexities improve the prior best policy-gradient dependence from $|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3$ to $|S|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3+|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^2$ in the tabular setting and from $|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^5$ to $d\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3$ under LFA. Matching information-theoretic lower bounds establish that both critics are optimal up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: A New Upper Bound for 7-Universal Tournaments
