papers.abstract: A tournament is $k$-universal if it contains every tournament on $k$ vertices as a subtournament. We give a 7-universal tournament on 14 vertices, improving the upper bound of 15 due to Zhang and Szeider. Together with their lower bound, it follows that the smallest 7-universal tournament has 13 or 14 vertices.

papers.title: Fast Almost-Uniform Sampling of Random $k$-SAT Solutions
papers.abstract: We study approximately uniform sampling of satisfying assignments from random $k$-SAT formulas. Fix a constant $B>0$. For every $k\ge 2^{20}$ and density $0<α\le 2^k/k^{16}$, we prove that, with high probability over a random formula on $n$ variables, every accuracy $n^{-B}\le\varepsilon\le 1/2$ admits a sampler whose output distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on satisfying assignments with expected running time $$\widetilde O_B\left(\mathrm{poly}(k,α+1)n^{2+η}\right),\quad 0<η\le 2^{16-k}.$$ In particular, the exponent of $n$ is $2+O(2^{-k})$ while the dependence on the width and density is polynomial with a universal degree. This improves the parameter-dependent polynomial exponent of the sampling algorithm of Chen, Lonkar, Wang, Yang, and Yin (STOC 2025) in the density regime $2^k/\mathrm{poly}(k)$. Our algorithm separates a high-degree core from the remaining variables. Every residual formula on the good variables is a deletion subformula of a common bounded-dependency formula. Adapting the rejection--repair framework of Liu, Wang, Yin, Zhang and Zhou (arXiv 2026), we construct an executable sampler for all such residual formulas using ordinary connected violation sets replacing weighted 2-tree witnesses and use it to simulate approximate block heat-bath updates on the core. To analyze the resulting core chain, we integrate out the good variables, represent the core marginal by an absolutely convergent polymer expansion and combine a component-swap variance comparison with an adaptive exploration bound. Absorbing single-component interactions into the local weights leaves interactions of cluster size at least two; retaining their additional decay gives a spectral gap of at least $1/(2s n^{2^{12-k}})$ where $s$ counts core components. Together with the residual sampler, this yields the stated running time.
papers.comments: A revised version with fast expected running time

papers.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Turán problems
papers.abstract: Given a graph $T$ and a nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a host graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman [Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error of $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. Previous advances toward this conjecture include the resolution of the canonical case $T=K_2$ by Alon, Shapira, and Sudakov [Ann. of Math., 2009], as well as the case of $\operatorname{ex}(G,K_m,K_k)$ by Alon and Shikhelman. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for every bipartite graph $T$ and every clique $T$. Our proof reductions combine several techniques, including iterative leaf additions, symmetric rooted extensions, and random transversals. Together, they encode the optimal value of the NP-hard Max $r$-Colorable Subgraph problem into the objectives $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ for a suitably constructed graph $G$.

papers.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
papers.abstract: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source--destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---a central conjecture in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $Θ(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is \[ O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+ \frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon} \right]\right), \] where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $Θ\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+ \frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean~4.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Lean 4 formalization and verification code: https://github.com/rtyu-1/coded-sorting-lean

papers.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
papers.abstract: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.
papers.comments: v2: revised/extended; new title (v1: "Keep Pace to Learn: Movable Antennas Restore the Backpropagated Gradient Under User Mobility"); added coauthor Zhaoyang Zhang. Same research question/system model; expanded analysis/experiments. Extended manuscript submitted to IEEE JSAC; Appendices C-K omitted from journal submission for space. 22 pages, 15 figures, 10 tables

papers.title: A general recipe for data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for iterative algorithms
papers.abstract: Most convergence guarantees for iterative stochastic algorithms are stated at a fixed iteration count and do not justify stopping at a data-dependent time. Recent anytime-valid envelopes do, but deterministic ones are typically too conservative for practical stopping, and existing data-adaptive ones are derived case-by-case, each concerned with a specific algorithm and a specific noise model and boundary construction. This paper provides a general recipe for sharp, data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for a large class of iterative algorithms. Our approach has two key steps: an optimization module derives a one-step recursion that performance measures of many such algorithms satisfy, reducing the error analysis to time-uniform concentration for predictably weighted sums of noise. Then, a statistical module ports the sub-$ψ$ condition to vector-valued processes, uniformly over predictable weights, and derives off-the-shelf boundaries via mixtures, stitching, and product betting martingales. Combining the two yields readymade envelopes for many iterative algoithms including but not limited to stochastic gradient descent (SGD), Oja's algorithm, temporal difference learning, Q-learning, and Bures-Wasserstein SGD, many with no prior data-adaptive anytime-valid guarantees. Specifically, for SGD, our framework recovers, often under weaker conditions, or significantly sharpens every existing envelope we are aware of. Our constructions come with explicit implementation details and are substantiated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Majorization for superpositions of nonorthogonal states and the existence of golden states
papers.abstract: Golden states, from which every state can be prepared by free operations, are the units of a resource theory. In the resource theory of superposition relative to linearly independent, nonorthogonal reference states, they were known only for two reference states and for special overlap matrices, all of them maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. We determine what decides their existence and when this Löwdin pattern holds. For every overlap matrix, the robustness and the geometric measure of superposition are maximized by the same states, which overlap equally with all reference states; the maximal values are set by the ground-state energy of a classical $XY$ model on the dual basis. These states, and only these, are golden under the maximal superposition-free operations, but they need not be maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove Gram majorization, a necessary and sufficient criterion for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients, which reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that every golden state of these operations is maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis, yet golden states exist only for special overlap matrices: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit one if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $Φ$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(π+|Φ|)/3]$, so that a geometric phase decides whether the theory has a unit. Finally, equal-overlap states yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the Löwdin basis, which show that white noise is a resource unless the reference states are orthonormal.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
papers.abstract: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.

papers.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodictive tests: a unifying classical variational principle
papers.abstract: A single classical f-divergence has several inequivalent quantum versions, but what distinguishes them operationally is less clear. Matsumoto's reverse tests characterize the maximal quantum f-divergence as the least classical distinguishability needed to prepare two quantum states with one device. Here we introduce retrodictive tests, in which two reverse tests sharing a reference state are coupled via Bayesian retrodiction to define a forward and a reverse stochastic process. In the forward process, the system is prepared by the first device and measured by the Petz transpose of the second; the reverse process interchanges their roles. We seek the least classical distinguishability between these two processes, as measured by the f-divergence between their joint laws, for fixed prescribed states and reference. For full-rank states in finite dimension, we prove that the canonical spectral implementations attain this minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. The reference then determines which quantum f-divergence is obtained: a flat reference gives the standard divergences, with the Nussbaum--Szkoła distributions as optimal joint laws; either prescribed state as reference recovers Matsumoto's reverse tests and the maximal divergences; and power references give the geodesic family. In particular, the Umegaki and Belavkin--Staszewski relative entropies arise from the same classical variational principle under different choices of reference. Spectral optimality extends to processes containing a quantum channel; for channels with full-rank Choi operator, the minimum of the forward relative entropy agrees with a known average entropy production.
papers.comments: v3: 17 pages, improved presentation and figures, submitted version; v2: 20 pages, 2 figures, improved presentation; v1: 18 pages, 2 figures, preliminary version, comments welcome; 100th arXiv post

papers.title: Classification of the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection
papers.abstract: We show that $K_6^{(2)} \cap X_6^{(2)} = D_6^{(1)} \cup C_6^{(1)}$ up to standard Hadamard equivalence, where $C_6^{(1)}$ is a non-affine one-parameter family of complex Hadamard matrices. This demonstrates that the intersection of the two-parameter Hadamard families of Karlsson and Szöllősi is strictly larger than the affine Diţă curve $D_6^{(1)}$. Our new parametrisation of the Szöllősi family $X_6^{(2)}$ in Karlsson coordinates and our constructive classification of the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection shed light on the intersection of block-reducible forms and hypocycloid constraints. This may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions.

papers.title: On the Error Analysis of Triangular Transport Maps for Conditional Generation via MMD-based Objectives
papers.abstract: Conditional generative models parameterized by triangular transport maps are widely used for conditional sampling, yet theoretical guarantees on the quality of the conditional measures they produce remain scarce. We address this question for minimum divergence estimators of triangular maps. We use MMD-based objectives as a tractable setting in which the gap between joint and conditional errors can be analyzed precisely, and we measure performance through the average conditional estimation error, defined as the squared maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between the estimated and the true conditionals, averaged over the conditioning variable. We first show that the common practice of minimizing a joint MMD may fail to recover the conditionals: writing the joint and the conditional criteria as quadratic energies of the same conditional mean embedding residual, we prove that, for parametric classes, joint minimizers are generically inconsistent in the misspecified setting. We then analyze an estimator that directly minimizes the conditional criterion through a surrogate loss computable from joint target samples and reference samples. We prove a non-asymptotic error bound that decomposes the average conditional estimation error into approximation, estimation, and reference sampling errors, with fast rates independent of the ambient dimension in the parametric setting. Finally, for joint MMDs built from concentrating Gaussian kernels on the conditioning variable, we show that the joint criterion approximates a density-reweighted version of the conditional one, and we derive an error bound for the joint minimizer whose rate suffers from a curse of dimensionality in the conditioning variable. Our results suggest that training criteria for conditional generative models should target the conditional rather than the joint error, a principle that extends to other divergences and to dynamic transport.
papers.comments: 69 pages, 1 figure. v2: added discussion of related work on engression error analyses that appeared while this manuscript was in preparation. Minor corrections

papers.title: MPS overlaps and Sklyanin determinants
papers.abstract: We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.

papers.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).

papers.title: Reflected constraint algebras of open Carroll--Weyl null strings
papers.abstract: We study whether open null strings admit the full Carroll--Weyl gauge symmetry consistently with endpoint conditions and nontrivial physical degrees of freedom. For endpoints constrained to timelike defects, natural variations imply that any nonzero Carroll flow must be tangent to the worldsheet boundary. For a fixed linear defect through the target origin, we construct a differentiable Hamiltonian system on this branch. Its complete Carroll--Weyl generator requires no additional boundary charge. Smooth reflection defines a preserved subdomain and gives a circle interpretation to selected sine and cosine modes of the constraints. Their centreless algebra extends the two-constraint open-string algebra by the local scale constraint. An endpoint obstruction shows that this reflection condition excludes some gauge orbits of the natural interval theory: we exhibit a regular four-dimensional solution with no corresponding reflected representative. Within the reflected sector, we construct a local canonical field pair and conserved target-space Lorentz charges. A separate solution family has nonzero boost charge and a nondegenerate two-dimensional symplectic pullback. The constraint algebra, the boundary choice, and the physical observables thus provide complementary information about the open theory.
papers.comments: Major revision with structure rearranged, 26 pages, 2 figures

papers.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
papers.abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $Π_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[ρ]\in H^3(BG,Π_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=Π_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 9 figures; Added acknowledgement, 3.4.2 deleted, Appendix C restructured

papers.title: Accelerating Nonlinear MPC by Behavior Cloning with Separated Timescales: Application to Nuclear Reactor Load-Following
papers.abstract: Behavior Cloning (BC) of expert controllers for multiscale dynamical systems is challenging: state variables evolving at widely separated timescales induce highly nonlinear couplings that a shared latent space may fail to adequately represent, degrading closed-loop generalization. We propose Structured Representation Learning for Behavior Cloning (SRLBC), an architecture designed to leverage the physical knowledge of multiscale systems in which slow state variables, fast (stiff) state variables, and predictable exogenous inputs evolve at different timescales. On 500 long-horizon roll-outs of a pressurized water reactor (PWR) load-following benchmark -a high-dimensional, stiff industrial system with challenging safety constraints -and across 20 training seeds, separated embeddings systematically outperform shared embedding baselines on cumulative cost, imitation accuracy and constraint satisfaction. The resulting standalone policies approach NMPC closed-loop performance at a computational cost 15 times lower on average. Since standalone policies still leave a few percent of trajectories infeasible, we embed the learned policies in a safety-augmented approximate NMPC framework, in which the optimizer is only called when the predicted input sequence is not certified as safe. This yields controllers still 6.8 times faster than the NMPC controller on average, with a feasibility (i.e., constraint satisfaction) of at least 99.8% for all architectures, SRLBC retaining the lowest closed-loop cost. Under distribution shift, standalone BC policies degrade sharply: SRLBC degrades the least, and once safety-augmented, it retains a feasibility above 98% with the lowest closed-loop cost. Beyond the quantitative results, Jacobian-based sensitivity analysis shows that the resulting controller relies on a sparse and less redundant set of latent features, each attributable to a single group of physical variables, and aligned with the physical timescale decomposition of the system.

papers.title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
papers.abstract: Deep lid-driven cavities contain strong motion beneath the lid and much weaker recirculation at depth, so agreement in bulk velocity is an incomplete assessment of a computed flow. We examine data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for steady, two-dimensional incompressible flow in a cavity of depth-to-width ratio five at Reynolds numbers 100, 250, 500 and 1000. An established hard-constrained streamfunction formulation is combined with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants. Independent spectral/$hp$ calculations with the same Gaussian-regularized lid provide the reference fields. For a cavity of depth-to-width ratio $D/W=5$ at Reynolds numbers $\mathrm{Re}=100$, 250, 500, and 1000, evaluation on a common $121\times605$ grid gives interior relative velocity discrepancies of 5.130\%--7.850\%. Over the same cases, floor-region relative velocity discrepancies remain below 5\%, with absolute RMS discrepancies ranging from $1.255\times10^{-10}U$ to $2.332\times10^{-9}U$, where $U$ is the lid-velocity scale. In a separate $161\times801$ assessment at $\Rey=1000$, the refined workflow lowers interior velocity discrepancy from 5.624\% to 2.658\% and gauge-aligned pressure RMS discrepancy from $2.793\times10^{-3}$ to $1.167\times10^{-3}ρU^2$. The improvements compare accumulated training workflows and do not isolate regional sampling. Configuration rankings depend on both region and observable. These finite-budget comparisons establish where the retained workflows agree with the reference and where rotational-field discrepancies remain substantial.

papers.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.

papers.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE
papers.abstract: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.
papers.comments: 93 pages. Ancillary files: exact local checks (Python 3, standard library only). v2: explicit horizon in Corollary 55, minor corrections

papers.title: Quasinormal-mode encounters: Pseudospectra near Kerr--Newman exceptional points
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. Along matched parameter paths toward the selected EPs, the frequency splitting follows a square-root law and the condition numbers grow as the inverse square root of the distance to the EP. Their product, which approximates the norm of the double-pole coefficient, does not depend on the offset or, for GE, on the angular truncation and projection used. The pseudospectral contours resolve the transition from individual-mode sensitivity to the collective response of the pair. At the selected backgrounds and resolution, both pair members are more sensitive than two more-damped modes at the same background, but this ordering holds only below a crossover offset that decreases with radial resolution. For the GE pair, angular refinement also displaces the coalescence by more than the selected offset. Within the discretized problems and energy norms considered here, these results describe qualitative trends of spectral instability near EPs rather than continuum magnitudes, and motivate further study of their possible role in black-hole ringdown.
papers.comments: 14 pages + appendices, 8 figures, 8 tables, references added
